Light Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

name: Bandit Captain
classification: Medium humanoid (any race), any non-lawful alignment
description: A gang leader or pirate captain who keeps a crew in line through cunning and force. Prisoners might earn better treatment by flattering the captain.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee Scimitar attacks and one melee Dagger attack, or two ranged Dagger attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack would hit, the captain can gain +2 AC against it if the captain can see the attacker and is wielding a melee weapon.

name: Commoner
description: Use this profile for ordinary townsfolk and travelers, such as artisans, merchants, servants, and pilgrims.

sections.Actions: Club. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.

name: Air Elemental
description: A moving funnel of air with a face that briefly forms among the dust and debris.

sections.Damage resistances: Lightning, thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Air Form. It can move into a hostile creature’s space and stop there. It can pass through an opening as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Elemental Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Whirlwind (Recharge 4–6). Each creature in the elemental’s space makes a DC 13 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 15 (3d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage, is thrown 20 ft. away in a random direction, and falls prone. If the thrown creature hits an object, including a wall or floor, it takes an additional 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage per 10 ft. it was thrown. If thrown at another creature, the second creature makes a DC 13 Dexterity save. On a failure it takes the same collision damage and falls prone. A creature that succeeds on the initial Strength save takes half the initial damage and keeps its position and posture.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 123–124. Damage resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Earth Elemental
description: A walking mass of soil and jagged stone that can sense footsteps through the ground.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Senses: Darkvision 60 ft., tremorsense 60 ft., passive Perception 10.
sections.Traits:
Earth Glide. It can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone without disturbing it.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures.
Elemental Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 123–124. Damage resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Fire Elemental
description: A flickering humanoid outline at the center of a wandering blaze.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Fire Form. It can move into a hostile creature’s space and stop there. It can pass through an opening as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing. A creature that touches it, or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft., takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. The first time the elemental enters a creature’s space on a turn, that creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage and ignites. The burning creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until someone uses an action to put out the flames.
Illumination. It sheds bright light for 30 ft. and dim light for another 30 ft.
Water Susceptibility. It takes 1 cold damage per 5 ft. it moves in water and per gallon of water splashed on it.
Elemental Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Touch attacks.
Touch. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 10 (2d6 + 3) fire damage. A creature or flammable object hit by this attack ignites and takes 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until a creature uses an action to extinguish it.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 123 and 125. Damage resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Water Elemental
description: A cresting wave that rolls across the ground and briefly takes on a recognizable shape.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Water Form. It can move into a hostile creature’s space and stop there. It can pass through an opening as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Freeze. Cold damage partially freezes the elemental and reduces its speed by 20 ft. until the end of its next turn.
Elemental Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Whelm (Recharge 4–6). Each creature in the elemental’s space makes a DC 15 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If Large or smaller, it is also grappled (escape DC 14). While held, it is restrained and can breathe only if it can breathe water. On a success, the creature is pushed out of the elemental’s space. The elemental can hold one Large creature or up to two Medium or smaller creatures at once. At the start of each of the elemental’s turns, every target it holds takes another 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A creature within 5 ft. can use an action and succeed on a DC 14 Strength check to pull a creature or object out.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 123 and 125. Errata specifies a Strength check to pull a target out of Whelm and updates damage resistance wording.

name: Invisible Stalker
description: An air elemental bound into service as a tracker. Magic that reveals invisible creatures shows its faint outline.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious.
sections.Languages: Auran. It understands Common but cannot speak it.
sections.Traits:
Invisibility. It is naturally invisible, including while it attacks.
Faultless Tracker. The summoner assigns a quarry. The stalker knows the quarry’s direction and distance while they share a plane. It also knows its summoner’s location.
Elemental Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Directed hunter: The stalker waits with its summoner until given a task. It can be tasked to find and kill a specific creature or retrieve an object. Any other assignment breaks the binding and releases the stalker. When it finishes, it returns for more orders while the binding lasts. If its summoner dies before the task is done, it vanishes once it completes the task. Defeat or expiration of the binding also dismisses it. It resents its orders and may exploit vague wording on long assignments.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 192. Damage resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Azer
description: A bronze-skinned craftsperson with a fiery beard, sculpted by another azer and animated from the maker’s own flame.

sections.Traits:
Heated Body. A creature that touches the azer, or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft., takes 5 (1d10) fire damage.
Heated Weapons. The azer adds 3 (1d6) fire damage to a hit with a metal melee weapon. The Warhammer action already includes this damage.
Illumination. It sheds bright light for 10 ft. and dim light for another 10 ft.
Living Fire. It needs no food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Warhammer. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage with one hand or 8 (1d10 + 3) with two hands. Add 3 (1d6) fire damage to either.

name: Cloud Giant
classification: Huge giant, neutral good (50%) or neutral evil (50%)
description: Cloud giants live in mountain castles and on solid clouds. Treasure, beautiful works of art, and lavish gifts earn them standing among their kin.

sections.Traits: Keen Smell. The giant has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on scent.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma. The giant needs no material components for these spells. For a spell that calls for a save, use DC 15, calculated from Charisma +3 and proficiency +4.
At will. Detect Magic, Fog Cloud, Light.
3/day each. Feather Fall, Fly, Misty Step, Telekinesis.
1/day each. Control Weather, Gaseous Form.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Morningstar attacks.
Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 21 (3d8 + 8) piercing damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +12 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 151 and 154. The official errata corrects the Constitution saving throw to +10.

name: Hill Giant
description: Hill giants roam hills and valleys looking for food. They raid farms and press smaller creatures into feeding them.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Greatclub attacks.
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 18 (3d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit 21 (3d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

name: Stone Giant
description: Stone giants carve their secluded caverns into settlements. They prize skilled sculptors and judge rock throwing by grace as well as strength.

sections.Traits: Stone Camouflage. When hiding in rocky terrain, the giant has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Greatclub attacks.
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage. On a hit, a creature must make a DC 17 Strength save or fall Prone.
sections.Reactions: Rock Catching. When someone throws a rock or similar object at the giant, it can attempt a DC 10 Dexterity save as a reaction. On a success, it catches the object and takes no bludgeoning damage from it.

name: Bugbear
description: A bugbear waits out of sight until a target comes close enough for a heavy first blow.

sections.Traits:
Brute. On a hit with a melee weapon, roll one extra weapon damage die. The attacks below already include it where applicable.
Surprise Attack. If the bugbear surprised a creature, its hits against that creature in the first round of combat deal an extra 7 (2d6) damage.
sections.Actions:
Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d8 + 2) piercing damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing damage in melee or 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage when thrown.

name: Gnoll
description: This hyena-headed raider closes on its next prey as soon as its first target falls.

sections.Traits: Rampage. On its turn, if the gnoll drops a creature to 0 HP with a melee attack, it can spend a bonus action to move up to half its speed and make one Bite attack.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) with a two-handed melee attack.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

name: Goblin
description: A shield and a shortbow let the goblin harry travelers and duck back into cover.

sections.Traits: Nimble Escape. The goblin can Disengage or Hide as a bonus action on each of its turns.
sections.Actions:
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

name: Hobgoblin
description: An armored hobgoblin works with its allies to punish any foe they pin in place.

sections.Traits: Martial Advantage. Once per turn, when the hobgoblin hits a creature with a weapon, it can deal an extra 7 (2d6) damage if one of its allies is within 5 ft. of the target and is not Incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage, or 6 (1d10 + 1) if wielded with two hands.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

name: Kobold
description: A kobold fights best with allies close by, away from direct sun.

sections.Traits:
Sunlight Sensitivity. While the kobold is in sunlight, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
Pack Tactics. The kobold has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally within 5 ft. of that creature is not Incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Dagger. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Sling. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

name: Lizardfolk
description: Lizardfolk make armor and tools from hides, shells, and bones. They can approach a fight underwater.

sections.Traits: Hold Breath. The lizardfolk can go up to 15 minutes without taking a breath.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks, each with a different weapon.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Heavy Club. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Spiked Shield. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

name: Orc
description: This lightly armored warrior carries a greataxe for close combat and a javelin for targets farther away.

sections.Traits: Aggressive. The orc can use a bonus action to move up to its speed toward a hostile creature it can see.
sections.Actions:
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (1d12 + 3) slashing damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

name: Grimlock
description: An eyeless Underdark hunter that tracks prey by sound and scent.

sections.Senses: Blindsight 30 ft., reduced to 10 ft. while Deafened. The grimlock is blind beyond that radius. Passive Perception 13.
sections.Traits:
Blind Senses. The grimlock loses its blindsight if it is both Deafened and unable to smell.
Keen Hearing and Smell. The grimlock has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
Stone Camouflage. The grimlock has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in rocky terrain.
sections.Actions: Spiked Bone Club. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) piercing damage.

name: Centaur
description: Centaurs follow long migration routes and trade with travelers they trust.

sections.Traits: Charge. After moving at least 30 ft. straight toward a target, a Pike hit against it on the same turn deals an extra 10 (3d6) piercing damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Pike attack and one Hooves attack, or two Longbow attacks.
Pike. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 9 (1d10 + 4) piercing damage.
Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

name: Deva
description: Devas carry divine messages between planes and often take an ordinary mortal form when dealing with mortals.

sections.Damage resistances: Radiant. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Angelic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical and deal an extra 4d8 radiant damage on a hit. The Mace damage already includes this.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Immortal Nature. It needs no food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma (spell save DC 17). Only verbal components are required.
At will. Detect Evil and Good.
1/day each. Commune, Raise Dead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Mace. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage.
Healing Touch (3/day). Touch another creature. It magically regains 20 (4d8 + 2) HP and is freed of any curse, disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.
Change Shape. Magically take the form of a humanoid or beast of CR 10 or lower, or return to true form. Death restores the true form. The deva chooses whether its equipment merges into the new form or stays on it. It keeps its ability to speak and its other statistics, but uses the new form’s AC, movement modes, Strength, Dexterity, and special senses. It also gains the new form’s statistics and abilities it lacks, except for class features, legendary actions, and lair actions.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 15–16. Official errata gives Insight +9 and updates resistance wording.

name: Doppelganger
description: A doppelganger watches the people it intends to impersonate and reads their surface thoughts to learn details a disguise cannot supply.

sections.Traits:
Shapechanger. As an action, take the form of a Small or Medium humanoid it has seen, or return to true form. Only its size changes. Its equipment keeps its form. Death restores its true form.
Ambusher. In the first round of combat, it has advantage on attack rolls against creatures it surprised.
Surprise Attack. If it surprises a creature and hits that creature during the first round of combat, the attack deals an extra 10 (3d6) damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Read Thoughts. Magically read the surface thoughts of one creature within 60 ft. The effect passes through barriers unless blocked by 3 ft. of wood or earth, 2 ft. of stone, 2 in. of metal, or a thin sheet of lead. Keep reading while the target stays in range and the doppelganger maintains concentration as if on a spell. While reading its mind, the doppelganger has advantage on Wisdom (Insight) and Charisma (Deception, Intimidation, and Persuasion) checks against the creature.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 82. Official errata limits Ambusher to the first round.

name: Harpy
description: Harpies nest in places where their victims have trouble moving safely. Their song can lure prey toward a cliff or patch of quicksand.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claws attack and one Club attack.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (2d4 + 1) slashing damage.
Club. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.
Luring Song. Each humanoid and giant within 300 ft. that hears the magical song must make a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure the creature is Charmed until the song ends. The harpy uses a bonus action on each subsequent turn to continue singing. It can stop at any time, and the song ends if it is Incapacitated.
A creature Charmed this way is Incapacitated and ignores other harpies’ songs. If it is more than 5 ft. away, it must move toward the harpy by the most direct route on its turn, without avoiding opportunity attacks. It can repeat the save before entering damaging terrain, whenever damaged by a source other than the harpy, and at the end of each of its turns. A successful initial or repeat save grants immunity to this harpy’s song for 24 hours and ends any active effect.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 181. Official errata makes movement toward the harpy mandatory.

name: Lamia
description: A lamia hides the ruin of its lair with illusions. Jackalweres bring captives and stolen goods while it watches the roads with Scrying.

sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma (spell save DC 13). No material components required.
At will. Disguise Self (any humanoid form), Major Image.
3/day each. Charm Person, Mirror Image, Scrying, Suggestion.
1/day. Geas.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claws attack and either one Dagger attack or one Intoxicating Touch attack.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d10 + 3) slashing damage.
Dagger. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
Intoxicating Touch. Melee spell attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit magically curses the target for 1 hour. The curse gives it disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws and all ability checks.

name: Medusa
description: A medusa may hide among its former victims in a ruined estate. It keeps polished surfaces out of its lair to avoid seeing its own reflection.

sections.Traits:
Petrifying Gaze. When a creature starts its turn within 30 ft. and can see the medusa’s eyes, the medusa can force a DC 14 Constitution saving throw if it can see that creature and is not Incapacitated. Failure by 5 or more immediately Petrifies the creature. A smaller failure Restrains it as it begins turning to stone. At the end of its next turn it repeats the save. Failure Petrifies it and success ends the effect. Greater Restoration or other magic can end the petrification.
Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes at the start of its turn to avoid the save. It cannot see the medusa until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the medusa in the meantime, it must immediately save. The medusa is subject to its own gaze if it sees its reflection on a polished surface within 30 ft. in an area of bright light.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Snake Hair attack and two Shortsword attacks, or two Longbow attacks.
Snake Hair. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) poison damage.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.

name: Minotaur
description: A minotaur hunts through mazes, caves, and old passageways. It can retrace every route it has taken.

sections.Traits:
Charge. If the minotaur moves at least 10 ft. straight toward a target and hits it with Gore on the same turn, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) piercing damage. A creature hit this way must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or be pushed up to 10 ft. away and knocked Prone.
Labyrinthine Recall. It perfectly recalls any path it has traveled.
Reckless. At the start of its turn, it can gain advantage on all melee weapon attack rolls it makes that turn. If it does, attack rolls against it have advantage until the start of its next turn.
sections.Actions:
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d12 + 4) slashing damage.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.

name: Rakshasa
description: A rakshasa often poses as a merchant, aristocrat, or priest. Its tigerlike face and reversed hands reveal its true form.

sections.Damage vulnerabilities: Piercing damage from magical weapons wielded by good creatures.
sections.Damage immunities: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Limited Magic Immunity. Spells of 6th level or lower cannot affect or detect the rakshasa unless it allows them to. It has advantage on saving throws against all other spells and magical effects.
Evil Reborn. If it dies on the Material Plane, its essence returns to the Nine Hells. Its body reforms over months or years, and it keeps its memories. Death in the Nine Hells destroys it permanently.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma (spell save DC 18, +10 to hit with spell attacks). No material components required.
At will. Detect Thoughts, Disguise Self, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
3/day each. Charm Person, Detect Magic, Invisibility, Major Image, Suggestion.
1/day each. Dominate Person, Fly, Plane Shift, True Seeing.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d6 + 2) slashing damage. A creature hit is also magically cursed. Horrible visions and dreams afflict it whenever it takes a short or long rest, and it gains no benefit from completing the rest. Remove Curse or similar magic ends the curse.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 257. Official errata adds protection from detection to Limited Magic Immunity and updates damage immunity wording.

name: Ankheg
description: An enormous burrowing insect that waits beneath trails or pasture for prey to pass overhead.

sections.Armor: Natural armor. AC falls to 11 while prone.
sections.Senses: Darkvision 60 ft. and tremorsense 60 ft. Passive Perception 11.
sections.Encounter notes: The ankheg leaves narrow, partly collapsed tunnels as it burrows through earth. Molted chitin or hatched eggs can mark its tunnels.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) acid damage. A Large or smaller creature is grappled, escape DC 13. Until this grapple ends, the ankheg can bite only the creature it holds and has advantage on those Bite attacks.
Acid Spray (recharge 6). Use only while the ankheg is grappling no creature. Each creature in a line 30 ft. long and 5 ft. wide makes a DC 13 Dexterity save. Deal 10 (3d6) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 21. The official errata sets the Bite average slashing damage to 10.

name: Basilisk
description: A low-slung cave predator that turns prey to stone before feeding.

sections.Traits:
Petrifying Gaze. Unless incapacitated, the basilisk can force a DC 12 Constitution save at the start of another creature’s turn when that creature is within 30 ft. and the two can see each other. On a failure the creature starts turning to stone and becomes restrained. It saves again at the end of its next turn. Success ends the effect. Failure petrifies it until Greater Restoration or other magic frees it.
A creature that begins its turn without being surprised can avert its eyes to avoid the initial save. It cannot see the basilisk until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. Looking at the basilisk before then forces an immediate save.
If the basilisk sees its own reflection in bright light within 30 ft., it takes the reflection for a rival and directs the gaze at itself.
sections.Encounter notes: A basilisk raised in captivity can be trained to avoid meeting the eyes of creatures its keeper wants to protect. The book also describes oil derived from a basilisk’s gullet that reverses petrification. Lost parts stay missing, and the oil fails if the creature is missing a vital part.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage on a hit.

name: Chimera
description: A winged hunter with dragon, lion, and goat heads. It dives on prey and can breathe fire before landing.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite, one Horns attack, and one Claws attack. If Fire Breath is available, it can replace either Bite or Horns.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage on a hit.
Horns. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 10 (1d12 + 4) bludgeoning damage on a hit.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage on a hit.
Fire Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Deal 31 (7d8) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.

name: Mimic
description: An ambush predator that often takes the shape of a chest or door and waits for someone to touch it.

sections.Traits:
Shapechanger. As an action, take the form of an object or return to the true, amorphous form. Both forms use the same statistics and any worn or carried gear stays as it is. Death restores the true form.
Adhesive (object form only). Anything that touches the mimic sticks to it. A Huge or smaller creature that sticks is also grappled, escape DC 13. Escape checks have disadvantage.
False Appearance (object form only). While motionless, the mimic looks exactly like an ordinary object.
Grappler. The mimic has advantage on attack rolls against creatures it is grappling.
sections.Encounter notes: Rare mimics can hold a simple conversation in Common or Undercommon and may trade information or safe passage for food.
sections.Actions:
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage on a hit. The hit also applies Adhesive while the mimic is in object form.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) acid damage on a hit.

name: Shambling Mound
description: A mass of roots and rotting vegetation that lies still in a swamp until prey passes within reach.

sections.Senses: Blindsight 60 ft. The mound is blind beyond that range. Passive Perception 10.
sections.Traits: Lightning Absorption. Lightning deals no damage to the mound. It regains HP equal to the lightning damage it would have taken.
sections.Encounter notes: The living root-stem can feign death by collapsing its outer mound. A surviving root-stem may root itself and slowly regrow at an unspecified rate.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks. If both hit the same Medium or smaller target, it is grappled, escape DC 14, and the mound immediately uses Engulf on it.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage on a hit.
Engulf. Choose a Medium or smaller creature the mound is grappling. The creature becomes blinded and restrained, cannot breathe, and moves with the mound. At the start of each of the mound’s turns, the creature must make a DC 14 Constitution save or take 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. The mound can engulf only one creature at a time.

name: Wyvern
description: A two-legged flying dragon with a long venomous stinger. It usually attacks from the air.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Stinger attack. While flying, the wyvern can replace either one with Claws.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Deal 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage on a hit.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage on a hit.
Stinger. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage. The creature makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking another 24 (7d6) poison damage on a failure or half the poison damage on a success.

name: Roc
description: A solitary bird of prey large enough to carry off a giant. It nests high on remote peaks.

sections.Traits: Keen Sight. Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Beak attack and one Talons attack.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Deal 27 (4d8 + 9) piercing damage on a hit.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 23 (4d6 + 9) slashing damage and grapple the target, escape DC 19. While the grapple lasts, the target is restrained and the roc cannot use Talons on anyone else.

name: Winter Wolf
description: A giant white wolf with freezing breath. Frost giants keep winter wolves as guards and hunting companions.

sections.Traits:
Keen Hearing and Smell. Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on hearing or smell.
Pack Tactics. The wolf has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if one of the wolf’s allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and is not incapacitated.
Snow Camouflage. Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy terrain.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage on a hit. A creature that takes the hit must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.
Cold Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. Deal 18 (4d8) cold damage on a failure or half on a success.

name: Fire Giant
description: Fire giants build foundries and fortresses around sources of intense heat. They prize smithcraft and train children for war.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Greatsword attacks.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 28 (6d6 + 7) slashing damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +11 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit 29 (4d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage.

name: Frost Giant
description: Frost giants hunt and raid from high peaks and glacial strongholds. Their standing depends on feats of strength and trophies won in battle.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Greataxe attacks.
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 25 (3d12 + 6) slashing damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

name: Storm Giant
description: Storm giants live in secluded places, including underwater palaces. They watch the sea and sky for omens.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The giant breathes air and water.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma, spell save DC 17. The giant casts these spells without material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Levitate, Light.
3/day each. Control Weather, Water Breathing.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Greatsword attacks.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 30 (6d6 + 9) slashing damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +14 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit 35 (4d12 + 9) bludgeoning damage.
Lightning Strike (recharge 5–6). Choose a point the giant can see within 500 ft. and strike it with magical lightning. Every creature within 10 ft. of that point makes a DC 17 Dexterity save. It takes 54 (12d8) lightning damage on a failure or half that on a success.

name: Cyclops
description: A cyclops often lives alone or with a small family, tending a herd and driving strangers away from its territory.

sections.Traits: Poor Depth Perception. The cyclops rolls attacks with disadvantage against targets more than 30 ft. away.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Greatclub attacks.
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

name: Ettin
description: An ettin has two independent minds and one body. Its heads bicker constantly but can work together when threatened.

sections.Traits:
Two Heads. The ettin has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and on saves against being Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Stunned, or knocked Unconscious.
Wakeful. If either head sleeps, the other stays awake.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Battleaxe attack and one Morningstar attack.
Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage.
Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage.

name: Ogre
description: Ogres wander the edges of settlements, raiding isolated farms for food. They fill their sacks with whatever catches their eye.

sections.Actions:
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage.

name: Oni
description: An oni infiltrates settlements in a borrowed guise. It may serve a hag or wizard in return for a safe lair or a magic item.

sections.Traits:
Magic Weapons. The oni makes magical weapon attacks.
Regeneration. At the start of its turn, the oni regains 10 HP if it has at least 1 HP.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma, spell save DC 13. The oni casts these spells without material components.
At will. Darkness, Invisibility.
1/day each. Charm Person, Cone of Cold, Gaseous Form, Sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks with its claws or glaive.
Claw (oni form only). Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Glaive. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d10 + 4) slashing damage, or 9 (1d10 + 4) in Small or Medium form.
Change Shape. The oni magically takes the form of a Small or Medium humanoid or a Large giant, or returns to its true form. Its statistics stay the same except for size. Its glaive is the only gear that changes, shrinking in humanoid form so the oni can wield it. When the oni dies, it returns to its true form and the glaive returns to its normal size.

name: Succubus
description: A shapechanging fiend that starts by tempting mortals in their dreams, then visits them in a familiar guise.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning, and poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Languages: Abyssal, Common, Infernal, and telepathy 60 ft.
sections.Traits:
Telepathic Bond. The fiend can communicate telepathically with a creature under its Charm regardless of distance or plane.
Shapechanger. Use an action to take the shape of a Small or Medium humanoid, or resume true form. Only size and speed can change. The fiend loses its fly speed in a wingless form. Worn and carried gear keep their form. On death it resumes its true form.
sections.Actions:
Claw (fiend form only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Charm. Choose one visible humanoid within 30 ft. It makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or becomes magically Charmed for 1 day and follows the fiend's verbal or telepathic commands. A target that suffers harm or receives a suicidal command can repeat the save, ending the effect on a success. After a successful save against the effect or when it ends, the target is immune to this fiend's Charm for 24 hours. The fiend can charm only one target at once. Charming a new target ends the effect on the previous one.
Draining Kiss. Kiss a willing creature or one under the fiend's Charm. It makes a DC 15 Constitution save against this magic, taking 32 (5d10 + 5) psychic damage on a failure or half on a success. Reduce its hit point maximum by the damage dealt until it finishes a long rest. It dies if this reduction brings its maximum to 0.
Etherealness. The fiend uses magic to move between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane.
sections.Forms: A succubus and an incubus are forms of the same fiend. It can switch between them and typically prefers one. The book gives both forms a shared stat block.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 284–285. Damage resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Incubus
description: A shapechanging fiend that starts by tempting mortals in their dreams, then visits them in a familiar guise.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning, and poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Languages: Abyssal, Common, Infernal, and telepathy 60 ft.
sections.Traits:
Telepathic Bond. The fiend can communicate telepathically with a creature under its Charm regardless of distance or plane.
Shapechanger. Use an action to take the shape of a Small or Medium humanoid, or resume true form. Only size and speed can change. The fiend loses its fly speed in a wingless form. Worn and carried gear keep their form. On death it resumes its true form.
sections.Actions:
Claw (fiend form only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Charm. Choose one visible humanoid within 30 ft. It makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or becomes magically Charmed for 1 day and follows the fiend's verbal or telepathic commands. A target that suffers harm or receives a suicidal command can repeat the save, ending the effect on a success. After a successful save against the effect or when it ends, the target is immune to this fiend's Charm for 24 hours. The fiend can charm only one target at once. Charming a new target ends the effect on the previous one.
Draining Kiss. Kiss a willing creature or one under the fiend's Charm. It makes a DC 15 Constitution save against this magic, taking 32 (5d10 + 5) psychic damage on a failure or half on a success. Reduce its hit point maximum by the damage dealt until it finishes a long rest. It dies if this reduction brings its maximum to 0.
Etherealness. The fiend uses magic to move between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane.
sections.Forms: A succubus and an incubus are forms of the same fiend. It can switch between them and typically prefers one. The book gives both forms a shared stat block.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 284–285. Damage resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Grick
description: A mottled cave predator that rests among rubble or on ledges. Four barbed tentacles open around its beak when prey approaches.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits: Stone Camouflage. The grick has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in rocky terrain.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Tentacles attack. On a hit, the grick can make a Beak attack against the same target.
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 173. Damage resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Will-o'-Wisp
description: A drifting undead light that looks like a lantern at a distance. It draws travelers toward bogs, pits, and monster lairs.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, necrotic, and thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, and Unconscious.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Ephemeral. The wisp cannot wear or carry anything.
Incorporeal Movement. Moving through creatures or objects counts as difficult terrain. The wisp takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Variable Illumination. The wisp sheds bright light in a radius it sets between 5 and 20 ft., with dim light for the same distance beyond it.
Undead Nature. The wisp needs no air, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Shock. Melee spell attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 9 (2d8) lightning damage.
Invisibility. The wisp and its light become magically Invisible. This lasts until it attacks, uses Consume Life, or loses Concentration as if concentrating on a spell.
sections.Bonus actions:
Consume Life. Choose one visible living creature within 5 ft. that has 0 hit points. It makes a DC 10 Constitution save against this magic. On a failure, it dies and the wisp regains 10 (3d6) hit points.
Variable Illumination. Change the radius of the wisp's light.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 301. The official errata corrects the Invisibility reference to Consume Life and updates the damage resistance wording.

name: Yeti
description: A white-furred alpine hunter that tracks prey by scent and blends in with snow. Its gaze can freeze a victim in place.

sections.Traits:
Fear of Fire. If the yeti takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.
Keen Smell. The yeti has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on smell.
Snow Camouflage. The yeti has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in snowy terrain.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The yeti makes two Claw attacks and can also use Chilling Gaze.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) cold damage.
Chilling Gaze. Choose one visible creature within 30 ft. If it can see the yeti, it makes a DC 13 Constitution save against this magic. On a failure, it takes 10 (3d6) cold damage and becomes Paralyzed for 1 minute. Cold immunity prevents both effects. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect on a success. If it succeeds on a save or the effect on it ends, it is immune to the Chilling Gaze of all normal yetis for 1 hour. The hour of immunity does not apply to abominable yetis.

name: Sahuagin
description: An aquatic raider that worships the shark god Sekolah. A hunting party sounds a conch horn and can command sharks to join a raid.

sections.Traits:
Blood Frenzy. The sahuagin has advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures below their hit point maximum.
Limited Amphibiousness. It can breathe air and water. It must submerge at least once every 4 hours to avoid suffocating.
Shark Telepathy. The sahuagin can give magical telepathic commands to any shark within 120 ft.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks, one Bite and either Claws or Spear.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 3 (1d4 + 1) slashing damage.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage with a two-handed melee attack.

name: Cultist
classification: Medium humanoid (any race), any non-good alignment
description: A follower of a demon lord, archdevil, or other dark power. Many hide their devotion from neighbors and authorities.

sections.Traits: Dark Devotion. It has advantage on saving throws against being Charmed or Frightened.
sections.Actions: Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.

name: Cult Fanatic
classification: Medium humanoid (any race), any non-good alignment
description: A cult leader who uses doctrine and personal influence to recruit followers and build power.

sections.Traits: Dark Devotion. It has advantage on saving throws against being Charmed or Frightened.
sections.Spellcasting:
4th-level cleric spellcaster using Wisdom. Spell save DC 11. Spell attacks +3.
Cantrips (at will): Light, Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy.
1st level (4 slots): Command, Inflict Wounds, Shield of Faith.
2nd level (3 slots): Hold Person, Spiritual Weapon.
For magic item use and attunement, treat this NPC as a cleric with access to the cleric spell list.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 10 and 345. Includes official passive Perception and spellcasting corrections.

name: Guard
description: A watch officer, a fortified gate sentry, or a bodyguard hired by a merchant or noble.

sections.Actions: Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing if used with two hands in melee.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 347. Includes the official addition for a two-handed melee spear strike.

name: Gladiator
description: An arena fighter. Some are pit fighters who expect every match to turn deadly. Others are prized duelists who rarely kill an opponent.

sections.Traits:
Brave. The gladiator has advantage on saves against being Frightened.
Brute. On a hit with a melee weapon, roll one more die of that weapon's damage. The attack entries already include the extra die.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks or two ranged attacks.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing if used with two hands in melee.
Shield Bash. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller creature that fails a DC 15 Strength saving throw falls Prone.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack would hit the gladiator, it can add 3 to its AC against that attack if it can see the attacker and is wielding a melee weapon.

name: Noble
description: A noble or courtier whose money and connections buy influence. Guards and household servants often travel with them.

sections.Actions: Rapier. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack would hit the noble, they can add 2 to their AC against that attack if they can see the attacker and are wielding a melee weapon.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 348. Uses the officially corrected passive Perception.

name: Priest
description: A temple or shrine leader who teaches the faith and conducts rites. Acolytes often help with ceremonies.

sections.Spellcasting:
5th-level cleric spellcaster using Wisdom. Spell save DC 13. Spell attacks +5.
Cantrips (at will): Light, Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy.
1st level (4 slots): Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt, Sanctuary.
2nd level (3 slots): Lesser Restoration, Spiritual Weapon.
3rd level (2 slots): Dispel Magic, Spirit Guardians.
For magic item use and attunement, treat this NPC as a cleric with access to the cleric spell list.
sections.Actions: Mace. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Divine Eminence. As a bonus action, spend a spell slot to add magical radiant damage to each melee weapon attack that hits until the end of this turn. A 1st-level slot adds 10 (3d6) radiant damage. Add another 1d6 per slot level above 1st.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 10 and 348. Includes official corrections to speed, Religion, and spellcasting.

name: Veteran
description: A professional fighter who takes up arms for pay or for a cause. They might have served in an army or spent years fighting on their own.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Longsword attacks. If the veteran has a shortsword drawn, it can also make one Shortsword attack.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing with two hands.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 350. Uses the officially corrected heavy crossbow damage.

name: Ghost
description: A lingering soul bound to a person, place, or object that mattered in life.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, fire, lightning, and thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Ethereal Sight. It can see 60 ft. into the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane and 60 ft. into the Material Plane from the Ethereal Plane.
Incorporeal Movement. Treat creatures and objects as difficult terrain when passing through them. Ending a turn inside an object deals 5 (1d10) force damage to this creature.
Undead Nature. It can exist without air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Withering Touch. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 17 (4d6 + 3) necrotic damage.
Etherealness. The ghost moves between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane. Creatures can see the ghost from the Material Plane when it is in the Border Ethereal and from the Border Ethereal when it is on the Material Plane. Effects cannot reach in either direction across the planar boundary.
Horrifying Visage. Each non-undead creature within 60 ft. that can see the ghost makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. On a failure, the creature is Frightened for 1 minute. If that save fails by 5 or more, it also ages 1d4 × 10 years. While Frightened, it can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the condition. A successful save or the end of the effect grants 24 hours of immunity to this ghost's Horrifying Visage. Greater Restoration reverses the aging if cast within 24 hours of the aging.
Possession (recharge 6). Choose one visible Humanoid within 5 ft. On a failed DC 13 Charisma save, the ghost disappears into the target and controls its body. The target is Incapacitated and remains aware. Only effects that turn undead can target the ghost while it possesses the body. The ghost keeps its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being Charmed or Frightened. For everything else it uses the host's statistics, with no access to the host's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. Possession ends when the body reaches 0 HP, the ghost leaves as a bonus action, an effect turns the ghost, or an effect such as Dispel Evil and Good forces it out. The ghost then returns to an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the body. For 24 hours after a successful initial save or the end of possession, the target is immune to Possession by that ghost.
sections.Haunting: Resolving the ghost's unfinished business can end the haunting. An object, event, or sensation linked to its former life may also expose a weakness.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 147. The official errata adds hover and updates resistance wording.

name: Ghast
description: A ghoul infused with enough Abyssal power to lead a pack and resist attempts to turn it.

sections.Traits:
Stench. A creature that starts its turn within 5 ft. of the ghast makes a DC 10 Constitution save. On a failure, it is Poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a success, it gains 24 hours of immunity to that ghast's Stench.
Turning Defiance. The ghast rolls saves against turning effects with advantage. Ghouls within 30 ft. of the ghast gain the same advantage.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage. A non-undead creature hit by the claws makes a DC 10 Constitution save. Failure leaves it Paralyzed for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

name: Ghoul
description: A flesh-eating undead that hunts in packs around tombs and places of decay.

sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage. A creature that is neither an elf nor undead makes a DC 10 Constitution save or becomes Paralyzed for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

name: Shadow
description: A twisted humanoid silhouette that stalks the dark and feeds on living strength.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, and thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained.
sections.Traits:
Amorphous. It passes through openings at least 1 inch wide without squeezing.
Shadow Stealth. In dim light or darkness, its Stealth bonus rises to +6 and it can Hide as a bonus action.
Sunlight Weakness. Sunlight gives it disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.
Undead Nature. It can exist without air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Strength Drain. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 9 (2d6 + 2) necrotic damage and reduce the target's Strength score by 1d4. Reaching Strength 0 this way kills the target. A surviving target recovers the lost Strength when it finishes a short or long rest. If the attack kills a non-evil Humanoid, a new Shadow rises from the corpse after 1d4 hours.
sections.Return from death: If a creature that produced a Shadow returns to life, its Shadow senses the return. The creature casts no shadow until the undead Shadow is destroyed.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 269. Resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Skeleton
description: Animated bones that can carry out detailed orders and sometimes repeat habits from life.

sections.Languages: Understands every language it knew in life. It cannot speak.
sections.Traits: Undead Nature. It can exist without air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

name: Specter
description: A restless humanoid spirit severed from its former life. It emerges from dark refuges at night to attack the living.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, and thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious.
sections.Languages: Understands every language it knew in life. It cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Incorporeal Movement. Treat creatures and objects as difficult terrain when passing through them. Ending a turn inside an object deals 5 (1d10) force damage to this creature.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
Undead Nature. It can exist without air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Life Drain. Melee spell attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. On a failed DC 10 Constitution save, lower the target's maximum HP by the damage it took until it finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect lowers its maximum HP to 0.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 279. Resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Adult Black Dragon
description: Curved horns frame its skull-like face. It keeps its hoard in a flooded swamp cave or ruined stronghold.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. Breathe air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can choose to succeed after failing a saving throw.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. The dragon can first use Frightful Presence. It then attacks once with Bite and twice with Claw.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing plus 4 (1d8) acid damage.
