Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage.
Breath Weapons (recharge 5–6). Use one of the following breaths.
Cold Breath. Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 17 Constitution save. Failure deals 54 (12d8) cold damage. Success halves it.
Paralyzing Breath. Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 17 Constitution save or becomes Paralyzed for 1 minute. An affected creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
sections.Variant spellcasting: Under the optional dragon spellcasting rule, choose 4 spells of 3rd level or lower. The dragon uses Charisma to cast each once per day without material components. Its spell save DC is 16 and its spell attack bonus is +8. The DM chooses the spells.

name: Chuul
description: These armored servants of aboleths still collect magic and guard ancient ruins long after their empire fell.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The chuul breathes both air and water.
Sense Magic. It senses magic within 120 ft. at will. This ability is nonmagical and otherwise follows Detect Magic.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Pincer attacks. If the chuul has a creature grappled, it may also use Tentacles once.
Pincer. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature is also grappled, escape DC 14, provided the chuul has fewer than two other creatures grappled.
Tentacles. Choose one creature the chuul has grappled. It makes a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure it is poisoned for 1 minute and paralyzed while the poison lasts. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the effect on a success.

name: Duergar
description: Gray dwarves live in fortified Underdark cities and use their magic to infiltrate strongholds or grow large enough to fight alongside much taller creatures.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar has advantage on saves against poison, spells, and illusions and on saves to resist being charmed or paralyzed.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Enlarge (recharges after a short or long rest). The duergar and everything it wears or carries magically grow for 1 minute. It becomes Large, or the largest size the space allows. It doubles the damage dice of its Strength-based weapon attacks, already reflected in the enlarged damage below, and gains advantage on Strength checks and Strength saves.
War Pick. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage, or 11 (2d8 + 2) while enlarged.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage, or 9 (2d6 + 2) while enlarged.
Invisibility (recharges after a short or long rest). The duergar and everything it wears or carries magically become invisible for up to 1 hour. It concentrates as it would on a spell. The effect ends early if concentration breaks or the duergar attacks, casts a spell, or uses Enlarge.

name: Kraken
description: An ancient leviathan that sinks fleets and draws sailors into the depths. It may live in a deep ocean trench, a sunken cavern, or a freshwater lake.

sections.Languages: Understands Abyssal, Celestial, Infernal, and Primordial. Cannot speak. Telepathy 120 ft.
sections.Damage immunities: Lightning and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The kraken breathes both air and water.
Freedom of Movement. It ignores difficult terrain. Magic cannot reduce its speed or restrain it. It may spend 5 ft. of movement to free itself from a nonmagical restraint or a grapple.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Tentacle attacks. The kraken can replace any of them with Fling.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 23 (3d8 + 10) piercing damage. A Large or smaller creature hit by this attack is swallowed if the kraken is already grappling it. Swallowing ends the grapple. The swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects originating outside the kraken, and takes 42 (12d6) acid damage at the start of every kraken turn. If a creature inside the kraken deals at least 50 damage to it in a single turn, the kraken makes a DC 25 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On failure it regurgitates every swallowed creature. They land prone in a space within 10 ft. of the kraken. If the kraken dies, its victims are no longer restrained by it and can spend 15 ft. of movement to crawl out of the corpse, landing prone.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. The target is grappled, escape DC 18, and restrained for as long as the grapple lasts. Each of its ten tentacles can hold one target.
Fling. Throw one Large or smaller held object or grappled creature up to 60 ft. in a random direction. The target lands prone. If it hits a solid surface it takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage per 10 ft. thrown. If the kraken throws it at a creature, that creature makes a DC 18 Dexterity save. Failure deals the same damage and knocks it prone.
Lightning Storm. Make three magical lightning bolts. Choose for each a target the kraken can see within 120 ft. A target makes a DC 23 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) lightning damage on failure or half on success.
sections.Legendary actions:
The kraken has 3 legendary actions. It spends them on one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn and regains them at the start of its own turn. It cannot take them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it waits until after its first turn.
Tentacle Attack or Fling (1 action). Make one Tentacle attack or use Fling.
Lightning Storm (2 actions). Use Lightning Storm.
Ink Cloud (3 actions). Underwater, release ink in a 60-ft. radius. It spreads around corners and heavily obscures the area for everyone except the kraken. Another creature that ends its turn in the cloud makes a DC 23 Constitution save, taking 16 (3d10) poison damage on failure or half on success. A strong current disperses the ink. Otherwise the cloud dissipates at the end of the kraken's next turn.
sections.Lair actions:
On initiative count 20, after any turns tied at 20, the kraken can choose one effect. It cannot do so while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it waits until after its first turn.
Current. Each creature within 60 ft. of the kraken makes a DC 23 Strength save. Push it up to 60 ft. away on failure or 10 ft. away on success.
Lightning Vulnerability. Creatures in water within 60 ft. of the kraken gain vulnerability to lightning damage until initiative count 20 of the next round.
Electrified Water. All creatures within 120 ft. make a DC 23 Constitution save, taking 10 (3d6) lightning damage on failure or half on success.
sections.Regional effects:
Within 6 miles of the lair, the kraken can change the weather at will as with Control Weather.
Water elementals form within 6 miles. They remain in the water and each has Intelligence and Charisma 1, with a modifier of -5.
Aquatic creatures within 6 miles with Intelligence 2 or lower are charmed by the kraken and act aggressively toward intruders.
All regional effects end immediately when the kraken dies. A creature assuming the kraken's form gains none of its legendary actions, lair actions, or regional effects.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 196–197. Official errata revises the saving throw modifiers, Bite and Tentacle attack bonuses, nonmagical attack wording, and general legendary creature rules.

name: Merfolk
description: Merfolk build settlements in coastal reefs, flooded ruins, and sea caves. They often defend their homes with spears made from salvaged materials.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The merfolk can breathe both air and water.
sections.Actions: Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 3 (1d6) piercing damage, or 4 (1d8) when wielded in two hands for a melee attack.

name: Merrow
description: Abyss-twisted hunters raid coastal waters and drag prey back to their underwater caves.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The merrow can breathe both air and water.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claws or Harpoon attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d4 + 4) slashing damage.
Harpoon. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it must win a Strength contest against the merrow or be pulled up to 20 ft. toward it.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 219. Official errata sets passive Perception to 10.

name: Otyugh
description: An ambush hunter hides beneath heaps of refuse and uses simple telepathic lures to draw creatures within reach.

sections.Traits: Limited Telepathy. The otyugh can magically send simple messages and images to creatures within 120 ft. that understand a language. The recipient cannot use this link to answer.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Tentacle attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage. A creature hit makes a DC 15 Constitution save against disease. On failure it is poisoned until the disease is cured. Repeat the save every 24 hours. On each failure, reduce maximum HP by 5 (1d10). Success cures the disease, ending the poison and restoring the lost maximum. The creature dies if the disease reduces its maximum HP to 0.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller target is grappled, escape DC 13, and restrained until the grapple ends. Each of the otyugh's two tentacles can hold one target.
Tentacle Slam. Slam the creatures the otyugh is grappling into each other or into a hard surface. Each makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On failure it takes 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage and is stunned through the end of the otyugh's next turn. Success halves the damage and prevents the stun.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 248. Official errata changes the Tentacle Slam save to Constitution.

name: Salamander
description: A master smith from the Elemental Plane of Fire, hot enough to work metal barehanded and burn enemies that get within reach.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Heated Body. A creature takes 7 (2d6) fire damage if it touches the salamander or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft.
Heated Weapons. A metal melee weapon the salamander wields adds 3 (1d6) fire damage on a hit. The Spear damage below already includes this bonus.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Spear attack and one Tail attack.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) for a two-handed melee hit, plus 3 (1d6) fire damage in either case.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage. The target is grappled, escape DC 14. While held it is restrained, and the salamander can hit it automatically with its tail. The salamander cannot attack another target with its tail while this grapple lasts.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 265–266. Uses the official errata wording for resistance to nonmagical attacks.

name: Gargoyle
description: A creature of living stone lies in wait on roofs and cliffs, where it passes for a carved ornament.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't adamantine.
sections.Traits:
False Appearance. While motionless, it looks exactly like an inanimate statue.
Elemental Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 140. Resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Griffon
description: This eagle-lion hunter nests on high cliffs and favors horses as prey. An expert can raise one from an egg as a mount.

sections.Traits: Keen Sight. The griffon has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Beak attack and one Claws attack.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.

name: Treant
description: This awakened tree defends its forest. It often stands rooted for long stretches, watching for anything that threatens the grove.

sections.Traits:
False Appearance. While motionless, it looks exactly like an ordinary tree.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 16 (3d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +10 to hit, range 60/180 ft., one target. Hit 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Animate Trees (1/day). Magically animate one or two trees it can see within 60 ft. Each acts as its ally and keeps the treant's statistics with three changes. Its Intelligence and Charisma are both 1, it cannot speak, and Slam is its only listed action option. A tree stays animated for up to 1 day. The effect ends early if the tree dies, if the treant dies or gets more than 120 ft. away, or if the treant uses a bonus action to turn it back into an ordinary tree. It then takes root if possible.

name: Tribal Warrior
description: A spear fighter who relies on fighting alongside allies. The profile can fit fighters from many kinds of communities.

sections.Traits: Pack Tactics. The warrior has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally is within 5 ft. of that creature and the ally is not Incapacitated.
sections.Actions: Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage with a two-handed melee attack.

name: Unicorn
description: A celestial guardian with an ivory horn and healing magic. It typically protects a forest or another place held sacred.

sections.Traits:
Charge. It must move at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hit that target with Horn on the same turn. The hit then deals an extra 9 (2d8) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must pass a DC 15 Strength save or fall Prone.
Magic Resistance. The unicorn has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma, spell save DC 14. No components.
At will. Detect Evil and Good, Druidcraft, Pass without Trace.
1/day each. Calm Emotions, Dispel Evil and Good, Entangle.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Hooves attack and one Horn attack.
Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Horn. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Healing Touch (3/day). Touch another creature with the horn. That creature magically regains 11 (2d8 + 2) HP, loses all diseases, and has all poisons affecting it neutralized.
Teleport (1/day). Move magically to a familiar location up to 1 mile away. The unicorn can take up to three willing creatures it sees within 5 ft. and all equipment the travelers wear or carry.
sections.Legendary actions:
The unicorn has 3 legendary actions. Use one option at the end of another creature's turn and regain spent actions at the start of its turn. It can skip an opportunity. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it cannot use them until after its first turn.
Hooves (1 action). Make one Hooves attack.
Shimmering Shield (2 actions). Place a magical shield on itself or another creature it can see within 60 ft. That creature gains +2 AC until the end of the unicorn's next turn.
Heal Self (3 actions). Magically regain 11 (2d8 + 2) HP.
sections.Lair: Its lair can be a quiet woodland site, such as an overgrown ruin, misty clearing, or flower-covered hill.
sections.Regional effects:
The DM can use any of these effects within the unicorn's domain. They end immediately if it dies.
Open nonmagical flames go out. Closed lanterns keep burning.
Creatures native to the domain have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide.
If one good-aligned creature uses a spell or magical effect to heal another good-aligned creature, the target regains the maximum possible HP for that spell or effect.
Curses on good-aligned creatures are suppressed.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 293–294. Legendary action timing follows p. 11 and the official errata.

name: Minotaur Skeleton
description: The animated bones of a minotaur retain the force of its charge and can still wield a greataxe.

sections.Traits:
Charge. It must move at least 10 ft. straight toward a target and hit that target with Gore on the same turn. The hit then deals an extra 9 (2d8) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, a failed DC 14 Strength save pushes it up to 10 ft. away and knocks it Prone.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d12 + 4) slashing damage.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.

name: Warhorse Skeleton
description: An animated warhorse skeleton still wears scraps of its barding.

sections.Traits: Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

name: Mummy
description: A preserved tomb guardian rises when someone breaks the conditions of its burial rite.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits: Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. It can use Dreadful Glare and make one Rotting Fist attack.
Rotting Fist. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 12 Constitution save or contract mummy rot. While cursed, it cannot regain HP and loses 10 (3d6) maximum HP for every 24 hours that pass. At 0 maximum HP it dies and crumbles to dust. Remove Curse or other magic can end the curse.
Dreadful Glare. Choose one creature the mummy sees within 60 ft. If it can see the mummy, it must make a DC 11 Wisdom save against the magic. On a failure it is Frightened until the end of the mummy's next turn, and a failure by 5 or more also makes it Paralyzed for that duration. A successful save grants 24 hours of immunity to Dreadful Glare from all ordinary mummies.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 227–228. Resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Mummy Lord
description: A dead ruler or priest retains its will and magic. It rises again unless its hidden heart is destroyed.

sections.Damage immunities: Necrotic and poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Rejuvenation. A destroyed mummy lord with an intact heart returns after 24 hours at full HP. The new body appears within 5 ft. of the heart. The heart has AC 5 and 25 HP. Only fire damage can harm it. Burning it to ashes prevents further re-forming.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Spellcasting:
10th-level cleric spellcaster. Wisdom is its spellcasting ability (save DC 17, +9 on spell attacks). It counts as a cleric when attuning to or using items that require that class or spell list.
Cantrips at will. Sacred Flame and Thaumaturgy.
1st level, 4 slots. Command, Guiding Bolt, Shield of Faith.
2nd level, 3 slots. Hold Person, Silence, Spiritual Weapon.
3rd level, 3 slots. Animate Dead, Dispel Magic.
4th level, 3 slots. Divination, Guardian of Faith.
5th level, 2 slots. Contagion, Insect Plague.
6th level, 1 slot. Harm.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. It can use Dreadful Glare and make one Rotting Fist attack.
Rotting Fist. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (3d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 16 Constitution save or contract mummy rot. While cursed, it cannot regain HP and loses 10 (3d6) maximum HP for every 24 hours that pass. At 0 maximum HP it dies and crumbles to dust. Remove Curse or other magic can end the curse.
Dreadful Glare. Choose one creature the mummy lord sees within 60 ft. If it can see the mummy lord, it must make a DC 16 Wisdom save against the magic. On a failure it is Frightened until the end of the mummy lord's next turn, and a failure by 5 or more also makes it Paralyzed for that duration. A successful save grants 24 hours of immunity to Dreadful Glare from all mummies and mummy lords.
sections.Legendary actions:
It has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at a time, at the end of another creature's turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must wait until its first turn has ended.
Attack. Make one Rotting Fist attack or use Dreadful Glare.
Blinding Dust. Every creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 16 Constitution save or is Blinded until the end of its next turn.
Blasphemous Word (2 actions). Every non-undead creature within 10 ft. that hears the magical utterance makes a DC 16 Constitution save or is Stunned until the end of the mummy lord's next turn.
Channel Negative Energy (2 actions). Creatures within 60 ft., including those behind barriers or around corners, cannot regain HP until the end of the mummy lord's next turn.
Whirlwind of Sand (2 actions). It turns into sand, moves up to 60 ft., and reforms. During this movement it is immune to damage and cannot be Grappled, Petrified, knocked Prone, Restrained, or Stunned. It keeps worn and carried equipment.
sections.Lair actions:
In its lair the mummy lord is CR 16 (15,000 XP). At initiative count 20, losing ties, it can choose one effect and cannot repeat the previous round's effect. It cannot do so while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must wait until after its first turn.
Each undead in the lair knows the exact location of every living creature within 120 ft. of itself until initiative count 20 next round.
Each undead in the lair has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead until initiative count 20 next round.
Until initiative count 20 next round, a non-undead creature attempting a spell of 4th level or lower in the lair feels pain and can choose a different action. If it tries to cast the spell, it makes a DC 16 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 1d6 necrotic damage per spell level, and the spell is wasted without effect.
sections.Regional effects: Food brought into the lair molds instantly, water evaporates at once, and other nonmagical drinks spoil. A divination spell cast there by anyone other than the mummy lord has a 25 percent chance to give misleading results chosen by the DM. An existing chance of failure or unreliability increases by 25 percentage points. Anyone who takes treasure from the lair has disadvantage on every saving throw until the treasure is returned or Remove Curse or other magic lifts the curse. All regional effects end as soon as the mummy lord is destroyed.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 227–229. Resistance and immunity wording, spellcasting prerequisites, and legendary and lair action timing follow the official errata.

name: Wight
description: A once-mortal warrior keeps its ambitions in undeath and raises the victims of its life drain as servants.

sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Longsword attacks, or make two Longbow attacks. Life Drain can replace one Longsword attack.
Life Drain. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) necrotic damage. The target makes a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure its maximum HP falls by the damage it took, until it finishes a long rest. It dies if the reduction takes its maximum HP to 0. A humanoid this attack kills rises as a Zombie under the wight's control after 24 hours unless it is restored to life or its body is destroyed. The wight can control up to 12 zombies at a time.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) slashing damage, or 7 (1d10 + 2) when used with both hands.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 300. Resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Wraith
description: An incorporeal spirit that drains the living and binds the restless dead to its service.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, and thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Incorporeal Movement. It treats creatures and objects as difficult terrain when moving through them. Ending its turn inside an object deals 5 (1d10) force damage to it.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Life Drain. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 21 (4d8 + 3) necrotic damage. The target makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure its maximum HP falls by the damage it took, until it finishes a long rest. It dies if the reduction takes its maximum HP to 0.
Create Specter. Choose a humanoid within 10 ft. that died violently no more than 1 minute ago. Its spirit rises as a Specter in the corpse's space or the nearest unoccupied space. The wraith controls the specter and can control up to seven specters at once.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2014), p. 302. Resistance wording follows the official errata.

name: Zombie
description: A reanimated corpse that follows simple orders and keeps advancing through danger.

sections.Languages: It understands the languages it knew in life and cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Undead Fortitude. If damage drops it to 0 HP, make a Constitution save with a DC of 5 plus the damage taken. Skip the save for radiant damage or damage from a critical hit. On a success it drops to 1 HP.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Slam. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

name: Ogre Zombie
description: A lumbering ogre corpse with enough strength left to swing a heavy morningstar.

sections.Languages: It understands Common and Giant and cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Undead Fortitude. If damage drops it to 0 HP, make a Constitution save with a DC of 5 plus the damage taken. Skip the save for radiant damage or damage from a critical hit. On a success it drops to 1 HP.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

name: Black Dragon Wyrmling
description: A swamp hatchling with glossy black scales and the beginnings of a skull-like face.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The wyrmling breathes both air and water.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing plus 2 (1d4) acid damage.
Acid Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. line 5 ft. wide makes a DC 11 Dexterity save. Failure deals 22 (5d8) acid damage. Success halves it.

name: Blue Dragon Wyrmling
description: A burrowing desert dragon with flared ears and a ridged horn above its snout.

sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing plus 3 (1d6) lightning damage.
Lightning Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. line 5 ft. wide makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. Failure deals 22 (4d10) lightning damage. Success halves it.

name: Green Dragon Wyrmling
description: A long-necked forest hatchling that moves between streams and dense cover.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The wyrmling breathes both air and water.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing plus 3 (1d6) poison damage.

speed: 30 ft., burrow 15 ft., fly 60 ft., swim 30 ft.
description: A white-scaled arctic hatchling with a spined crest and a breath of freezing hail.

Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing plus 2 (1d4) cold damage.
Cold Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 12 Constitution save. Failure deals 22 (5d8) cold damage. Success halves it.

description: Mottled brown scales and a broad plate across its forehead mark this wyrmling. It seeks heat, sunshine, and conversation.

Sleep Breath. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 11 Constitution save. On a failure, it falls Unconscious for 1 minute. Taking damage or having another creature use an action to wake it ends the effect.

description: This coastal wyrmling has webbed feet, yellow-green scales, and a ridged crest.

Repulsion Breath. Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 12 Strength save. On a failure, it is pushed 30 ft. away from the dragon.

description: This rocky upland wyrmling likes jokes and riddles. It prizes metal and gems.

description: Metal flecks show in the wyrmling’s dark yellow scales. Long whiskers frame its face.

description: Silver highlights mark this wyrmling’s blue-gray scales. A spiny crest runs from its head down its back.

name: Animated Armor
description: An empty suit of armor carries out its creator’s orders.

False Appearance. While motionless, it passes for an ordinary suit of armor.
Constructed Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep. At 0 HP the magic animating it ends, leaving a badly damaged inanimate object.
sections.Actions:

Immutable Form. Spells and other effects cannot change its form.

Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical.
Constructed Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

Damage Transfer. While it grapples a creature, half of any damage dealt to the rug goes to that creature. The rug takes the remaining half.

Constructed Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep. At 0 HP the magic animating it ends, leaving a badly damaged inanimate object.

Until that grapple ends, the target is Restrained and Blinded and risks suffocation. The rug cannot Smother another creature during the grapple. The victim takes 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns.

name: Shield Guardian
description: A construct protects whoever wears its matching amulet and can release a stored spell when needed.

sections.Languages: Understands commands in any language. It cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Bound. While the guardian and amulet are on the same plane, the wearer can telepathically call the guardian to come to the amulet. The guardian knows the direction and distance to it. If the guardian is within 60 ft. of the wearer, it takes half of any damage dealt to the wearer, rounded up, in the wearer’s place.
Regeneration. At the start of its turn, it regains 10 HP if it has at least 1 HP.
Constructed Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Master’s amulet: The guardian has one linked amulet. The wearer can order it to attack or guard. Destroying the amulet Incapacitates the guardian until a replacement is made. An amulet can be targeted directly if nobody is wearing or carrying it. It has AC 10, 10 HP, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. Making a replacement takes 1 week and costs 1,000 gp in components.
sections.Spell Storing: A spellcaster wearing the amulet can cast a spell of 4th level or lower on the guardian. The spell is stored without taking effect. The guardian casts it when the wearer orders it to, or when a condition set by the caster occurs. The original caster sets the spell’s parameters, and the guardian needs no components. Casting empties the store. Storing a new spell replaces the previous one.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Fist attacks.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Reactions: Shield. When a creature attacks the amulet wearer, the guardian can give the wearer +2 AC against that attack if the guardian is within 5 ft. of the wearer.

name: Berserker
classification: Medium humanoid (any race), any chaotic alignment
description: A ferocious warrior who leaves an opening to land a decisive blow.

sections.Traits: Reckless. At the start of its turn, the berserker can choose to gain advantage on all melee weapon attack rolls it makes that turn. If it does, attacks against it have advantage until its next turn starts.
sections.Actions: Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (1d12 + 3) slashing damage.

name: Druid
description: A keeper of wild places who can speak with animals and harden their skin before a fight.

sections.Spellcasting:
4th-level druid spellcaster using Wisdom. Spell save DC 12. Spell attacks +4.
Cantrips (at will): Druidcraft, Produce Flame, Shillelagh.
1st level (4 slots): Entangle, Longstrider, Speak with Animals, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots): Animal Messenger, Barkskin.
Treat this NPC as a druid with access to the druid spell list for any class or spell-list requirements on magic item use and attunement.
sections.Actions: Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage in one hand or 4 (1d8) in two hands. With Shillelagh, use +4 to hit and deal 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

name: Knight

Leadership (recharges after a short or long rest). For 1 minute, the knight can call out whenever a nonhostile creature it can see within 30 ft. rolls an attack or saving throw. The creature can add 1d4 if it hears and understands the knight. It can benefit from one Leadership die at a time. Leadership ends if the knight becomes Incapacitated.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack would hit the knight, it can add 2 to its AC against that attack if it sees the attacker and holds a melee weapon.

Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

description: An informant trained to gather secrets and escape if discovered.

sections.Traits: Sneak Attack (once per turn). A weapon hit deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage if the spy had advantage on the roll. The spy can also deal that damage with a hit if it had no disadvantage and an ally within 5 ft. of the target is not Incapacitated.
sections.Actions:

Skewer (once per turn). A melee trident hit deals an extra 10 (3d6) damage and grants the lizardfolk temporary HP equal to the extra damage dealt.

name: Githzerai Monk

sections.Traits: Psychic Defense. The monk adds its Wisdom modifier to AC while unarmored and without a shield. Its listed AC includes this bonus.

The monk casts these spells using Wisdom and needs no components.
At will: Mage Hand (the hand is invisible).
3/day each: Feather Fall, Jump, See Invisibility, Shield.

Multiattack. Make two Unarmed Strike attacks.
Unarmed Strike. Magical melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) psychic damage.

name: Androsphinx
description: A winged guardian watches over divine secrets and challenges those who seek them.

sections.Traits:
Inscrutable. Effects cannot read the sphinx's thoughts or sense its emotions. It can refuse any divination spell and is immune to that spell if it does. Wisdom (Insight) checks to judge its intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical.
Divine Vigil. The sphinx needs neither sleep nor food while it keeps watch.
sections.Legendary actions:
The sphinx has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at the end of another creature's turn. It can pass, and it cannot act while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to take actions. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using these options.
Claw Attack. Make one Claw attack.
Teleport (2 actions). Magically teleport up to 120 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space. Worn and carried equipment goes along.
Cast a Spell (3 actions). Cast one of its prepared spells and spend a spell slot as usual.
sections.Lair actions:
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one magical effect. Each option is available once per short or long rest. The sphinx cannot use its lair actions while outside its lair, Incapacitated, or otherwise unable to take actions. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using an option.
Reroll initiative. Every creature in the lair rolls initiative again. The sphinx may keep its current roll.
Change age. Each creature in the lair makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, it ages or grows younger by 1d20 years, as the sphinx chooses. No creature becomes younger than 1 year old. Greater Restoration can return a creature to its normal age.
Shift time. Move everything in the lair up to 10 years ahead or back, as the sphinx chooses. The sphinx alone notices the change immediately. Wish can restore its caster and up to seven creatures the caster designates to their normal time.
Shift planes. Move the sphinx and up to seven other creatures it can see in the lair to another plane. On its turn, the sphinx can return to its lair as a bonus action and take up to seven creatures with it.
