publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A dire troll lashes out with several arms. Even at 0 hit points it can regenerate unless an attack delivers enough acid or fire to kill it.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits: Regeneration. At the start of its turn, the troll regains 10 hit points. After taking acid or fire damage, the troll regains 5 hit points at the start of its next turn. The troll dies only when an attack hits it while it has 0 hit points and deals at least 10 acid or fire damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and four Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d8 + 6) piercing damage plus 5 (1d10) poison damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (3d6 + 6) slashing damage.
Whirlwind of Claws (recharge 5–6). Each creature within 10 ft. of the troll makes a DC 19 Dexterity save, taking 44 (8d10) slashing damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 246.

name: Diviner Wizard
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A wizard trained to see hidden things and glimpse possible outcomes.

sections.Armor: AC 15 while Mage Armor is active.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Arcane Burst attacks.
Arcane Burst. Melee or ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (3d10 + 4) radiant damage.
Overwhelming Revelation (recharge 5–6). Magically light up a sphere with a 10-foot radius centered on a point within 120 ft. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, it takes 45 (10d8) psychic damage and is stunned until the end of the diviner’s next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and avoids the stun.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 15).
At will. Mage Hand, Message, Prestidigitation.
2/day each. Arcane Eye, Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Fly, Lightning Bolt, Locate Object, Mage Armor, Rary’s Telepathic Bond.
1/day. True Seeing.
sections.Reactions: Portent (3/day). When the diviner or a creature the diviner can see makes an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check, roll a d20. The diviner may substitute this result for the d20 rolled for that attack, save, or check.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 261.

name: Dolphin Delighter
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A fey dolphin that shares protective light and can carry a companion along when it teleports.

sections.Traits: Hold Breath. The dolphin can go without breathing for 20 minutes by holding its breath.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Dazzling Slam attacks.
Dazzling Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage and 7 (2d6) psychic damage. The target is blinded until the start of the dolphin’s next turn.
sections.Bonus actions:
Delightful Light (recharge 5–6). The dolphin briefly fills a 10-foot radius around itself with magical light. It and each creature it chooses in that light gain 11 (2d10) temporary hit points.
Fey Leap. Teleport up to 30 ft. to an unoccupied space the dolphin can see. Just before teleporting, the dolphin can choose one creature within 5 ft. That creature may teleport with it and appears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the dolphin’s destination.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 97.

name: Draegloth
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A four-armed demon that an elf priest of Lolth creates through a rare ritual that draws on a glabrezu’s fiendish essence. It usually serves its creator.

sections.Traits: Fey Ancestry. The creature has advantage on saves to avoid being charmed. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) slashing damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell without material components using Charisma (spell save DC 11).
At will. Dancing Lights, Darkness.
1/day each. Confusion, Faerie Fire.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 98.

name: Drow Arachnomancer
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A devotee of Lolth who draws magic from the Demonweb Pits and can take the form of a large spider.

sections.Languages: Elvish, Undercommon, can speak with spiders.
sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The creature has advantage on saves to avoid being charmed. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Spider Climb. The drow climbs difficult surfaces, including ceilings while upside down, without making an ability check.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
Web Walker. Webbing does not restrict the drow’s movement.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using any combination of Bite, Poisonous Touch, and Web that the current form allows. Spellcasting can replace one of those attacks.
Bite (spider form only). Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 31 (7d8) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. If this poison damage drops the target to 0 hit points, it is stable and poisoned for 1 hour, even if it regains hit points. While poisoned this way, it is also paralyzed.
Poisonous Touch (humanoid form only). Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 35 (10d6) poison damage.
Web (spider form only, recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one target. A hit restrains the target in webbing. The target can spend an action to break the webbing with a successful DC 15 Strength check. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10, 5 hit points, vulnerable to fire damage and immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell without material components using Intelligence (spell save DC 17).
At will. Dancing Lights, Mage Hand.
1/day each. Darkness, Dispel Magic, Etherealness, Faerie Fire, Fly, Insect Plague, Invisibility.
sections.Bonus actions: Change Shape (recharges after a short or long rest). Magically become a Large spider for up to 1 hour or return to true form. Only size changes. The drow can speak and cast spells as a spider. Anything worn or carried in humanoid form merges into the spider, and the drow cannot use or benefit from it in that form. Death restores the drow’s humanoid form.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 99.

name: Drow Favored Consort
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A powerful spellcaster who advises and protects a drow priestess. Some use that position to challenge Lolth’s influence.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The creature has advantage on saves to avoid being charmed. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using Scimitar or Arcane Eruption. Spellcasting can replace one of those attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) slashing damage and 27 (6d8) poison damage.
Arcane Eruption. Ranged spell attack, +10 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (8d8) force damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, the drow can push it up to 10 ft. away.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell without material components using Intelligence (spell save DC 18).
At will. Dancing Lights, Mage Armor, Mage Hand, Message.
3/day each. Dimension Door, Fireball, Invisibility.
1/day each. Darkness, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only).
sections.Reactions: Protective Shield (3/day). When an attack roll hits the drow or a creature within 10 ft. of it, give the target +5 AC until the start of the drow’s next turn. The extra AC can turn the triggering hit into a miss.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 100.

name: Drow House Captain
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An officer who leads the troops of an Underdark faction. Some defend noble houses, while others fight against Lolth.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The creature has advantage on saves to avoid being charmed. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks and one attack with Whip or Hand Crossbow.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage and 14 (4d6) poison damage.
Whip. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d4 + 4) slashing damage.
Hand Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage. On a failed DC 13 Constitution save, the target is poisoned for 1 hour. If it fails by 5 or more, it is also unconscious while poisoned in this way. Taking damage or being shaken by another creature as an action wakes it.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell without material components using Charisma (spell save DC 13).
At will. Dancing Lights.
1/day each. Darkness, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only).
sections.Bonus actions: Battle Command. Choose one creature the captain can see within 30 ft. If it can see or hear the captain, it can use its reaction to make one melee attack or take the Dodge or Hide action.
sections.Reactions: Parry. If a melee attack roll would hit the captain, add +3 AC against that roll. The captain must see the attacker and wield a melee weapon.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 101.

name: Drow Inquisitor
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
classification: Medium humanoid (cleric, elf), typically neutral evil
description: A priest of Lolth appointed to uncover treachery. Within the noble houses, drow matron mothers are the inquisitor’s only equals in authority.

sections.Traits:
Discern Lie. The drow recognizes a spoken lie from a creature in earshot if the drow knows the language.
Fey Ancestry. The creature has advantage on saves to avoid being charmed. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Death Lance attacks.
Death Lance. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage and 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. Reduce the target’s hit point maximum by the necrotic damage it actually took. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if its maximum drops to 0.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell without material components using Charisma (spell save DC 18).
At will. Dancing Lights, Detect Magic, Message, Thaumaturgy.
1/day each. Clairvoyance, Darkness, Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only), Silence, Suggestion, True Seeing.
sections.Bonus actions: Spectral Dagger (recharges after a short or long rest). Conjure a floating dagger within 60 ft. The drow can make a melee spell attack, +10 to hit, against one creature within 5 ft. of the dagger. A hit deals 9 (1d8 + 5) force damage. The dagger lasts 1 minute. On later turns, the drow can use a bonus action to move it up to 20 ft. and repeat the attack against one creature within 5 ft. of it.
sections.Variant action: Summon Demon (1/day). The inquisitor magically attempts to summon a yochlol with a 50 percent chance of success. On a failure, the inquisitor takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage. On a success, the yochlol appears in an unoccupied space within 60 ft., acts as the inquisitor’s ally, and cannot summon other demons. It remains for 10 minutes or until either creature dies or the inquisitor dismisses it as an action.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 102.

name: Drow Matron Mother
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
classification: Medium humanoid (drow elf, cleric), typically neutral evil
description: A priestess of Lolth who leads a noble drow house. A Drow Favored Consort and Drow House Captain usually accompany her.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saves against being charmed. Magic can't put the drow to sleep.
Special Equipment. The matron mother wields a Tentacle Rod.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Demon Staff attacks, or one Demon Staff attack and three Tentacle Rod attacks.
Demon Staff. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage with one hand or 8 (1d8 + 4) with two. Add 14 (4d6) psychic damage either way. The target must pass a DC 19 Wisdom save or be frightened of the matron mother for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
Tentacle Rod. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one creature. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage. Three rod hits on the same turn force a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, for 1 minute the creature's speed is halved, it has disadvantage on Dexterity saves, and it can't take reactions. On each of its turns it can take an action or a bonus action, but only one. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end all these effects.
Divine Flame (2/day). Place a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high column of fire within 120 ft. Each creature in it makes a DC 20 Dexterity save, taking 14 (4d6) fire plus 14 (4d6) radiant damage on a failure or half of each on a success.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one of these spells using Charisma (spell save DC 20). Material components are waived.
At will. Command, Dancing Lights, Detect Magic, Thaumaturgy.
2/day each. Banishment, Blade Barrier, Cure Wounds, Hold Person, Plane Shift, Silence.
1/day each. Clairvoyance, Darkness, Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Faerie Fire, Gate, Levitate (self only), Suggestion.
sections.Bonus actions:
Lolth's Fickle Favor. Choose one ally she can see within 30 ft. The ally takes 7 (2d6) psychic damage and gains advantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn.
Summon Servant (1/day). Magically summon a Glabrezu or Yochlol to an unoccupied space within 60 ft. It fights as an ally and can't summon other demons. It stays for 10 minutes, until it or the matron mother dies, or until she spends an action to dismiss it.
sections.Legendary actions:
The matron mother has 3 legendary actions. She can use one option at the end of another creature's turn, paying its listed cost. Spent actions return at the start of her turn. She can't use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, she must finish her first turn before using them.
Compel Demon (1 action). An allied demon within 30 ft. uses its reaction to attack once against a target she chooses and can see.
Demon Staff (1 action). Make one Demon Staff attack.
Cast a Spell (2 actions). Use Spellcasting.
sections.Lair actions:
The matron mother's palace is her lair. A temple to Lolth also qualifies while she is inside, provided she still follows Lolth and no other matron mother is present. If two or more matron mothers gather in such a temple, none can use its lair actions.
On initiative count 20, losing ties, she can use one option in her lair. She must be able to act. If surprised, she can act on count 20 only after her first turn. She can't choose the same option in consecutive rounds.
Perceive Interlopers. Until initiative count 20 in the next round, hostile creatures in the lair can't become hidden from her and get no benefit from invisibility against her.
Spectral Web. Choose a visible point within 120 ft. Each creature within 60 ft. of it must pass a DC 19 Dexterity save or be restrained for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
Telekinetic Throw. Choose a visible creature within 60 ft. On a failed DC 19 Strength save, it flies 2d6 × 10 ft. through the air. If it strikes a solid object, it takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 10 ft. moved. Apply normal falling damage if released in midair.
sections.Mothers of Rebellion: A matron mother who renounces Lolth can have any alignment and loses Lolth's Fickle Favor, Summon Servant, and Compel Demon.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, pp. 103–104.

name: Drow Shadowblade
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An Underdark spy or assassin whose power over shadows comes from trapping the essence of a Shadow Demon.

sections.Traits:
Devil's Sight. Magical darkness doesn't obstruct the drow's darkvision.
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saves against being charmed. Magic can't put the drow to sleep.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Shadow Sword attacks. The shadowblade can replace one of them with a Hand Crossbow attack. It can also use Spellcasting to cast Darkness as part of this action.
Shadow Sword. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 27 (7d6 + 5) necrotic damage.
Hand Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage. The target must pass a DC 13 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 hour. On a failure by 5 or more it is also unconscious while this poison lasts. Damage or another creature spending an action to shake it awake ends the unconsciousness.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one of these spells using Charisma (spell save DC 13). Material components are waived.
At will. Dancing Lights, Darkness.
1/day each. Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only).
sections.Bonus actions: Shadow Step. From dim light or darkness, teleport with worn or carried equipment up to 60 ft. to a visible unoccupied space in dim light or darkness. The shadowblade has advantage on its first melee attack before the turn ends.
sections.Optional action: Summon Shadow Demon (1/day). Make a magical summoning attempt with a 50 percent chance of success. On a failure, the drow takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage. On a success, a Shadow Demon appears in an unoccupied space within 60 ft. It acts as an ally and can't summon other demons. It stays for 10 minutes, until it or the shadowblade dies, or until the shadowblade dismisses it as an action.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 105.

name: Duergar Despot
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A duergar who controls mechanical replacements for parts of its body with psionic power.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The despot has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Psychic Engine. When a critical hit strikes the despot or it drops to 0 HP, each creature within 5 ft. of it takes 14 (4d6) psychic damage.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Iron Fist and two Stomping Foot attacks. Replace up to one attack with Flame Jet. After one attack the despot can move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Iron Fist. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 23 (4d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must pass a DC 17 Strength save or be pushed up to 30 ft. straight away and knocked prone.
Stomping Foot. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage, or 21 (3d10 + 5) if the target is prone.
Flame Jet. Each creature in a 100-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line makes a DC 16 Dexterity save, taking 18 (4d8) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Spellcasting:
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast one of these spells using Intelligence (spell save DC 12). No spell components are required.
At will. Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
1/day. Stinking Cloud.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 107.

name: Duergar Hammerer
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A duergar tunneling machine that doubles as a siege engine.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Traits: Siege Monster. The hammerer deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claw and one Hammer attack.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Hammer. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Reactions: Engine of Pain. Immediately after a creature within 5 ft. hits the hammerer with an attack roll, it makes a Hammer attack against that creature.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 112.

name: Duergar Kavalrachni
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Underdark cavalry trained to ride Female Steeders or other suitable mounts.

sections.Traits:
Cavalry Training. When the kavalrachni hits with a melee attack while mounted, the mount can use its reaction to make one melee attack against the same target.
Duergar Resilience. The duergar has advantage on saves against spells and against being charmed, paralyzed, or poisoned.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two War Pick attacks.
War Pick. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing plus 5 (2d4) poison damage.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +2 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d10) piercing damage.
Shared Invisibility (recharges after a short or long rest). Magically turn invisible with worn and carried equipment for up to 1 hour. The effect ends if the duergar attacks, forces a saving throw, or stops concentrating as if on a spell. While the invisible duergar is mounted, the mount is invisible too. The mount's invisibility ends immediately after it attacks.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 107.

name: Duergar Mind Master
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A masked duergar spy who uses psionics to see through illusions and shrink small enough to slip into guarded places.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar has advantage on saves against spells and against being charmed, paralyzed, or poisoned.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Mind-Poison Dagger attacks. Mind Mastery can replace one attack.
Mind-Poison Dagger. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing plus 10 (3d6) psychic damage. While reduced, deal 1 piercing plus 10 (3d6) psychic instead.
Invisibility (Recharge 4–6). Magically turn invisible with worn and carried equipment for up to 1 hour. The effect ends if the duergar attacks, forces a saving throw, or stops concentrating as if on a spell.
Mind Mastery. Choose a creature the duergar can see within 60 ft. A creature immune to being charmed is unaffected. On a failed DC 12 Intelligence save, the target uses its reaction if available. The duergar chooses either a single weapon attack against another creature the duergar can see or movement up to 10 ft. in a direction the duergar chooses.
sections.Bonus actions: Reduce (recharges after a short or long rest). Magically become Tiny for 1 minute, shrinking worn and carried gear as well. Weapon damage drops to 1. Strength-based attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws have disadvantage. Gain +5 AC and +5 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks. On each turn while reduced, the duergar can take the Hide action as a bonus action.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 108.

name: Duergar Screamer
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A duergar excavation machine that shatters rock and bowls over intruders with sound.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Drill attack and use Sonic Scream.
Drill. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d12 + 4) piercing damage.
Sonic Scream. Each creature in a 15-foot cube must pass a DC 11 Strength save or take 7 (2d6) thunder damage and fall prone.
sections.Reactions: Engine of Pain. Immediately after a creature within 5 ft. hits the screamer with an attack roll, it makes a Drill attack against that creature.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 111.

name: Duergar Soulblade
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Duergar soulblades form weapons from psionic energy.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar has advantage on saving throws against spells and on saves against the charmed, paralyzed, or poisoned conditions.
Sunlight Sensitivity. While in sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Soulblade. Melee spell attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) force damage, or 13 (3d6 + 3) force damage while enlarged.
Invisibility (recharges after a short or long rest). The duergar and its equipment become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. This effect ends early if the duergar attacks, forces a creature to make a saving throw, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.
sections.Bonus actions: Enlarge (recharges after a short or long rest). For 1 minute, the duergar and its equipment grow magically. The duergar becomes Large or grows as much as the available space allows. It makes Strength checks and Strength saves with advantage and doubles the damage dice of its Strength-based weapon attacks. The attack descriptions already include the increased damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 109.

name: Duergar Stone Guard
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Stone guards reinforce duergar formations and form strike teams for specific missions.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar has advantage on saving throws against spells and on saves against the charmed, paralyzed, or poisoned conditions.
Phalanx Formation. The duergar has advantage on attack rolls and Dexterity saves while standing within 5 ft. of an ally wielding a shield.
Sunlight Sensitivity. While in sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Shortsword, Javelin, or one of each.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage while enlarged.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage while enlarged.
Invisibility (recharges after a short or long rest). The duergar and its equipment become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. This effect ends early if the duergar attacks, forces a creature to make a saving throw, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.
sections.Bonus actions: Enlarge (recharges after a short or long rest). For 1 minute, the duergar and its equipment grow magically. The duergar becomes Large or grows as much as the available space allows. It makes Strength checks and Strength saves with advantage and doubles the damage dice of its Strength-based weapon attacks. The attack descriptions already include the increased damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 110.

name: Duergar Warlord
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Duergar warlords direct their troops and can use psionic pain to drive an ally to fight harder.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar has advantage on saving throws against spells and on saves against the charmed, paralyzed, or poisoned conditions.
Sunlight Sensitivity. While in sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Psychic-Attuned Hammer or Javelin attacks in any combination and use Call to Attack.
Psychic-Attuned Hammer. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage, or 15 (2d10 + 4) while enlarged, plus 5 (1d10) psychic damage in either case.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage while enlarged.
Call to Attack. Up to three allies within 120 ft. who can hear the duergar may each use a reaction to make one weapon attack.
Invisibility (recharge 4–6). The duergar and its equipment become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. This effect ends early if the duergar attacks, forces a creature to make a saving throw, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.
sections.Bonus actions: Enlarge (recharges after a short or long rest). For 1 minute, the duergar and its equipment grow magically. The duergar becomes Large or grows as much as the available space allows. It makes Strength checks and Strength saves with advantage and doubles the damage dice of its Strength-based weapon attacks. The attack descriptions already include the increased damage.
sections.Reactions: Scouring Instruction. When an ally the warlord can see rolls a d20, the warlord can roll a d6. The ally can take 3 (1d6) psychic damage to add the result of the warlord's d6 to its d20 roll.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 111.

name: Duergar Xarrorn
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Xarrorn combine alchemy and psionics to build weapons such as the fire lance.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar has advantage on saving throws against spells and on saves against the charmed, paralyzed, or poisoned conditions.
Sunlight Sensitivity. While in sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight.
sections.Actions:
Fire Lance. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d12 + 3) piercing damage, or 16 (2d12 + 3) while enlarged, plus 3 (1d6) fire damage in either case.
Fire Spray (recharge 5–6). The fire lance projects a 15-ft. cone or a line 30 ft. long and 5 ft. wide. Each creature in the area makes a DC 12 Dexterity save, taking 10 (3d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
Invisibility (recharges after a short or long rest). The duergar and its equipment become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. This effect ends early if the duergar attacks, forces a creature to make a saving throw, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.
sections.Bonus actions: Enlarge (recharges after a short or long rest). For 1 minute, the duergar and its equipment grow magically. The duergar becomes Large or grows as much as the available space allows. It makes Strength checks and Strength saves with advantage and doubles the damage dice of its Strength-based weapon attacks. The attack descriptions already include the increased damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 111.

name: Dybbuk
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A dybbuk is an airborne demon with a jellyfish-like body. It uses intact corpses to move among the living and frighten witnesses.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained.
sections.Traits:
Incorporeal Movement. The dybbuk can move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Magic Resistance. The dybbuk has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, reduce its hit point maximum by 3 (1d6) until it finishes a short or long rest. If the maximum falls to 0, the creature dies.
Possess Corpse (recharge 6). The dybbuk disappears into an intact corpse within 5 ft. that belonged to a Large or smaller Beast or Humanoid. The dybbuk gains 20 temporary hit points. It takes the corpse's size and cannot use Incorporeal Movement while inside, but its other statistics stay the same. The possession ends when it loses those temporary hit points or ends it as a bonus action. It then appears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the corpse.
sections.Spellcasting:
The dybbuk casts one spell as an action using Charisma, with spell save DC 12. It needs no material components.
At will. Dimension Door.
3/day. Phantasmal Force.
sections.Bonus actions: Control Corpse. While possessing a corpse, the dybbuk makes it move or behave in an unnatural way. Each Beast or Humanoid that sees this makes a DC 12 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is frightened of the dybbuk for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Any creature that succeeds on the save is immune to Control Corpse for 24 hours.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 113.
sections.Movement interpretation: The printed speed gives 0 ft. on land and 40 ft. with hover but leaves the second movement mode unnamed. Use a flying speed for its natural form, which the book describes moving through the air.

name: Earth Elemental Myrmidon
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An earth elemental bound into plate armor that strikes with a maul charged with force.

sections.Languages: Terran, one language of its creator's choice.
sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Maul attacks.
Maul. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) force damage.
Thunderous Strike (recharge 6). Make one Maul attack. On a hit, the target also takes 22 (4d10) thunder damage and makes a DC 14 Strength save. On a failure, it falls prone.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 122.

name: Eidolon
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An eidolon guards a sacred place and can animate a statue prepared to hold its spirit.

sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Acid, fire, lightning, thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained.
sections.Traits:
Incorporeal Movement. The eidolon can move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. If it ends its turn inside an object other than a Sacred Statue, it takes 5 (1d10) force damage.
Sacred Animation (recharge 5–6). When the eidolon enters a Sacred Statue's space, it can disappear into the statue. The statue becomes a creature under its control, and the eidolon uses the Sacred Statue stat block while inside.
Turn Resistance. The eidolon has advantage on saving throws against effects that turn undead.
Unusual Nature. The eidolon needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Divine Dread. Each creature within 60 ft. that can see the eidolon makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or is frightened of it for 1 minute. At the start of each turn while frightened this way, the creature must take the Dash action and move away by the safest available route. If it has nowhere to go, it is also stunned until it can move again. The creature repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success. When it succeeds or the effect ends, it is immune to every eidolon's Divine Dread for 24 hours.
sections.Sacred Statue encounter:
The Sacred Statue is an object until an eidolon enters it. The animated statue is a Large construct with the eidolon's alignment, AC 19 (natural armor), 95 HP (10d10 + 40), and speed 25 ft. It has Str 19, Dex 8, Con 19, Int 14, Wis 19, Cha 16, and a +8 Wisdom save. It has darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 14, and the eidolon's languages. It resists acid, fire, and lightning, plus bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. It is immune to cold, necrotic, and poison damage and to the charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
False Appearance. If motionless at the start of combat, the statue has advantage on initiative. A creature that has never seen the statue move or act needs a successful DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to tell it is a creature.
Ghostly Inhabitant. The eidolon leaves the statue if the statue reaches 0 HP, if the eidolon leaves as a bonus action, or if it is turned or forced out, such as by Dispel Evil and Good. It then appears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the statue and uses its own stat block again.
Multiattack. The statue makes two Slam or Rock attacks in any combination.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 43 (6d12 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 37 (6d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 114.

name: Elder Brain
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
classification: Large aberration (mind flayer), typically lawful evil
description: The mind flayer colony tends this immense brain in a pool of psionically charged brine. It coordinates the colony by telepathy and feeds on other creatures’ brains.

sections.Languages: Understands Common, Deep Speech, and Undercommon. It cannot speak. Telepathy 5 miles.
sections.Traits:
Creature Sense. Within 5 miles, the brain knows the distance, direction, and Intelligence score of every creature with Intelligence 4 or higher. This trait reveals no other information. Mind Blank, Nondetection, or similar magic shields the creature from this sense.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When the brain fails a saving throw, it can succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. The brain has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Telepathic Hub. Start and maintain telepathic conversations with up to ten creatures at once. The brain can let those creatures hear each other telepathically.
sections.Actions:
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (4d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage. A Huge or smaller creature is also grappled (escape DC 15) and takes 9 (1d8 + 5) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns while grappled this way. The brain can grapple up to four targets at once.
Mind Blast (Recharge 5–6). Choose any creatures within 60 ft. Each makes a DC 18 Intelligence save. On a failure, it takes 32 (5d10 + 5) psychic damage and is stunned for 1 minute. A stunned target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the stun on a success.
sections.Spellcasting:
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 18). No components are required.
At will. Detect Thoughts, Levitate.
3/day. Modify Memory.
1/day each. Dominate Monster, Plane Shift (self only).
sections.Bonus actions:
Psychic Link. Link with one incapacitated creature detected by Creature Sense. While linked, the brain perceives everything the target senses. When the target recovers from incapacitation, it notices the mental link. The target can use its action to make a DC 18 Charisma save, breaking the link and taking 10 (3d6) psychic damage on a success. The brain can end the link without an action at any time. It also ends when the two are more than 5 miles apart. The brain can maintain up to ten links at once.
Sense Thoughts. Choose a creature linked by Psychic Link. The brain learns its emotional state and most immediate thoughts, including its worries, loves, or hates.
sections.Legendary actions:
The brain has 3 legendary actions. Spend the listed cost immediately after another creature’s turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use these actions only when able to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using one.
Break Concentration (1 action). Choose a linked creature within 120 ft. End its concentration on a spell it cast and deal 2 (1d4) psychic damage per level of that spell.
Psychic Pulse (1 action). Choose a linked creature within 120 ft. The target and the brain’s enemies within 30 ft. of the target take 10 (3d6) psychic damage.
Sever Psychic Link (1 action). End the link with one linked creature within 120 ft. That creature has disadvantage on ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws until the end of its next turn.
Tentacle (2 actions). Make one Tentacle attack.
sections.Lair actions:
While in its lair, the brain can use one option on initiative count 20, losing ties. It must be able to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using an option. It cannot repeat the same option in consecutive rounds.
Force Wall. Cast Wall of Force.
Psionic Anchor. Choose a creature the brain can sense within 120 ft. On a failed DC 18 Charisma save, its speed becomes 0 and it cannot teleport. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Psychic Inspiration. Choose a friendly creature the brain can sense within 120 ft. It gains advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw of its choice before the end of its next turn.
sections.Regional effects:
Use one or more of these effects around the lair. They end as soon as the brain dies.
Paranoia. Creatures within 5 miles feel they are being followed.
Psychic Whispers. A linked creature hears faint, unintelligible fragments of the brain’s thoughts and those of its other linked creatures.
Telepathic Eavesdropping. The brain can overhear telepathic conversations within 5 miles. When contact begins, its initiator makes a DC 18 Wisdom save. On a success, the initiator notices the eavesdropping without learning who is listening.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 120.

name: Elder Oblex
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An oblex steals memories and uses them to imitate people. Its doubles can pass for their originals, apart from a faint sulfur smell.

sections.Traits:
Amorphous. The oblex can move through a gap as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Aversion to Fire. After taking fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.
Unusual Nature. The oblex does not need sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Pseudopod attacks and use Eat Memories.
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (4d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) psychic damage.
Eat Memories. Choose one visible creature within 5 ft. It makes a DC 18 Wisdom save. Constructs, Oozes, Plants, and Undead succeed automatically. On a failure, the target takes 44 (8d10) psychic damage and is memory drained. A short or long rest, Greater Restoration, or Heal ends the drain. While drained, the target subtracts a d4 roll from each ability check and attack roll. Each further drain increases the die by one size through d6, d8, d10, d12, then d20. When the die reaches d20, the target falls unconscious for 1 hour, then the effect ends. The oblex learns all the drained creature’s languages and gains all its skill proficiencies.
sections.Spellcasting:
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 18). No components are required.
At will. Charm Person (cast at 5th level), Detect Thoughts.
3/day each. Dimension Door, Dominate Person, Hypnotic Pattern, Telekinesis.
sections.Bonus actions: Sulfurous Impersonation. Form a double of a Medium or smaller creature whose memories the oblex stole. The double looks, sounds, and feels like the original but smells faintly of sulfur. The oblex can imitate 2d6 + 1 different creatures. Each double is part of the oblex, which occupies both its own space and the double’s space. A strand up to 120 ft. long connects each double to the body. The strand is immune to damage. The strand severs if no opening at least 1 inch wide connects the double and the body. The double then disappears.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 199.

name: Elder Tempest
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An immense serpent made of wind, cloud, and lightning. A storm travels with it, flooding the ground beneath its flight.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned.
sections.Traits:
Air Form. The tempest can enter and stop in a hostile creature’s space. It can move through a gap as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attack.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When the tempest fails a saving throw, it can succeed instead.
Living Storm. A storm 1d6 + 4 miles across stays centered on the tempest. Heavy rain or snow lightly obscures the area. Heavy rain puts out open flames and imposes disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing. Strong winds throughout the storm impose disadvantage on ranged attack rolls, put out open flames, and disperse fog.
Siege Monster. The tempest deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Thunderous Slam attacks.
Thunderous Slam. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 23 (4d6 + 9) thunder damage.
Lightning Storm (Recharge 6). Each creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 21 Dexterity save, taking 27 (6d8) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success. A creature that fails by 5 or more is also stunned until the end of its next turn.
sections.Legendary actions:
The tempest has 3 legendary actions. Spend the listed cost immediately after another creature’s turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use these actions only when able to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using one.
Move (1 action). Move up to its speed.
Lightning Strike (2 actions). Strike a point on the ground anywhere under the storm. Each creature within 5 ft. of that point makes a DC 21 Dexterity save, taking 16 (3d10) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.
Screaming Gale (3 actions). Blast a 300-ft. line, 20 ft. wide. Objects in the line take 22 (4d10) thunder damage. Each creature in the line makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 22 (4d10) thunder damage and is thrown up to 60 ft. away from the line. Hitting an immovable object or another creature deals the thrown creature 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage for every 10 ft. traveled before impact. A creature struck by the thrown creature makes a DC 19 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes the same impact damage and falls prone.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 121.

name: Enchanter Wizard
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A wizard who influences minds, whether to prevent a fight or turn someone against their allies.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Arcane Burst attacks.
Arcane Burst. Melee or ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d10 + 3) psychic damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 14).
At will. Friends, Mage Hand, Message.
2/day each. Charm Person, Mage Armor, Hold Person, Invisibility, Suggestion, Tongues.
sections.Reactions: Instinctive Charm (Recharge 4–6). When a creature the wizard can see within 30 ft. makes an attack roll against the wizard, the attacker makes a DC 14 Wisdom save. On a failure, the attacker redirects the roll to the nearest creature to itself, excluding itself and the wizard. The attacker chooses among tied creatures.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 261.

name: Evoker Wizard
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A battle wizard who can direct an explosion through a group of enemies and spare selected allies.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Arcane Burst attacks.
Arcane Burst. Melee or ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 25 (4d10 + 3) force damage.
Sculpted Explosion (Recharge 4–6). Choose cold, fire, lightning, or thunder. A magical explosion fills a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered on a point within 150 ft. The wizard can spare up to three creatures it can see in the area. Each remaining creature makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. A failed save deals 40 (9d8) damage of the chosen type and knocks the creature prone. On a success, the creature takes half damage only.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 15).
At will. Light, Mage Hand, Message, Prestidigitation.
2/day each. Ice Storm, Lightning Bolt, Mage Armor.
1/day. Wall of Ice.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 262.

name: Female Steeder
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: This spiderlike Underdark hunter leaps onto prey and holds it with sticky legs. Duergar train female steeders as mounts.

sections.Traits:
Extraordinary Leap. Triple the distance of a long jump. Every foot of walking speed spent on that jump moves the steeder 3 ft.
Spider Climb. The steeder can climb difficult surfaces and move upside down on ceilings without making an ability check.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.
Sticky Leg. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. On a hit, the target sticks to a leg and is grappled (escape DC 12). The steeder can grapple only one creature at a time.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 231.

name: Fire Elemental Myrmidon
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An elemental bound in plate armor, with no memory of its former life. It obeys its creator and strikes with a scimitar.

sections.Languages: Ignan and one language chosen by its creator.
sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Illumination. The myrmidon sheds bright light out to 20 ft. and dim light out to 40 ft.
Water Susceptibility. For every 5 ft. it moves through water at least 1 ft. deep, the myrmidon takes 2 (1d4) cold damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Scimitar attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) force damage.
Fiery Strikes (Recharge 6). Use Multiattack. Each hit deals 7 (2d6) additional fire damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 123.

name: Fire Giant Dreadnought
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Fire giant foundries put their strongest workers to use moving coal and ore. In battle, a dreadnought fills its two spiked shields with hot coals and drives forward behind them.

sections.Traits: Dual Shields. The pair grants a total +3 bonus to AC, already included in the giant's AC.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks in any combination of Fireshield and Rock.
Fireshield. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (4d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage, 7 (2d6) fire damage, and 7 (2d6) piercing damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +13 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Shield Charge (Recharge 5–6). Move up to 30 ft. in a straight line. The giant can pass through the spaces of creatures smaller than Huge. The first time it enters each creature's space during the move, that creature makes a DC 21 Strength save. On a failure, the creature takes 36 (8d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and 14 (4d6) fire damage, is pushed up to 30 ft., and falls prone.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 124.

name: Firenewt Warlock of Imix
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Warlocks of Imix lead firenewt theocracies or advise their high priests. They revere fire for its power to destroy.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The warlock breathes air and water.
Devil's Sight. Its darkvision works in magical darkness.
Imix's Blessing. When the warlock drops an enemy to 0 hit points, it gains 5 temporary hit points.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Morningstar and Fire Ray.
Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.
Fire Ray. Ranged spell attack, +4 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) fire damage.
sections.Spellcasting: As an action, cast one of these spells at will using Charisma (spell save DC 12). Guidance, Light, Mage Armor, Mage Hand, or Prestidigitation.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 125.

name: Firenewt Warrior
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Firenewt warriors live near sources of moist heat. Many feed and shelter giant striders, which willingly carry them into battle.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The warrior breathes air and water.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.
Spit Fire (Recharges after a short or long rest). Target one creature within 10 ft. It makes a DC 11 Dexterity save, taking 9 (2d8) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 125.

name: Flail Snail
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An earth elemental with club-tipped tentacles and a colorful shell. The mineral trail it leaves hardens into glass thin enough to cut into window panes.

sections.Traits: Antimagic Shell. The snail has advantage on saves against spells, and spell attacks against it have disadvantage. If the snail saves successfully against a spell of 1st level or higher or that spell's attack misses it, its shell releases stored force. Every creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 3 (1d6) force damage per spell level on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make five Flail Tentacle attacks.
Flail Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Scintillating Shell (Recharges after a short or long rest). The shell casts bright light for 30 ft. and dim light for another 30 ft. through the end of the snail's next turn. While the light lasts, creatures that can see the snail have disadvantage on attacks against it. When the light first appears, each creature in the bright area that can see the snail must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or remain stunned until the light ends.
Shell Defense. The snail retreats into its shell. It gains +4 AC and is restrained until it emerges.
sections.Bonus actions: Emerge. On its turn, the snail can leave its shell to end Shell Defense.
sections.Using the shell: An intact shell weighs about 250 pounds and can sell for 5,000 gp. A skilled armorer can cut it into three shields. For 1 month, each shield grants its wielder Antimagic Shell. A shield whose magic has faded can form the base for a Spellguard Shield. Ground shell can also go into the dye and serve as a ritual component for a Robe of Scintillating Colors.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 126.

name: Flind
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: Yeenoghu transforms especially vicious gnolls into flinds. A flind leads its war band's charge with a flail that disorients, hurts, or paralyzes its targets.

sections.Traits: Aura of Blood Thirst. A creature within 10 ft. of the flind that has the Rampage trait can make a Bite attack as a bonus action. This aura is inactive while the flind is incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Flail of Chaos, one Flail of Pain, and one Flail of Paralysis attack, or make three Longbow attacks.
Flail of Chaos. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage. On a failed DC 16 Wisdom save, the target must use its reaction, if available, to make one melee attack against a randomly chosen creature other than the flind within reach. If there is no such creature, it moves half its speed in a random direction instead.
Flail of Pain. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage and 16 (3d10) psychic damage.
Flail of Paralysis. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage. On a failed DC 16 Constitution save, the target is paralyzed until the end of its next turn.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 127.

name: Fraz-Urb’luu
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: The Prince of Deception recruits mortals under false identities. He sends his servants to find the scattered pieces of the staff taken from him during his imprisonment beneath Castle Greyhawk.

sections.Damage immunities: Poison. Nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). After failing a save, Fraz-Urb’luu can spend one use to succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. He has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Undetectable. Divination magic cannot target him. Magical scrying sensors cannot perceive him, and abilities that sense demons or fiends cannot detect him.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Fist attacks, and use Phantasmal Terror.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d6 + 9) force damage.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d8 + 9) force damage.
Phantasmal Terror. Choose one visible creature within 120 ft. On a failed DC 23 Wisdom save, it takes 16 (3d10) psychic damage and is frightened of Fraz-Urb’luu until the end of its next turn.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Charisma (spell save DC 23). No material components are required.
At will. Alter Self, Detect Magic, Dispel Magic, and Phantasmal Force. Alter Self can make him Medium when he uses its appearance option.
3/day each. Mislead, Programmed Illusion, and Seeming.
1/day each. Modify Memory and Project Image.
sections.Legendary actions:
Fraz-Urb’luu has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of his turn. He can choose one option immediately after another creature finishes its turn. He loses access to these actions while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before using one.
Tail (1 action). Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) force damage. A Large or smaller creature is also grappled (escape DC 24) and remains restrained for the duration of the grapple. His tail can grapple only one creature at a time.
Terror (2 actions). Use Phantasmal Terror.
sections.Lair: Fraz-Urb’luu lairs in the fortress city of Zoragmelok in Hollow’s Heart. In his lair he is CR 24 (62,000 XP).
sections.Lair actions:
On initiative count 20, after anyone tied at 20, choose one action while Fraz-Urb’luu is in his lair. He cannot repeat an option in consecutive rounds. He must be able to act and, if surprised, must finish his first turn before using a lair action.
Conjure Walls and Doors. Turn up to five doors in the lair into walls and open an equal number of new doors in walls that had none.
Psychic Anguish. Every creature he can see in the lair makes a DC 23 Wisdom save, taking 33 (6d10) psychic damage on a failure.
Simulacrum. Pick one humanoid in the lair and instantly make a duplicate as with the Simulacrum spell. The duplicate obeys him and is destroyed at the next initiative count 20.
sections.Regional effects:
Choose one or more of these effects for the area surrounding the lair.
Beguiling Realm. Within 6 miles, Charisma (Persuasion) and Wisdom (Insight) checks have disadvantage. Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks have advantage.
Nostalgic Pangs. Within 1 mile, sapient creatures often catch brief glimpses of long-dead friends or companions.
Twisted Paths. Within 6 miles, roads and trails bend back on themselves and make navigation difficult.
If Fraz-Urb’luu dies, the effects fade over 1d10 days.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 129.

name: Froghemoth
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: This amphibious predator hides in murky pools with only its three-eyed stalk showing. Bullywugs sometimes feed and shelter one as a god.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The froghemoth breathes air and water.
Shock Susceptibility. When it takes lightning damage, its speed is halved and it has disadvantage on Dexterity saves until the end of its next turn.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Tentacle attacks. The froghemoth can also use Tongue.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage and swallows a Medium or smaller creature. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects from outside the froghemoth, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the froghemoth's turns. Its gullet holds up to two creatures.
If one creature inside deals 20 damage or more to the froghemoth in a single turn, the froghemoth makes a DC 20 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On a failure, it regurgitates every swallowed creature, which falls prone in a space within 10 ft. If the froghemoth dies, the creatures are no longer restrained and can spend 10 ft. of movement to escape its corpse. Each falls prone on exit.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage and grapples a Huge or smaller creature (escape DC 16). The froghemoth has four tentacles. A tentacle that has a creature grappled cannot target another creature.
Tongue. Target one visible Medium or smaller creature within 20 ft. On a failed DC 18 Strength save, pull it to an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the froghemoth.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 130.

name: Frost Giant Everlasting One
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A frost giant who gained a troll's regenerative power by accepting Vaprak's gift.

sections.Traits:
Extra Heads. Roll a 25 percent chance that the giant has more than one head. If it does, it has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and on saves against becoming blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or unconscious.
Regeneration. The giant regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn. Acid or fire damage suppresses the trait at the start of its next turn. It dies only if it starts its turn at 0 hit points and fails to regenerate.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Greataxe or Rock.
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 26 (3d12 + 7) slashing damage, or 30 (3d12 + 11) while raging.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +11 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 29 (4d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Vaprak's Rage (recharges after a short or long rest). The giant rages for 1 minute or until incapacitated. During the rage it has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saves, adds +4 to damage rolls for melee weapon attacks, and resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 131.

name: Frost Salamander
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A heat-seeking predator from the Frostfell that digs extensive networks of caves in ice.

sections.Traits: Burning Fury. Taking fire damage immediately recharges Freezing Breath.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and four Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d8 + 5) piercing damage plus 5 (1d10) cold damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage.
Freezing Breath (Recharge 6). Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 17 Constitution save. It takes 44 (8d10) cold damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 132.

name: Gauth
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A beholder relative with six eyestalks and a hunger for the power stored in magic items.

sections.Traits:
Stunning Gaze. When a creature starts its turn within 30 ft. and can see the central eye, the gauth can force a DC 14 Wisdom save if it can see the creature and isn't incapacitated. Failure stuns the creature until the start of its next turn. A creature that is not surprised can avert its eyes at the start of its turn to avoid the save. It then cannot see the gauth until its next turn starts, when it can avert its eyes again. Looking at the gauth sooner requires the save immediately.
Death Throes. The gauth releases explosive magical energy when it dies. Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 14 Dexterity save, taking 13 (3d8) force damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d8) piercing damage.
Eye Rays. Roll three d6s, rerolling duplicates, for three magical rays. Choose one to three creatures the gauth can see within 120 ft.
1. Devour Magic Ray. On a failed DC 14 Dexterity save, a randomly selected magic item of the target loses its magical properties until the start of the gauth's next turn. Exclude single-use items such as potions and scrolls. An item with charges also loses 1d4 charges.
2. Enervation Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. A failure deals 18 (4d8) necrotic damage, and a success halves it.
3. Fire Ray. A failed DC 14 Dexterity save deals 22 (4d10) fire damage.
4. Paralyzing Ray. A failed DC 14 Constitution save paralyzes the target for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
5. Pushing Ray. A failed DC 14 Strength save pushes the target up to 15 ft. away and halves its speed until the start of the gauth's next turn.
6. Sleep Ray. A failed DC 14 Wisdom save leaves the target asleep and unconscious for 1 minute. Damage or an action from another creature to wake it ends the sleep. Constructs and undead are unaffected.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 133.

name: Gazer
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A tiny creature born from a beholder's dreams. It mimics overheard speech and follows its creator around the lair.

sections.Traits: Mimicry. The gazer imitates simple speech sounds it has heard in any language. A listener recognizes the imitation on a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Insight) check.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 1 piercing damage.
Eye Rays. Roll two d4s, rerolling duplicates, for two magical rays. Choose one or two targets the gazer can see within 60 ft.
1. Dazing Ray. A creature that fails a DC 12 Wisdom save is charmed until the start of the gazer's next turn. While charmed this way, its speed is halved and its attack rolls have disadvantage.
2. Fear Ray. A creature that fails a DC 12 Wisdom save is frightened until the start of the gazer's next turn.
3. Frost Ray. A failed DC 12 Dexterity save deals 10 (3d6) cold damage.
4. Telekinetic Ray. A Medium or smaller creature that fails a DC 12 Strength save moves up to 30 ft. directly away. The gazer can move a Tiny object up to 30 ft. in any direction if the object is neither worn nor carried. It can also manipulate a simple tool or open a container.
sections.Bonus actions: Aggressive. Move up to its speed toward a hostile creature it can see.
sections.Gazer familiar (optional): A gazer can form a telepathic bond with a willing master who is at least a 3rd-level spellcaster. The master can use the gazer's senses while the two are within 1 mile of each other. Physical harm from the master ends the gazer's service and breaks the bond.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 134.

name: Geryon
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: An archdevil who hunts from the fortress of Coldsteel and contests Levistus for control of Stygia.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When Geryon fails a save, he can spend a use to succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. Geryon has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Regeneration. Geryon regains 20 hit points at the start of his turn. Radiant damage suppresses the trait at the start of his next turn. He dies only if he starts his turn at 0 hit points and does not regenerate.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claw and one Stinger attack.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 23 (4d6 + 9) cold damage. A Large or smaller target is grappled (escape DC 24) and restrained until the grapple ends. Geryon can grapple only one creature at a time. A target already in his grapple takes an extra 27 (6d8) cold damage.
Stinger. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one creature. A hit deals 14 (2d4 + 9) force damage. On a failed DC 21 Constitution save, the target also takes 13 (2d12) poison damage and is poisoned until it finishes a short or long rest. Reduce its hit point maximum by half the poison damage it took until the poisoned condition ends. It dies if this reduces its hit point maximum to 0.
Teleport. Geryon and his worn or carried equipment teleport up to 120 ft. to an unoccupied space he can see.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast a listed spell using Charisma (spell save DC 21). No material components are required.
At will. Alter Self (can become Medium when changing his appearance), Detect Magic, Ice Storm, Invisibility (self only), Locate Object, Suggestion, Wall of Ice.
1/day. Banishment.
sections.Legendary actions:
3 actions. Spend the indicated cost for one option at the end of another creature's turn. Regain spent actions at the start of Geryon's turn. Geryon cannot use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before using one.
Infernal Glare (1 action). Choose one creature Geryon can see within 60 ft. A failed DC 23 Wisdom save leaves it frightened of him until the end of its next turn.
Teleport (1 action). Use Teleport.
Swift Sting (2 actions). Make one Stinger attack.
sections.Lair actions:
At initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option while Geryon is in the lair and able to act. He cannot choose the same option in consecutive rounds. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before taking a lair action.
Banish. Cast Banishment.
Chill Blast. Choose a point Geryon can see within 120 ft. A blast of cold rises from the ground in a 10-ft. cube centered there. A creature in the cube that fails a DC 21 Constitution save takes 28 (8d6) cold damage.
Hateful Restraints. A creature Geryon can see within 60 ft. must pass a DC 21 Wisdom save or be restrained for 1 minute. The target can end the effect on itself by dealing any damage to one or more of its allies.
sections.Regional effects:
Choose one or more effects within 1 mile of the lair.
Chilling Wind. Strong, freezing winds blow throughout the area.
Enervating Screams. Howls fill the air. A creature that finishes a short or long rest must pass a DC 21 Wisdom save to gain any benefit.
Hellish Doorways. Sapient creatures frequently see portals that seem to lead to places they consider safe. Anyone who crosses a portal arrives somewhere in Stygia.
The effects fade over 1d10 days if Geryon dies.
sections.Sound the Horn (optional): Once per day, Geryon can sound his horn as an action, summoning 5d4 minotaurs into unoccupied spaces he chooses within 600 ft. They roll initiative on arrival and obey him. Each remains until it dies or until Geryon uses an action to dismiss some or all of them.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 136.

name: Giant Strider
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A fire-breathing creature with birdlike and reptilian features that firenewt warriors keep as willing mounts.

sections.Traits: Fire Absorption. Fire damage instead restores hit points equal to half the damage dealt.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Fire Burst (Recharge 5–6). Choose a point the strider can see within 60 ft. Each creature in a 10-ft.-radius sphere centered there makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. It takes 14 (4d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The fire spreads around corners and ignites flammable objects that are neither worn nor carried.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 137.

name: Giff
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A hippopotamus-headed Wildspace mercenary whose regiment relies on muskets and grenades.

sections.Traits:
Firearms Knowledge. Ignore the loading property when using muskets and pistols.
Headfirst Charge. If the giff travels at least 20 ft. in a straight line and ends within 5 ft. of a Large or smaller creature, it can force that creature to make a DC 14 Strength save. A failure deals 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage and knocks it prone.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Longsword, Musket, or Pistol.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage one-handed or 9 (1d10 + 4) two-handed.
Musket. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 40/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d12 + 2) piercing damage.
Pistol. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/90 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage.
Fragmentation Grenade (1/day). Throw the grenade up to 60 ft. Each creature in the resulting 20-ft.-radius sphere makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 17 (5d6) piercing damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Gunpowder keg (encounter option): As an action, the giff lights a keg's fuse and can throw the keg up to 15 ft. It explodes at the start of the giff's next turn. A creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On a failure it takes 24 (7d6) fire damage and falls prone. On a success it takes half damage and the blast does not knock it prone. Each other keg within 20 ft. of an exploding keg has a 50 percent chance to explode. Check each keg once per turn.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 138.

name: Girallon
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A white-furred, four-armed predator that scales ruins and attacks from high perches.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and four Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Aggressive. Move up to its speed toward a hostile creature it can see.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 139.

name: Githyanki Gish
publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
description: A githyanki warrior who fights with a longsword and psionic magic.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Longsword and Telekinetic Bolt, or make one of those attacks and use Spellcasting.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage with both hands, plus 22 (5d8) psychic damage either way.
Telekinetic Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (8d6) force damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell with no components, using Intelligence (spell save DC 15).
At will. Light, Mage Hand (invisible hand), Message.
3/day each. Fireball, Invisibility, Nondetection (self only).
1/day each. Dimension Door, Plane Shift, Telekinesis.
