Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dreadnought can turn a failed save into a success.
Magic Weapons. The dreadnought's weapon attacks count as magical.
Sever Silver Cord. On a critical hit against a creature traveling by Astral Projection, it can cut that creature's silver cord instead of dealing damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (5d10 + 9) piercing damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature and is incapacitated or dropped to 0 HP by this damage, swallow it. It and its gear appear in an unoccupied space on the Donjon floor.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d6 + 9) slashing damage.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dreadnought has 3 legendary actions and can spend the listed cost for one option at the end of another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It cannot use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it can use them after its first turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Donjon Visit (2 actions). A visible Huge or smaller creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 19 Charisma save. On a failure it teleports magically to an unoccupied space on the Donjon floor. At the end of its next turn it returns to the space it left, or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is filled.
Psychic Projection (3 actions). Each creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. It takes 15 (2d10 + 4) psychic damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Titanic Nature: The dreadnought needs no air, food, drink, or sleep. The Donjon has gravity and breathable air, and organic matter decays there.

name: Autumn Eladrin
description: In the autumn aspect, an eladrin heals and shelters those who seek aid. Violence in its presence draws a swift response.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Enchanting Presence. A creature other than an eladrin that starts its turn within 60 ft. makes a DC 16 Wisdom save. On a failure the eladrin charms it for 1 minute. On a success the creature gains immunity to any eladrin's Enchanting Presence for 24 hours. The target can repeat the save whenever the eladrin damages it, ending the charm on a success.
Magic Resistance. The eladrin makes saving throws against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma (spell save DC 16). No material components.
At will. Calm Emotions, Sleep.
3/day each. Cure Wounds (5th level), Lesser Restoration.
1/day each. Greater Restoration, Heal, Raise Dead.
sections.Actions:
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage, or 6 (1d10 + 1) slashing with two hands, plus 18 (4d8) psychic damage either way.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage and 18 (4d8) psychic damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Fey Step (Recharge 4–6). Teleport up to 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space.
sections.Reactions: Foster Peace. When a creature charmed by this eladrin hits with an attack roll within 60 ft., the eladrin can magically turn the hit into a miss if it can see the attacker.

name: Bael
description: Mammon's Bronze General commands sixty-six companies of barbed devils. He sometimes spares defeated foes who pledge their souls and service.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Bael can turn a failed save into a success.
Magic Resistance. Bael makes saving throws against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Magic Weapons. Bael's weapon attacks count as magical.
Regeneration. Bael regains 20 HP at the start of his turn. Cold or radiant damage prevents regeneration at the start of his next turn. He dies only if he starts his turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma (spell save DC 21, +13 to hit with spell attacks). No material components.
At will. Alter Self (can become Medium when changing appearance), Animate Dead, Charm Person, Detect Magic, Inflict Wounds (8th level), Invisibility (self only), Major Image.
3/day each. Counterspell, Dispel Magic, Fly, Suggestion, Wall of Fire.
1/day each. Dominate Monster, Symbol (stunning only).
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Hellish Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d8 + 7) piercing damage and 13 (3d8) necrotic damage.
Infernal Command. Allies within 60 ft. of Bael cannot be charmed or frightened until the end of his next turn.
Teleport. Bael magically moves up to 120 ft. with his gear to a visible, unoccupied space.
sections.Bonus actions: Dreadful. Until the start of Bael's next turn, each creature other than a devil that starts its turn within 10 ft. must pass a DC 22 Wisdom save or be frightened until the start of that creature's next turn.
sections.Legendary actions:
Bael has 3 legendary actions and can spend the listed cost for one option at the end of another creature's turn. He regains spent actions at the start of his turn. He cannot use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, he can use them after his first turn.
Attack (2 actions). Make one Hellish Morningstar attack.
Awaken Greed (1 action). Cast Charm Person or Major Image.
Infernal Command (1 action). Use Infernal Command.
Teleport (1 action). Use Teleport.

name: Balhannoth
description: A Shadowfell predator that lures travelers by shaping its lair into the place they most want to find.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (2/day). The balhannoth can turn a failed save into a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and up to two Tentacle attacks, or make up to four Tentacle attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 25 (4d10 + 3) piercing damage.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, grapples the target (escape DC 15), and pulls it up to 5 ft. toward the balhannoth. The target is restrained until the grapple ends. The balhannoth has four tentacles. A tentacle holding a target cannot attack another one.
sections.Legendary actions:
The balhannoth has 3 legendary actions and can spend one for one option at the end of another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It cannot use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it can use them after its first turn.
Bite Attack. Make one Bite attack against one creature it has grappled.
Teleport. Magically move up to 60 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space, bringing all gear and grappled creatures.
Vanish. Magically become invisible for up to 10 minutes, ending immediately after the balhannoth makes an attack roll.
sections.Lair actions:
Inside the lair, use one option on initiative count 20, losing ties. It cannot choose the same option in consecutive rounds. It cannot use lair actions while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it can use them after its first turn.
Reshape terrain. Choose an area no larger than a square 500 ft. on a side. After 10 minutes, its nonliving terrain takes the appearance of a place sought by an intelligent creature whose mind the balhannoth has read. Created objects have no moving parts or magic, and close examination reveals they are fakes. The changes last until it dies or uses this option again.
Move intruder. One creature within 500 ft. makes a DC 16 Wisdom save. On a failure, the balhannoth teleports the target and its gear to an unoccupied space of its choice within 60 ft. of itself.
Hide from intruder. One creature within 500 ft. makes a DC 16 Wisdom save. On a failure, the balhannoth is invisible to that creature for 1 minute, or until the balhannoth attacks it.
sections.Regional effects:
The following effects vanish immediately when the balhannoth dies.
False hope. Creatures within 1 mile of the lair feel as though they are nearing whatever they desire most. The feeling intensifies as they approach.
Sense desire. The balhannoth senses the strongest desires of Humanoids within 1 mile of itself and learns whether those desires concern a place.

name: Baphomet
description: The Horned King hunts trespassers through a labyrinth that can seal its passages and twist the rooms around them.

sections.Damage immunities: Poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage when the damage is nonmagical.
sections.Traits:
Charge. Move at least 10 ft. straight toward a target before hitting it with Gore on the same turn to deal an extra 16 (3d10) piercing damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 25 Strength save or be pushed up to 10 ft. away and knocked prone.
Labyrinthine Recall. Baphomet remembers every path he has traveled perfectly and is immune to Maze.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Baphomet can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. Baphomet has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Baphomet’s weapon attacks are magical.
Reckless. At the start of his turn, Baphomet can gain advantage on melee weapon attack rolls for that turn. If he does, attack rolls against him have advantage until the start of his next turn.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Heartcleaver attack, one Bite attack, and one Gore attack.
Heartcleaver. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) slashing damage.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) piercing damage.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d6 + 10) piercing damage.
Frightful Presence. Each chosen creature within 120 ft. that is aware of Baphomet must make a DC 18 Wisdom save or become frightened for 1 minute. Each affected creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if Baphomet is in its line of sight. A successful save ends the effect. When the creature saves successfully or the effect otherwise ends, it is immune to this Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Use Charisma (spell save DC 18). These spells require no material components.
At will. Detect Magic.
3/day each. Dispel Magic, Dominate Beast, Hunter’s Mark, Maze, Wall of Stone.
1/day. Teleport.
sections.Legendary actions:
Baphomet has 3 legendary actions. Use one option at a time, at the end of another creature’s turn. He regains spent actions at the start of his turn and must be able to act. If surprised, he first has to complete his first turn.
Heartcleaver Attack (1 action). Make one Heartcleaver attack.
Charge (2 actions). Move up to Baphomet’s speed, then make one Gore attack.
sections.Lair actions:
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one magical effect. Baphomet cannot choose the same effect two rounds in a row. He must be able to act. If surprised, he first has to complete his first turn.
Seal an entrance. Fill one unoccupied doorway or other entrance within the lair with solid stone. The stone lasts for 1 minute or until Baphomet uses this option again.
Reverse gravity. Choose a room within the lair no larger than 100 ft. in any dimension. Gravity reverses there until the next initiative count 20. Creatures and objects in the room fall in the new direction unless they can stay aloft. Baphomet can ignore the reversal if he is in the room.
Mirage Arcane. Cast Mirage Arcane on one room within the lair no larger than 100 ft. in any dimension. The spell ends on the next initiative count 20.
sections.Regional effects:
Plants within 1 mile of the lair grow into dense walls that form small mazes.
Beasts within 1 mile of the lair become frightened and disoriented. They may panic or lash out without an obvious threat.
A humanoid that spends at least 1 hour within 1 mile of the lair must pass a DC 18 Wisdom save or gain a flaw from Madness of Baphomet. A successful save grants immunity to this regional effect for 24 hours.
If Baphomet dies, these regional effects fade over 1d10 days.
sections.Madness of Baphomet:
If a creature goes mad in the lair or within Baphomet’s line of sight, roll d100 for a flaw that persists until cured.
01–20. Once provoked, the creature is too angry to listen to reason.
21–40. The creature slips into animal behavior.
41–60. The creature treats the world as its hunting ground and other people as prey.
61–80. The creature slips easily from hatred into rage.
81–00. The creature regards anyone who opposes it as fair game.

name: Berbalang
description: This collector of secrets questions the dead and sends a spectral double to spy on the living.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Spectral Duplicate (recharges after a short or long rest). Create one spectral duplicate in a visible, unoccupied space within 60 ft. The berbalang is unconscious while the duplicate exists and can have only one duplicate at a time. The duplicate has the same statistics and knowledge as the berbalang. Everything it experiences becomes known to the berbalang, and its attacks deal psychic damage in place of their normal damage types. The duplicate disappears when it or the berbalang reaches 0 HP, or when the berbalang dismisses it without spending an action.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Use Intelligence (spell save DC 13). These spells require no material components.
At will. Speak with Dead.
1/day. Plane Shift (self only).

name: Black Abishai
description: This winged devil hides in darkness that it can move across the battlefield.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered.
sections.Traits:
Devil’s Sight. Magical darkness does not block the abishai’s darkvision.
Magic Resistance. The abishai has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. The abishai’s weapon attacks are magical.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks and one Bite attack.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) acid damage.
Creeping Darkness (Recharge 6). Cast Darkness on a point within 120 ft. without components, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability.
sections.Bonus actions:
Shadow Stealth. The abishai can Hide while in dim light or darkness.
Move Creeping Darkness. While its Darkness spell from Creeping Darkness persists, the abishai can move that area of darkness up to 60 ft.

name: Blue Abishai
description: This winged devil studies wizardry and carries a quarterstaff.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered.
sections.Traits:
Devil’s Sight. Magical darkness does not block the abishai’s darkvision.
Magic Resistance. The abishai has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. The abishai’s weapon attacks are magical.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Quarterstaff attack and one Bite attack.
Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage when wielded with two hands.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d10 + 2) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) lightning damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
The abishai casts as a 13th-level wizard using Intelligence (spell save DC 20, +12 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips (at will). Friends, Mage Hand, Message, Minor Illusion, Shocking Grasp.
Level 1 (4 slots). Chromatic Orb, Disguise Self, Expeditious Retreat, Magic Missile, Charm Person, Thunderwave.
Level 2 (3 slots). Darkness, Mirror Image, Misty Step.
Level 3 (3 slots). Dispel Magic, Fear, Lightning Bolt.
Level 4 (3 slots). Dimension Door, Greater Invisibility, Ice Storm.
Level 5 (2 slots). Cone of Cold, Wall of Force.
Level 6 (1 slot). Chain Lightning.
Level 7 (1 slot). Teleport.

name: Boneclaw
description: A failed lich can return as this long-clawed undead, bound to a cruel master. Destroying its body buys time while that bond holds.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Languages: Common plus the main language of its master.
sections.Traits: Rejuvenation. If destroyed while its master lives, the boneclaw returns in 1d10 hours at full HP. Its new body appears within 1 mile of its master.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Piercing Claw attacks.
Piercing Claw. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (3d10 + 4) piercing damage. The boneclaw can pull a creature hit up to 10 ft. closer, and the creature is grappled (escape DC 14). The boneclaw has two claws. While a claw is grappling a creature, it can attack only that creature.
Shadow Jump. If the boneclaw is in dim light or darkness, each creature it chooses within 5 ft. makes a DC 14 Constitution save or takes 34 (5d12 + 2) necrotic damage. The boneclaw then magically teleports up to 60 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space. It can take one creature it is grappling, placing it in a visible, unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the boneclaw’s destination. Both destinations must be in dim light or darkness.
sections.Bonus actions: Shadow Stealth. The boneclaw can Hide while in dim light or darkness.
sections.Reactions: Deadly Reach. When an enemy the boneclaw can see moves into its reach, it makes one Piercing Claw attack against the enemy. If that attack hits, it can make a second Piercing Claw attack against the same target.

name: Bronze Scout
description: This burrowing clockwork scout sends lightning through the ground when enemies get close.

sections.Damage immunities: Poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't adamantine.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Languages: Understands one language of its creator but can't speak.
sections.Traits:
Earth Armor. Burrowing does not provoke opportunity attacks for the bronze scout.
Magic Resistance. The bronze scout has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) lightning damage.
Lightning Flare (recharges after a short or long rest). Every creature touching the ground within 15 ft. makes a DC 13 Dexterity save, taking 14 (4d6) lightning damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.

name: Bulezau
description: Bulezaus gather in the crags and canyons of the Abyss. Stronger demons press them into service as foot soldiers. Left on their own, they fight among themselves until they find another target.

sections.Traits:
Rotting Presence. When a creature other than a demon starts its turn within 30 ft. of at least one bulezau, it must pass a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 1d6 necrotic damage plus 1 necrotic damage for each bulezau within 30 ft. of it.
Standing Leap. It can long jump up to 20 ft. and high jump up to 10 ft., with or without a running start.
Sure-Footed. It has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saves against effects that would knock it prone.
sections.Actions: Barbed Tail. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d12 + 2) piercing damage. A creature hit must make a DC 13 Constitution save against disease. On a failure, it is poisoned until the disease ends. While poisoned this way, it develops festering boils, coughs up flies, and sheds rotting skin. After each 24-hour period it repeats the save. A success ends the disease. A failure reduces its hit point maximum by 4 (1d8). The creature dies if its hit point maximum reaches 0.

name: Cadaver Collector
description: This war machine from Acheron scavenges armor and weapons from battlefields and carries the fallen on its spikes. It answers mortal summons at the site of a past, present, or imminent battle.

sections.Damage immunities: Necrotic, poison, psychic, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not adamantine.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Languages: Understands all languages but cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The collector has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Constructed Nature. The collector needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (3d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 16 (3d10) necrotic damage.
Paralyzing Breath (Recharge 5–6). The collector releases gas in a 30-ft. cone. Each creature in the cone must succeed on a DC 18 Constitution save or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A paralyzed creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the effect on itself on a success.
sections.Bonus actions: Summon Specters (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Call up 1d6 Specters from creatures the collector killed. They lack Sunlight Sensitivity and appear in unoccupied spaces within 15 ft. They share the collector's initiative count and act immediately after it. They fight until destroyed and disappear if the collector is destroyed.
sections.Table notes: Mordenkainen notes that destroying a summoned specter prevents the collector from calling that spirit again.

name: Canoloth
description: A canoloth guards valuables under contract. Its tongue drags intruders close, and the terms of its contract determine whether it holds them or kills them.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Dimensional Lock. Creatures other than the canoloth cannot teleport into or out of a space within 60 ft. of it. An attempt to do so is wasted.
Magic Resistance. The canoloth has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. The canoloth's weapon attacks are magical.
Uncanny Senses. The canoloth can be surprised only while incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite or Tongue attack and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 25 (6d6 + 4) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d10 + 4) slashing damage.
Tongue. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d12 + 4) piercing damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, the canoloth grapples it (escape DC 15) and pulls it up to 30 ft. closer. The target remains restrained until the grapple ends. The tongue can grapple one target at a time.

name: Choker
description: A choker waits deep inside a crevice and leaves its last catch outside as bait. Its tentacles can reach prey while its body stays out of sight.

sections.Traits:
Aberrant Quickness (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The choker can take an extra action on its turn.
Boneless. It can enter and occupy an opening as narrow as 4 inches without squeezing.
Spider Climb. It can climb difficult surfaces and move upside down on ceilings without an ability check.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) piercing damage. A Large or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 15) and restrained until the grapple ends. The choker has two tentacles and cannot use the one holding a creature against a different target. A creature grappled by a critical hit also cannot breathe or speak until the grapple ends.

name: Corpse Flower
description: A corpse flower can sprout over a necromancer's grave or the remains of powerful undead. Once it uproots itself, it searches graveyards and battlefields for bodies.

sections.Traits:
Corpses. When first encountered, the flower contains 1d6 + 3 humanoid corpses. It can hold up to nine. Stored corpses have total cover against attacks and effects outside the flower. If the flower dies, the corpses can be pulled free.
Spider Climb. The flower can climb difficult surfaces and move upside down on ceilings without an ability check.
Stench of Death. When a creature other than a construct or undead starts its turn within 10 ft. of the flower or one of its zombies, it makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it is incapacitated until the end of that turn. Immunity to poison damage or the poisoned condition makes the save an automatic success. A creature that succeeds is immune to the stench of all corpse flowers for 24 hours.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage. The target must then make a DC 14 Constitution save, taking 14 (4d6) poison damage on a failure.
Harvest the Dead. Take one unsecured humanoid corpse within 10 ft. into the flower's body, together with anything it wears or carries. The flower can use the remains for its Corpses trait.
sections.Bonus actions:
The flower can choose one of the following options while it contains at least one humanoid corpse.
Digest. Consume a stored corpse to regain 11 (2d10) hit points immediately. The body is destroyed and its equipment drops into the flower's space.
Animate. Turn a stored corpse into a Zombie in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. The zombie acts directly after the flower in initiative and allies with it. The flower has no control over the zombie, which carries the flower's Stench of Death.
sections.Field notes: After the flower dies, the smell of decay fades over 2d4 days.

name: Deathlock
description: A warlock who broke a pact and rose from the dead to finish its patron’s work. A powerful necromancer can bind a deathlock as well.

sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.
sections.Traits: Turn Resistance. The Deathlock has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
sections.Undead nature: The Deathlock does not need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
The Deathlock uses Charisma (save DC 13) for its innate spells. It needs no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Mage Armor.
sections.Spellcasting:
A 5th-level warlock spellcaster using Charisma (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). It regains spent slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips (at will). Chill Touch, Eldritch Blast, Mage Hand.
1st through 3rd level (two 3rd-level slots). Arms of Hadar, Dispel Magic, Hold Person, Hunger of Hadar, Invisibility, Spider Climb.
sections.Actions: Deathly Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) necrotic damage.
sections.Patron-specific spells:
The sidebar offers patron lists for replacing some or all of the leveled warlock spells. Keep the base spell slots and cantrips.
Archfey patron. Blink, Faerie Fire, Hunger of Hadar, Hypnotic Pattern, Phantasmal Force, Sleep.
Fiend patron. Blindness/Deafness, Burning Hands, Command, Fireball, Hellish Rebuke, Scorching Ray.
Great Old One patron. Armor of Agathys, Detect Thoughts, Dissonant Whispers, Hunger of Hadar, Tasha's Hideous Laughter, Phantasmal Force.

name: Deathlock Mastermind
description: A powerful Deathlock with enough freedom to plan its own tactics. It recruits servants and builds conspiracies to carry out its patron’s orders.

sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.
sections.Traits: Turn Resistance. The Deathlock has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
sections.Undead nature: The Deathlock does not need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
The Deathlock uses Charisma (save DC 14) for its innate spells. It needs no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Mage Armor.
sections.Spellcasting:
A 10th-level warlock spellcaster using Charisma (save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). It regains spent slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips (at will). Chill Touch, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Poison Spray.
1st through 5th level (two 5th-level slots). Arms of Hadar, Blight, Counterspell, Crown of Madness, Darkness, Dimension Door, Dispel Magic, Fly, Hold Monster, Invisibility.
sections.Actions:
Deathly Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (3d6 + 3) necrotic damage.
Grave Bolts. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one or two targets. A hit deals 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. A target of Large size or smaller must pass a DC 16 Strength save or be restrained by shadowy tendrils for 1 minute. A restrained target can use its action to repeat the save and end the effect on a success.

name: Deathlock Wight
description: An undead warlock stripped of much of its magic as punishment by a patron or necromancer.

sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits: Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the wight has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
sections.Undead nature: The Deathlock does not need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
The wight uses Charisma (save DC 13) for its innate spells. It needs neither verbal nor material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Mage Armor.
1/day each. Fear, Hold Person, Misty Step.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Grave Bolt attacks.
Grave Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) necrotic damage.
Life Drain. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) necrotic damage. On a failed DC 13 Constitution save, reduce the target’s hit point maximum by the damage taken until it finishes a long rest. The target dies if this drops its maximum to 0. A Humanoid slain by this attack rises 24 hours later as a Zombie under the wight’s control unless the Humanoid is revived or its body is destroyed. The wight can control up to twelve Zombies this way.

name: Demogorgon
description: The Prince of Demons is a two-headed lord of the Abyss. The rival heads Aameul and Hathradiah share an apelike torso, a reptilian lower body and tentacles.

sections.Damage immunities: Poison. Nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Demogorgon uses Charisma (save DC 23) and needs no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Major Image.
3/day each. Dispel Magic, Fear, Telekinesis.
1/day each. Feeblemind, Project Image.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). When Demogorgon fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. Demogorgon has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Demogorgon’s weapon attacks count as magical.
Two Heads. Demogorgon has advantage on saving throws to avoid being blinded, deafened, stunned or knocked unconscious.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (3d12 + 9) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it makes a DC 23 Constitution save. On a failure, reduce its hit point maximum by the damage taken until it finishes a long rest. It dies if this drops its maximum to 0.
Gaze. Choose one creature Demogorgon can see within 120 ft. It makes a DC 23 Wisdom save against his magical gaze. A target that is not incapacitated can avert its eyes and pass the save automatically. It then cannot see Demogorgon until the start of his next turn. If it looks at him before then, it must immediately make the save. On a failed save, Demogorgon chooses one of the three effects or determines it at random.
Beguiling Gaze. The target is stunned until the start of Demogorgon’s next turn or until he is out of its line of sight.
Hypnotic Gaze. The target is charmed until the start of Demogorgon’s next turn. He chooses how it spends its actions, reactions and movement. Both heads are occupied, so Demogorgon cannot use Maddening Gaze until the start of his next turn.
Insanity Gaze. Apply Confusion without an extra save or concentration until the start of Demogorgon’s next turn.
sections.Legendary actions:
Demogorgon has two legendary actions and regains spent uses at the start of his turn. He can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn. Each option costs one use.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage plus 11 (2d10) necrotic damage.
Maddening Gaze. Use Gaze with either the Beguiling or Insanity effect.
sections.Lair actions:
At initiative count 20, losing ties, Demogorgon may use either option. He cannot repeat the same option in consecutive rounds.
Illusory duplicate. An illusion of Demogorgon appears in his space and lasts until initiative count 20 of the next round. On his turn, he can move the duplicate up to his walking speed without using an action. The first time a creature or object physically interacts with him, there is a 50% chance it affects the duplicate. The duplicate vanishes if affected.
Darkness. Cast Darkness at its lowest level in four different areas without concentration. All four effects end on initiative count 20 of the next round.
sections.Regional effects:
The following effects can occur around Abysm, his palace in the Gaping Maw.
Venomous beasts. Lizards, venomous snakes and other venomous beasts overpopulate the area within 6 miles.
Violent beasts. Within 1 mile, beasts grow violent even if normally docile.
Madness. After at least an hour within 1 mile, a Humanoid makes a DC 23 Wisdom save. On a failure, roll on Madness of Demogorgon. A success makes the creature immune to this regional effect for 24 hours.
The effects fade over 1d10 days if Demogorgon dies.
sections.Madness of Demogorgon:
When a creature goes mad in Demogorgon’s lair or within sight of him, roll d100. The flaw lasts until cured.
01–20. The creature believes someone plans to kill it and must be attacked first.
21–40. The creature believes killing everyone involved will solve its problems.
41–60. The creature believes it shares its head with another mind.
61–80. The creature tries to force anyone who disagrees to submit through violence.
81–00. The creature fears theft and refuses to let others touch its belongings.

name: Deathlock Mastermind (Fiend Patron)
description: A powerful Deathlock with enough freedom to plan its own tactics. It recruits servants and builds conspiracies to carry out its patron’s orders.

sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.
sections.Traits: Turn Resistance. The Deathlock has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
sections.Undead nature: The Deathlock does not need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
The Deathlock uses Charisma (save DC 14) for its innate spells. It needs no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Mage Armor.
sections.Spellcasting:
A 10th-level warlock spellcaster using Charisma (save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). It regains spent slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips (at will). Chill Touch, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Poison Spray.
1st through 5th level (two 5th-level slots). Blindness/Deafness, Burning Hands, Command, Fire Shield, Fireball, Flame Strike, Hellish Rebuke, Scorching Ray, Stinking Cloud, Wall of Fire.
sections.Actions:
Deathly Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (3d6 + 3) necrotic damage.
Grave Bolts. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one or two targets. A hit deals 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. A Large or smaller target hit by a bolt must pass a DC 16 Strength save or be restrained by shadowy tendrils for 1 minute. A restrained target can use its action to repeat the save and end the effect on a success.
sections.Patron-specific spells: This profile uses the full example list for its patron. The sidebar also lets a DM replace only some of the leveled warlock spells. Keep the original cantrips, innate spells, and spell slots.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes, pp. 128–129, Deathlock Mastermind and Patron-Specific Spells sidebar.

name: Demonic Cambion (Baphomet)
description: A winged champion of Baphomet who singles out an enemy so an ally can strike.

sections.Armor: Scale mail. The listed AC includes Fiendish Blessing.
sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning, and poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Fiendish Blessing. Add its Charisma bonus to AC.
Horned One's Call. If both attacks from the cambion’s Multiattack target the same creature, the cambion can choose a visible ally within 30 ft. That ally can spend its reaction to make one melee attack against a target it chooses.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma is its spellcasting ability (save DC 14). It casts these spells without material components.
3/day each. Alter Self, Command, Detect Magic.
1/day. Plane Shift (self only).
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks or use Fire Ray twice.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage for a two-handed melee hit. Add 3 (1d6) fire damage to either.
Fire Ray. Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit 10 (3d6) fire damage.
sections.Optional signature spells: As an option, replace Command or Detect Magic with Hunter's Mark. It can also replace Alter Self with Beast Sense. Each replacement spell is usable once per day. Slow is also a 3rd-level signature spell, but the standard cambion has no 3rd-level spell to exchange for it.
sections.Optional demonic boon:
Baphomet’s boon can grant these traits.
Unerring Tracker. As a bonus action, the cambion magically links to a visible creature. For up to 1 hour, it can spend a bonus action to learn the target’s distance and direction if they are on the same plane. The link ends if the cambion becomes incapacitated or links to another target.
Incite the Hunters (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). As an action, the cambion lets each ally within 30 ft. that has Unerring Tracker spend its reaction to make one weapon attack against the creature that ally is tracking.
Labyrinthine Recall. The cambion recalls any route it has traveled.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes, p. 32, Demonic Cambions, with optional boons on pp. 30–31. Base statistics and resistance errata follow the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 36.

name: Demonic Cambion (Orcus)
description: A winged champion of Orcus who raises corpses and bolsters nearby undead as it fights.

sections.Armor: Scale mail. The listed AC includes Fiendish Blessing.
sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning, and poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Fiendish Blessing. Add its Charisma bonus to AC.
Spawn of the Grave. At the end of each of the cambion’s turns, if it is not incapacitated, choose any number of undead it can see within 30 ft. Each gains 10 temporary hit points.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma is its spellcasting ability (save DC 14). It casts these spells without material components.
3/day each. Alter Self, Animate Dead, Command, Detect Magic.
1/day. Plane Shift (self only).
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks or use Fire Ray twice.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage for a two-handed melee hit. Add 3 (1d6) fire damage to either.
Fire Ray. Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit 10 (3d6) fire damage.
sections.Optional signature spells: As an option, replace Command or Detect Magic with False Life. It can also replace Alter Self with Ray of Enfeeblement. Each replacement spell is usable once per day. Animate Dead is already included above through Spawn of the Grave.
sections.Optional demonic boon:
Orcus’s boon can grant these traits.
Undying Soul (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). When reduced to 0 hit points, the cambion immediately makes a DC 10 Constitution save. On a success, it drops to 1 hit point instead.
Aura of Death. While the cambion is not incapacitated, it projects an aura out to 30 ft. from its space. Total cover blocks it. Within the aura, the cambion and friendly undead are immune to being frightened and resist radiant damage. Enemies within the aura have disadvantage on death saving throws.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes, p. 32, Demonic Cambions, with optional boons on pp. 30–31. Base statistics and resistance errata follow the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 36.

name: Derro
description: Bands of derro shelter in the Underdark. They prey on weaker travelers, back down before stronger foes, and look to their sorcerous savants for leadership.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The derro makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the derro has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks made using sight.
sections.Actions:
Hooked Spear. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) piercing damage. On a hit against a Medium or smaller creature, the derro can knock it prone instead of dealing damage.
Light Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Roleplaying: The Derro Savant profile includes an optional d20 table for roleplaying any derro.

name: Derro Savant
description: Derro revere their sorcerers as leaders blessed by Diirinka. A savant can turn rival bands against a common foe by claiming to carry a message from that god.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The savant makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the savant has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks made using sight.
sections.Spellcasting:
The savant casts as a 5th-level sorcerer using Charisma (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips (at will). Acid Splash, Mage Hand, Message, Prestidigitation, Ray of Frost.
1st level (4 slots). Burning Hands, Chromatic Orb, Sleep.
2nd level (3 slots). Invisibility, Spider Climb.
3rd level (2 slots). Lightning Bolt.
sections.Actions: Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack, +1 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 2 (1d6 - 1) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Roleplaying:
Roll a d20 one or more times to give any derro an optional mannerism.
1. Avoids washing or fresh clothes.
2. Fidgets with their hair or mustache.
3. Talks to an absent companion.
4. Walks backward when they can.
5. Avoids eye contact.
6. Grinds their teeth between sentences.
7. Spits out part of every bite and sip.
8. Opens conversations with an insult.
9. Puts a hand on anyone they talk to.
10. Sees spirits rise from the newly dead.
11. Passes out at their first exposure to bright light.
12. Licks their palms repeatedly.
13. Hears voices.
14. Fears the sight of written words.
15. Tastes whatever they pick up.
16. Crowds people when they speak.
17. Breathes noisily.
18. Drools all the time.
19. Speaks under their breath.
20. Gets around by hopping.

name: Dhergoloth
description: A squat yugoloth with five pairs of claws, the dhergoloth takes contracts to disperse crowds, put down revolts, or hunt scouts. It follows simple orders and tends to forget the rest.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The dhergoloth makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks count as magical.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
The dhergoloth casts using Charisma (spell save DC 10) without material components.
At will. Darkness, Fear.
3/day. Sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d8 + 3) slashing damage.
Flailing Claws (Recharge 5–6). Move in a straight line up to the dhergoloth’s walking speed. Each creature within 5 ft. of it at any point during this move makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 22 (3d12 + 3) slashing damage.
Teleport. The dhergoloth magically teleports up to 60 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space, bringing its worn and carried gear.

name: Dire Troll
description: A dire troll grows by feeding on other trolls and grafting stolen flesh onto its wounds. Its regeneration can incorporate extra eyes and arms, leaving it with more claws than its prey can fend off.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Keen Senses. The troll makes Wisdom (Perception) checks using smell or sight with advantage.
Regeneration. The troll regains 10 HP at the start of its turn. If it takes acid or fire damage, it regains 5 HP at the start of its next turn instead. It dies only if an attack deals at least 10 acid or fire damage to it while it has 0 HP.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and four Claws attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d8 + 6) piercing damage plus 5 (1d10) poison damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (3d6 + 6) slashing damage.
Whirlwind of Claws (Recharge 5–6). Each creature within 10 ft. of the troll makes a DC 19 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 44 (8d10) slashing damage. On a success, it takes half as much.

name: Drow Arachnomancer
description: A devotee of Lolth who draws on the spiders of the Demonweb Pits and can take the shape of a giant spider.

sections.Languages: Elvish, Undercommon, can speak with spiders
sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saves against being charmed and is immune to magical sleep.
Spider Climb. The drow crosses difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
Web Walker. Webbing does not impede the drow’s movement.
sections.Bonus actions: Change Shape (recharges after a short or long rest). The drow magically becomes a Giant Spider for up to 1 hour. Its size changes, but the rest of its statistics stay the same. The spider can speak and cast spells. Worn and carried equipment melds into the spider, which cannot use it or gain its benefits. Another bonus action returns the drow to humanoid form early. It also returns to humanoid form when it dies.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make either two Poisonous Touch attacks or two Bite attacks. The first of those attacks to hit each round deals an additional 26 (4d12) poison damage.
Poisonous Touch (humanoid form only). Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (8d6) poison damage.
Bite (Giant Spider form only). Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage. The target must make a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 26 (4d12) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. If that poison damage drops the target to 0 hit points, it is stable and poisoned for 1 hour, even if it regains hit points. It is paralyzed while poisoned by this bite.
Web (Giant Spider form only, recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one target. A hit restrains the target in webbing. It can use an action to break free with a DC 15 Strength check. The webbing has AC 10 and 5 hit points, is vulnerable to fire, and is immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma sets the innate spell save DC at 16. The spells require no material components.
At will. Dancing Lights.
1/day each. Darkness, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only).
sections.Spellcasting:
The drow casts as a 16th-level warlock using Charisma (spell save DC 16, +8 to hit with spell attacks). It regains spent spell slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips (at will). Chill Touch, Eldritch Blast, Mage Hand, Poison Spray.
1st–5th level (three 5th-level slots). Conjure Animals (spiders only), Crown of Madness, Dimension Door, Dispel Magic, Fear, Fly, Giant Insect, Hold Monster, Insect Plague, Invisibility, Vampiric Touch, Web, Witch Bolt.
1/day each. Dominate Monster, Etherealness, Eyebite.

name: Drow Favored Consort
description: A battle mage who pairs poisonous swordplay with wizard spells and advises a priestess of Lolth.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saves against being charmed and is immune to magical sleep.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
sections.Bonus actions: War Magic. After the drow uses its action to cast a spell, it can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Scimitar attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) slashing damage and 18 (4d8) poison damage. The target has disadvantage on its next save against a spell the drow casts before the end of the drow’s next turn.
Hand Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +11 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage. The target must make a DC 13 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 hour. Failure by 5 or more also leaves the target unconscious while this poison lasts. Damage wakes it, as does another creature using an action to shake it awake.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma sets the innate spell save DC at 18. The spells require no material components.
At will. Dancing Lights.
1/day each. Darkness, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only).
sections.Spellcasting:
The drow casts as an 11th-level wizard using Intelligence (spell save DC 18, +10 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips (at will). Mage Hand, Message, Poison Spray, Shocking Grasp, Ray of Frost.
1st level (4 slots). Burning Hands, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Shield.
2nd level (3 slots). Gust of Wind, Invisibility, Misty Step, Shatter.
3rd level (3 slots). Counterspell, Fireball, Haste.
4th level (3 slots). Dimension Door, Otiluke’s Resilient Sphere.
5th level (2 slots). Cone of Cold.
6th level (1 slot). Chain Lightning.

name: Drow House Captain
description: A noble house’s battlefield commander who directs nearby allies while fighting with scimitar, whip, and hand crossbow.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saves against being charmed and is immune to magical sleep.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
sections.Bonus actions: Battle Command. Choose one ally the captain can see within 30 ft. If the ally sees or hears the captain, the ally can spend its reaction to make one melee attack or take the Dodge or Hide action.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks and either one Whip or one Hand Crossbow attack.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage and 14 (4d6) poison damage.
Whip. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d4 + 4) slashing damage. If it hits an ally, that ally has advantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.
Hand Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage. The target must make a DC 13 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 hour. Failure by 5 or more also leaves the target unconscious while this poison lasts. Damage wakes it, as does another creature using an action to shake it awake.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack would hit the captain, add 3 to the captain’s AC against that attack. The captain must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma sets the innate spell save DC at 13. The spells require no material components.
At will. Dancing Lights.
1/day each. Darkness, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only).

name: Drow Inquisitor
description: A priestess empowered to investigate threats to the drow hierarchy. Her death lance withers those it wounds.

sections.Traits:
Discern Lie. When the drow hears someone lie in a language it understands, it recognizes the lie.
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saves against being charmed and is immune to magical sleep.
Magic Resistance. The drow makes saving throws against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Death Lance attacks.
Death Lance. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage and 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. Reduce the target’s hit point maximum by the necrotic damage it takes. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. A target whose maximum reaches 0 dies.
sections.Variant rules: Summon Demon (1/day). Some drow of this kind can attempt to summon a Yochlol as an action. The magical summon has a 50% chance to work. Failure deals 5 (1d10) psychic damage to the drow. On success, the demon appears in an unoccupied space within 60 ft. of the drow. It acts as the drow’s ally and cannot summon other demons. It departs after 10 minutes, if it or the drow dies, or if the drow uses an action to dismiss it.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes, p. 184. Yochlol Summoning variant, p. 185.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma sets the innate spell save DC at 18. The spells require no material components.
At will. Dancing Lights, Detect Magic.
1/day each. Clairvoyance, Darkness, Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only), Suggestion.
sections.Spellcasting:
The drow casts as a 12th-level cleric using Wisdom (spell save DC 18, +10 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips (at will). Guidance, Message, Poison Spray, Resistance, Thaumaturgy.
1st level (4 slots). Bane, Cure Wounds, Inflict Wounds.
2nd level (3 slots). Blindness/Deafness, Silence, Spiritual Weapon.
3rd level (3 slots). Bestow Curse, Dispel Magic, Magic Circle.
4th level (3 slots). Banishment, Divination, Freedom of Movement.
5th level (2 slots). Contagion, Dispel Evil and Good, Insect Plague.
6th level (1 slot). Harm, True Seeing.

ruleNotes: The stat block prints Strength 11 with a +1 modifier. The standard modifier for Strength 11 is +0, which the ability display uses.

name: Drow Matron Mother
description: The ruling priestess of a drow noble house, backed by high cleric magic, summoned servants, and Lolth’s uncertain favor.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saves against being charmed and is immune to magical sleep.
Magic Resistance. The drow makes saving throws against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
sections.Bonus actions: Lolth’s Fickle Favor. Choose one ally the matron can see within 30 ft. The ally takes 7 (2d6) psychic damage and gains advantage on the next attack roll it makes by the end of its next turn.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make either two Demon Staff attacks or three Tentacle Rod attacks.
Demon Staff. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) with two hands, and 14 (4d6) psychic damage. The target must pass a DC 19 Wisdom save or be frightened of the matron for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Tentacle Rod. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage. If the rod hits a target three times during one turn, that target must pass a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, its speed is halved, it has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws, and it cannot take reactions for 1 minute. On each of its turns during that time, it can take only one action or one bonus action. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Summon Servant (1/day). Magically summon a Retriever or a Yochlol in an unoccupied space within 60 ft. The servant acts as the matron’s ally and cannot summon other demons. It departs after 10 minutes, if it or the matron dies, or if the matron dismisses it as an action.
sections.Legendary actions:
The matron has 3 legendary actions and regains all spent actions at the start of her turn. She can choose one option at the end of another creature’s turn. She cannot use these actions if incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, she can use them after completing her first turn.
Demon Staff (1 action). Make one Demon Staff attack.
Compel Demon (2 actions). One allied demon within 30 ft. spends its reaction to make one attack against a target the matron chooses and can see.
Cast a Spell (1–3 actions). Expend a spell slot to cast a prepared 1st-, 2nd-, or 3rd-level spell. The cost is one legendary action per level of the spell.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma sets the innate spell save DC at 20. The spells require no material components.
At will. Dancing Lights, Detect Magic.
1/day each. Clairvoyance, Darkness, Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only), Suggestion.
sections.Spellcasting:
The drow casts as a 20th-level cleric using Wisdom (spell save DC 19, +11 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips (at will). Guidance, Mending, Resistance, Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy.
1st level (4 slots). Bane, Command, Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt.
2nd level (3 slots). Hold Person, Silence, Spiritual Weapon.
3rd level (3 slots). Bestow Curse, Clairvoyance, Dispel Magic, Spirit Guardians.
4th level (3 slots). Banishment, Death Ward, Freedom of Movement, Guardian of Faith.
5th level (3 slots). Contagion, Flame Strike, Geas, Mass Cure Wounds.
6th level (2 slots). Blade Barrier, Harm.
7th level (2 slots). Divine Word, Plane Shift.
8th level (1 slot). Holy Aura.
9th level (1 slot). Gate.

name: Drow Shadowblade
description: An assassin who teleports between shadows and stores magical darkness in the spaces around a fight.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saves against being charmed and is immune to magical sleep.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
sections.Bonus actions: Shadow Step. While in dim light or darkness, teleport up to 60 ft. to an unoccupied space the drow can see in dim light or darkness. The drow has advantage on the first melee attack it makes before the turn ends.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shadow Sword attacks. Once per turn, if either hits a target within 10 ft. of a cube of darkness the sword created on an earlier turn, the drow can dismiss the cube to deal an additional 21 (6d6) necrotic damage to the target.
Shadow Sword. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage, 10 (3d6) necrotic damage, and 10 (3d6) poison damage. The drow can then fill an unoccupied 5-foot cube within 5 ft. of the target with magical darkness for 1 minute.
Hand Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage. The target must make a DC 13 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 hour. Failure by 5 or more also leaves the target unconscious while this poison lasts. Damage wakes it, as does another creature using an action to shake it awake.
sections.Variant rules: Summon Shadow Demon (1/day). Some drow of this kind can attempt to summon a Shadow Demon as an action. The magical summon has a 50% chance to work. Failure deals 5 (1d10) psychic damage to the drow. On success, the demon appears in an unoccupied space within 60 ft. of the drow. It acts as the drow’s ally and cannot summon other demons. It departs after 10 minutes, if it or the drow dies, or if the drow uses an action to dismiss it.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma sets the innate spell save DC at 13. The spells require no material components.
At will. Dancing Lights.
1/day each. Darkness, Faerie Fire, Levitate (self only).
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes, p. 187. Shadow Demon Summoning variant is on the same page.

name: Duergar Despot
description: A despot controls its mechanical limbs with psionics and can swap its crushing attacks for long jets of flame.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The despot has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Psychic Engine. A critical hit against the despot or a drop to 0 hit points triggers a burst. Each creature within 5 ft. takes 14 (4d6) psychic damage.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
The despot's psionics use Intelligence (spell save DC 12) and require no components.
At will. Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
1/day each. Counterspell, Misty Step, Stinking Cloud.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Iron Fist attacks and two Stomping Foot attacks. Any or all four attacks can be replaced with Flame Jet.
Iron Fist. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must also pass a DC 17 Strength save. On a failure, the despot throws it up to 30 ft. away in a straight line. It lands prone and takes another 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage.
Stomping Foot. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 9 (1d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage, or 18 (3d8 + 5) if the target is prone.
Flame Jet. Each creature in a 100-ft. line 5 ft. wide makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. It takes 18 (4d8) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.

name: Duergar Hammerer
description: A captive duergar powers this digging machine through pain. Duergar put hammerers to work tunneling and defending their strongholds.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Engine of Pain. An attacker can aim at the duergar inside the hammerer once per turn, rolling with disadvantage. A hit deals an extra 5 (1d10) damage to the hammerer, which can use its reaction to make its Multiattack.
Siege Monster. The hammerer doubles its damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claw attack and one Hammer attack.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Hammer. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

name: Duergar Kavalrachni
description: Duergar cavalry ride female steeders into battle. The rider can conceal both of them and create openings for the mount to strike.

sections.Traits:
Cavalry Training. When the rider hits with a melee attack while mounted on a female steeder, the steeder can use its reaction to make one melee attack against that target.
Duergar Resilience. The duergar makes saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions with advantage. It also has advantage on saves to resist being charmed or paralyzed.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two War Pick attacks.
War Pick. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 5 (2d4) poison damage.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +2 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d10) piercing damage.
Shared Invisibility (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. The effect ends if the duergar attacks, casts a spell, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell. A female steeder the invisible duergar is riding is also invisible. The steeder's invisibility ends immediately if it attacks.

name: Duergar Mind Master
description: A psionic spy who sees through illusions and shrinks to slip into places a full-size intruder could never reach.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar makes saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions with advantage. It also has advantage on saves to resist being charmed or paralyzed.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks. Mind Mastery can replace one of them.
Mind-Poison Dagger. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) psychic damage. While reduced, a hit instead deals 1 piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) psychic damage.
Invisibility (Recharge 4–6). The duergar and its gear become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. The effect ends if the duergar attacks, casts a spell, uses Reduce, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.
Mind Mastery. Choose a creature the duergar can see within 60 ft. A creature that can't be charmed is immune. On a failed DC 12 Intelligence save, the target must use its reaction to make one weapon attack against another creature the duergar can see, or move up to 10 ft. in a direction the duergar chooses. The duergar picks the option.
Reduce (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear shrink for 1 minute. It becomes Tiny and deals 1 weapon damage, with the dagger's reduced damage listed above. It has disadvantage on attacks, checks, and saves that use Strength. Its AC increases by 5 to 19, and its Dexterity (Stealth) checks gain a +5 bonus. It can take the Hide action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

name: Duergar Screamer
description: This rock-grinding construct turns the pain of a captive duergar into a destructive burst of sound.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Traits: Engine of Pain. An attacker can aim at the duergar inside the screamer once per turn, rolling with disadvantage. A hit deals an extra 11 (2d10) damage to the screamer, which can use its reaction to make its Multiattack.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Drill attack and use Sonic Scream.
Drill. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d12 + 4) piercing damage.
Sonic Scream. Each creature in a 15-ft. cube makes a DC 11 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 7 (2d6) thunder damage and falls prone.

name: Duergar Soulblade
description: This warrior forms a blade of psionic energy in its hand and strikes hardest when it has an opening.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar makes saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions with advantage. It also has advantage on saves to resist being charmed or paralyzed.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
The duergar's psionics use Wisdom (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks) and require no components.
At will. Blade Ward, True Strike.
3/day each. Jump, Hunter's Mark.
sections.Bonus actions: Create Soulblade. A visible, shortsword-sized psionic blade forms in the duergar's hand. It vanishes if the duergar releases it, dies, or becomes incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Soulblade. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) force damage, or 10 (2d6 + 3) while enlarged. Add 3 (1d6) force damage on a hit if the duergar had advantage on the attack roll.
Enlarge (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear grow for 1 minute. It becomes Large, or as large as the available space permits. While enlarged, it has advantage on Strength checks and saves and doubles the damage dice of Strength-based weapon attacks. The enlarged attack formulas already include the extra dice.
Invisibility (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. The effect ends if the duergar attacks, casts a spell, uses Enlarge, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.

name: Duergar Stone Guard
description: Elite duergar troops fight in shield formations and assemble into small strike teams for specific missions.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar makes saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions with advantage. It also has advantage on saves to resist being charmed or paralyzed.
Phalanx Formation. While standing within 5 ft. of a duergar ally who wields a shield, the stone guard has advantage on attack rolls and Dexterity saves.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Actions:
King's Knife (Shortsword). Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 11 (2d6 + 4) while enlarged.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 11 (2d6 + 4) while enlarged.
Enlarge (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear grow for 1 minute. It becomes Large, or as large as the available space permits. While enlarged, it has advantage on Strength checks and saves and doubles the damage dice of Strength-based weapon attacks. The enlarged attack formulas already include the extra dice.
Invisibility (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. The effect ends if the duergar attacks, casts a spell, uses Enlarge, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.

name: Duergar Warlord
description: A duergar commander whose orders send allies into action and whose psionic reprimands can turn a poor roll around.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar makes saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions with advantage. It also has advantage on saves to resist being charmed or paralyzed.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using Psychic-Attuned Hammer or Javelin. Also use Call to Attack, or Enlarge if it is available.
Psychic-Attuned Hammer. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 5 (1d10) psychic damage. While enlarged, the bludgeoning damage becomes 15 (2d10 + 4) and the psychic damage stays the same.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 11 (2d6 + 4) while enlarged.
Call to Attack. Choose up to three allied duergar within 120 ft. who can hear the warlord. Each can use its reaction to make one weapon attack.
Enlarge (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear grow for 1 minute. It becomes Large, or as large as the available space permits. While enlarged, it has advantage on Strength checks and saves and doubles the damage dice of Strength-based weapon attacks. The enlarged attack formulas already include the extra dice.
Invisibility (Recharge 4–6). The duergar and its gear become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. The effect ends if the duergar attacks, casts a spell, uses Enlarge, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.
sections.Reactions: Scouring Instruction. When a visible ally makes a d20 roll, the warlord can roll a d6. The ally can add the result to its d20 roll by taking 3 (1d6) psychic damage. Immunity to psychic damage prevents this effect.

name: Duergar Xarrorn
description: The xarrorn uses alchemy and psionics to build weapons. Its fire lance can reach past the front rank and spray fire across a formation.

sections.Traits:
Duergar Resilience. The duergar makes saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions with advantage. It also has advantage on saves to resist being charmed or paralyzed.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
sections.Actions:
Fire Lance. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Roll with disadvantage if the target is within 5 ft. A hit deals 9 (1d12 + 3) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage. While enlarged, the piercing damage becomes 16 (2d12 + 3) and the fire damage stays the same.
Fire Spray (Recharge 5–6). Choose a 15-ft. cone or a 30-ft. line 5 ft. wide. Each creature in that area makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. It takes 10 (3d6) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.
Enlarge (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear grow for 1 minute. It becomes Large, or as large as the available space permits. While enlarged, it has advantage on Strength checks and saves and doubles the damage dice of Strength-based weapon attacks. The enlarged attack formulas already include the extra dice.
Invisibility (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The duergar and its gear become magically invisible for up to 1 hour. The effect ends if the duergar attacks, casts a spell, uses Enlarge, or loses concentration as if concentrating on a spell.

name: Dybbuk
description: This translucent, jellyfish-like demon can pass as the person whose body it inhabits. Its behavior usually gives it away.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone and restrained.
sections.Traits:
Incorporeal Movement. Move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. Ending its turn inside an object deals 5 (1d10) force damage to the dybbuk.
Magic Resistance. The dybbuk has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma sets the save DC at 12. The dybbuk needs no material components.
At will. Dimension Door.
3/day each. Fear, Phantasmal Force.
sections.Bonus actions:
Violate Corpse. While possessing a body, the dybbuk can make it behave in an unnatural way. A beast or humanoid that sees this must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom save or become frightened of the dybbuk for 1 minute. An affected creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect on a success. A successful save against Violate Corpse grants immunity to it for 24 hours.
End Possession. The dybbuk can leave the body as a bonus action. It appears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the corpse.
sections.Actions:
Tendril. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) necrotic damage. A creature hit also loses 3 (1d6) from its hit point maximum until it finishes a short or long rest. If this reduces its maximum to 0, it dies.
Possess Corpse (Recharge 6). Enter a visible, intact corpse within 5 ft. It must be the body of a Large or smaller beast or humanoid. The dybbuk becomes undead and looks alive. It gains temporary hit points equal to the body’s hit point maximum in life. The dybbuk retains its own hit points, alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, telepathy and immunity to poison damage, exhaustion, charmed and frightened. It uses the corpse’s other game statistics and gains its knowledge and proficiencies. Its class features are unavailable. The body becomes a corpse again when the temporary hit points run out or the dybbuk leaves as a bonus action. The dybbuk then appears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the corpse.

name: Earth Elemental Myrmidon
description: Magic binds an earth elemental into this suit of plate armor. It has forgotten its former life and follows its creator’s commands.

sections.Languages: Terran and one language chosen by its creator.
sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits: Magic Weapons. The myrmidon’s weapon attacks are magical.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Maul attacks.
Maul. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Thunderous Strike (Recharge 6). Make one Maul attack. A hit deals an extra 16 (3d10) thunder damage and knocks the target prone unless it succeeds on a DC 14 Strength save.

name: Eidolon
description: An oath binds this devoted spirit to a sacred site. When intruders arrive, the eidolon enters a prepared statue and uses it to fight.

sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Acid, fire, lightning, thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone and restrained.
sections.Traits:
Incorporeal Movement. Move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. Ending its turn inside an object other than a Sacred Statue deals 5 (1d10) force damage to the eidolon.
Sacred Animation (Recharge 5–6). When the eidolon enters a Sacred Statue’s space, it can disappear into the statue. The statue becomes a creature under its control. Use the Sacred Statue’s statistics instead of the eidolon’s until it leaves.
Turn Resistance. The eidolon has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
sections.Actions: Divine Dread. Every creature within 60 ft. that can see the eidolon must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom save or become frightened of it for 1 minute. At the start of each of its turns while frightened this way, the target must take the Dash action and move away by the safest available route. If it has nowhere to go, it is also stunned until it can move again. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect on a success. A successful save or the end of the effect makes the target immune to any eidolon’s Divine Dread for 24 hours.
sections.Sacred Statue: Use the Sacred Statue on the same page. This printing’s Multiattack makes two Slam attacks. While motionless the statue looks like an ordinary statue. It is an object when unoccupied.
