While poisoned this way, the target is blinded and deafened. At the end of each of its turns, the target can attempt a DC 26 Constitution save to end the effect. The DC and ability for this repeat save are a table ruling.
Teleport. Zariel and her worn or carried equipment magically move up to 120 ft. to an unoccupied space she can see.
sections.Legendary actions:
Zariel has 3 legendary actions. She can use one option at the end of another creature's turn and recovers all spent actions at the start of her turn.
Immolating Gaze (2 actions). One creature Zariel can see within 120 ft. makes a DC 26 Wisdom save. On a failure, it takes 22 (4d10) fire damage.
Teleport (1 action). Use Teleport.
sections.Lair actions:
On initiative count 20, losing initiative ties, choose one option. Zariel cannot repeat the same option in consecutive rounds.
Illusions. Cast Major Image four times at its lowest level in different areas. Zariel need not concentrate and the images disappear at initiative count 20 of the next round. Each creature that sees the illusions makes a DC 26 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is frightened of the illusion for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the fear on a success.
Fireball. Cast her innate Fireball.
sections.Regional effects:
Choose one or more effects around the lair.
Screams and the smell of burning meat fill the area within 9 miles.
Within 1 mile, a 10-ft.-high burst of flame rises every 60 ft. Touching a flame deals 7 (2d6) fire damage to a creature or object, at most once per round.
Smoke heavily obscures the area from 500 ft. to 2 miles from the lair. The smoke cannot be dispersed.
The effects fade over 1d10 days after Zariel dies.
sections.Source notes: Page 180 gives Horrid Touch an attack roll and allows a repeat saving throw, but leaves out the save's ability and DC. name: Zuggtmoy
description: The Demon Queen of Fungi reshapes living creatures into fungal servants. Her palace on Shedaklah is built from enormous mushrooms.

sections.Damage immunities: Poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical sources.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Zuggtmoy uses Charisma (spell save DC 22) and needs no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Locate Animals or Plants, Ray of Sickness.
3/day each. Dispel Magic, Ensnaring Strike, Entangle, Plant Growth.
1/day each. Etherealness, Teleport.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Zuggtmoy can choose to succeed on a failed saving throw.
Magic Resistance. She has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Pseudopod attacks.
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.
Infestation Spores (3/day). A spore cloud fills a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered on Zuggtmoy and lasts 1 minute. Each flesh-and-blood creature inside when it appears or that enters it later makes a DC 19 Constitution save. A success grants immunity to infection by these spores for 24 hours. On a failure, the target contracts the spores of Zuggtmoy, rolls on her madness table, and cannot be reinfected while the disease lasts. The madness lasts until the target is cured or dies. The target repeats the save after every 24 hours. A success ends the infection. Each failed repeat save advances the fungal takeover. After three failed repeat saves, the target dies and reanimates as a spore servant if eligible under the Monster Manual's Myconids entry.
Mind Control Spores (Recharge 5–6). A spore cloud fills a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered on Zuggtmoy and lasts 1 minute. Each humanoid or beast inside when it appears or that enters it later makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. A success grants immunity to infection by these spores for 24 hours. On a failure the target contracts the influence of Zuggtmoy for 24 hours. While infected, it is charmed by her and cannot be reinfected by the same spores.
sections.Reactions: Protective Thrall. When an attack hits Zuggtmoy, one creature she has charmed within 5 ft. of her must use its reaction to take the hit in her place.
sections.Legendary actions:
Zuggtmoy has 3 legendary actions. She can use one option at the end of another creature's turn and recovers all spent actions at the start of her turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Pseudopod attack.
Exert Will (1 action). One creature charmed by Zuggtmoy that she can see must use its reaction to move up to its speed as she directs or make one weapon attack against a target she picks.
sections.Lair actions:
On initiative count 20, losing initiative ties, choose one option. Zuggtmoy cannot repeat the same option in consecutive rounds.
Spawn Fungi. Four gas spores or violet fungi appear in unoccupied spaces she chooses within the lair and vanish after 1 hour.
Command Plants. Up to four friendly plant creatures Zuggtmoy can see can use their reactions to move up to their speed and make one weapon attack each.
Fungal Source. Use Infestation Spores or Mind Control Spores, centered on a mushroom or other fungus within the lair.
sections.Regional effects:
Choose one or more effects around the lair.
Mold and fungi take hold on surfaces within 6 miles, even if the surface would normally resist their growth.
Parasitic fungi infest and gradually deform plants within 1 mile.
A humanoid that spends at least 1 hour within 1 mile makes a DC 17 Wisdom save. On a failure it rolls on the Madness of Zuggtmoy table. A success grants 24 hours of immunity to this effect.
The effects fade over 1d10 days after Zuggtmoy dies.
sections.Madness of Zuggtmoy:
Roll d100 when a creature goes mad in the lair or in Zuggtmoy's line of sight. The resulting flaw lasts until cured, subject to the duration in Infestation Spores when applicable.
01–20. Sees visions nobody else can see.
21–40. Periodically goes still and stares into the distance.
41–60. Believes an altered version of events even when the evidence contradicts it.
61–80. Feels their thoughts sharpen and slip away without warning.
81–100. Continually scratches at fungal infections nobody else can see.

description: The dragon patrols deep tunnels for incursions from the Far Realm and can shape its lair’s stone to control routes.

sections.Actions:

Claw. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.

1/day each. Dissonant Whispers, Hold Monster, Meld into Stone, Telekinesis, Teleport.

description: A copper dragon can become a greatwyrm by bringing together counterparts across worlds. It can breathe acid or release a cone of sapping gas.

sections.Traits:
Metallic Awakening (recharges after a short or long rest). When the creature would drop to 0 HP, set its current HP to 450, recharge Breath Weapon, and restore all spent uses of Legendary Resistance. The creature can take mythic actions for the following hour. Award 120,000 extra XP if defeated after this trait activates (240,000 XP total).
Legendary Resistance (4/day). Turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 20) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can hold only one creature with this attack at a time.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Breath Weapon (recharge 5–6). Choose Elemental Breath or Sapping Breath.
Elemental Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save, taking 84 (13d12) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sapping Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Constitution save. A failure leaves the creature unconscious for 1 minute. An unconscious creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds on the first save has disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of the greatwyrm’s next turn.
Change Shape. Magically take the form of any Medium or Small creature, retaining the greatwyrm’s statistics except size. The form ends if the greatwyrm drops to 0 HP or spends an action to end it.
sections.Legendary actions:
The creature has 3 legendary actions. It can take one option at the end of another creature’s turn and regains spent actions at the start of its turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 30 ft. must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and fall prone. The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its flying speed.
sections.Mythic actions:
For 1 hour after Metallic Awakening activates, the greatwyrm can spend legendary actions on these options.
Bite (1 action). Make one Bite attack.
Shattering Roar (2 actions). Each creature in a 120-ft.-radius sphere centered on the greatwyrm must succeed on a DC 26 Constitution save or take 19 (3d12) thunder damage and be incapacitated until the end of its next turn.
sections.Dragon customization: Customize the dragon’s languages or skills to suit its history. Skill changes can include double proficiency or tool proficiencies. Use the optional innate spellcasting guidance for the dragon’s color when adding magic. Other options on p. 34 include alternate senses and the Change Shape, Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation, and Tunneler traits or actions.
sections.Printed source: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons, pp. 208–209, copper variant of the Metallic Greatwyrm. The printed block lists Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence and Charisma saving throw bonuses. Dragon customization appears on p. 34.

name: Crystal Dragon Wyrmling
speed: 30 ft., burrow 15 ft., climb 30 ft., fly 60 ft.
description: A young gem dragon with pale scales and crystalline points. Its breath shines with energy from the Positive Plane.

sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) radiant damage.
Scintillating Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 12 Constitution save, taking 18 (4d8) radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The wyrmling then gains 5 temporary hit points.
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast Dancing Lights or Guidance at will, using Intelligence and requiring no components.
sections.Optional customization: Fizban’s customization guidance (p. 34) allows changes to languages, skill and tool proficiencies, senses, and traits. Its examples include Change Shape, Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation and Tunneler.

name: Crystal Greatwyrm
speed: 60 ft., burrow 60 ft., fly 120 ft. (hover), swim 60 ft.
description: Traces of the greatwyrm’s many lives across the Material Plane come together in a body that gleams like cut crystal.

sections.Traits:
Gem Awakening (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). When the greatwyrm would drop to 0 hit points, it instead resets to 400 hit points, recharges Breath Weapon and recovers all spent Legendary Resistance uses. It can use Mass Telekinesis for the next hour. Defeating it after Gem Awakening grants an extra 90,000 XP, or 180,000 XP total.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The greatwyrm can turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) piercing damage plus 16 (3d10) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d8 + 9) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 19) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can grapple only one creature this way at a time.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. A failure deals 71 (11d12) force damage and knocks the creature prone. A success halves the damage. The creature’s speed is 0 until the end of its next turn on either result.
Mass Telekinesis (Gem Awakening Only, Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Choose any number of visible creatures or objects within 120 ft., each weighing at most 4,000 lb. Worn or carried objects are ineligible. Each chosen creature must pass a DC 26 Strength save or be restrained in the greatwyrm’s grip. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, escaping on a success. At the end of each of the greatwyrm’s turns, it can move each target still in its grip up to 60 ft. in any direction, within 120 ft. of itself. It can also deal 45 (7d12) force damage to each restrained creature it chooses.
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast one spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 26, +18 to hit) and requiring no components. Dispel Magic, Forcecage, Plane Shift, Reverse Gravity and Time Stop are each usable once per day.
sections.Bonus actions:
Change Shape. Magically take the shape of a Small or Medium creature. Only size changes. The transformation ends when the greatwyrm drops to 0 hit points or spends a bonus action to end it.
Psychic Step. Magically teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 ft.
sections.Legendary actions:
The greatwyrm has three legendary actions and recovers spent actions at the start of its turn. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Psychic Beam (3 actions). Each creature in a 90-ft. line 10 ft. wide makes a DC 26 Intelligence save, taking 27 (5d10) psychic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Optional customization: Fizban’s customization guidance (p. 34) allows changes to languages, skill and tool proficiencies, senses, and traits. Its examples include Change Shape, Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation and Tunneler.
sections.Printed source: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons, p. 201, Gem Greatwyrm stat block, crystal variant.

name: Deep Dragon Wyrmling
speed: 30 ft., burrow 15 ft., fly 60 ft., swim 30 ft.
description: An Underdark dragon with a narrow frame that slips through tight spaces. Its breath is a cloud of nightmare-inducing spores.

sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage.
Nightmare Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. A failure deals 5 (1d10) psychic damage and leaves the creature frightened of the wyrmling for 1 minute. A success halves the damage and prevents the fright. A frightened creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
sections.Optional customization: Fizban’s customization guidance (p. 34) allows changes to languages, skill and tool proficiencies, senses, and traits. Its examples include Change Shape, Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation and Tunneler. The chapter 3 spellcasting variant is optional. This printed block has no spell actions.

name: Dracohydra
description: A winged, many-tailed hydra made in an attempt to reproduce Tiamat’s power. Its five heads feed constantly and can pour their breath into a single cone.

sections.Traits:
Multiple Heads. The dracohydra starts with five heads. While it has more than one, it has advantage on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned or knocked unconscious. Whenever it takes 30 or more damage in one turn, one head dies. It dies if it loses all its heads. At the end of its turn, it grows two heads for each one that died since its last turn and regains 10 hit points per head grown. Radiant damage taken since its last turn prevents this regrowth.
Reactive Heads. For each head beyond the first, it has an extra reaction usable only for opportunity attacks.
Wakeful. At least one head stays awake while the dracohydra sleeps.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack per living head.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) damage. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning or poison.
Prismatic Breath (Recharge 4–6). All heads exhale together in a 60-ft. cone. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning or poison. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 17 Dexterity save, taking 33 (6d10) damage of that type on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Draconian Dreadnought
description: A powerful draconian born from a magically warped dragon egg. It fights with a serrated blade and can take the shape of a slain humanoid.

sections.Traits: Death Throes. At 0 hit points, the dreadnought burns to ash. Each creature within 10 ft. must pass a DC 13 Dexterity save or take 10 (3d6) fire damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Serrated Sword attacks and one Tail attack.
Serrated Sword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must pass a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Reactions: Shape Theft. After killing a Medium or smaller humanoid, the dreadnought can magically take on that creature’s look and feel. It retains its statistics except size. The change lasts until the dreadnought dies or spends an action to end it.

name: Draconian Foot Soldier
description: A rank-and-file draconian bred from a corrupted dragon egg. Its corpse hardens into stone and gives off a gas that can petrify nearby creatures.

sections.Traits:
Controlled Fall. When the draconian falls without being incapacitated, reduce the distance used to calculate its falling damage by up to 100 ft.
Death Throes. At 0 HP, the draconian turns to stone and releases petrifying gas. Each creature within 5 ft. must pass a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be restrained. A restrained creature repeats the save at the end of its next turn. A success ends the effect. A failure petrifies it for 1 minute. The draconian’s body crumbles to dust after 1 minute.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shortsword attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage.

name: Draconian Infiltrator
description: A draconian scout and spy that scales walls and glides from heights. Two hits from its envenomed daggers can paralyze the same target.

sections.Traits:
Death Throes. At 0 HP, the draconian dissolves into acid. Each creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, acid coats it for 1 minute and deals 7 (2d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can use an action to scrape or wash the acid off itself or another creature.
Glide. While falling and not incapacitated, subtract up to 100 ft. from the distance used to calculate falling damage. For each foot of descent, the draconian can also move up to 2 ft. horizontally.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Dagger attacks. If both hit the same creature, it must pass a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the end of its next turn. While poisoned by this attack it is also paralyzed.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.

name: Draconian Mage
description: A winged draconian spellcaster that fights with a trident or a ray of necrotic energy. Its bones explode when it dies.

sections.Traits:
Death Throes. At 0 HP, the draconian’s flesh and scales wither immediately and its bones explode. Each creature within 10 ft. must pass a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 9 (2d8) force damage.
Glide. While falling and not incapacitated, subtract up to 100 ft. from the distance used to calculate falling damage. For each foot of descent, the draconian can also move up to 2 ft. horizontally.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Trident or Necrotic Ray for each.
Trident. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage on a melee hit made with two hands.
Necrotic Ray. Ranged spell attack, +4 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.
Spellcasting. Cast Enlarge/Reduce, Invisibility, or Stinking Cloud, each once per day. Spellcasting uses Charisma (save DC 12) and requires no material components.

name: Draconian Mastermind
description: A cunning draconian that uses illusion and mobility to direct a fight. Its magic arcs between nearby creatures when it falls.

sections.Traits: Death Throes. At 0 HP, lightning strikes the nearest creature within 30 ft., then arcs to up to two other creatures within 15 ft. of the first. Each target makes a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 9 (2d8) lightning damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half the damage and avoids the stun.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks, choosing Rend or Energy Ray for each.
Rend. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Energy Ray. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d10 + 3) force damage.
Noxious Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it takes 21 (6d6) poison damage and gains one level of exhaustion. On a success, it takes half damage, avoids exhaustion, and is immune to Noxious Breath from all draconians for 24 hours.
Spellcasting. Cast Invisibility or Mage Hand at will, or Dimension Door, Disguise Self, or Sending twice per day each. Spellcasting uses Charisma (save DC 14) and requires no material components.
sections.Reactions: Magic Shield (3/day). When an attack roll hits the draconian, it can raise its AC by 5 against that attack, potentially turning the hit into a miss.

name: Draconic Shard
description: The psychic remnant of a gem dragon. It can appear as a spectral dragon or inhabit a treasure as an intelligent magic item, steering its bearer toward unfinished business.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid and fire. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone.
sections.Traits:
Deflection. The listed AC already includes the shard’s Intelligence modifier.
Incorporeal Movement. The shard treats creatures and objects as difficult terrain when moving through them. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When the shard fails a saving throw, it can succeed instead.
Rejuvenation. At 0 HP, the shard disappears and leaves a Tiny cracked gemstone in its space. The gem matches the kind of dragon the shard once was. The gem has AC 20, 15 HP, and immunity to every damage type except force. After 1d20 days, an intact gem dissipates and the shard returns at full HP in that space or the nearest unoccupied space. Destroying the gem prevents its return.
Unusual Nature. The shard requires no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Telekinetic Rend attacks.
Telekinetic Rend. Melee or ranged spell attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d8 + 6) force damage.
Inhabit Object. The shard disappears into a visible, nonsentient object of Medium size or smaller within 30 ft. Use the shard’s AC for the object and apply damage to the shard’s HP. Possession ends if the shard uses an action to leave, is turned, reaches 0 HP, or an effect such as Dispel Evil and Good ends the possession. The shard reappears in the nearest unoccupied space when it leaves. The inhabited object becomes a magic item if it was not one already, and a Tiny cracked gemstone of the shard’s ancestral kind appears on it. The shard can fly the object at its own flying speed, use its senses, speak aloud or telepathically, cast spells, and use legendary actions. If a creature wears or carries the object, the shard can give that creature resistance to psychic damage and an extra 1d8 force damage each time an attack hits.
Psychic Crush (Recharge 5–6). Each creature the shard chooses in a 60-ft.-radius sphere centered on the shard makes a DC 20 Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, it takes 55 (10d10) psychic damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and avoids the stun.
Spellcasting (Psionics). Cast Detect Thoughts, Invisibility, or Telekinesis at will. Spellcasting uses Intelligence (save DC 20) and requires no components.
sections.Legendary actions:
The shard gets three legendary actions and regains them at the start of its turn. It can use one option at a time, at the end of another creature’s turn.
Rend (1 action). Make one Telekinetic Rend attack.
Cast a Spell (2 actions). Use Spellcasting.
Commanding Thought (2 actions). One creature the shard can see within 30 ft. must pass a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed until the end of its next turn. While charmed, it moves and acts as the shard directs telepathically. On its turn, its only action options are Dash and Attack, and the shard chooses the target of any Attack.

name: Dragon Blessed
description: An acolyte who reveres a dragon as a god and uses magic to heal its allies and punish its enemies.

sections.Languages: Common, Draconic, and two other languages.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Mace or Radiant Bolt for each.
Mace. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage.
Radiant Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (5d8) radiant damage and restores 5 (1d10) hit points to the blessed.
Spellcasting. Cast one listed spell using Wisdom (spell save DC 14).
At will. Light, Thaumaturgy.
1/day each. Enhance Ability, Flame Strike, Mass Cure Wounds, Revivify, Tongues.
sections.Dragon followers: Dragon followers take cues from their patron dragon. Some serve it directly, while others follow it to learn the secrets of dragonkind. A Blessed can support a Dragon Chosen guarding a Dragon Speaker.

name: Dragon Chosen
description: A warrior who takes on a patron dragon’s power and enforces its will, often guarding a Dragon Speaker.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Handaxe attack and two Shortsword attacks.
Handaxe. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage. The axe returns magically to the chosen’s hand immediately after a ranged attack, whether it hits or misses.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.
sections.Reactions: Biting Rebuke. Immediately after taking damage from a creature within 5 ft., the chosen can make a Shortsword attack against that creature with advantage.

name: Dragon Speaker
description: A dragon’s envoy who negotiates for supplies, alliances, and treasure. The same voice can calm a crowd or knock a foe backward.

sections.Languages: Common, Draconic, and two other languages.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Thunder Bolt attacks.
Thunder Bolt. Melee or ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (3d8) thunder damage and pushes the target horizontally up to 10 ft. away from the speaker.
Spellcasting. Cast one listed spell using Charisma (spell save DC 13).
At will. Dancing Lights.
1/day each. Calm Emotions, Charm Person, Command, Comprehend Languages.
sections.Reactions: Disarming Words (3/day). When a visible creature within 60 ft. rolls damage, the speaker can roll 1d6 and subtract the result from that damage roll.

name: Dragon Turtle Wyrmling
description: A young dragon turtle that swims through coastal waters. One might make its home in a geyser among steam mephits.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The wyrmling breathes air and water.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d12 + 3) piercing damage.
Steam Breath (Recharge 5–6). The wyrmling exhales a 15-ft. cone of steam. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 12 Dexterity save, taking 17 (5d6) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. Being underwater grants no resistance to this damage.
sections.Source notes: Page 192 gives Bite as 9 (1d12 + 3) and calls for a Dexterity save against Steam Breath. The standard rounded-down average of the Bite dice is also 9.
sections.Optional dragon customization: Chapter 3 (p. 34) offers optional changes to languages, skill and tool proficiencies, senses, and traits.

name: Dragonblood Ooze
description: An alchemical accident that gave congealed dragon blood a will of its own. It can briefly shape itself like a dragon before collapsing into a heap.

sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, prone, restrained.
sections.Senses: Blindsight 120 ft. The ooze is blind beyond that radius.
sections.Languages: Understands Draconic and its creator’s languages. It cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Amorphous. The ooze fits through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Spider Climb. The ooze can climb difficult surfaces and cross ceilings upside down without a check.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Pseudopod attacks, or replace one with Slime Breath when available.
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) acid damage. A Large or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 15) and takes 7 (2d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns until the grapple ends.
Slime Breath (Recharge 6). The ooze ejects part of its body in a 30-ft. cone. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 22 (4d10) acid damage and is pulled up to 30 ft. straight toward the ooze. On a success, it takes half damage and stays where it is.

name: Dragonbone Golem
description: A dragon animates the etched bones of defeated rivals and binds them with adamantine wire to make a lair guardian.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Languages: Understands Draconic and its creator’s languages. It cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Fear Aura. When a creature of the golem’s choice starts its turn within 20 ft., it makes a DC 15 Wisdom save unless the golem is incapacitated. A failure leaves it frightened until the start of its next turn. A success grants 24 hours of immunity to this golem’s aura.
Magic Resistance. The golem makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Unusual Nature. The golem needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Pinion attack and two Rend attacks.
Pinion. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit is pinned and restrained. Each of the golem’s two pinions can restrain one creature. An occupied pinion cannot attack. At the start of its turn, the restrained creature can free itself with a DC 17 Strength (Athletics) check.
Rend. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage plus 5 (1d10) necrotic damage.
Petrifying Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Constitution save. A failure deals 35 (10d6) poison damage and restrains the creature while it starts to turn to stone. The restrained creature repeats the save at the end of its next turn. The effect ends on a success and petrifies it on a failure.

name: Dragonborn of Bahamut
description: These platinum-winged knights champion Bahamut. Some serve orders that protect people from evil dragons.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (1/day). After failing a saving throw, the dragonborn can succeed instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Longsword attacks.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage with two hands, plus 13 (3d8) radiant damage. Once per turn, the dragonborn can make the sword flare on a hit. The target then makes a DC 14 Constitution save or is blinded until the start of the dragonborn’s next turn.
Healing Touch (1/day). Touch another creature within 5 ft. It magically regains 40 hit points, and the touch removes every disease and poison affecting it.
Radiant Breath (Recharge 6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 15 Dexterity save. On a failure, a creature takes 44 (8d10) radiant damage. On a success, it takes half. The dragonborn can exempt up to three creatures in the cone. Each regains 22 (4d10) hit points and takes no damage from the breath.

name: Dragonborn of Sardior
description: These psionic champions believe that Sardior’s essence survives in gem dragons. Many belong to the Inheritors of the First World and can lift themselves through the air by telekinesis.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (1/day). After failing a saving throw, the dragonborn can succeed instead.
Mental Defense. While unarmored, the dragonborn adds its Intelligence modifier to its Armor Class.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Mind Blade attacks.
Mind Blade. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) psychic damage.
Heat Breath (Recharge 6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 14 Constitution save, taking 27 (6d8) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. Metal objects in the cone stay red-hot until the end of the dragonborn’s next turn. A creature that starts its turn in physical contact with one of these objects makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 9 (2d8) fire damage and has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of its next turn.
Spellcasting (Psionics). Use an action to cast Bigby’s Hand, Hypnotic Pattern or Telekinesis, each once per day. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability (save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks). The spells require no components.

name: Dragonborn of Tiamat
description: Often called Talons of Tiamat, these champions seek to free the Dragon Queen from Avernus. Some work with the Cult of the Dragon.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (1/day). After failing a saving throw, the dragonborn can succeed instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Greataxe attacks.
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (1d12 + 5) slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) necrotic damage.
Necrotic Breath (Recharge 6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, a creature takes 36 (8d8) necrotic damage and is frightened of the dragonborn for 1 minute. On a success, it takes half damage and avoids the fear. A frightened creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the fear on a success.

name: Dragonflesh Abomination
description: A grafter in the final stage of transformation grows wings and a tail and loses its former identity. It hoards treasure around abandoned dragon lairs and other sites tied to dragons.

sections.Languages: Understands Common and Draconic but cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Cloying Miasma. At the start of the abomination’s turn, each creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it is poisoned until the start of the abomination’s next turn.
Regeneration. At the start of its turn, the abomination regains 10 hit points if it has at least 1 hit point.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks, choosing Claw or Acidic Spit for each. The abomination can replace one of those attacks with Tail.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage plus 5 (1d10) poison damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d12 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must make a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
Acidic Spit. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (3d6) acid damage.
Acid Belch (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 14 Constitution save, taking 28 (8d6) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.

name: Dragonflesh Grafter
description: Grafters use dragon remains in rituals to take on draconic features. Growing scales and an acidic breath weapon accompany their fixation on hoarding treasure.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claw attack and one Greatclub attack.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage plus 5 (1d10) poison damage.
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Acid Retch (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 12 Dexterity save, taking 14 (4d6) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.

name: Dragonnel
description: A distant relative of true dragons, the dragonnel swoops at prey from the air. Dragonnels raised from eggs can become protective mounts, while wild ones may throw riders from the saddle.

sections.Languages: Understands Draconic and Common but cannot speak.
sections.Traits: Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke an opportunity attack from that enemy.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Rend attacks.
Rend. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
sections.Dragonnel Steeds: With the DM’s permission, a paladin can use Find Greater Steed to summon a spirit in dragonnel form.

name: Egg Hunter Adult
description: This dragon-egg parasite drains eggs and leaves its own clutch concealed in the empty shells. It can lie motionless and pass for an inert object.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The egg hunter breathes air and water.
False Appearance. If motionless at the start of combat, it rolls initiative with advantage. A creature that has never seen it move or act must pass a DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize it as animate. Dragons have disadvantage on the check.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Barbed Proboscis attacks. The egg hunter can also use Torpor Spores if available.
Barbed Proboscis. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. The egg hunter regains hit points equal to the necrotic damage dealt.
Torpor Spores (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on the egg hunter must pass a DC 14 Constitution save or become poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned this way, the creature can take only one of an action or a bonus action on its turn. It cannot take reactions. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. When it succeeds on the save or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to this egg hunter’s Torpor Spores for 24 hours.
sections.Reactions: Rapid Adaptation. When the egg hunter takes damage, it gains resistance to that damage.

name: Egg Hunter Hatchling
description: A young dragon-egg parasite with a tooth that can puncture eggshells. It can climb, burrow, and retreat quickly.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The egg hunter breathes air and water.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Egg Tooth attacks.
Egg Tooth. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage, or 17 (4d6 + 3) piercing damage against an object.
sections.Bonus actions: Rapid Movement. Take the Dash or Disengage action.

name: Elder Brain Dragon
description: An elder brain takes control of a captive dragon and uses the host’s mobility to lead an illithid army. Its brine breath can turn victims into mind flayers.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The dragon can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Siege Monster. The dragon deals double damage to objects and structures.
Unusual Nature. The dragon needs neither air nor sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite, two Claw attacks, and one Tentacle attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (1d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 15 ft., one creature. A hit deals 12 (1d8 + 8) psychic damage. A Huge or smaller target is also grappled (escape DC 18). The dragon can grapple up to four creatures with its tentacles at once.
Tadpole Brine Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a line 120 ft. long and 15 ft. wide makes a DC 22 Constitution save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) psychic damage. Success halves the damage. Either result infests the creature with illithid tadpoles unless it is a Construct or an Undead.
Infestation. An infested creature starts each of its turns by taking 16 (3d10) psychic damage. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, clearing the infestation after three successes. Magic that ends a curse or restores at least 40 hit points to the creature kills the tadpoles and ends the infestation immediately.
Ceremorphosis. If an infested Humanoid drops to 0 hit points, it is stable and remains unconscious for 6d12 hours. It then becomes a Mind Flayer with full hit points. Casting Wish on it while unconscious ends the infestation and prevents the transformation.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has three legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tentacle (1 action). Make one Tentacle attack.
Shatter Concentration (2 actions). Choose a creature the dragon has grappled. Its concentration on a spell or ability ends, and it takes 19 (3d12) psychic damage.

name: Emerald Dragon Wyrmling
description: A young emerald dragon that uses illusions and burrowing to observe others without revealing its position.

sections.Traits: Tunneler. The dragon burrows through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and can leave a tunnel 5 ft. in diameter.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) psychic damage.
Disorienting Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 12 Intelligence save. Failure deals 17 (5d6) psychic damage. Until the end of its next turn, the creature also subtracts 1d4 from each attack roll and ability check it makes. Success halves the damage and avoids the penalty.
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast Mage Hand (invisible hand) or Minor Illusion at will using Intelligence (spell save DC 12). Neither spell requires components.
sections.Optional young lair guidance: Page 65 allows reduced lair actions or regional effects for a young dragon or wyrmling at the DM’s discretion. The base wyrmling has no lair actions. Consider smaller areas and lower DCs. Regional effects do not affect CR. Lair actions can raise the CR of a dragon without legendary actions by 1 or more.
sections.Optional customization: Page 34 gives options for changing languages, proficiencies, senses, and traits to suit the individual dragon.
sections.Source notes: The printed Tunneler trait gives the wyrmling a 5-foot tunnel. The young emerald dragon can make a 10-foot tunnel.

name: Emerald Greatwyrm
speed: 60 ft., burrow 60 ft., fly 120 ft. (hover), swim 60 ft.
description: An emerald dragon whose crystalline form and vast psionic reach reflect centuries of merging with its echoes. Smargad is the emerald thane named in the book’s sidebar on Sardior.

sections.Traits:
Gem Awakening (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). When the greatwyrm would drop to 0 hit points, it instead resets to 400 hit points, recharges Breath Weapon and recovers all spent Legendary Resistance uses. It can use Mass Telekinesis for the next hour. Defeating it after Gem Awakening grants an extra 90,000 XP, for 180,000 XP total.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The greatwyrm can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) piercing damage plus 16 (3d10) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d8 + 9) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 19) and restrained while grappled. The greatwyrm can hold only one creature with its Claw.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. A failure deals 71 (11d12) force damage and knocks the creature prone. Success halves the damage and prevents the knockdown. On either result its speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.
Mass Telekinesis (Gem Awakening Only, Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Choose any number of visible creatures or objects within 120 ft., each weighing up to 4,000 lb. Worn or carried objects are ineligible. Each chosen creature must pass a DC 26 Strength save or be restrained by the grip. It can repeat this save at the end of each of its turns to escape. At the end of each of the greatwyrm’s turns, it can move each creature or object still in the grip up to 60 ft. in any direction, within 120 ft. of itself. It can also deal 45 (7d12) force damage to each creature it chooses that remains restrained by the grip.
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast a listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 26, +18 to hit with spell attacks) and no components. Dispel Magic, Forcecage, Plane Shift, Reverse Gravity, and Time Stop are each usable once per day.
sections.Bonus actions:
Change Shape. Magically take the shape of a Small or Medium creature. The greatwyrm retains its game statistics apart from size. The change ends at 0 hit points or when the greatwyrm spends a bonus action to end it.
Psychic Step. Magically teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 ft.
sections.Legendary actions:
The greatwyrm has three legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Psychic Beam (3 actions). Each creature in a line 90 ft. long and 10 ft. wide makes a DC 26 Intelligence save. Failure deals 27 (5d10) psychic damage. Success halves the damage.
sections.Optional customization: Page 34 gives options for changing languages, proficiencies, senses, and traits to suit the individual dragon.
sections.Printed source: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons, p. 201, Gem Greatwyrm stat block with the emerald variant’s psychic immunity.

name: Eyedrake
description: A beholder’s dreams of a dragon rival can give rise to this limbless flying aberration. A large eye in its mouth projects antimagic, and the eyestalks in its wings fire rays.

sections.Traits: Unusual Nature. The eyedrake needs no food or drink.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (3d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Antimagic Breath (Recharge 6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Constitution save. Failure deals 39 (6d12) force damage. Success halves the damage. Every spell of 3rd level or lower ends on creatures or objects of the eyedrake’s choice in the cone.
Eye Rays. Roll three different rays at random, rerolling duplicates. For each ray, choose one creature the eyedrake can see within 60 ft.
1. Freezing Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, take 17 (5d6) cold damage and halve speed until the end of the target’s next turn. Success halves the damage without reducing speed.
2. Debilitating Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, take 7 (2d6) thunder damage and become incapacitated until the end of the target’s next turn.
3. Repulsion Ray. DC 14 Strength save. On a failure, take 14 (4d6) force damage and be pushed up to 60 ft. away from the eyedrake.
4. Fire Ray. DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, take 21 (6d6) fire damage. Success halves the damage.
5. Paralyzing Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, become paralyzed for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
6. Death Ray. DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, take 28 (8d6) necrotic damage. Success halves the damage. The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 hit points.

name: Gem Stalker
description: A gem dragon can remake the body of a slain aberration as a crystal-studded guardian. The kind of dragon that created it determines its Crystal Dart effect.

sections.Languages: Understands Draconic but cannot speak, telepathy 60 ft.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. The stalker can climb difficult surfaces and ceilings without an ability check.
Unusual Nature. The stalker needs no food or drink.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make four Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
sections.Bonus actions:
Crystal Dart. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) force damage and adds the effect corresponding to the stalker’s creator.
Amethyst. The stalker can teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 30 ft.
Crystal. The stalker gains temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt.
Emerald. The target subtracts 1d4 from its next attack roll before the start of the stalker’s next turn.
Sapphire. The target must pass a DC 13 Strength save or be pushed horizontally up to 10 ft. away from the stalker and knocked prone.
Topaz. The target must pass a DC 13 Constitution save or be poisoned until the start of the stalker’s next turn.
sections.Reactions: Protective Link. When another creature the stalker can see within 30 ft. is about to take damage, reduce that damage by 10 (3d6). The stalker then takes damage equal to the reduction.

name: Ghost Dragon
description: A dragon’s attachment to its hoard can outlast its death. Often a single treasured object keeps its ghost bound to the hoard.

sections.Condition immunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained.
sections.Traits:
Incorporeal Movement. The dragon can pass through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Unusual Nature. The dragon needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 32 (6d8 + 5) cold damage and halves the target’s speed until the start of the dragon’s next turn.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d8 + 5) necrotic damage.
Terrifying Breath (Recharge 6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 21 Constitution save. Failure deals 40 (9d8) cold damage and leaves it frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature is paralyzed while frightened of the dragon this way. Success halves the damage and prevents the condition. A frightened creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. After succeeding on the save or when the effect ends for it, a creature is immune to this dragon’s Terrifying Breath for 24 hours.

name: Gold Greatwyrm
speed: 60 ft., burrow 60 ft., fly 120 ft., swim 60 ft.
description: A gold dragon can become a greatwyrm by merging with its counterparts from other worlds. Its breath can burn an army or sap its strength.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (4/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Metallic Awakening (recharges after a short or long rest). When the greatwyrm would drop to 0 HP, set its current HP to 450, recharge Breath Weapon, and restore all spent uses of Legendary Resistance. It can use mythic actions for the next hour. If defeated after this trait activates, award 120,000 extra XP (240,000 total).
Unusual Nature. It needs no food or drink.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature is grappled (escape DC 20) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can hold one creature with this attack at a time.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Breath Weapon (recharge 5–6). Use Elemental Breath or Sapping Breath.
Elemental Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save, taking 84 (13d12) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sapping Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Constitution save. On a failure it falls unconscious for 1 minute and can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect on a success. On an initial success, it has disadvantage on attacks and saving throws until the end of the greatwyrm's next turn.
Change Shape. Magically become any Medium or Small creature. The greatwyrm retains its statistics except for size. The change ends if it reaches 0 HP or uses an action to end it.
sections.Legendary actions:
The greatwyrm can spend up to 3 legendary actions, using one option at the end of another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 30 ft. must pass a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and fall prone. The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its fly speed.
sections.Mythic actions:
For 1 hour after Metallic Awakening activates, the greatwyrm can spend legendary actions on these options.
Bite (1 action). Make one Bite attack.
Shattering Roar (2 actions). Each creature within 120 ft. must pass a DC 26 Constitution save or take 19 (3d12) thunder damage and be incapacitated until the end of its next turn.
sections.Dragon customization: Page 34 offers language and proficiency changes, alternate senses, and traits such as Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation, and Tunneler. For an innate spellcasting variant, the general rule permits up to ten spells of 9th level or lower, once per day each, without material components. Charisma gives a spell save DC of 26 and a spell attack bonus of +18. This profile uses the printed actions unless you choose a variant.
sections.Source notes: The printed saving throw row omits Wisdom. Use the dragon's Wisdom modifier (+6) as printed. The indexed +14 includes proficiency.
sections.Printed source: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons, pp. 208–209, Metallic Greatwyrm with the gold damage type. Dragon customization appears on p. 34.

name: Green Greatwyrm
speed: 60 ft., burrow 60 ft., fly 120 ft., swim 60 ft.
description: An ancient green dragon can become a greatwyrm by fusing with its counterparts from other worlds. Poison suffuses its breath and gathers under its scales.

sections.Traits:
Chromatic Awakening (recharges after a short or long rest). When the greatwyrm would drop to 0 HP, set its current HP to 425, recharge Breath Weapon, and restore all spent uses of Legendary Resistance. It can use mythic actions for the next hour. If defeated after this trait activates, award 105,000 extra XP (210,000 total).
Legendary Resistance (4/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Unusual Nature. It needs no food or drink.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature is grappled (escape DC 20) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can hold one creature with this attack at a time.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Breath Weapon (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 26 Dexterity save, taking 78 (12d12) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Legendary actions:
The greatwyrm can spend up to 3 legendary actions, using one option at the end of another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 30 ft. must pass a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and fall prone. The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its fly speed.
Arcane Spear (3 actions). Launch four spears. Each automatically hits a creature of the greatwyrm's choice that it can see within 120 ft., deals 12 (1d8 + 8) force damage, then vanishes.
sections.Mythic actions:
For 1 hour after Chromatic Awakening activates, the greatwyrm can spend legendary actions on these options.
Bite (1 action). Make one Bite attack.
Chromatic Flare (2 actions). Each creature within 60 ft. must pass a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 22 (5d8) poison damage.
sections.Dragon customization: Page 34 offers language and proficiency changes, alternate senses, and traits such as Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation, and Tunneler. For an innate spellcasting variant, the general rule permits up to eight spells of 9th level or lower, once per day each, without material components. Charisma gives a spell save DC of 24 and a spell attack bonus of +16. This profile uses the printed actions unless you choose a variant.
sections.Printed source: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons, pp. 168–169, Chromatic Greatwyrm with the green damage type. Dragon customization appears on p. 34.

name: Hoard Mimic
description: This giant shapechanger poses as a pile of treasure. Some dragons use one as a decoy. A cornered hoard mimic may trade the real hoard's location for its life.

sections.Traits: False Appearance (hoard form only). If motionless when combat starts, the mimic has advantage on initiative. A creature that has never seen it move or act must pass a DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize that it is animate.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Pseudopod attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) acid damage.
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage and the mimic sticks to the target. A creature it sticks to is grappled (escape DC 16) and restrained until the grapple ends. Ability checks to escape have disadvantage.
Caustic Mist (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure it takes 27 (6d8) acid damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn. A success halves the damage and prevents blindness.
Shapechanger. Change into a treasure hoard or return to the mimic's amorphous form. Its statistics and equipment stay the same. It reverts to its true form on death.

name: Hoard Scarab
description: This coinlike beetle scavenges mites from a dragon's scales and lair. Its dust marks trespassers so nearby dragons can find them.

sections.Traits: False Appearance. If motionless when combat starts, the scarab has advantage on initiative. A creature that has never seen it move or act must pass a DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize that it is animate.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage. A creature hit has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of its next turn.
sections.Bonus actions: Scale Dust (1/day). Each creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 13 Dexterity save. On a failure it glows blue for 10 minutes, sheds dim light in a 10-ft. radius, and cannot benefit from being invisible. Every dragon within 1 mile of the creature becomes aware of it and can track it unerringly. Dispel Magic cast on the creature ends the effect.

name: Hollow Dragon
description: A metallic dragon can bind radiant energy into its empty hide to keep an oath or guard an artifact after death. Its scattered body can reassemble around its head.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Reconstruction. At 0 HP the dragon breaks into nine pieces: two arms, two legs, two wings, a tail, a torso, and a head. Each is a Large object with AC 19, 27 HP, and immunity to psychic and poison damage. After 1d6 days, if all pieces remain within 6 miles of one another, they teleport to the head and merge. The dragon returns to full HP and becomes active again.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks. The dragon can also use Sapping Presence.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage.
Sapping Presence. Each creature the dragon chooses within 60 ft. makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. On a failure its speed is halved and it has disadvantage on attacks until the end of its next turn. A success grants immunity to this dragon's Sapping Presence for 24 hours.
Radiant Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 19 Dexterity save, taking 54 (12d8) radiant damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon can spend up to 3 legendary actions, using one option at the end of another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Ghostly Binding (2 actions). A creature the dragon can see within 60 ft. must pass a DC 19 Strength save or be restrained until the end of the dragon's next turn.
Booming Scales (3 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 19 Constitution save, taking 24 (7d6) thunder damage on a failure or half on a success.

name: Liondrake
description: The solitary liondrake has a lion's body and a brass dragon's wings and long neck. It hunts within its territory and can paralyze intruders with its roar.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit must pass a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.
Blood-Chilling Roar (recharge 4–6). The roar is audible out to 300 ft. Each creature that hears it within 30 ft. must pass a DC 14 Wisdom save or be frightened of the liondrake for 1 minute. A creature that fails by 5 or more is also paralyzed for that duration. A creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect on a success. A successful save or the end of the effect grants immunity to this liondrake's roar for 24 hours.

name: Metallic Peacekeeper
description: A metallic dragon can forge a peacekeeper to guard a settlement in its place. The construct may watch over the community for centuries.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Immutable Form. Spells and effects cannot alter the peacekeeper's form.
Telepathic Bond. While on the same plane as its creator, the peacekeeper can magically relay what it senses to the creator. They can speak to one another telepathically.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (3d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Calming Mist (recharge 5–6). Each creature within 30 ft. of the peacekeeper must pass a DC 14 Charisma save or be charmed by it for 1 minute. A creature charmed this way is incapacitated with speed 0.

name: Metallic Warbler
description: A dragonforged metal songbird quietly watches a settlement and can alert its creator when danger threatens.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Languages: Understands Common and Draconic but can't speak.
sections.Traits:
Immutable Form. Spells and effects cannot alter the warbler's form.
Telepathic Bond. While on the same plane as its creator, the warbler can magically relay what it senses to the creator. They can speak to one another telepathically.
sections.Actions:
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.
Calming Mist (recharge 5–6). Each creature within 5 ft. of the warbler must pass a DC 11 Charisma save or be charmed by it for 1 minute. A creature charmed this way is incapacitated with speed 0.

name: Moonstone Dragon Wyrmling
description: A small moonstone dragon can put intruders to sleep or burn them with a beam of moonlight.

sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) radiant damage.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Choose Dream Breath or Moonlight Breath.
Dream Breath. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or become unconscious for 10 minutes. The effect ends for a creature if it takes damage or someone uses an action to wake it.

name: Young Sapphire Dragon
speed: 40 ft., burrow 20 ft., climb 40 ft., fly 80 ft.
description: This gem dragon can cling to ceilings and bore through rock. Its breath can incapacitate enemies with a pulse of sound.

sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. It can cross difficult surfaces and ceilings without an ability check.
Tunneler. It can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed, leaving a 10-ft.-diameter tunnel if it chooses.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) thunder damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) slashing damage.
Debilitating Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 17 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 33 (6d10) thunder damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and can act normally.
sections.Spellcasting (Psionics):
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 15). No components are required.
1/day each. Dissonant Whispers, Hold Person, Meld into Stone.

name: Young Topaz Dragon
description: This amphibious gem dragon breathes necrotic energy that saps the strength of creatures caught in its path.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The dragon can breathe air and water.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d10 + 3) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) necrotic damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Desiccating Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 28 (8d6) necrotic damage and is weakened through the end of its next turn. While weakened, it has disadvantage on Strength checks and saves, and its weapon attacks that use Strength deal half damage. On a success, it takes half damage and suffers no weakening.
sections.Spellcasting (Psionics):
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 14). No components are required.
1/day each. Bane, Create or Destroy Water.
sections.Optional dragon customization: Page 34 allows the DM to adapt languages, skill or tool proficiencies, senses, and traits for an individual dragon. The stat block uses the listed defaults.
sections.Optional lair guidance: Page 65 lets a DM give a young dragon regional effects or lair actions. Consider smaller regions and lower DCs. Regional effects leave CR unchanged. Lair actions can raise it by 1 or more for a dragon without legendary actions.
sections.Printed source: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons, p. 223. Customization on p. 34 and optional lair guidance on p. 65.

name: Young Sea Serpent
description: This sea dragon hides along reefs before ambushing ship crews. It coils around its prey or drives it into the water with its tail.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The serpent breathes air and water.
Siege Monster. The serpent deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Constrict or Tail attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage plus 5 (1d10) cold damage.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 20 ft., one creature. A hit deals 22 (4d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If the creature is Large or smaller, it is grappled (escape DC 15) and restrained until the grapple ends. The serpent cannot constrict another target while this grapple lasts.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or be pushed up to 20 ft. away and knocked prone.
Rime Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Constitution save, taking 38 (7d10) cold damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Aerosaur
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A colossal pterosaur with a wingspan near 200 feet. Lightning-like markings trace its scales, and its wingbeats unleash thunder.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The creature rolls with advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Talons attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 27 (3d12 + 8) piercing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 18) and restrained for the duration of the grapple. The aerosaur cannot bite another target while this grapple lasts.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 24 (3d10 + 8) slashing damage.
Wing Gusts (Recharge 5–6). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 20 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 38 (7d10) thunder damage, is pushed up to 30 ft. horizontally away from the aerosaur, and falls prone. On a success, it takes half damage and is pushed up to 15 ft. horizontally away from the aerosaur.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 128.

name: Altisaur
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: An eight-legged sauropod with a ridged back and glowing seams in its hide. Its tail can gouge a channel through the ground.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The creature rolls with advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Stomp attack and one Tail attack against different targets.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 33 (7d6 + 9) bludgeoning damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit must pass a DC 22 Strength save or fall prone.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 45 (8d8 + 9) bludgeoning damage and pushes the target up to 20 ft. horizontally away from the altisaur.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 129.

name: Bag Jelly
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: An olive-colored ooze that feeds on scraps in giant bags. Its adhesive surface can trap a thief long enough to wake the owner.

sections.Senses: Blindsight 60 ft. The jelly cannot see beyond that range.
sections.Traits: Amorphous. The jelly can pass through a gap as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Pseudopod attacks.
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (2d6 + 1) acid damage and grapples the target if it is a Medium or smaller creature (escape DC 11). The target has disadvantage on ability checks to escape that grapple.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 120.

name: Barrowghast
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A hill giant may rise as a barrowghast after dying hungry and furious. It feeds on life energy and often seeks out people it knew.

sections.Traits: Stench. A creature that starts its turn within 10 ft. must make a DC 16 Constitution save. Failure poisons it for 1 minute and prevents it from regaining HP while poisoned this way. Success makes it immune to all barrowghast Stench traits for 24 hours.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks, or make one Slam and one Life Drain attack.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d12 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Life Drain. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. A hit deals 9 (1d8 + 5) necrotic damage. On a failed DC 16 Constitution save, reduce its maximum HP by the damage it took until it finishes a long rest. It dies if this reduction brings its maximum HP to 0. A Humanoid killed by Life Drain immediately rises as a zombie ally of the barrowghast and acts independently.
sections.Reactions: Noxious Wound. Immediately after the barrowghast takes piercing or slashing damage, each creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 16 Dexterity save against the ichor it sprays. A creature takes 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 121.

name: Cairnwight
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A stone giant that dies while carving a masterwork may rise to finish and guard it. Its lichen-covered body blends into the cavern.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks or two Rock attacks. Also use Petrifying Touch if it is available.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +10 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. The target must pass a DC 17 Strength save or fall prone.
Petrifying Touch (Recharge 5–6). Touch one visible creature within 10 ft. It must make a DC 17 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 26 (4d12) force damage and becomes restrained as it turns to stone. The affected creature repeats the save at the end of its next turn. Success ends the effect. Failure replaces restrained with petrified.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 122.

name: Ceratops
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A horned monstrosity more than 200 feet long, with green light running through its thick scales. A charging ceratops can trample a forest.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The creature rolls with advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Gore attack and one Stomp attack.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 29 (4d10 + 7) piercing damage. If the ceratops moved at least 20 ft. straight toward the target immediately before hitting, the hit deals another 11 (2d10) piercing damage. A creature hit after that charge must also pass a DC 19 Strength save or be pushed up to 20 ft. away and fall prone.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 29 (4d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 129.

name: Cinder Hulk
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A descendant of fire giants whose body has become a shifting mass of ash and embers. It collapses into a cloud of searing smoke when it dies.

sections.Traits: Death Burst. On death, a 10-ft.-radius sphere of cinders and smoke forms around the hulk’s space. The sphere is heavily obscured. A creature that moves into it for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must pass a DC 16 Constitution save or take 10 (3d6) fire damage. The cloud lasts for 1 minute unless a strong wind disperses it sooner.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) fire damage.
Wave of Cinders (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 31 (7d8) fire damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 123.

name: Cloud Giant Destiny Gambler
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A cloud giant lays wagers against rivals across the planes and wears a runic half mask that cuts through magical trickery.

sections.Traits: Cloud Rune. A mask in the giant’s possession bears the rune. While holding or wearing it, the giant has truesight out to 30 ft. and can use Thunderous Clap and Negate Spell. The mask has AC 15, 45 HP, and immunity to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. It recovers all its HP at the end of every turn. It turns to dust at 0 HP or when the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can inscribe it on a mask it possesses when it finishes a short or long rest.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Flying Staff attacks.
Flying Staff. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. or range 30/90 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 18 (3d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 16 (3d10) thunder damage. The staff magically returns to the giant’s hand immediately after a ranged attack, hit or miss.
Thunderous Clap (requires Cloud Rune). Magically summon a thundercloud in a 30-ft.-radius sphere around a visible point within 60 ft. It spreads around corners. Each creature in the cloud makes a DC 20 Constitution save. Failure deals 52 (8d12) thunder damage and knocks the creature prone. Success halves the damage and avoids being knocked prone. The clap is audible 300 ft. from the center. The cloud heavily obscures the area until the start of the giant’s next turn or until strong wind disperses it.
Spellcasting. Cast one listed spell without material components, using Charisma (save DC 20).
At will. Detect Magic, Fog Cloud, Light, Minor Illusion.
1/day each. Dream (as an action), Gaseous Form, Major Image.
sections.Reactions: Negate Spell (requires Cloud Rune). When the giant sees a creature within 60 ft. casting a spell, it can interrupt the casting.
