A spell cast with a slot of 3rd level or lower fails. For a spell of 4th level or higher, the caster must pass a DC 18 Intelligence save or the spell fails.
sections.Optional wager spells: For a giant that has won a wager for spellcasting power, add one or more of Circle of Death, Harm, Otiluke’s Freezing Sphere, and Sunbeam to Spellcasting. Each added spell is usable once per day.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 124–125.

name: Cloud Giant of Evil Air
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: An adherent of Yan-C-Bin takes flight in a magical vest fitted with roc feathers. The vest works only for its wearer.

sections.Traits: Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke an opportunity attack.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks and one Storm Boomerang attack.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 18 (3d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Storm Boomerang. Ranged weapon attack, +12 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 15 (3d4 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) thunder damage. The target must pass a DC 16 Constitution save or become stunned until the end of its next turn. The boomerang magically returns to the giant’s hand immediately after the attack, hit or miss.
Spellcasting. Cast one listed spell without material components, using Charisma (save DC 16).
At will. Detect Magic, Fog Cloud, Light.
2/day. Telekinesis.
1/day. Gaseous Form.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 125.

name: Cradle of the Cloud Scion
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A persistent cloud tower holds a sleeping scion. Disturb it and the cloud takes the shape of a towering wind elemental.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned.
sections.Traits:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle dissipates into wisps of cloud. Scion of Memnor immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke an opportunity attack.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Slam and Wind Javelin.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 31 (4d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage plus 19 (3d12) thunder damage.
Wind Javelin. Ranged weapon attack, +17 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 27 (4d8 + 9) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) thunder damage. The target must pass a DC 25 Strength save or fall prone.
Vortex (recharge 5–6). Center a cylinder 30 ft. in radius and 100 ft. high on a visible point within 90 ft. Each creature other than the cradle inside makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Failure deals 71 (11d12) bludgeoning damage and restrains the creature in the vortex. Success halves the damage and pushes the creature to the nearest unoccupied space outside the cylinder. The vortex lasts until the start of the cradle’s next turn. Creatures still restrained by it fall prone when it ends.
A creature restrained by the vortex can use an action to attempt a DC 19 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. On success, it escapes and moves 3d6 × 10 ft. away in a random direction.
sections.Reactions: Thunderclap. Immediately after taking damage, the cradle can force every other creature in a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on itself to make a DC 25 Constitution save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) thunder damage and deafens the creature for 1 minute.
sections.Regional effects: One or more of the regional effects listed under Scion of Memnor can begin while the scion still sleeps inside the cradle.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 166–167.

name: Cradle of the Fire Scion
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A dormant volcano hides a scion of Surtur. Its cradle rises from the chambers below as a walking mass of molten rock.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle hardens and crumbles into ash. Scion of Surtur immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Slam and Hurl Lava.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 31 (4d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) fire damage.
Hurl Lava. Ranged weapon attack, +17 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 27 (4d8 + 9) fire damage. A creature or flammable object hit ignites and takes 10 (3d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature within 5 ft. of the fire can use an action to put it out.
Erupting Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 24 Dexterity save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) fire damage and poisons the creature for 1 minute. Success halves the damage and avoids the poison. A poisoned creature can make a DC 24 Constitution save at the end of each of its turns, ending the poison on a success.
sections.Bonus actions: Lava Geyser. Center a cylinder 20 ft. in radius and 50 ft. high over a visible point on the ground within 120 ft. Each creature in the cylinder takes 14 (4d6) fire damage on a failed DC 21 Dexterity save.
sections.Regional effects: One or more of the regional effects listed under Scion of Surtur can begin while the scion still sleeps inside the cradle.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 172–173.

name: Cradle of the Frost Scion
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A glacier shelters a sleeping scion of Thrym. Its animated cradle wields frost, mist, and ice.

sections.Damage resistances: Fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle shatters into ice shards. Scion of Thrym immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam or Hurl Icicle attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 11 (2d10) cold damage.
Hurl Icicle. Ranged weapon attack, +15 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 26 (4d8 + 8) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) cold damage. The target must pass a DC 23 Strength save or fall prone.
Freezing Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 23 Constitution save. Failure deals 52 (8d12) cold damage and reduces speed to 0 until the end of the creature’s next turn. Success halves the damage and leaves speed unchanged.
If the breath’s damage would drop a target to 0 HP, it drops to 1 HP and becomes a petrified ice statue. Bludgeoning damage shatters the statue and kills the creature. Fire damage instead thaws the statue and ends the petrification without dealing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Chilling Mist. Magically conjure a sphere 30 ft. in radius on a visible point within 90 ft. The mist spreads around corners. Each creature inside must pass a DC 19 Constitution save or take 28 (8d6) cold damage and lose its reactions until the start of its next turn. The mist disappears at the end of the cradle’s turn.
sections.Regional effects: One or more of the regional effects listed under Scion of Thrym can begin while the scion still sleeps inside the cradle.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 174–175.

name: Cradle of the Hill Scion
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A mass of earth and roots rises to defend a slumbering scion of Grolantor.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle crumbles into soil and moss. Scion of Grolantor immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Slam and Spit Rock, plus one Grasping Root attack.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 33 (4d12 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
Spit Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +14 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 25 (4d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage. The target must pass a DC 22 Strength save or fall prone.
Grasping Root. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 30 ft., one creature the cradle isn’t already grappling. A hit grapples the target (escape DC 17). While grappled, the target takes 29 (4d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. The root has AC 19. A single hit that deals at least 15 slashing damage to the root severs it, freeing the target without damaging the cradle.
Rolling Hills (recharge 6). Magically create a wave of dirt from a point on the ground within 120 ft. It can extend up to 30 ft. in length, height, and width. Each creature in the wave makes a DC 22 Strength save. Failure deals 58 (9d12) bludgeoning damage, knocks the creature prone, and buries it. Success halves the damage only.
A buried creature is restrained, has total cover, and can’t breathe. The buried creature or an unburied creature within 5 ft. can use an action to make a DC 17 Strength (Athletics) check. Success ends the prone and restrained conditions from the burial.
sections.Regional effects: One or more of the regional effects listed under Scion of Grolantor can begin while the scion still sleeps inside the cradle.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 164–165.

name: Cradle of the Stone Scion
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A bipedal mass of rock and crystal defends the slumbering scion deep inside a mountain.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone.
sections.Traits:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle crumbles into dust. Scion of Skoraeus immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam or Spit Rock attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Spit Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +15 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 24 (3d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage. The target must pass a DC 23 Strength save or fall prone.
Shattering Roar (recharge 5–6). Each creature within 60 ft. of the cradle makes a DC 23 Constitution save. Failure deals 33 (6d10) thunder damage and leaves the creature incapacitated until the end of its next turn.
sections.Bonus actions:
Crystal Flare. Each creature within 30 ft. of the cradle makes a DC 22 Constitution save. Failure deals 21 (6d6) radiant damage and blinds the creature until the end of the cradle’s next turn.
Stone Spikes. Choose a 20-ft. square of ground within 90 ft. Crystal spikes turn it into difficult terrain until the beginning of the cradle’s next turn. A creature takes 10 (3d6) piercing damage for each 5 ft. it moves in the area.
sections.Regional effects: One or more of the regional effects listed under Scion of Skoraeus can begin while the scion still sleeps inside the cradle.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 168–169.

name: Cradle of the Storm Scion
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A storm-wrapped elemental shelters a sleeping scion of Stronmaus. It can fight from land, air, or water.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, thunder. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned.
sections.Traits:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle bursts into light. Scion of Stronmaus immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Slam and Spit Hailstone.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 36 (4d12 + 10) bludgeoning damage plus 19 (3d12) lightning damage.
Spit Hailstone. Ranged weapon attack, +18 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 32 (4d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) cold damage. The target must pass a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Lightning Barrage (recharge 5–6). Hurl magical lightning bolts at up to two visible creatures within 500 ft. Each target makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. Failure deals 71 (11d12) lightning damage and stuns the creature until the end of its next turn. Success halves the damage and avoids the stun.
sections.Reactions: Booming Step. Immediately after taking damage, the cradle can magically teleport up to 60 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space. Each creature within 10 ft. of the space it left makes a DC 22 Constitution save. Failure deals 14 (4d6) thunder damage. Success halves the damage.
sections.Regional effects: One or more of the regional effects listed under Scion of Stronmaus can begin while the scion still sleeps inside the cradle.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 170–171.

name: Death Giant Reaper
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A death giant reaper wears armor shaped like an insect carapace and carries a great scythe. Its shadow magic helps it strike from a distance and sap frightened foes.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Scythe or Soul Bolt.
Scythe. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) necrotic damage.
Soul Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one creature. A hit deals 26 (4d10 + 4) necrotic damage. If the creature is frightened, the giant gains temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt.
sections.Bonus actions: Frightening Teleport (Recharge 4–6). Magically teleport the giant and its worn or carried equipment up to 40 ft. to an unoccupied space it can see. Each creature within 10 ft. of the space the giant left must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom save or become frightened until the end of that creature’s next turn.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 126.

name: Death Giant Shrouded One
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: This death giant inscribes its magic on a fallen giant’s skull. With the skull in hand, it can give its staff a spectral blade or wrap itself in a shroud of souls.

sections.Traits: Death Rune. The giant can use Reaping Scythe and Shroud of Souls while holding or wearing the skull marked with this rune. The skull has AC 18, 35 HP, and immunity to necrotic, poison and psychic damage. It returns to full HP at the end of every turn. It crumbles to dust if it reaches 0 HP or the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can mark another skull it possesses when it finishes a short or long rest.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Soul Burst attacks. If the giant has its death rune, it can make three Reaping Scythe attacks instead.
Soul Burst. Melee or ranged spell attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d10 + 6) necrotic damage. If the target is frightened, the giant gains temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt.
Reaping Scythe (Requires Death Rune). Melee spell attack, +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one creature. A hit deals 38 (7d10) necrotic damage. The creature cannot regain hit points until the end of its next turn and dies if this attack reduces it to 0 HP.
Spellcasting. The giant casts one spell from this list using Intelligence. At will, Detect Magic and Mage Armor. Three times per day each, Speak with Dead and Tenser’s Floating Disk. Mage Armor raises AC to 15.
sections.Bonus actions:
Frightening Teleport (Recharge 4–6). Magically teleport the giant and its worn or carried equipment up to 40 ft. to an unoccupied space it can see. Each creature within 10 ft. of the space the giant left must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom save or become frightened until the end of that creature’s next turn.
Shroud of Souls (Requires Death Rune). The giant surrounds itself with a torrent of souls. A creature starting its turn within 5 ft. of the shrouded giant must pass a DC 19 Wisdom save or have disadvantage on saving throws until the end of its next turn. The shroud ends after 1 minute or sooner if the giant dies, uses Shroud of Souls again, or loses its death rune to destruction.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 127.

name: Dust Hulk
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: This descendant of stone giants moves as a cloud of grit and gravel. Its constantly shifting body is both its artwork and its means of slipping through narrow cracks.

sections.Condition immunities: exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, restrained.
sections.Traits:
Air Form. The dust hulk can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. It can move through gaps as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Death Burst. When the dust hulk dies, its dust fills a 10-ft.-radius sphere centered on it. Each creature in the sphere must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution save or be blinded for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the blindness on a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Slam attacks. The dust hulk can replace one with Stinging Dust.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Stinging Dust. Choose one creature in the dust hulk’s space. It makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage and becomes blinded until the end of its next turn. On a success it takes half damage only.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 131.

name: Echo of Demogorgon
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Demogorgon can transform a devoted ettin into a two-headed fiend with tentacles for arms. Its heads bicker and howl with enough force to turn nearby creatures against one another.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The echo has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Wakeful. If one head is asleep, the other stays awake.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage.
sections.Bonus actions:
Discordant Screams. Choose one creature the echo can see within 60 ft. It must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or suffer one of the following effects, chosen by the echo.
Confused Reaction. The creature must spend its reaction to make a melee attack against another creature the echo chooses and can see.
Psychic Torment. The creature takes 13 (2d12) psychic damage.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 132.

name: Ettin Ceremorph
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Two tadpoles can transform an ettin into a guardian for a mind flayer colony. One head sinks into the body and directs its movements while the other uses psionics.

sections.Languages: Deep Speech, Giant, telepathy 60 ft., Undercommon.
sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The ceremorph has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Tentacles attack and one Slam attack. The ceremorph can replace either attack with Mind Bolt if available.
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. A hit deals 15 (2d10 + 4) psychic damage. A Large or smaller target is also grappled (escape DC 14) and must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence save or be stunned until that grapple ends.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (4d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Extract Brain. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one incapacitated Humanoid grappled by the ceremorph. A hit deals 55 (10d10) piercing damage. If that damage reduces the target to 0 HP, the ceremorph eats its brain and kills it.
Mind Bolt (3/day). Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one creature. A hit deals 17 (2d12 + 4) psychic damage. The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence save or be stunned until the end of its next turn.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 133.

name: Fensir Devourer
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: After a thousand years or more in Ysgard, some fensirs grow to about 25 feet tall and develop a hunger they cannot satisfy. A devourer can curse nearby creatures as it dies.

sections.Traits:
Death Curse. If the fensir starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate, each creature within 30 ft. of it when it dies must make a DC 13 Charisma save. A creature that fails is cursed for 24 hours. It gains no benefit from a short or long rest and must make a DC 13 Charisma save at the end of every hour or take 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
Regeneration. The fensir regains 10 HP at the start of its turn if outside sunlight. Taking acid or fire damage suppresses regeneration at the start of its next turn. The fensir dies only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. If the fensir starts its turn in sunlight, it must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or be petrified until it is out of the sunlight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks in any combination of Rend and Boulder.
Rend. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d10 + 5) slashing damage.
Boulder. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d12 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must succeed on a DC 16 Strength save or fall prone. Roll a d6 after each throw. On a 4 or lower, the fensir runs out of boulders.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 135.

name: Fensir Skirmisher
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Years of fighting in Ysgard teach skirmishers to wield earth as a weapon. They can hurl a fleck of gravel that grows into a boulder on its way to the target.

sections.Traits:
Regeneration. The fensir regains 10 HP at the start of its turn if outside sunlight. Taking acid or fire damage suppresses regeneration at the start of its next turn. The fensir dies only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. If the fensir starts its turn in sunlight, it must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or be petrified until it is out of the sunlight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Battleaxe attacks or two Magic Stone attacks.
Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 15 (2d10 + 4) slashing damage if used with two hands.
Magic Stone. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d12 + 2) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
Mud to Stone (Recharge 6). Choose a point the fensir can see within 60 ft. Magical mud fills a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered there. Each creature other than a fensir in the sphere must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity save or take 13 (3d8) bludgeoning damage and become restrained. The creature must roll the save again at the end of its next turn. A success ends the effect, while a failure petrifies it for 24 hours.
Spellcasting. The fensir uses Intelligence to cast Create or Destroy Water, Detect Magic, or Pass without Trace. It can cast each spell once per day.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 135.

name: Firbolg Primeval Warden
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Wardens of Hiatea teach children and tend the hearth. Those who patrol the borders hunt down dangers before they reach the community.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Spear or Fire Lance.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) fire damage.
Fire Lance. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d10 + 3) fire damage.
Spellcasting. Cast one of the following spells using Wisdom (spell save DC 13).
At will. Entangle, Speak with Animals, Speak with Plants.
1/day each. Commune with Nature (cast as an action), Detect Magic, Disguise Self.
sections.Bonus actions: Hidden Step (2/day). The warden becomes magically invisible until the start of its next turn. Making an attack roll or forcing a creature to make a saving throw ends the effect early.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 136.

name: Firbolg Wanderer
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Wanderers model themselves on Diancastra. They use disguises and misdirection to make their own names.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Longsword, Bewitching Bolt, or both.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage if wielded with two hands, plus 9 (2d8) psychic damage in either case.
Bewitching Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) psychic damage. The creature must succeed on a DC 14 Charisma saving throw or be charmed until the start of its next turn.
Spellcasting. Cast one of the following spells using Wisdom (spell save DC 14).
At will. Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Tasha's Hideous Laughter.
1/day each. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Dispel Magic, Polymorph.
sections.Bonus actions: Duplicitous Movement (1/day). Create an illusory duplicate in a visible unoccupied space within 30 ft., then optionally swap places with it. The duplicate vanishes after 1 minute, if the wanderer is incapacitated, or if it is more than 120 ft. from the wanderer. On later turns the wanderer can move the existing illusion up to 30 ft. as a bonus action, then optionally swap places with it.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 137.

name: Fire Giant Forgecaller
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A forgecaller tends forges and defends its community, often in Surtur’s name. Its armor contains enough heat to propel it through the air.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). After failing a saving throw, the giant can choose to succeed.
Fire Rune. The giant can use Magma Wave and Furnace Armor while it holds or wears the inscribed object. The object has AC 15, 40 HP, and immunity to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. It recovers all HP at the end of every turn. It crumbles if it reaches 0 HP or the giant dies. After the rune is destroyed, the giant can inscribe a new one on an object it possesses when it finishes a short or long rest.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Forge Hammer attacks or two Heated Rock attacks.
Forge Hammer. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 24 (5d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage. On a hit or miss, the giant can heat metal objects in a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on the target until the start of the giant’s next turn. A creature touching heated metal at the start of its turn makes a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failure it takes 10 (3d6) fire damage and has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of its next turn. Fire immunity prevents this disadvantage. The hammer can produce the heat burst once per turn.
Heated Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +13 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 23 (3d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage plus 19 (3d12) fire damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must succeed on a DC 21 Strength saving throw or fall prone. After each throw, roll 1d6. On a 1–3 the giant runs out of rocks.
Magma Wave (requires Fire Rune). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure it takes 36 (8d8) fire damage and is restrained by rock. On a success it takes half damage. A creature can use an action to make a DC 19 Strength (Athletics) check to free itself or a creature within its reach. Each mass of restraining rock has AC 17, 20 HP, and immunity to fire, poison, and psychic damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Furnace Armor (requires Fire Rune). Smoke and cinders fill a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on the giant and grant it half cover. The smoke lasts for 1 minute or until the giant dies, the rune is destroyed, or the giant dismisses it with a bonus action.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 138.

name: Fire Giant of Evil Fire
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Devotion to Imix gives this giant the power to brand its enemies. Its armor fuses to its body when donned and bursts apart when it dies.

sections.Traits: Shrapnel Explosion. At 0 HP the giant’s armor explodes and destroys its body. Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) piercing damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Searing Scepter attacks or two Bolt of Imix attacks.
Searing Scepter. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (3d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) fire damage and leaves a magical brand. The target becomes visible if invisible, cannot become invisible, and sheds dim light in a 5-ft. radius. The brand lasts 24 hours or until a spell that ends curses removes it from the creature or object.
Bolt of Imix. Ranged spell attack, +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (3d10 + 4) fire damage. The target must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the end of its next turn.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 139.

name: Fire Hellion
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A fire giant’s pact can turn it into a horned infernal smith. The weapons it forges send the souls of its kills to Avernus.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The hellion has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Soul Taker. A Giant or Humanoid the hellion reduces to 0 HP dies. Its soul rises as a lemure in Avernus in 1d4 hours unless the creature is revived first. Once it rises, restoring the creature requires Wish or killing the lemure and casting True Resurrection on the original body.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Morningstar attacks.
Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (3d8 + 7) piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) fire damage. A creature hit cannot regain HP until the start of the hellion’s next turn.
Infernal Orb. Choose a visible point within 120 ft. The magical orb bursts in a 20-ft.-radius sphere that spreads around corners. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) fire damage and 18 (4d8) necrotic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 140.

name: Firegaunt
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A fire giant can rise as a firegaunt when hatred keeps it from passing on. Crimson fire runs through the corpse as it hunts the living.

sections.Traits: Fire Blood. A creature within 5 ft. that hits the firegaunt with a melee attack dealing piercing or slashing damage takes 5 (1d10) fire damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Heated Maul attacks.
Heated Maul. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 23 (3d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage. Once per turn the firegaunt can make the maul erupt during this attack. The target must succeed on a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw or take another 10 (3d6) fire damage and 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.
Crimson Rays (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 31 (7d8) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. It catches fire either way. While burning, it cannot regain HP and takes 5 (1d10) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. It or another creature within reach can use an action to put out the fire.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 137.

name: Flesh Colossus
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: An adamantine skeleton supports the bodies of fallen giants. An elemental core inside the chest powers the construct and keeps it under control.

sections.Damage immunities: lightning, poison, psychic, bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Berserk. Destroying the core makes the colossus berserk until it is destroyed. On each of its turns it attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is close enough to reach and attack, it attacks an object.
Immutable Form. Spells and other effects cannot change its form.
Magic Resistance. The colossus has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Fist attacks.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Roll with advantage while berserk. A hit deals 17 (3d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit is pulled up to 15 ft. toward the colossus and becomes grappled (escape DC 17). It is restrained until this grapple ends. The colossus can hold up to two creatures this way.
Elemental Breath (Recharge 5–6). Choose acid, cold, fire, or lightning. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 40 (9d8) damage of the chosen type on a failure or half as much on a success. When it exhales, creatures inside its chest cavity also take 40 (9d8) force damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Large or smaller creature grappled by the colossus. A hit deals 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage and swallows the creature. The chest cavity can hold up to two swallowed creatures. A swallowed creature is restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects outside the colossus, and takes 10 (3d6) force damage at the start of each of the colossus’s turns.
sections.Elemental core: The core is a Large object within the chest cavity with AC 16, 140 HP, and immunity to lightning, poison, and psychic damage. It sheds dim light in a 10-ft. radius. Destroying it makes the colossus berserk and prevents further swallowing. The colossus ejects all swallowed creatures, which land prone in spaces within 10 ft. If the colossus dies, swallowed creatures lose the restrained condition and can spend 10 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting prone.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 141.

name: Fomorian Deep Crawler
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: This long-limbed fomorian hunts in Underdark tunnels, moving easily across walls and ceilings.

sections.Traits:
Contortionist. A space that fits a Large creature does not require the fomorian to squeeze.
Crawling Stance. When prone, the fomorian crawls without spending extra movement. Being prone does not grant advantage to attacks against it.
Spider Climb. The fomorian can climb difficult surfaces and ceilings without an ability check.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks and use Crawling Hex if it is available.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Crawling Hex (Recharge 4–6). Choose one creature the fomorian can see within 60 ft. On a failed DC 15 Wisdom save, it takes 31 (7d8) psychic damage, falls prone, and is cursed for 1 hour. While cursed, it cannot stand up to end its own prone condition.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 142.

name: Fomorian Noble
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: These scholars escaped the curse that changed their kin by leaving for the Inner Planes before the assault on the Feywild.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rod attacks.
Rod. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (3d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 11 (2d10) force damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 17). Mage Armor raises the fomorian's AC to 17.
At will. Mage Armor (self only), Mage Hand, Prestidigitation.
1/day each. Chain Lightning, Cone of Cold (6th level), Fireball (6th level), Fly, Plane Shift (self only).
sections.Bonus actions: Beguiling Presence. Choose one creature the fomorian can see within 60 ft. On a failed DC 17 Wisdom save, the target is charmed for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns and each time it takes damage, ending the effect on a success. If it succeeds on the save or the effect ends, it is immune to Beguiling Presence from every fomorian for 24 hours.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 143.

name: Fomorian Warlock of the Dark
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A pact with a power of the Underdark lets this warlock shape darkness into a weapon.

sections.Traits:
Blood Rune. The fomorian's Corrupting Hex and Poisoning Rebuke require it to hold or wear the rune-bearing object. The object has AC 15 and 30 HP and is immune to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. It regains all HP at the end of every turn. It crumbles to dust at 0 HP or when the fomorian dies. If the rune is destroyed, the fomorian can inscribe one on an object in its possession when it finishes a short or long rest.
Devil's Sight. Magical darkness does not block the fomorian's darkvision.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The fomorian can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Greatclub attacks. With the blood rune, one can be replaced with Corrupting Hex.
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.
Corrupting Hex (requires Blood Rune). Choose one creature the fomorian can see within 60 ft. On a failed DC 16 Charisma save, it takes 27 (6d8) necrotic damage and is cursed for 24 hours. The curse halves its speed. Before casting a spell, it must pass a DC 16 Intelligence check or the spell fails and is wasted.
Eldritch Burst. Center a 20-ft.-radius sphere of magical energy on a point the fomorian can see within 120 ft. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 32 (5d12) force damage and falls prone. On a success, it takes half damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Charisma (spell save DC 16).
At will. Detect Magic, Levitate, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation.
1/day each. Detect Thoughts, Suggestion, Telekinesis.
sections.Bonus actions: Creeping Gloom (Recharge 6). Briefly conjure darkness in a 30-ft.-radius sphere around a point the fomorian can see within 120 ft. Each creature in the sphere must pass a DC 16 Constitution save or take 11 (2d10) necrotic damage and be blinded until the end of its next turn.
sections.Reactions: Poisoning Rebuke (requires Blood Rune). When a creature the fomorian can see within 60 ft. damages it, that creature must pass a DC 16 Constitution save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 144.

name: Frost Giant Ice Shaper
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Frost rune magic lets these giants turn ice into armor or send whole packs of wolves after an intruder.

sections.Traits:
Frost Rune. The giant must hold or wear the rune-bearing object to use Ice Wolves or Ice Armor. The object has AC 16 and 40 HP and is immune to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. It regains all HP at the end of every turn. It crumbles to dust at 0 HP or when the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can inscribe one on an object in its possession when it finishes a short or long rest.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The giant can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Greataxe and Freezing Ray.
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) cold damage.
Freezing Ray. Ranged spell attack, +10 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (3d8 + 4) cold damage, and the target makes a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure, it is restrained until the end of its next turn. On a success, its speed drops by 10 ft. until the end of its next turn.
Ice Wolves (requires Frost Rune). Magically summon 1d4 ice wolves in unoccupied spaces the giant can see within 30 ft. Use the Winter Wolf stat block and change their creature type to Elemental. They obey the giant and act immediately after it on the same initiative count. Each gains +6 to attack and damage rolls within 30 ft. of the giant. They vanish after 1 minute, when the giant dies, or when it uses Ice Wolves again.
sections.Reactions: Ice Armor (requires Frost Rune). When a creature the giant can see rolls an attack against it, the giant gains +6 AC against that attack. After the hit or miss is resolved, the ice breaks. Each creature within 5 ft. of the giant must pass a DC 18 Dexterity save or take 13 (3d8) cold damage.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 145.

name: Frost Giant of Evil Water
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: An amphibious follower of Olhydra uses a barbed harpoon to pull prey toward the water.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The giant breathes air and water.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Battleaxe attacks and one Harpoon attack.
Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) slashing damage with one hand or 22 (3d10 + 6) with two hands, plus 7 (2d6) cold damage either way.
Harpoon. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 50/200 ft., one creature. A hit deals 14 (2d10 + 3) piercing damage and grapples the creature (escape DC 16). Its speed stays the same, but it cannot move farther from the giant. It takes 5 (1d10) slashing damage if it escapes or if its escape attempt fails. The giant can hold only one target in this grapple.
sections.Bonus actions: Reel In. Pull the creature grappled by Harpoon up to 20 ft. toward the giant.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 146.

name: Frostmourn
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A frost giant murdered dishonorably can rise as this vengeful undead creature.

sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Freezing Touch and one Icy Axe attack. One of the two can be replaced with Polar Ray.
Freezing Touch. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 18 (4d8) cold damage plus 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. If this damage would drop the target to 0 HP, it drops to 1 HP instead and is petrified as a frozen statue. Bludgeoning damage shatters the statue and kills the creature. Fire damage thaws it without dealing damage and ends the petrification.
Icy Axe. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) cold damage.
Polar Ray. Ranged spell attack, +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 31 (5d10 + 4) cold damage and reduces the target's speed by 10 ft. until the end of its next turn.
sections.Reactions: Blizzard Escape. Immediately after a creature the frostmourn can see hits it with an attack roll, the frostmourn halves the damage it takes. It can then magically teleport to an unoccupied space it can see within 30 ft.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 147.

name: Fury of Kostchtchie
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Kostchtchie grants some frost giant devotees immense strength and a bitter chill that drives them to seek out fights.

sections.Traits:
Chilling Aura. A creature starting its turn within 10 ft. of the fury must pass a DC 20 Constitution save or take 11 (2d10) cold damage.
Magic Resistance. The fury has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Fist or Rock in any combination.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) cold damage. The cold damage rises to 17 (5d6) if Chilling Aura damaged the target since the end of the fury's last turn.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +13 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Charge. Move up to the fury's speed toward an enemy it can see.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 148.

name: Gargantua
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Born among giants, a gargantua develops horns and purple skin as it reaches adulthood. It can grow past forty feet tall and often settles far from other giants.

sections.Traits: Weird Aura. At the start of the gargantua’s turn, each creature it chooses within 30 ft. makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. On a failure, the target takes 17 (5d6) psychic damage and is frightened until the start of its next turn. It sees the gargantua as the embodiment of its worst fears. A successful save grants immunity to this gargantua’s aura for 24 hours.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Slam or Rock.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 27 (3d12 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +15 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 24 (3d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Bonus actions:
Baleful Hex. Choose one creature the gargantua can see within 120 ft. It must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom save or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn.
Teleport. The gargantua and its worn or carried equipment teleport to a visible, unoccupied space within 120 ft.
sections.Reactions:
Flick. Immediately after a visible creature of Large size or smaller within 20 ft. damages the gargantua, the creature makes a DC 23 Strength save. On a failure, it takes 18 (3d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage, is pushed up to 100 ft. horizontally away from the gargantua, and falls prone.
Spell Mimicry (1/day). Immediately after a visible creature casts a spell of 5th level or lower, it makes a DC 19 Charisma save. On a failure, the gargantua casts the same spell at the same level, chooses the targets, and needs no material components. Use +11 to hit with spell attacks or DC 19 for a spell saving throw.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 149.

name: Giant Child
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Use this commoner-based profile for a young giant who is still child-sized. The child’s club could be a toy or an object picked up in a hurry.

sections.Actions: Club. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Giant child customization:
The sidebar derives this profile from the Commoner by setting Strength to 14, changing its type to Giant, giving it Giant as its only language, and replacing its Club attack. The DM can give a young giant its parents’ innate traits, damage resistances, or damage immunities.
Teenager. Start with the Ogre. Use 10 or the corresponding parent’s score, whichever is lower, for Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. Set passive Perception to 10. Keep darkvision only for a stone giant teenager and choose appropriate armor and weapons.
Young adult. Use a giant lower in the ordning as the starting profile. The book cites the Young Cloud Giant from Storm King’s Thunder, which adapts the Hill Giant.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 34, Giant Children sidebar. This profile applies the sidebar’s changes to the 2014 Commoner.

name: Giant Goose
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Giants keep these fey geese as sentries and livestock. Their honks drive off intruders, and a keeper can sometimes coax one into laying a golden egg.

sections.Languages: Understands Giant and Sylvan but cannot speak.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Beak attack and two Wing attacks.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Wing. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) bludgeoning damage. The target must make a DC 12 Strength save or fall prone.
Thunderous Honk (Recharge 5–6). Every other creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 12 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 16 (3d10) thunder damage and is deafened until the start of the goose’s next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and avoids deafening. The sound carries 300 ft.
sections.Golden egg: On its keeper’s command, the goose can lay a golden egg once per year and a day. The hollow shell is 1 foot long, weighs 2 lb., and is worth 100 gp. Roll on Goose Egg Trinket to determine what is inside.
sections.Goose Egg Trinket:
Roll d12.
1. Empty shell with a poem or detailed artwork on the inside.
2. A candy egg.
3. A toy goose that honks when squeezed.
4. A Potion of Giant Strength (hill giant), without a bottle.
5. A Pearl of Power.
6. A Brooch of Shielding.
7. A Figurine of Wondrous Power (silver raven) that activates as the egg opens, releasing what looks like a living bird.
8–12. Empty.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 150.

name: Giant Lynx
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: These hunters come from the Feywild’s snowy forests. They scout with divination, work together to trap prey, and sometimes befriend frost or cloud giants.

sections.Traits:
Lynx’s Sight (1/day). The lynx casts Clairvoyance using Wisdom and needs no spell components.
Woodland Camouflage. The lynx has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in undergrowth or snowy terrain.
sections.Actions: Claws. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage. If the lynx moved at least 20 ft. straight toward the target immediately before hitting, the target must succeed on a DC 12 Strength save or fall prone. If the target is prone, the lynx can make another Claws attack against it as a bonus action.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 151.

name: Scion of Grolantor
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: The hungry, 50-foot scion carries a whole tree as a club. A settlement can prosper for centuries on the slopes of its sleeping cradle.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (6/Day). When the scion fails a save, it can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The scion makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Siege Monster. The scion deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Great Tree Club attack and two Slam attacks, or make three Boulder attacks.
Great Tree Club. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must make a DC 23 Strength save. On a failure, the scion pushes it straight away horizontally by up to 100 ft. and knocks it prone.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 26 (4d8 + 8) force damage.
Boulder. Ranged weapon attack, +15 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 27 (3d12 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Inhale (Recharge 5–6). Each Huge or smaller creature in a 120-ft. line that is 15 ft. wide must make a DC 23 Strength save. On a failure, the scion pulls it up to 120 ft. straight toward itself and swallows it. The scion can hold up to two creatures at a time. They are restrained, have total cover against attacks and other effects originating outside the scion, and take 24 (7d6) force damage at the start of each of the scion’s turns. If one creature inside deals at least 60 damage to the scion in a single turn, the scion must pass a DC 17 Constitution save at that turn’s end or regurgitate every swallowed creature. Each lands prone in a space within 10 ft. of the scion. If the scion dies, swallowed creatures cease to be restrained and can spend 15 ft. of movement to escape its corpse, exiting prone.
sections.Bonus actions: Earth-Shaking Movement. Move up to the scion’s speed, then send a shock wave through the ground in a 60-ft.-radius circle centered on the scion. Each concentrating creature on the ground there loses concentration unless it makes a DC 23 Constitution save.
sections.Reactions: Feed. Immediately after taking damage while it has a creature swallowed, the scion deals 10 (3d6) force damage to each swallowed creature and regains 10 HP.
sections.Cradle encounter: The Cradle of the Hill Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.
sections.Regional effects:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Abundant Food. Crops and livestock grow and reproduce unusually fast within 6 miles.
Empowered Hill Giants. Hill giants within 1,000 ft. gain +7 to attack and damage rolls.
Farming Weather. Within 6 miles the weather stays warm and sunny, with occasional showers that favor farming.
On the scion’s death, all of these effects end immediately.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 164–165. The scion’s stat block is on p. 165.

name: Scion of Memnor
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A lanky, 75-foot giant with a weapon made of dense cloud. It turns fighting creatures against one another for its own amusement.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke opportunity attacks.
Legendary Resistance (6/Day). When the scion fails a save, it can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The scion makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Siege Monster. The scion deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one attack with Cloud Morningstar or Wind Javelin, then two Slam attacks.
Cloud Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 32 (4d10 + 10) force damage plus 22 (4d10) thunder damage.
Wind Javelin. Ranged weapon attack, +18 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 42 (5d12 + 10) thunder damage. The target falls prone unless it makes a DC 26 Strength save.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d8 + 10) force damage.
Thunderous Vortex (Recharge 5–6). Center a 60-ft.-radius sphere of magical wind on a visible point within 120 ft. Each creature in it must make a DC 24 Strength save or be pulled straight toward the center, stopping in the nearest unoccupied space to that point. Then the scion releases thunder in a 30-ft.-radius sphere at that same point. Each creature in the smaller sphere takes 52 (8d12) thunder damage and must pass a DC 24 Constitution save or be stunned until the end of its next turn.
sections.Bonus actions: Fog of Deception. Center a 30-ft.-radius magical cloud on a visible point within 90 ft. Each creature in the cloud makes a DC 24 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is charmed until the end of its next turn. It must use its action for a melee attack against another creature the scion chooses. If none is within reach, it instead makes a ranged attack against a creature the scion chooses, throwing its weapon if necessary. Success makes the creature immune to this scion’s Fog of Deception for 24 hours.
sections.Cradle encounter: The Cradle of the Cloud Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.
sections.Regional effects:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Compulsory Offering. The first time a sapient creature comes within 6 miles, it makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, it feels compelled to hide an offering worth at least 5 gp. Cloud giants within 6 miles of the cradle or scion immediately sense where the gift is. A creature can be affected by the compulsion only once.
Empowered Cloud Giants. Cloud giants within 1,000 ft. gain +8 to attack and damage rolls.
Mischievous Whispers. Within 1 mile, the wind carries indistinct whispers. A creature with Intelligence 5 or higher takes them as directions for a prank it can play on someone else.
On the scion’s death, all of these effects end immediately.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 166–167. The scion’s stat block is on p. 167.

name: Scion of Skoraeus
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A titan nearly 70 feet tall who shapes stone and deepens the veins of gemstones around its resting place. It carries a great crystal club.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (6/Day). When the scion fails a save, it can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The scion makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Siege Monster. The scion deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Crystal Club attack and two Slam attacks, then use Entombing Grasp if available. Alternatively, make two Runic Boulder attacks.
Crystal Club. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 35 (4d12 + 9) bludgeoning damage. Hit or miss, the scion can make its club flash. On a failed DC 22 Constitution save, the target takes 18 (4d8) radiant damage and is blinded until the start of the scion’s next turn.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 31 (4d10 + 9) force damage.
Runic Boulder. Ranged weapon attack, +16 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 27 (4d8 + 9) bludgeoning damage. Hit or miss, the boulder explodes. The target and each creature within 30 ft. of it make a DC 22 Dexterity save. Failure deals 19 (3d12) force damage and knocks the creature prone. Success halves the force damage and does not knock the creature prone.
Entombing Grasp (Recharge 6). Touch one visible Huge or smaller creature within 20 ft. On a failed DC 24 Dexterity save, it takes 28 (8d6) force damage and is grappled (escape DC 19). At the start of the scion’s next turn, the target is petrified if still grappled.
sections.Bonus actions: Earth-Shaking Movement. Move up to the scion’s speed, then send a shock wave through the ground in a 60-ft.-radius circle centered on the scion. Each concentrating creature on the ground there loses concentration unless it makes a DC 24 Constitution save.
sections.Cradle encounter: The Cradle of the Stone Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.
sections.Regional effects:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Abundant Stone and Minerals. Smooth stone and gemstones grow within 6 miles.
Edible Moss. Cavern walls within 6 miles grow carpets of golden moss that stone giants enjoy eating.
Empowered Stone Giants. Stone giants within 1,000 ft. gain +7 to attack and damage rolls.
On the scion’s death, the bonus ends immediately and new moss and minerals stop forming. Existing moss dies in 1d10 days.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 168–169. The scion’s stat block is on p. 169.

name: Scion of Stronmaus
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: An 80-foot giant who can sleep in the upper sky or the ocean depths. Its storm cradle may rouse in response to nightmares.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, prone.
sections.Traits:
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke opportunity attacks.
Legendary Resistance (6/Day). When the scion fails a save, it can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The scion makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Siege Monster. The scion deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one attack with Lightning Sword or Hailstone, then two Slam attacks.
Lightning Sword. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (4d12 + 10) force damage plus 22 (4d10) lightning damage.
Hailstone. Ranged weapon attack, +18 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 32 (4d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) cold damage. The target falls prone unless it passes a DC 26 Strength save.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (4d12 + 10) force damage.
sections.Bonus actions:
Vengeful Storm (Recharge 6). Create a heavily obscuring storm cloud in a 30-ft.-radius, 10-ft.-tall cylinder centered within 120 ft. It lasts 1 minute or until the scion dies or conjures a new cloud. When it appears, and as a bonus action on later turns, the scion can move the cloud up to 30 ft. and cause one effect below in a 30-ft.-radius, 120-ft.-high cylinder directly beneath it. It cannot choose the same effect two rounds in a row.
Acid Rain. Each creature in the cylinder makes a DC 25 Constitution save. On a failure, acid coats it for 1 minute or until a creature uses an action to remove the acid from itself or another creature. A coated creature takes 26 (4d12) acid damage at the start of each of its turns.
Freezing Storm. Each creature in the cylinder makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Failure deals 28 (8d6) cold damage and reduces its speed to 0 for 1 minute. The creature, or another creature within reach, can use an action to break away the ice and end the effect.
Lightning Bolts. Each creature in the cylinder makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 18 (4d8) lightning damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn.
sections.Cradle encounter: The Cradle of the Storm Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.
sections.Regional effects:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Elemental Portals. Two-way portals within 1 mile of the cradle or scion admit elemental creatures. They connect to the Elemental Plane of Air if the scion is in the sky, or the Elemental Plane of Water if it is in the ocean.
Empowered Storm Giants. Storm giants within 1,000 ft. gain +8 to attack and damage rolls.
Extreme Weather. Within 1 mile, the weather swings sharply from day to day, from bright sunshine to punishing hail.
On the scion’s death, all of these effects end immediately.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 170–171. The scion’s stat block is on p. 171.

name: Scion of Surtur
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Ash veils this 60-foot titan, who shapes a weapon from lava and looks for a fire giant army to lead.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (6/Day). When the scion fails a save, it can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The scion makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Siege Monster. The scion deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one attack with Lava Blade or Lava Ball, then two Slam attacks.
Lava Blade. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 32 (4d10 + 10) slashing damage plus 18 (4d8) fire damage.
Lava Ball. Ranged weapon attack, +18 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 29 (3d12 + 10) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) fire damage. The target must pass a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d8 + 10) force damage.
Lava Wave (Recharge 5–6). Release lava from the scion’s blade, hands, or mouth in a 90-ft. cone. Each creature there makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Failure deals 60 (11d10) fire damage and leaves it restrained in hardened rock. Success halves the damage and avoids the restraint. A creature can use an action to attempt a DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check to free itself or a creature within reach. The rock has AC 17 and 40 HP, and is immune to fire, poison, and psychic damage.
sections.Bonus actions:
Earth-Shaking Movement. Move up to the scion’s speed, then send a shock wave through the ground in a 60-ft.-radius circle centered on the scion. Each concentrating creature on the ground there loses concentration unless it makes a DC 26 Constitution save.
Incendiary Smoke. The scion creates a 30-ft.-radius sphere of smoke and embers centered on itself that moves with it. Ranged attacks against the scion have disadvantage while it emits smoke. A creature that enters the smoke for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 14 (4d6) fire damage unless it makes a DC 25 Constitution save. The smoke ends after 1 minute, when the scion dies, or when the scion uses this bonus action to stop it.
sections.Cradle encounter: The Cradle of the Fire Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.
sections.Regional effects:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Abundant Ore. Precious metals and ore are unusually common within 6 miles.
Desertification. Almost no precipitation falls within 6 miles, drying the land and withering most plants.
Empowered Fire Giants. Fire giants within 1,000 ft. gain +8 to attack and damage rolls.
On the scion’s death, ore veins stop forming and the other effects end immediately. Existing ore remains.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 172–173. The scion’s stat block is on p. 173.

name: Scion of Thrym
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A 70-foot giant that slumbers in icebergs or mountain glaciers. It forms a double-bladed ice axe when it wakes.

sections.Damage resistances: Fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (6/Day). When the scion fails a save, it can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The scion makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Siege Monster. The scion deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Ice Axe attack and two Slam attacks, or make two Glacier Throw attacks.
Ice Axe. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (4d12 + 10) force damage plus 18 (4d8) cold damage.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 32 (4d10 + 10) force damage.
Glacier Throw. Ranged weapon attack, +17 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (4d12 + 10) bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) cold damage. The target falls prone unless it makes a DC 25 Strength save.
Glacial Upheaval (Recharge 5–6). Choose a visible point within 30 ft. The scion digs into the ground and launches conjured ice. Each creature other than the scion in a 30-ft.-radius, 100-ft.-high cylinder centered on the point makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. A failure deals 36 (8d8) bludgeoning damage plus 19 (3d12) cold damage and pushes the creature vertically to the top of the cylinder, from which it falls. Success halves the damage and pushes it to the nearest unoccupied space outside the cylinder. At the start of the scion’s next turn, the ice falls at a visible point within 60 ft. of the original point. Center another 30-ft.-radius, 100-ft.-high cylinder there. Each creature in it makes a DC 25 Dexterity save or takes 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) cold damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Earth-Shaking Movement. Move up to the scion’s speed, then send a shock wave through the ground in a 60-ft.-radius circle centered on the scion. Each concentrating creature on the ground there loses concentration unless it makes a DC 25 Constitution save.
sections.Cradle encounter: The Cradle of the Frost Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.
sections.Regional effects:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Biting Chill. Extreme cold covers the land within 6 miles. If the region already had extreme cold, creatures without cold resistance or immunity there also have disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks.
Empowered Frost Giants. Frost giants within 1,000 ft. gain +7 to attack and damage rolls.
Thriving Wildlife. Beasts within 6 miles reproduce quickly and flourish.
On the scion’s death, all of these effects end immediately.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 174–175. The scion’s stat block is on p. 175.

name: Giant Ox
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: These shaggy oxen pull giants’ plows and haul their carts. Their coats can be bright blue or deep violet.

sections.Languages: Understands Giant and Sylvan but cannot speak.
sections.Traits: Beast of Burden. Count the ox as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity.
sections.Actions: Gore. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d6 + 6) piercing damage. If the ox moved at least 20 ft. straight toward the target immediately before the hit, it deals another 7 (2d6) piercing damage and the target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or fall prone.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 152.

name: Giant Ram
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Giants prize this ram for its fleece, which stores ambient magic and absorbs spells. The ram releases that energy to drive off predators.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The ram has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Ram. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) force damage. If the ram moved at least 20 ft. straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or fall prone.
Force Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +4 to hit, range 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (2d6) force damage.
sections.Reactions: Absorbent Fleece (Recharge 6). Immediately after the ram succeeds on a saving throw against a spell or a spell attack misses it, it can make one Force Bolt attack.
sections.Magic fleece: Fleece shorn without harming the ram can be woven into a Cloak of Protection or used to line Armor of Resistance to cold, fire, or lightning.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 153.

name: Giant Tick
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A boar-sized parasite that feeds on giants and readily attacks smaller prey.

sections.Actions:
Proboscis. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage and attaches the tick to the target. It cannot use Proboscis while attached. It can spend 5 ft. of movement to detach. A creature within reach of the tick can use an action and succeed on a DC 13 Strength check to detach it.
Blood Drain. Choose one creature the tick is attached to, other than a construct or undead. It takes 10 (2d6 + 3) necrotic damage, or 17 (4d6 + 3) if it is a giant. The tick regains HP equal to the damage dealt.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 153.

name: Gigant
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: An immense beetle-like hunter pulls prey with its hooked legs so it can catch them in its mandibles. Giants are its preferred prey.

sections.Traits: Spell-Resistant Carapace. The gigant has advantage on saves against spells. Spell attack rolls against it have disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Mandibles attack and two Talons attacks.
Mandibles. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. A hit deals 21 (4d6 + 7) slashing damage and grapples the target (escape DC 17). Until the grapple ends, the target takes 21 (4d6 + 7) slashing damage at the start of each of the gigant’s turns. The gigant cannot use Mandibles on another target during that grapple.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (3d6 + 7) slashing damage and pulls the target 10 ft. straight toward the gigant.
Scale Dust (Recharge 5–6). The gigant releases magical dust from its wings in a 30-ft. cube. Each creature there makes a DC 19 Constitution saving throw, taking 45 (10d8) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. Either result leaves the creature poisoned for 1 hour. It cannot regain hit points while poisoned this way.
sections.Bonus actions: Drone. Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it takes 10 (3d6) thunder damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. The gigant can then fly up to half its flying speed.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 154.

name: Goliath Giant-Kin
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Goliaths recognized as kin by giants often mediate between giant clans and other peoples. Their melee strikes can channel their clan’s magic.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Spear attacks.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage with a two-handed melee attack.
sections.Bonus actions: Giant’s Strikes (Recharge 5–6). Until the end of this turn, each of the goliath’s melee attacks deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage. The type depends on its giant community: cold for frost, fire for fire, force for stone, lightning for storm, piercing for hill, and thunder for cloud.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 155.

name: Grinning Cat
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: A huge, mischievous cat that questions travelers from an unseen perch. It sometimes reveals only its grin or tail while it talks.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. The cat has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) slashing damage. If the cat was invisible before the attack, the target must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or fall prone. If the target is prone, the cat can Bite it as a bonus action.
Fade Away. The cat and its equipment magically become invisible over the course of the cat’s turn. The effect lasts for 1 hour or until the cat attacks. The cat can leave a body part such as its tail or grin visible.
sections.Bonus actions:
Fade Back. The cat makes itself or part of its body visible. Any equipment on the visible part reappears with it.
Grinning Step. The cat and its equipment teleport up to 60 ft. to an unoccupied space it can see.
sections.Enchanted whiskers: A cat can be persuaded to give someone a whisker. A creature holding one can cast Misty Step with it once, after which the whisker goes up in smoke. A slain cat yields 2d12 of these whiskers.
sections.Printed source: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 156.

name: Hill Giant Avalancher
publication: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants
description: Hill giant rune workers hang rocks from their armor on ropes or chains. Their control of earth and stone often earns them leadership of a band.

sections.Traits:
Hill Rune. While the giant wears or holds the rock or other object that bears its rune, it can use Stone Avalanche and Hill Rebuff. The object has AC 15 and 20 HP, is immune to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage, and regains all HP at the end of every turn. It turns to dust when it drops to 0 HP or the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can inscribe another on an object it possesses when it finishes a short or long rest.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The giant can choose to succeed on a saving throw it fails.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Greatclub attack and use Stone Bolas.
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (3d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) thunder damage.
Stone Bolas. Throw three stones linked by magical force at a visible creature within 60 ft. It makes a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it is restrained until the start of the giant’s next turn and the stones erupt, dealing 14 (4d6) thunder damage to the target and each creature within 10 ft. of it. On a success, the stones vanish without erupting.
