sections.Printed source: Mythic Odysseys of Theros, pp. 188–189, Broken King Antigonos encounter. Uses the 2014 Monster Manual Minotaur (p. 223) with the printed encounter changes.

name: Bronze Sable
description: Purphoros gave his first bronze sables to Karametra to guard her temples. Others scout places too dangerous for their makers.

sections.Languages: Understands one language of its creator but can't speak.
sections.Traits:
Constructed Nature. This construct needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
False Appearance. While motionless, the sable looks like an ordinary statue.
Pack Tactics. The sable has advantage on attacks against a creature if one of the sable's allies is within 5 ft. of that creature and isn't incapacitated.
Surprise Attack. If the sable surprises a creature and hits it in the first round, the attack deals 10 (3d6) extra damage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Bite attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Mythic Odysseys of Theros, p. 210. Shared Anvilwrought rules appear on p. 209.

name: Burnished Hart
description: One of the earliest anvilwroughts, the hart leaves Mount Velus to seek sights worth carrying back to Purphoros.

sections.Languages: Understands one language of its creator but can't speak.
sections.Traits:
Constructed Nature. This construct needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Charge. After moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a target, hitting it with Antlers on the same turn deals 7 (2d6) extra fire damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
Heated Body. A creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage if it touches the hart or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 ft.
Sure-Footed. The hart has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saves against effects that would knock it prone.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Antlers attack and one Hooves attack.
Antlers. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.
Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) fire damage.
sections.Printed source: Mythic Odysseys of Theros, p. 211. Shared Anvilwrought rules appear on p. 209.

name: Colossus of Akros
description: A bronze-and-iron golem stands on twin plinths above the road to Akros. In a crisis, priests of Purphoros awaken it to defend the city.

sections.Damage immunities: Fire, poison, psychic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, stunned, unconscious.
sections.Languages: Understands Common and Celestial but can't speak.
sections.Traits:
Constructed Nature. This construct needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Crumbling Destruction. At 0 HP, the colossus crumbles and is destroyed. Each creature on the ground within 30 ft. makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. A creature takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning plus 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
Fire Absorption. When fire would damage the colossus, it instead regains HP equal to that fire damage.
Immutable Form. Spells and effects can't alter its form.
Magic Weapons. The colossus's weapon attacks are magical.
Siege Monster. The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft. or range 200/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 23 (4d6 + 9) piercing damage, or 27 (4d8 + 9) if wielded with two hands for a melee attack. The spear magically returns after a ranged attack.
Sword. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (6d8 + 9) slashing damage.
Flames of Akros (Recharge 6). Choose up to three visible creatures within 90 ft. Each makes a DC 24 Dexterity save against the magical flames. On a failure, it takes 36 (8d8) fire damage and catches fire for 1 minute. On a success, it takes half damage and doesn't catch fire. A burning creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, taking 18 (4d8) fire damage on a failure or ending the effect on a success.

name: Doomwake Giant
description: A doomwake giant is a Nyxborn creature formed from a community’s fear of destruction. It goes on to wreak the disaster the community dreaded.

sections.Traits:
Aura of Erebos. A creature that starts its turn within 10 ft. makes a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 10 (3d6) necrotic damage and can't regain HP until the start of its next turn. On a success, it is immune to this giant's Aura of Erebos for 24 hours.
Magic Resistance. The giant has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.
Noxious Gust (Recharge 5–6). The giant exhales mist in a line 60 ft. long and 10 ft. wide. Each creature in it makes a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure, the creature takes 36 (8d8) necrotic damage and falls prone. On a success, it takes half damage and isn’t knocked prone.

name: Eater of Hope
description: An Underworld fiend that hoards gold to tempt mortals and waits for despair to wear them down before it attacks.

sections.Traits:
Insatiable Greed. It senses gold within 1,000 ft., can pick out the direction of the largest concentration, and knows which way moving gold is traveling. A layer of clay or lead of any thickness blocks the sense if it lies directly between the fiend and the gold.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Immortal Nature. It needs no food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claws attacks.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.
Breath of Hopelessness (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Charisma save. On a failure, it takes 26 (4d12) necrotic damage and is cursed for 1 minute. While cursed, it takes an extra 6 (1d12) necrotic damage each time this eater of hope hits it with an attack. A success halves the breath damage and prevents the curse.

name: Fleecemane Lion
description: An enormous lion with a shining silver or gold mane that prowls places touched by Nyx.

sections.Traits:
Keen Smell. The lion has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on smell.
Pounce. After moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hitting it with Claw on the same turn, the lion forces it to make a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone. If the target is prone, the lion can make one Bite attack against it as a bonus action.
Running Leap. A running start of at least 10 ft. lets the lion long jump up to 25 ft.
Spell Turning. The lion has advantage on saves against spells that target it alone, excluding area spells. If it succeeds against a spell of 4th level or lower, the spell leaves the lion unaffected and targets its caster instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claw attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage.
sections.Legendary actions:
The lion has two legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Roar (2 actions). Each creature within 60 ft. that hears the magical roar must make a DC 12 Wisdom save or be frightened of the lion until the end of the lion’s next turn.

name: Flitterstep Eidolon
description: A wandering spirit born from the identity a Returned relinquished to leave the Underworld.

sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, restrained.
sections.Languages: The languages the eidolon knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Blurred Form. Attacks against the eidolon have disadvantage unless it is incapacitated.
Evasion. When a Dexterity save would normally halve damage, the eidolon takes no damage on a success and half on a failure. It loses this benefit while incapacitated.
Incorporeal Movement. The eidolon can move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. If it ends its turn inside an object, it takes 5 (1d10) force damage.
Turn Resistance. It has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
Undead Nature. The eidolon needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks. If available, Flitterstep can be used immediately before or after one of the attacks.
Flickering Dagger. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) psychic damage.
Flitterstep (Recharge 5–6). Magically teleport to an unoccupied space the eidolon can see within 30 ft. An attack it makes immediately after teleporting has advantage.

name: Ghostblade Eidolon
description: A lost identity shed by a Returned warrior, still fighting battles it believes never ended.

sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, restrained.
sections.Languages: The languages the eidolon knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Blurred Form. Attacks against the eidolon have disadvantage unless it is incapacitated.
Incorporeal Movement. The eidolon can move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. If it ends its turn inside an object, it takes 5 (1d10) force damage.
Turn Resistance. It has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
Undead Nature. The eidolon needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Ghostblade attacks.
Ghostblade. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 8 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) force damage.

name: Gold-Forged Sentinel
description: One of Purphoros’s early anvilwroughts. It may stand still for decades before resuming a mission known only to itself.

sections.Languages: Understands one language of its creator and cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Charge. If the sentinel travels at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hits it with Ram that turn, the hit deals 10 (3d6) extra bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must also make a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
Spell Turning. The sentinel has advantage on saves against spells that target it alone, excluding area spells. If it succeeds against a spell of 4th level or lower, the spell leaves the sentinel unaffected and targets its caster instead.
Constructed Nature. The sentinel needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Ram attacks.
Ram. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Fire Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 27 (6d8) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Printed source: Mythic Odysseys of Theros, p. 211, with Constructed Nature on p. 209.

name: Hippocamp
description: An aquatic steed that travels in herds and serves as a guide or mount for tritons and other seafarers.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The hippocamp breathes air and water.
Charge. If it moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and then hits with Ram that turn, the hit deals 7 (2d6) extra bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must also make a DC 12 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Actions:
Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 9 (2d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Ram. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

name: Hundred-Handed One
description: A giant artisan with pairs of arms orbiting its body. These giants carve monuments and memories into remote cliffs.

sections.Traits:
Reactive. The giant can take one reaction on each turn in combat.
Vigilant. The giant cannot be surprised.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make four Longsword attacks or two Rock attacks.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 21 (3d8 + 8) slashing damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +13 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must make a DC 21 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Reactions: Deflect Attack. When a weapon attack would hit the giant, it can add 5 to its AC against that attack if it can see the attacker and is wielding a melee weapon.

name: Hythonia
description: A medusa who rules the island of Skathos from a throne made of petrified devotees. She trades divine secrets for someone to add to it.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). Hythonia can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Petrifying Gaze. When a creature starts its turn within 30 ft. and can see Hythonia’s eyes, she can force a DC 18 Constitution save if she can see the creature and is not incapacitated. Failure by 5 or more petrifies the creature immediately. A lesser failure restrains it as it turns to stone. It repeats the save at the end of its next turn. Success ends the effect and failure petrifies it. Greater Restoration or other magic can end the petrification. A creature that is not surprised can avert its eyes at the start of its turn to avoid the save. It cannot see Hythonia until its next turn starts and must make the save immediately if it looks before then. Seeing her reflection on a polished surface within 30 ft. in bright light subjects Hythonia to her own gaze.
Shed Skin (Mythic Trait, Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). At 0 HP, Hythonia sheds her skin, regains 199 HP, and moves up to her speed without provoking opportunity attacks. She stays conscious and alive.
sections.Innate Spellcasting: Charisma sets spell save DC 18. Hythonia casts Animate Objects once per day with no material components.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claws attack, one Constrict attack, and one Snaky Hair attack.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) poison damage.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one Large or smaller creature. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage and grappled (escape DC 19). The target is restrained until the grapple ends and takes 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. Hythonia cannot constrict a second target while this grapple lasts.
Snaky Hair. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 31 (4d12 + 5) bludgeoning damage. Hythonia may also pull a Large or smaller creature up to 5 ft. closer.
sections.Legendary actions:
Hythonia has 3 legendary actions per round. She can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn and regains spent actions at the start of her turn.
Move (1 Action). Move up to her speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Snaky Hair (1 Action). Make one Snaky Hair attack.
Petrified Earth (2 Actions). Stone spikes make the ground in a 30-ft. radius around Hythonia difficult terrain until the start of her next turn. Other creatures take 9 (2d8) piercing damage for every 5 ft. they move across the spikes.
sections.Mythic actions:
Hythonia can spend legendary actions on these options for 1 hour after using Shed Skin. Award 36,000 XP in total if the party defeats her after she uses Shed Skin.
Numbing Claws (1 Action). Make two Claws attacks. If both hit the same creature, it takes an additional 7 (2d6) poison damage and must make a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure it is paralyzed until the start of Hythonia’s next turn.
Look at Me (3 Actions). Force one sighted creature Hythonia has grappled to look into her eyes and face her Petrifying Gaze.
sections.Lair actions:
On initiative count 20, after any creature tied at 20, Hythonia can choose one effect. She cannot choose the same effect in consecutive rounds.
Animated Statues. Briefly animate creatures petrified by her gaze. Each statue attacks one creature within 5 ft. at +11 to hit for 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller creature that takes this damage is also grappled (escape DC 15).
Spectral Snakes. Choose a point Hythonia can see within 150 ft. Each creature within 20 ft. of it makes a DC 19 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 5 (2d4) piercing damage and is poisoned until the end of its next turn. While poisoned this way, it has disadvantage on Intelligence checks and saves and acts as if affected by Confusion.
sections.Regional effects:
One or more effects can manifest around the lair.
Snakes are abundant in the region.
Trees within 1 mile are petrified wood. A plant that remains within 500 ft. of the lair for a day turns to stone.
Small bodies of water within 1 mile are poisonous. A creature that drinks the water must make a DC 19 Constitution save or be poisoned for 8 hours. It can repeat the save at the end of each hour to end the poison early.

name: Ironscale Hydra
description: A huge, acid-blooded hydra that stalks lakes and bog caverns in the wilds of Theros.

sections.Traits:
Acidic Blood. Whenever the hydra takes piercing or slashing damage, every creature within 5 ft. takes 9 (2d8) acid damage.
Hold Breath. The hydra can hold its breath for 1 hour.
Multiple Heads. It begins with five heads. While it has more than one, it has advantage on saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious. If it takes at least 35 damage in a single turn, one head dies. The hydra dies if it loses every head. At the end of its turn, it grows two heads for each head lost since its last turn and regains 10 HP per head grown. Any fire damage since its last turn prevents regrowth that turn.
Reactive Heads. Each head beyond the first grants an extra reaction usable only for an opportunity attack.
Wakeful. At least one head stays awake while the hydra sleeps.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack for each head.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage.

name: Lampad
description: A nymph of shadowed tombs and Underworld crossings. Lampads help Athreos guide the dead and retrieve souls that try to return to the living.

sections.Traits:
Corpse Stride. Once on its turn, the lampad can spend 10 ft. of movement to enter a corpse within reach and emerge in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of a second corpse. The two corpses must be within 60 ft. of each other and both must be Medium or larger.
Magic Resistance. The lampad has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Immortal Nature. The nymph needs no food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma grants +6 to spell attacks. These spells require no material components.
At will. Chill Touch, Gentle Repose.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Necrotic Touch or Chill Touch.
Necrotic Touch. Melee spell attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) necrotic damage.
Chill Touch (Cantrip). Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. The target cannot regain HP until the start of the lampad’s next turn. If it is undead, it has disadvantage on attacks against the lampad until the end of the lampad’s next turn.

name: Leonin Iconoclast
description: A hunter from Oreskos who protects leonin prides by pursuing servants of the gods and creatures born of Nyx.

sections.Traits:
Evasion. On a Dexterity save that normally halves damage on success, take no damage on success and half damage on failure. Evasion does not work while the iconoclast is incapacitated.
Unarmored Defense. Add the iconoclast’s Wisdom modifier to AC while it wears no armor and carries no shield.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Wisdom sets spell save DC 14. These spells require no material components.
1/day each. Banishment, Detect Evil and Good.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three weapon attacks.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) force damage.
Dart. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage.

name: Medusa
description: On Theros, a medusa has serpentine coils in place of legs. These servants of Pharika guard knowledge of medicine and immortality, sometimes offering it in exchange for a dangerous service.

sections.Traits: Petrifying Gaze. When a creature starts its turn within 30 ft. and can see the medusa’s eyes, it can force a DC 14 Constitution save if it can see the creature and is not incapacitated. Failure by 5 or more petrifies the creature immediately. A lesser failure restrains it as it turns to stone. It repeats the save at the end of its next turn. Success ends the effect and failure petrifies it. Greater Restoration or other magic can end the petrification. A creature that is not surprised can avert its eyes at the start of its turn to avoid the save. It cannot see the medusa until its next turn starts and must make the save immediately if it looks before then. Seeing its reflection on a polished surface within 30 ft. in bright light subjects the medusa to its own gaze.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Snake Hair attack, one Constrict attack, and one Shortsword attack, or make two Longbow attacks.
Snake Hair. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) poison damage.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature is also grappled (escape DC 11) and restrained until the grapple ends. The medusa cannot constrict another target while this grapple lasts.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.
sections.Printed source: Mythic Odysseys of Theros, p. 206. Use the 2014 Monster Manual medusa (p. 214) with the Theros Multiattack and Constrict.

name: Meletian Hoplite
description: A soldier of Meletis who combines spear and shield with wizard magic. The Reverent Army uses this training in flexible formations.

sections.Spellcasting:
A 3rd-level Intelligence spellcaster with spell save DC 13 and +5 to spell attacks. Prepared wizard spells:
Cantrips (at will). Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Ray of Frost.
1st level (4 slots). Color Spray, Expeditious Retreat, Sleep.
2nd level (2 slots). Blur, Cloud of Daggers, Invisibility.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three weapon attacks. The hoplite may replace one with Ray of Frost.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage, or 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage for a two-handed melee attack.
Shield Bash. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target must make a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
Ray of Frost (Cantrip). Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d8) cold damage, and the target’s speed drops by 10 ft. until the start of the hoplite’s next turn.
sections.Printed source: Mythic Odysseys of Theros, p. 229. The printed Spear action lists only the melee reach. Its ranged attack uses the standard spear’s 20/60-ft. thrown range.

name: Naiad
description: A guardian nymph bound to a stretch of water. Naiads collect curiosities from wrecks and are said to know hidden routes through Theros’s waters.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The naiad breathes air and water.
Invisible in Water. While fully submerged, the naiad is invisible.
Magic Resistance. The naiad has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Immortal Nature. The nymph needs no food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma sets spell save DC 14. These spells require no material components.
At will. Minor Illusion.
3/day. Phantasmal Force.
1/day each. Fly, Hypnotic Pattern.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Psychic Touch attacks.
Psychic Touch. Melee spell attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) psychic damage.

name: Nightmare Shepherd
description: A winged fiend of Erebos that drives the dead toward their assigned wards and preys on souls that stray.

sections.Traits:
Aura of Nightmares. Undead within 30 ft. of the shepherd get +5 to attack and damage rolls. When a creature other than the shepherd, an undead, or a construct starts its turn within 30 ft. of the shepherd, it must pass a DC 17 Wisdom save or take 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
Magic Resistance. The shepherd has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Immortal Nature. It needs no food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma is the spellcasting ability (save DC 17). The shepherd needs no material components.
1/day each. Confusion, Dispel Magic, Hold Person, Suggestion.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claws attack and one Staff attack.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage plus 16 (3d10) necrotic damage.
Staff. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage when used one-handed or 13 (2d8 + 4) when used two-handed. Either hit also deals 26 (4d12) psychic damage.
Herd the Underworld (recharges after a short or long rest). Summon 1d6 Shadows without Sunlight Weakness in unoccupied spaces within 20 ft. of the shepherd. The Shadows act immediately after the shepherd on its initiative count and fight until destroyed. They disappear if the shepherd dies.

name: Nyx-Fleece Ram
description: A mountain ram whose wool can carry a blessing. Divine servants guard the few herds that live high in Theros’s peaks.

sections.Traits:
Charge. If the ram moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hits it with Ram on the same turn, the hit deals an extra 5 (2d4) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit this way must pass a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
Magic Resistance. The ram has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Sure-Footed. The ram has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saves against effects that would knock it prone.
sections.Actions: Ram. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) force damage.
sections.Powers of the Fleece:
Shear the ram unharmed and turn its wool into a garment. Roll a d6 for the new garment’s power. A wearer must attune to it to gain the benefit.
1. Protection. Gain +1 to AC and saving throws.
2. Power of Nyx. Gain advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks.
3. Calming Presence. Cast Calm Emotions once per day (save DC 13).
4. Trail of Flowers. Flowers magically grow wherever the wearer walks and wilt after 1 hour.
5. Animal Affinity. A non-evil wearer can cast Animal Friendship once per day (save DC 13).
6. Abundance of Food. Cast Create Food and Water once per day.

name: Oracle
description: A mortal interpreter of Nyx. Some oracles speak for one god, while others read the night sky for signs of what lies ahead.

sections.Armor: The listed AC includes Blessings of the Gods.
sections.Traits: Blessings of the Gods. Add the oracle’s Wisdom modifier to its AC while it wears no armor and uses no shield. A creature within 5 ft. that hits the oracle with a melee attack takes 9 (2d8) force damage.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Wisdom is the spellcasting ability (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). The oracle needs no material components.
At will. Guidance, Light, Thaumaturgy.
3/day each. Bless, Guiding Bolt, Healing Word, Hold Person.
1/day each. Augury, Scrying.
sections.Actions: Eldritch Touch. Melee spell attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) force damage.
sections.Reactions: Divine Insight (3/day). When the oracle or a creature it can see makes an attack roll, a saving throw, or an ability check, the oracle can give that roll advantage or disadvantage.

name: Oread
description: A nymph of mountain crags and volcanoes. Oreads revel in eruptions and avalanches and avoid deliberately destroying another nymph’s home.

sections.Traits:
Invisible in Fire. The oread is invisible whenever fire completely surrounds it.
Magic Resistance. The oread has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Immortal Nature. It needs no food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma is the spellcasting ability (save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). The oread needs no material components.
At will. Fire Bolt (see Actions).
3/day. Burning Hands.
1/day each. Hellish Rebuke (see Reactions), Scorching Ray.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Attack twice with Fiery Touch or Fire Bolt.
Fiery Touch. Melee spell attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) fire damage.
Fire Bolt (cantrip). Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d10) fire damage.
sections.Reactions: Hellish Rebuke (2nd-level spell, 1/day). If a visible creature within 60 ft. damages the oread, that creature makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 16 (3d10) fire damage. On a success, it takes half as much.

name: Phylaskia
description: An armored skeletal guard that watches the borders between the wards of the Underworld and challenges those who would cross.

sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Gatekeeper’s Aura. When a creature starts its turn within 10 ft. of the phylaskia, it makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. A success grants immunity to this aura for 24 hours. On a failure, the creature has disadvantage on saves and half its usual speed until the start of its next turn.
Undead Fortitude. When damage reduces the phylaskia to 0 HP, it makes a Constitution save against DC 5 + the damage taken. On a success, it falls to 1 HP instead. Radiant damage and critical hits bypass this save.
Vigilant. The phylaskia can’t be surprised.
Undead Nature. The phylaskia needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Longsword attacks and use Strength Drain once.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage when used one-handed or 16 (2d10 + 5) when used two-handed. Either hit also deals 11 (2d10) necrotic damage.
Strength Drain. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) necrotic damage. If the target lacks immunity to necrotic damage, reduce its Strength by 1d4 until it finishes a short or long rest. The target dies if this reduces its Strength to 0.

name: Polukranos
description: The World Eater is an incarnation of the hydra’s eternal form. Its return portends strife among the gods and danger for Theros.

sections.Traits:
Acidic Blood. After Polukranos takes piercing or slashing damage, each creature within 5 ft. of it takes 10 (3d6) acid damage.
Hold Breath. Polukranos can go without a breath for up to 1 hour.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Polukranos can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Multiple Heads. Polukranos starts with five heads. While it has more than one, it has advantage on saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious. Taking 40 or more damage during a single turn kills one head. Losing every head kills Polukranos. At the end of its own turn, it grows two heads for each head lost since its last turn, unless it has taken at least 40 fire damage since its last turn. It heals 20 HP for each head it regrows.
Reactive Heads. Each head beyond the first grants an extra reaction for opportunity attacks only.
Siege Monster. Polukranos deals double damage to objects and structures.
Wakeful. At least one head remains awake when Polukranos sleeps.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack per living head.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d10 + 7) piercing damage.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 21 Strength save or be pushed up to 20 ft. away from Polukranos.
sections.Legendary actions:
Polukranos has three legendary actions and recovers spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Swipe (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Trampling Charge (3 actions). Move up to 50 ft. in a straight line. Polukranos can pass through spaces occupied by Huge or smaller creatures. The first time Polukranos enters each creature’s space during this move, it can make a Stomp attack against that creature.

name: Returned Drifter
description: A restless escapee from the Underworld who seeks solitude in tombs and necropoleis.

sections.Returned nature: Those who follow the Path of Phenax escape the Underworld as undead. Their lost identities take shape as separate eidolons. Returned hide their blank faces behind gold masks and can form only short-lived new memories. A mask is worth about 100 gp, depending on the metal and workmanship, but many Therans refuse to trade in them.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Turn Resistance. The Returned makes saving throws against effects that turn undead with advantage.
Unreadable Face. Effects that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts cannot affect the Returned. Wisdom (Insight) checks to judge its intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) poison damage.
Sling. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

name: Returned Kakomantis
description: A Returned spellcaster whose fascination with magic survived death.

sections.Returned nature: Those who follow the Path of Phenax escape the Underworld as undead. Their lost identities take shape as separate eidolons. Returned hide their blank faces behind gold masks and can form only short-lived new memories. A mask is worth about 100 gp, depending on the metal and workmanship, but many Therans refuse to trade in them.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Fleeting Anger. Damage dealt to the Returned by another creature gives the Returned advantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.
Turn Resistance. The Returned makes saving throws against effects that turn undead with advantage.
Unreadable Face. Effects that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts cannot affect the Returned. Wisdom (Insight) checks to judge its intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Underworld Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +4 to hit, range 120 ft., one creature. On a hit, the target takes 13 (2d8 + 2) necrotic damage and cannot regain hit points until the start of the Returned’s next turn. If the target is below its hit point maximum, it takes 17 (2d12 + 2) necrotic damage instead. The healing restriction applies in either case.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.
sections.Variant: Use the Returned Palamnite statistics with Underworld Bolt in place of Multiattack. The Shortsword attack remains available.
sections.Source notes: Page 240 lists 13 damage for the normal bolt alongside 2d8 + 2. The standard rounded-down average for those dice is 11. This profile preserves both printed values.
sections.Printed source: Mythic Odysseys of Theros, p. 240, Returned Kakomantis variant. Base Returned Palamnite block on p. 241.

name: Returned Palamnite
description: An enraged Returned drawn to violence. Many serve Tymaret in Odunos.

sections.Returned nature: Those who follow the Path of Phenax escape the Underworld as undead. Their lost identities take shape as separate eidolons. Returned hide their blank faces behind gold masks and can form only short-lived new memories. A mask is worth about 100 gp, depending on the metal and workmanship, but many Therans refuse to trade in them.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Fleeting Anger. Damage dealt to the Returned by another creature gives the Returned advantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.
Turn Resistance. The Returned makes saving throws against effects that turn undead with advantage.
Unreadable Face. Effects that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts cannot affect the Returned. Wisdom (Insight) checks to judge its intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shortsword attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.
sections.Variant: The Returned Kakomantis uses these statistics and replaces Multiattack with Underworld Bolt.

name: Returned Sentry
description: A tireless guard who works with other Returned to defend a necropolis.

sections.Returned nature: Those who follow the Path of Phenax escape the Underworld as undead. Their lost identities take shape as separate eidolons. Returned hide their blank faces behind gold masks and can form only short-lived new memories. A mask is worth about 100 gp, depending on the metal and workmanship, but many Therans refuse to trade in them.
sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Pack Tactics. The Returned gains advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one ally within 5 ft. of the target is not incapacitated.
Turn Resistance. The Returned makes saving throws against effects that turn undead with advantage.
Unreadable Face. Effects that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts cannot affect the Returned. Wisdom (Insight) checks to judge its intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage, or 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage when wielded with two hands for a melee attack. Either way, the attack also deals 7 (2d6) poison damage.
Sling. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

name: Satyr Reveler
description: A celebrant who uses music, dance, or another performance to draw rivals into the festivities.

sections.Traits:
Enthralling Performance. After at least 1 minute of performing, choose up to four humanoids within 60 ft. who watched or listened to the whole performance. Each must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or be charmed, idolizing the satyr and joining its revels. The charm ends after 1 hour, if the target takes damage, if the satyr attacks it, or if it sees the satyr attack or damage one of its allies.
Magic Resistance. The satyr has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Sleepless Reveler. Magic cannot put the satyr to sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Ram attacks or two Shortbow attacks.
Ram. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (2d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

name: Satyr Thornbearer
description: An archer of the Skola Vale who harasses intruders from the woods and disappears into cover.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The satyr has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Sleepless Reveler. Magic cannot put the satyr to sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Ram attacks or three Shortbow attacks.
Ram. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (2d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.
Hail of Arrows (recharges after a short or long rest). The satyr fires one arrow that magically splinters into a 30-ft. cone of missiles. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 14 Dexterity save, taking 17 (5d6) piercing damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Setessan Hoplite
description: A Setessan hunter and soldier who uses woodland cover, coordinated distractions, and poison-treated weapons.

sections.Traits: Pack Tactics. The hoplite gains advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one ally within 5 ft. of the hoplite is not incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks or two Longbow attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.

name: Theran Chimera
description: A wild predator made from several creatures. In Theros, unstable magic and portals to Nyx can spawn new chimeras near one another.

sections.Traits: Spell Turning. The chimera has advantage on saves against spells that target it alone. If it succeeds against a spell of 4th level or lower, the spell affects the caster instead.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Claws attack, one Head attack, and one Tail attack. If the breath weapon has recharged, it can replace Claws or Head.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage on a hit.
Head. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 10 (1d12 + 4) piercing damage on a hit.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Deal 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage on a hit.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Deal 32 (5d12) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Customizing a chimera: Use the base configuration or roll one d4 on each customization table you want to use. Apply the chosen body adjustments and replace the corresponding breath, head, or tail option. Claws remain available in every configuration. Choose which result to keep if two conflict.
sections.Body Composition (d4):
1. Plains Creature. Give it a large lowland body such as a bear or bull. Remove its wings and fly speed. It gains resistance to cold and fire damage.
2. Coast Creature. Give it a coastal or aquatic body such as a heron or shark. It gains a swim speed equal to its walking speed and can breathe air and water.
3. Mountain Creature. Give it a mountain creature’s body such as a ram or dragon. It can fly out of an enemy’s reach without provoking an opportunity attack.
4. Swamp Creature. Give it a swamp or cave creature’s body such as a giant lizard or spider. It gains a climb speed equal to its walking speed and can climb hard surfaces and ceilings without an ability check.
sections.Head Attacks (d4):
1. Bull Horns. If it moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hits with Head on that turn, deal an extra 7 (2d6) piercing damage. A creature hit must also pass a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
2. Shark Bite. Make Head attacks with advantage against creatures below their maximum hit points.
3. Unicorn Horn. Head is magical and deals an extra 4 (1d8) radiant damage.
4. Cockatrice Beak. A creature hit with Head must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or become restrained. It repeats the save at the end of its next turn. A success ends the restraint. A failure petrifies it for 24 hours.
sections.Breath Weapons (d4):
All four alternatives recharge on 5–6.
1. Lightning Breath. Each creature in a line 60 ft. long and 5 ft. wide makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Deal 36 (8d8) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.
2. Tidal Wave Breath. Each creature in a line 60 ft. long and 5 ft. wide makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. A failure deals 27 (5d10) acid damage and knocks the creature prone. A success halves the damage and leaves it standing.
3. Venom Spray. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or become poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned this way, it takes 35 (10d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
4. Necrotic Breath. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or take 31 (7d8) necrotic damage and lose the ability to regain hit points through the end of its next turn.
sections.Tail Attacks (d4):
1. Venomous Tail. The tail deals piercing damage. A creature hit by Tail must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or become poisoned for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
2. Perplexing Tail. Replace the tail with a second head. Multiattack uses Claws and two Head attacks. Use the Head Attacks table to determine the added head. The breath substitution remains available.
3. Shark Tail. When Tail hits a creature, the fin also pushes it up to 10 ft. away.
4. Constricting Tail. Tail also grapples a Large or smaller creature it hits (escape DC 15). That creature is restrained while grappled and the tail stays occupied until it escapes or is released.

name: Triton Master of Waves
description: A sea mage who commands living currents and defends Thassa’s waters with wind, ice, and water weirds.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The triton breathes air and water.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma is the spellcasting ability (save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks). The spells require no material components.
At will. Ray of Frost, as described under Actions.
2/day. Cone of Cold.
1/day each. Fog Cloud, Gust of Wind, Wind Wall.
sections.Bonus actions: Summon Water Weird (recharges after a short or long rest). Magically summon 1d4 water weirds in unoccupied spaces in water within 60 ft. They take their turns immediately after the triton on its initiative count and fight until destroyed. They disappear if the triton dies.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Wave Touch attacks and cast Ray of Frost.
Wave Touch. Melee spell attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 22 (4d10) cold damage on a hit.
Ray of Frost (cantrip). Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. Deal 13 (3d8) cold damage on a hit and reduce the creature’s speed by 10 ft. until the start of the triton’s next turn.
sections.Reactions: Frigid Shield. When a creature the triton can see targets it with an attack, the triton gains 10 temporary hit points. If the attack hits and depletes those temporary hit points, each creature within 5 ft. of the triton takes 9 (2d8) cold damage.

name: Triton Shorestalker
description: A coastal assassin who uses venomous urchin spines to retaliate against threats to triton communities or Thassa’s sacred waters.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The triton breathes air and water.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Wisdom is the spellcasting ability (save DC 12). The spells require no material components.
1/day each. Fog Cloud, Gust of Wind.
sections.Bonus actions: Nimble Escape. On each of its turns, the triton can Disengage or Hide.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Urchin-Spine Shortsword attacks.
Urchin-Spine Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage on a hit. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by the attack is stable and poisoned for 1 hour, even if healed. It is paralyzed while poisoned this way.
Poisoned Spine. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one target. Deal 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage on a hit.

name: Tromokratis
description: A wandering kraken that wrecks fleets and coastal settlements. After Tromokratis toppled the Pyrgnos, Meletis began watching the sea for its return.

sections.Damage immunities: Fire. Also bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. Tromokratis breathes air and water.
Hearts of the Kraken (mythic trait, recharges after a short or long rest). Upon dropping to 0 hit points, Tromokratis stays alive and conscious as its carapace cracks open. Track four hearts separately, two on the chest, one on the back, and one at the base of the tail. Each heart has AC 22 and 100 hit points. Each is immune to all conditions and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Use ability scores of 10 (+0) for any saving throw a heart must make. After Tromokratis finishes a short or long rest, the carapace seals over its hearts and any destroyed hearts regenerate. Destroy all four hearts to kill it.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Tromokratis can turn a failed save into a success.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures.
Spell-Resistant Carapace. It has advantage on saves against spells. Spell attack rolls against it have disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Pincer, one Tail, and one Tentacle Grasp attack.
Pincer. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Deal 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage on a hit. A creature hit is grappled (escape DC 26) and restrained. Tromokratis can target only that creature with Pincer until the grapple ends.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Deal 23 (3d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage on a hit. A creature hit falls prone.
Tentacle Grasp. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one creature. Deal 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage on a hit and grapple it (escape DC 26). If the creature is still grappled at the end of its next turn, Tromokratis throws it up to 60 ft. in a straight line. The creature lands prone and takes 21 (6d6) bludgeoning damage.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 29 (3d12 + 10) piercing damage on a hit. If the target is a Large or smaller creature that Tromokratis has grappled, the Bite also swallows it and ends the grapple. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover from attacks and effects outside the kraken, and takes 42 (12d6) acid damage at the start of each of Tromokratis’s turns. If any single swallowed creature deals at least 50 damage to Tromokratis on one turn, the kraken makes a DC 20 Constitution save at that turn’s end. On a failure it regurgitates all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in spaces within 10 ft. If Tromokratis dies, its restraint ends. A swallowed creature can then spend 15 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, emerging prone.
sections.Legendary actions:
Tromokratis has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Move (1 action). Move up to half its speed.
Tail (1 action). Make one Tail attack.
Bite (3 actions). Make one Bite attack.
sections.Mythic actions:
For 1 hour after Hearts of the Kraken activates, Tromokratis can spend legendary actions on these options while its mythic trait is active.
Rampage (1 action). Make one Tail attack and one Tentacle Grasp attack.
Coral Growth (2 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Deal 13 (3d8) slashing damage on a failure or half on a success. Tromokratis and each of its hearts gain +2 AC until the start of its next turn.
sections.Mythic encounter: For the optional second phase, use Hearts of the Kraken when the kraken drops to 0 HP. Treat the full encounter as two CR 26 creatures and award 180,000 XP if the party defeats Tromokratis after the hearts were exposed.

name: Two-Headed Cerberus
description: A two-headed hound of the dead patrols the mortal bank of the Tartyx River. It tends to let wandering souls pass and chase down the living.

sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, stunned.
sections.Traits:
Aggressive. As a bonus action, move up to the cerberus’s speed toward a hostile creature it can see.
Multiheaded. The cerberus is never surprised and rolls with advantage on saves against being knocked unconscious.
Pack Tactics. The cerberus has advantage on attacks against a creature within 5 ft. of one of its allies, provided that ally isn’t incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Bite attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage and 2 (1d4) fire damage.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Spray molten rock in a 15-ft. cone. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 12 Dexterity save, taking 10 (3d6) fire damage and becoming restrained by hardened rock on a failure. A success halves the damage and prevents the restraint. As an action, a creature can attempt a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check to free itself or a creature it can reach. The rock has AC 17 and 10 hit points, with immunity to fire, poison, and psychic damage.

name: Typhon
description: The soul of a tyrant can spend so long stewing in the Underworld that it emerges as a writhing typhon, hungrier for the living than for the dead it feeds on.

sections.Traits:
Keen Smell. Roll Wisdom (Perception) checks with advantage when they depend on scent.
Regeneration. At the start of its turn, the typhon recovers 20 hit points. Radiant damage turns off this recovery at the start of its next turn. It can die only by starting its turn at 0 hit points without regenerating.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Flurry of Bites, one Constrict, and one Maw attack.
Flurry of Bites. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 35 (8d6 + 7) piercing damage.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one Large or smaller creature. On a hit the target takes 17 (3d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage and is grappled (escape DC 19). While grappled this way, the target is restrained and takes another 17 (3d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. The typhon can hold two creatures this way at once.
Maw. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 26 (3d12 + 7) piercing damage and 19 (3d12) acid damage.

name: Underworld Cerberus
description: A three-headed hound guards the Underworld’s gates, prized souls, and treasures of Erebos. Left to roam, it drives souls into winding stretches of the Underworld and hunts them.

sections.Languages: Understands every language and cannot speak.
sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, stunned.
sections.Traits:
Aggressive. As a bonus action, move up to the cerberus’s speed toward a hostile creature it can see.
Multiheaded. The cerberus is never surprised and rolls with advantage on saves against being knocked unconscious.
Pack Tactics. The cerberus has advantage on attacks against a creature within 5 ft. of one of its allies, provided that ally isn’t incapacitated.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Bite attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage and 3 (1d6) fire damage.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Spray molten rock in a 30-ft. cone. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage and becoming restrained by hardened rock on a failure. A success halves the damage and prevents the restraint. As an action, a creature can attempt a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check to free itself or a creature it can reach. The rock has AC 17 and 20 hit points, with immunity to fire, poison, and psychic damage.

name: Winged Bull
description: A bull with wings carries archons into battle. Some Therans believe these mounts take shape from their riders’ will.

sections.Traits: Charge. After moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature, the bull deals an extra 19 (3d12) piercing damage if it hits that creature with Gore on the same turn.
sections.Actions: Gore. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d12 + 5) piercing damage.
sections.Archon riders: Archon of Falling Stars and Ashen Rider are two Theran archons that can ride a winged bull.

name: Winged Lion
description: This flying lion is one of the usual mounts of a Theran archon. Stories tell of the archon and its lion moving as if they share a mind.

sections.Traits: Pounce. When the lion moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature, then hits it with Claw on the same turn, the target must pass a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone. If the target is prone, the lion can Bite it once as a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage.
sections.Archon riders: Archon of Falling Stars and Ashen Rider are two Theran archons that can ride a winged lion.

name: Woe Strider
description: A long-limbed aberration grows from a soul that severed its ties to destiny. It reads the entrails of its victims in hopes of finding a way back into the weave of fate.

sections.Traits: Antimagic Cone. While its mouth is open, the strider projects the effect of Antimagic Field in a 60-ft. cone. At the start of its turn, it chooses the cone’s direction and whether to open or close its mouth.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks and one Bite. If both claws hit the same creature, it becomes grappled (escape DC 14).
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage and 3 (1d6) psychic damage.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature that is grappled, incapacitated, or restrained. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage and 16 (3d10) psychic damage. For 1 minute, every magic item the target carries loses its magic properties unless it is an artifact.

name: Aartuk Elder
description: A bark-covered warrior spreads five suction-tipped branches around its stalk head. Aartuks roam Wildspace in war bands after beholders destroyed their old homeworld.

sections.Traits: Spider Climb. The aartuk can cross difficult climbing surfaces, including ceilings, without making an ability check.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Branch or Radiant Pellet for each.
Branch. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Radiant Pellet. Ranged spell attack, +4 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (4d4) radiant damage.
sections.Spellcasting (Psionics):
As an action, cast one spell below without components. Wisdom is the spellcasting ability (save DC 12).
1/day each. Calm Emotions, Detect Magic, Sending.
sections.Bonus actions: Tongue (Recharge 6). Choose one Large or smaller creature the aartuk can see within 30 ft. It makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On a failure, it is grappled by the tongue (escape DC 14) and pulled up to 25 ft. toward the aartuk. The tongue can hold only one creature.

name: Aartuk Starhorror
description: A star-shaped plant with a stalk head creeps along the ceilings of captured spelljammers. A starhorror can rally a shaken war band or revive a fallen ally.

sections.Traits: Spider Climb. The aartuk can cross difficult climbing surfaces, including ceilings, without making an ability check.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Branch or Radiant Pellet for each.
Branch. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (2d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.
Radiant Pellet. Ranged spell attack, +2 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (3d4) radiant damage.
sections.Spellcasting (Psionics):
As an action, cast one spell below without components, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability.
1/day each. Revivify, Speak with Plants.
sections.Bonus actions:
Rally the Troops (1/day). The starhorror magically ends the charmed and frightened conditions on itself and any creatures it chooses that it can see within 30 ft.
Tongue (Recharge 6). Choose one Medium or smaller creature the aartuk can see within 30 ft. It makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On a failure, it is grappled by the tongue (escape DC 11) and pulled up to 25 ft. toward the aartuk. The tongue can hold only one creature.
sections.Printed source: Boo’s Astral Menagerie, p. 9. The official errata renamed the Aartuk Priest and updated its skill and spell list.

name: Aartuk Weedling
description: These war-band fighters cling to walls and ceilings on suction cups. A weedling shoots a sticky tongue to pull prey within reach of its branches.

sections.Traits: Spider Climb. The aartuk can cross difficult climbing surfaces, including ceilings, without making an ability check.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Branch or Radiant Pellet for each.
Branch. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Radiant Pellet. Ranged spell attack, +3 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (3d4 + 1) radiant damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Tongue (Recharge 6). Choose one Medium or smaller creature the aartuk can see within 30 ft. It makes a DC 11 Dexterity save. On a failure, it is grappled by the tongue (escape DC 12) and pulled up to 25 ft. toward the aartuk. The tongue can hold only one creature.
sections.Printed source: Boo’s Astral Menagerie, p. 9. The official errata renamed the Aartuk Warrior.

name: Adult Lunar Dragon
description: This moon dragon tunnels through rock and hoards trophies taken from trespassing crews. When it phases, half its body looks like a dark silhouette.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (2/day). The dragon can turn a failed save into a success.
Tunneler. The dragon can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and leaves a tunnel 15 ft. in diameter.
Unusual Nature. The dragon needs no air.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d6 + 6) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) cold damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Cold Breath (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 60-ft. cone make a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure, a creature takes 36 (8d8) cold damage and its speed becomes 0 through the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and its speed stays the same.
sections.Bonus actions: Phase (3/day). The dragon turns partly incorporeal while it maintains Concentration as if on a spell. It gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage for the duration. This form does not let it pass through creatures or solid objects.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 2 legendary actions and refreshes them at the start of its turn. Use at most one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Treacherous Ice (1 action). Pick a point the dragon sees up to 120 ft. away. Ice coats the ground in a 20-ft. radius centered there. It is difficult terrain for creatures other than lunar dragons and lasts 10 minutes or until this option is used again.
sections.Lair: The dragon burrows a cave system inside a barren moon. Hidden chambers hold its hoard, often with spelljamming helms taken from trespassing ships. The caves may shelter springs, vents, wild plants, or life adapted to the moon.
sections.Regional effects:
Choose one or more effects near the lair.
Black Frost. This frost coats the ground and kills ordinary plants within 3 miles of the lair.
Haunting Moan. The dragon chooses whether the moan grows louder or fainter as visitors approach. It is audible within 3 miles.
Moon Devils. Funnels of dust and frost intercept creatures within 1 mile of the lair. Each moon devil uses the Air Elemental stat block, acts independently, and deals cold damage in place of bludgeoning.
The moan and moon devils vanish when the dragon dies. The frost fades over 1d10 days and plants can recover.
sections.Printed source: Boo’s Astral Menagerie, p. 34, with the official Tail attack bonus correction. The lair and regional rules appear on pp. 33–34.

name: Adult Solar Dragon
description: A solar dragon patrols its hunting ground on glowing, cloudlike wings. It hunts kindori and scavvers and may approach a distant ship after mistaking it for prey.

sections.Traits:
Flyby. Leaving an enemy’s reach by flying does not provoke an opportunity attack.
Legendary Resistance (2/day). The dragon can turn a failed save into a success.
Nebulous Thoughts. Magic that attempts to read the dragon’s mind or thoughts fails.
Siege Monster. Double damage against objects and structures.
Unusual Nature. The dragon needs no air.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Tail attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d6 + 7) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) radiant damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
Photonic Breath (Recharge 5–6). Center a 30-ft.-radius sphere on a point the dragon sees up to 180 ft. away. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 19 Constitution save, taking 55 (10d10) radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions and refreshes them at the start of its turn. Use at most one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Burst of Light (2 actions). The dragon emits magical light. Each creature in a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered on the dragon makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is blinded through the end of its next turn.
sections.Lair: A solar dragon nests in the core of a star or within an immense hollow rock in its glare. An obsidian-shelled egg turns translucent just before it hatches.
sections.Regional effects:
Blinding Radiance. A creature inside the star or within 10 miles of it is blinded unless it wears eye protection such as Goggles of Night.
Stellar Incineration. A creature takes 132 (24d10) radiant damage when it enters the star or starts its turn inside it.
sections.Printed source: Boo’s Astral Menagerie, pp. 51–52. The official errata renames Blinding Brilliance to Burst of Light. The adult retains the printed 20-ft. radius and DC 19.

name: Ancient Lunar Dragon
description: A slate-colored moon dragon tunnels through deserted moons. Its lair can turn the land black with frost and send funnels of icy dust after intruders.

sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can turn a failed save into a success.
Tunneler. The dragon can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and leaves a tunnel 20 ft. in diameter.
Unusual Nature. The dragon needs no air.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d6 + 8) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) cold damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Cold Breath (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 90-ft. cone make a DC 21 Constitution save. On a failure, a creature takes 36 (8d8) cold damage and its speed becomes 0 through the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and its speed stays the same.
sections.Bonus actions: Phase (3/day). The dragon turns partly incorporeal while it maintains Concentration as if on a spell. It gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage for the duration. This form does not let it pass through creatures or solid objects.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions and refreshes them at the start of its turn. Use at most one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Treacherous Ice (1 action). Pick a point the dragon sees up to 120 ft. away. Ice coats the ground in a 20-ft. radius centered there. It is difficult terrain for creatures other than lunar dragons and lasts 10 minutes or until this option is used again.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 15 ft. of the dragon makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 12 (1d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage and falls prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
sections.Lair: The dragon burrows a cave system inside a barren moon. Hidden chambers hold its hoard, often with spelljamming helms taken from trespassing ships. The caves may shelter springs, vents, wild plants, or life adapted to the moon.
sections.Regional effects:
Choose one or more effects near the lair.
Black Frost. This frost coats the ground and kills ordinary plants within 6 miles of the lair.
Haunting Moan. The dragon chooses whether the moan grows louder or fainter as visitors approach. It is audible within 6 miles.
Moon Devils. Funnels of dust and frost intercept creatures within 1 mile of the lair. Each moon devil uses the Air Elemental stat block, acts independently, and deals cold damage in place of bludgeoning.
The moan and moon devils vanish when the dragon dies. The frost fades over 1d10 days and plants can recover.

name: Ancient Solar Dragon
description: A sun-born dragon with a long scaled body, luminous wings, and a pair of fins may claim an entire Wildspace system as its hunting ground. It guards the approach to its stellar nest, especially when it has eggs.

sections.Traits:
Flyby. Leaving an enemy’s reach by flying does not provoke an opportunity attack.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can turn a failed save into a success.
Nebulous Thoughts. Magic that attempts to read the dragon’s mind or thoughts fails.
Siege Monster. Double damage against objects and structures.
Unusual Nature. The dragon needs no air.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Tail attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d6 + 9) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) radiant damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (1d8 + 9) bludgeoning damage.
Photonic Breath (Recharge 5–6). Center a 40-ft.-radius sphere on a point the dragon sees up to 240 ft. away. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 23 Constitution save, taking 66 (12d10) radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions and refreshes them at the start of its turn. Use at most one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Burst of Light (2 actions). The dragon emits magical light. Each creature in a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on the dragon makes a DC 23 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is blinded through the end of its next turn.
sections.Lair: A solar dragon nests in the core of a star or within an immense hollow rock in its glare. An obsidian-shelled egg turns translucent just before it hatches.
sections.Regional effects:
Blinding Radiance. A creature inside the star or within 10 miles of it is blinded unless it wears eye protection such as Goggles of Night.
Stellar Incineration. A creature takes 132 (24d10) radiant damage when it enters the star or starts its turn inside it.
sections.Printed source: Boo’s Astral Menagerie, pp. 50–51. The official errata updates CR and HP and renames Blinding Brilliance to Burst of Light.

name: Astral Elf Aristocrat
description: A highborn astral elf who draws on starlight for magic and can call on a solar dragon.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The elf has advantage on saves to avoid or end the charmed condition on itself. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Unusual Nature. The elf has no need to sleep.
Special Equipment. The aristocrat wears Elven Chain.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks and use Radiant Beam if a use remains.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) radiant damage.
Radiant Beam (3/day). Project a 60-ft. line, 5 ft. wide. Each creature in the line makes a DC 16 Constitution save, taking 18 (4d8) radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Spellcasting: As an action, cast one spell using Intelligence. Each is available 1/day. Fly, Mislead, Sending.
sections.Bonus actions:
Starlight Step (3/day). Teleport up to 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space. Anything worn or carried comes along.
Summon Solar Dragon (1/day). The aristocrat has a 50 percent chance to summon a Young Solar Dragon to a visible, unoccupied space. The dragon rolls its own initiative and acts as the aristocrat's ally. It stays for up to 10 minutes. It vanishes if it or the aristocrat dies, or if the aristocrat dismisses it as an action.
sections.Astral Elf society:
Astral elves settled in the Astral Plane to live closer to their gods. They do not age or need sustenance there, and some count their lives in millennia. They often wear ornate visors when meeting outsiders.
Their crews shape Wildspace crystal and hardened plant material into ships such as star moths. Some cities and citadels occupy the petrified bodies of dead gods. Elves travel out of the Deep Astral to raise children and orbit stars to gather starlight for crystal growth and repairs or make pacts with solar dragons.
sections.Xaryxian Empire: Light of Xaryxis features an astral elf empire based in Xaryxispace. Its central star is Xaryxis.
sections.Printed source: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, Boo's Astral Menagerie, p. 11.

name: Astral Elf Commander
description: A commander leads astral elf warriors and often has one or more spelljamming ships under their authority. Teleport can get their troops out of a fight.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The elf has advantage on saves to avoid or end the charmed condition on itself. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Unusual Nature. The elf has no need to sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Longsword or Longbow.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage, or 6 (1d10 + 1) with two hands. Either grip adds 14 (4d6) radiant damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) radiant damage.
sections.Spellcasting: As an action, cast Teleport using Wisdom. Available 2/day.
sections.Astral Elf society:

Elves travel out of the Deep Astral to raise children and orbit stars to gather starlight for crystal growth and repairs or make pacts with solar dragons.
sections.Printed source: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, Boo's Astral Menagerie, p. 12.

name: Astral Elf Honor Guard
description: An elite astral elf soldier charged with protecting important people and places.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The elf has advantage on saves to avoid or end the charmed condition on itself. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Unusual Nature. The elf has no need to sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Longsword or Radiant Ray.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 11 (2d8 + 2) slashing damage, or 13 (2d10 + 2) with two hands. Either grip adds 10 (3d6) radiant damage.
Radiant Ray. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 22 (4d10) radiant damage.
sections.Astral Elf society:

sections.Printed source: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, Boo's Astral Menagerie, p. 12.

name: Astral Elf Star Priest
description: Star priests oversee worship of the elven gods. They often sail with astral elf crews and can pilot spelljamming ships themselves.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The elf has advantage on saves to avoid or end the charmed condition on itself. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Unusual Nature. The elf has no need to sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Morningstar attacks. The priest can replace one attack with Rain of Radiance.
Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 4 (1d8) piercing damage plus 17 (5d6) radiant damage.
Rain of Radiance. Choose a visible creature within 60 ft. It takes 22 (5d8) radiant damage on a failed DC 16 Dexterity save or half as much on a success.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell using Wisdom (save DC 16).
2/day each. Cure Wounds (cast at 8th level), Hold Person.
1/day each. Divination, Sending, Word of Recall.
sections.Bonus actions: Starlight Step (2/day). Teleport up to 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space. Anything worn or carried comes along.

sections.Printed source: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, Boo's Astral Menagerie, p. 13.

name: Astral Elf Warrior
description: Astral elf warriors crew their spelljamming ships and hold strongholds in the Astral Plane. Their weapons strike with radiant starlight.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The elf has advantage on saves to avoid or end the charmed condition on itself. Magic cannot put it to sleep.
Unusual Nature. The elf has no need to sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Longsword or Longbow.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage, or 6 (1d10 + 1) with two hands. Either grip adds 10 (3d6) radiant damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) radiant damage.
sections.Astral Elf society:
Astral elves settled in the Astral Plane to live closer to their gods. They do not age or need sustenance there, and some count their lives in millennia. They often wear ornate visors when meeting outsiders.

name: Autognome
description: A rock gnome builds an autognome in its own likeness, with painted features on a metal shell. Magic gives the machine a mind of its own, and a design flaw can leave it wandering Wildspace without orders.

sections.Traits:
Malfunction. If the autognome survives taking at least 15 damage from one source, roll a d20.
1–10. It keeps working.
11–12. It is incapacitated for 1 minute.
13–14. An arm drops off. It can make one fewer Shock attack until a creature uses an action to put that arm back on.
15–16. Its head falls off and switches off. It is blinded and deafened until a creature spends an action reattaching and reactivating its head.
17–20. The autognome explodes and is destroyed. Each creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 11 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) slashing damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
Unusual Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shock attacks, subject to Malfunction.
Shock. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (2d6) lightning damage.
