Cloud of Dust (encounter trigger). On Gloam’s first turn in combat or when it drops to 0 hit points, it releases a cloud that works like Dust of Sneezing and Choking. Gloam and creatures within 30 ft. that need to breathe make a DC 15 Constitution save. A creature that fails is incapacitated and suffocating. While conscious, it can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns. A success or Lesser Restoration ends the effect. Under the 2014 suffocation rule, a choking creature lasts a number of rounds equal to its Constitution modifier, with a minimum of one round. It then starts its next turn dying at 0 hit points and cannot heal or stabilize while it still cannot breathe.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, chapter 2, p. 93, area B10. Apply the printed changes to the 2014 Cat stat block. Cloud effects follow the 2014 Dust of Sneezing and Choking item.

name: Harengon Brigand
description: A rabbitfolk extortionist who waits along Feywild roads and trails with a small band.

sections.Traits:
Pack Tactics. The brigand has advantage on an attack roll if an ally that is not incapacitated is within 5 ft. of the target.
Standing Leap. The brigand jumps up to 20 ft. horizontally or 10 ft. vertically, even from a standstill.
sections.Actions:
Club. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Sling. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter context: Brigands demand tolls for safe passage and are quick to flee if outnumbered or beaten. At Agdon Longscarf’s camp, 1d4 brigands and 1d4 Harengon Snipers are present at any given time.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix C, p. 235. See chapter 2 for Agdon’s encampment.

name: Harengon Sniper
description: A rabbitfolk marksman who covers a brigand gang from a bluff, a high branch, or concealed ground.

sections.Traits: Standing Leap. The sniper jumps up to 20 ft. horizontally or 10 ft. vertically, even from a standstill.
sections.Actions:
Club. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.
Light Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 320 ft., one target. Ignore cover short of total cover and the usual long-range penalty. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. Immediately after the attack, hit or miss, the sniper can take the Hide action.
sections.Encounter context: Snipers position themselves above trails or behind shelter to cover Harengon Brigands, then Hide as soon as they fire.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix C, p. 235.

name: Iggwilv the Witch Queen
description: Prismeer knows the witch Natasha as Zybilna, the archfey who rules from the Palace of Heart’s Desire.

sections.Languages: Abyssal, Celestial, Common, Draconic, Elvish, Infernal, Sylvan.
sections.Traits:
Boon of Immortality. Magic and other effects cannot age Iggwilv, and old age cannot kill her.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When Iggwilv fails a save, she can choose to pass it.
Magic Resistance. Her Robe of the Archmagi gives her advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Special Equipment. Iggwilv wears an Amulet of the Planes and a Robe of the Archmagi.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Bewitching Bolt attacks.
Bewitching Bolt. Melee or ranged spell attack, +16 to hit, 5-ft. reach or 120-ft. range, one target. A hit deals 25 (5d6 + 8) lightning damage. If the target is a creature, it must pass a DC 22 Wisdom save or be charmed by Iggwilv until her next turn starts.
Abyssal Rift (recharge 5–6). Open a momentary rift with a 20-ft. radius at a point within 120 ft. Creatures in the sphere make a DC 22 Constitution save, taking 40 (9d8) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. Afterward, there is a 50% chance that three Hezrous appear in unoccupied spaces in the sphere. The demons are her allies and act immediately after her. They cannot summon other demons. They remain until they die or she uses an action to dismiss them.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence without material components. Spell save DC 24, spell attacks +16.
At will. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Invisibility, Light, Mage Hand, Message, Prestidigitation, Tasha’s Hideous Laughter.
3/day each. Dispel Magic, Fly, Polymorph.
1/day each. Maze, Telekinesis, Teleport, Wish.
sections.Bonus actions: Fey Step. Iggwilv teleports to an unoccupied space she can see within 30 ft., taking anything she wears or carries.
sections.Reactions: Negate Spell (2/day). When Iggwilv sees a creature within 60 ft. casting a spell, she can interrupt it. A spell using a slot of level 8 or lower fails automatically. A 9th-level spell fails if its caster fails a DC 22 Intelligence save.
sections.Legendary actions:
Iggwilv has three legendary actions and refreshes them when her turn starts. Spend them on one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Witchcraft (1 action). Use Spellcasting or Fey Step.
Dark Speech (2 actions). Choose one or two creatures Iggwilv can see within 60 ft. Each makes a DC 22 Wisdom save. On a failure, it takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage and is frightened of her for 1 minute. An affected creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. A success ends the effect and grants immunity to her Dark Speech for 24 hours.
Fey Beguilement (3 actions). Choose a creature Iggwilv can see within 60 ft. It must pass a DC 22 Charisma save or a fey spirit possesses it and makes it obey her commands. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. A success banishes the spirit and ends the possession.
sections.Palace encounter: The Hourglass Coven used Iggwilv’s Cauldron to freeze her and others in the palace. A frozen creature and its gear cannot be harmed or moved. As an action, touch Iggwilv with a unicorn horn while saying Natasha, her true name, to release her alone. Thaw the whole palace by touching the cauldron with the horn while reciting the Witch Queen’s Cauldron poem, or by shattering the cauldron with a Flame Tongue or Frost Brand weapon. Legend Lore can reveal the poem. Once freed, she can use the horn and poem to thaw the palace.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, chapter 5, pp. 173–174, ballroom P22, and pp. 204–206. Stat block on p. 205.

name: Jabberwock
speed: 30 ft., climb 30 ft., fly 60 ft., swim 30 ft.
description: A lone dragonlike hunter that stalks old forests and ruins. It can run upright or on all fours and fires beams from its eyes.

sections.Damage vulnerabilities: Slashing damage from a Vorpal Sword.
sections.Traits:
Confusing Burble. The jabberwock burbles while it is not incapacitated. A creature that starts its turn within 30 ft. and can hear it must make a DC 18 Charisma save. On a failure, it has no reactions until its next turn starts, and rolls 1d4 for its current turn. On 1–2, it does nothing. On 3, it only spends all its movement in a random direction. On 4, it makes one melee attack against a random visible creature in reach, or does nothing if none is in reach.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When the jabberwock fails a save, it can choose to pass it.
Regeneration. The jabberwock heals 10 hit points when its turn starts. Any slashing damage shuts off the healing at the start of its next turn. It dies only if it starts a turn at 0 hit points and does not regenerate.
Uncanny Tracker. It can track creatures it wounded within the last 24 hours and knows the direction and distance to its quarry as long as they share a plane.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Rend attacks.
Rend. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, 10-ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 21 (3d10 + 5) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, 15-ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Fiery Gaze (recharge 5–6). The jabberwock projects fire from its eyes in a line 120 ft. long and 5 ft. wide. Creatures in the line make a DC 18 Dexterity save, taking 31 (7d8) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. The jabberwock cannot use this action while blinded.
sections.Legendary actions:
The jabberwock refreshes its three legendary actions when its turn starts. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make one Tail attack.
Rend Attack (2 actions). Make one Rend attack.
Wing Attack (3 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 18 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 8 (1d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage and falls prone.
sections.Hunting and return: The jabberwock attacks its chosen prey until it kills it, the prey escapes, or the jabberwock dies. After one dies, another appears in 3d8 years within 1,000 miles of the place it died.
sections.Palace encounter: The jabberwock sleeps around Iggwilv’s Cauldron in P22. Loud noise, an attack against it, or disturbing the cauldron wakes it. It follows prey or music out of the palace. If the great owl Bloodybeak does not attack it as soon as it leaves, it hunts for 1d6 + 2 hours before returning. Food may distract it long enough to slip away. It is friendly to Iggwilv the Witch Queen and hostile to others. Snicker-Snock, the Vorpal Sword in P50, exploits its damage vulnerability.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix C, p. 236. See chapter 5, ballroom P22, Beware the Jabberwock, and vault P50 for the palace encounter.

name: Jingle Jangle
description: A friendly key collector who wears her finds on a jingling coat and fights with a flail made of padlocks.

sections.Traits: Nimble Escape. On each of her turns, she can take Disengage or Hide as a bonus action.
sections.Actions: Flail of Locks. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 7 (3d4) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter context: Jingle Jangle lives on Telemy Hill and always refers to herself in the third person. Bavlorna’s bargain traded her fear of being trapped by a locked door for a compulsion to collect keys. Harengon Brigands recently roughed her up and stole her truffles. She willingly gives visitors the silver key to Sir Talavar’s cage.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, chapter 2, pp. 70–71. Use the 2014 Goblin with the stated alignment and Flail of Locks replacing both weapon attacks.

name: Kelek
description: Kelek founded the League of Malevolence and wants to take Ringlerun’s Staff of Power. He makes a show of ruthlessness and falls back on magic when threatened.

sections.Traits: Special Equipment. Kelek wears Bracers of Defense and starts with a fully charged Staff of Striking (10 charges). Each dawn, the staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges. When the last charge is spent, roll a d20. On a 1, it becomes an ordinary quarterstaff.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using any combination of Sorcerer’s Bolt and Staff of Striking. Kelek can cast one spell from Spellcasting in place of one attack.
Sorcerer’s Bolt. Melee or ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. A hit deals 13 (2d12) force damage.
Staff of Striking. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. A hit deals 8 (1d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage, or 9 (1d8 + 5) if wielded with two hands. On a hit, spend up to three charges to add 3 (1d6) force damage per charge.
Fiery Explosion (Recharge 4–6). Choose a point Kelek can see within 120 ft. The point erupts in magical fire. Every creature in a 20-ft.-radius sphere around it makes a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw. It takes 35 (10d6) fire damage on a failure, or half on a success.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell using Charisma (save DC 14).
At will. Light, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation.
1/day each. Dominate Beast, Fly, Mirror Image, Web.
sections.Reactions: Arcane Defense (3/day). When an attack hits Kelek, an invisible barrier adds 5 to his AC through the end of his next turn. Apply the bonus to the triggering attack as well.
sections.Combat notes: Use Arcane Defense when Kelek’s low AC leaves him exposed. He uses Fiery Explosion whenever practical, even when allies are in the blast.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 219.

name: Kettlesteam the Kenku
description: A kenku warlock disrupts the Witchlight Carnival to learn why she lost contact with her patron Zybilna. She passes among the visitors using Disguise Self and speaks in the voice she stole from Candlefoot.

sections.Languages: Understands Auran and Common. She speaks through Mimicry.
sections.Traits: Mimicry. She can reproduce voices and any other sounds she has heard. A listener needs a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Insight) check to recognize an imitation.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Dagger attacks.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
Twilight Sleep (2/day). Choose one creature she can see within 10 ft. Magical gas forces a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature is unconscious for 1 minute. Damage wakes it immediately, as does another creature using an action to shake or slap it awake.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell using Charisma (save DC 13).
At will. Disguise Self, Friends, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
1/day each. Bestow Curse, Faerie Fire, Speak with Animals.
sections.Encounter notes: After an hour searching the carnival, a character can see through her disguise with a successful DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check. She flees to break line of sight and may talk to adventurers who say they are investigating the carnival. Her pact prevents her from entering Prismeer. She presses Mister Witch and Mister Light for answers and asks adventurers to find out what happened to Zybilna. Untie the thorny stem around her cornhusk doll to restore Candlefoot’s voice. A successful DC 12 Charisma (Intimidation or Persuasion) check persuades her to hand over the doll.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 52.

name: Living Doll
description: A spiteful spirit hides inside a toy or stuffed animal. The doll torments people who doubt themselves and uses laughter and psychic pain to fend off attackers.

sections.Traits:
False Appearance. If the doll is motionless when combat starts, it rolls initiative with advantage. A creature that has never seen it move or act needs a successful DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize that it is animate.
Regeneration. The doll regains 5 hit points at the start of its turn. Fire or psychic damage prevents this healing at the start of its next turn. It is destroyed only if it begins its turn at 0 hit points and fails to regenerate.
Unusual Nature. The doll needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Grabby Hands. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, one creature within reach 5 ft. A hit grapples the creature (escape DC 6). While grappled this way, the creature takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns. The doll can grapple only one creature at a time.
sections.Bonus actions: Cackle (Recharge 4–6). Choose one or two creatures the doll can see within 30 ft. A target that hears the doll must make a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw. Intelligence 4 or lower makes the save an automatic success. On a failure, it takes 5 (2d4) psychic damage and is incapacitated by laughter for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds on any of those saves is immune to this doll’s Cackle for 24 hours.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 238.

name: Mercion
description: A protective cleric of Valor’s Call. Mercion finds beauty in truth and follows that principle in place of a deity.

sections.Armor: Plate armor. Use her printed AC 19.
sections.Traits: Special Equipment. Mercion wields a +1 Quarterstaff.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Divine Radiance attack and one +1 Quarterstaff attack. Mercion can cast one spell from Spellcasting in place of either attack.
Divine Radiance. Melee or ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. A hit deals 13 (3d8) radiant damage.
+1 Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack with the printed +4 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, or 7 (1d8 + 3) if wielded with two hands.
Radiant Fire (Recharge 5–6). Pick a point Mercion can see within 120 ft. The point erupts in magical radiance. Each creature in a 20-ft.-radius sphere around it makes a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. It takes 28 (8d6) radiant damage on a failure, or half on a success.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one spell using Wisdom (save DC 13).
At will. Light, Spare the Dying.
2/day each. Command, Create Food and Water, Cure Wounds, Faerie Fire, Hold Person, Revivify.
1/day. Death Ward.
sections.Combat notes: Mercion heals from behind her armor. She uses Radiant Fire only when the blast is clear of allies and bystanders. Otherwise she favors Hold Person or Divine Radiance.
sections.Printing note: The stat block is on printed p. 225. Some indexes list p. 224. The printed stat block lists AC 19 and +4 to hit with the +1 Quarterstaff.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 225.

name: Mister Light
description: The flamboyant Witchlight Carnival emcee once went by Urmius Umbrage. He left a wealthy Shadowfell family to run the carnival with Mister Witch.

sections.Damage vulnerabilities: Lightning while holding the Witchlight Vane.
sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, deafened, petrified, stunned while attuned to the Witchlight Vane.
sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. Light has advantage on saves against being charmed. Magic cannot put him to sleep.
Special Equipment. Light carries and is attuned to the Witchlight Vane. He can wield it as a finesse weapon.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Witchlight Vane attacks.
Witchlight Vane. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) radiant damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
While carrying the Witchlight Vane, use an action to cast one spell with Charisma (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). No spell components are needed.
At will. Dancing Lights, Polymorph, Ray of Frost. After casting Polymorph, roll a d8. On a 3 or 8, Light loses access to Polymorph until the next dawn.
sections.Bonus actions: Blessing of the Raven Queen (1/day). Teleport up to 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space. Light takes all worn or carried equipment with him, looks ghostly, and has resistance to all damage until the start of his next turn.
sections.Encounter notes: Light and Mister Witch want Zybilna back. Their pact gives the Hourglass Coven permission to steal from unticketed guests. Use the Witchlight Vane’s Sense Mood to find the happiest creature on the carnival grounds as an action.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 26.
sections.Printing note: Use the published +5 to hit and 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning for Light’s attack. The Witchlight Vane’s separate item entry lists a generic magic weapon bonus.

name: Mister Witch
description: The Witchlight Carnival’s reserved co-owner used to tend a clock tower in Gloomwrought under the name Naeryx Krumple. His pocket watch can pack up the carnival or set it in motion.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. Witch has advantage on saves against being charmed. Magic cannot put him to sleep.
Special Equipment. Witch carries and is attuned to the Witchlight Watch.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Cane attacks.
Cane. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 6 (1d12) necrotic damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
While carrying the Witchlight Watch, use an action to cast one spell with Intelligence (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). No spell components are needed.
At will. Fire Bolt, Invisibility, Message. After casting Invisibility, roll a d8. On a 3 or 8, Witch loses access to Invisibility until the next dawn.
sections.Bonus actions: Blessing of the Raven Queen (1/day). Teleport up to 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space. Witch takes all worn or carried equipment with him, looks ghostly, and has resistance to all damage until the start of his next turn.
sections.Encounter notes: Witch and Mister Light keep the carnival running under the Hourglass Coven’s pact. The Witchlight Watch lets Witch start a one-hour magical setup or takedown as an action while he and the carnival are on the same plane. This moves the carnival’s objects and leaves creatures free to move safely.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 25.

name: Molliver
description: A quick-witted thief in Valor’s Call, Molliver gives most of their spoils to people in need. They often act first and count on friends to get them out of trouble.

sections.Traits:
Evasion. If a Dexterity save would allow half damage, Molliver takes none on a success and half on a failure. This ability does not work while incapacitated.
Special Equipment. Molliver wears +1 Leather Armor and Boots of Levitation.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks in any combination of Dagger and Shortsword.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage. Add 7 (2d6) piercing damage if Molliver has advantage on the attack or the target is within 5 ft. of one of Molliver’s allies.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, one creature within reach 5 ft. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage. Add 7 (2d6) piercing damage if Molliver has advantage on the attack or the target is within 5 ft. of one of Molliver’s allies.
Levitate. As an action while wearing the Boots of Levitation, cast Levitate on Molliver only.
sections.Reactions: Uncanny Dodge. Molliver takes half the damage from one attack if they can see the attacker.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 226.

name: Paper Bird
description: Endelyn folds enchanted writing paper into small winged couriers. Her birds can cut with their paper edges and carry letters to the other hags of the Hourglass Coven.

sections.Traits: Keen Sight. The bird makes Wisdom (Perception) checks that depend on sight with advantage.
sections.Actions: Sharp Edges. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 1 slashing damage.
sections.Motherhorn couriers: In area M20, three birds await release in a latched cage. They are hostile toward creatures outside the Hourglass Coven. An open cage releases them within seconds to carry out their deliveries. If a recipient is unreachable, including on another plane, that bird burns up as it launches. To recover a message, reach into the cage and use an action to grapple a bird. Success breaks the enchantment and leaves a folded letter. Loose enchanted paper can be caught as an action with a DC 10 Dexterity check. Folding that sheet into a flying bird takes 1 minute and a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.
sections.Base stat block: This encounter uses the 2014 Hawk rules, with the type, defenses and attack changes included above.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, ch. 4, p. 166 (area M20).

name: Raezil
description: Raezil Uthemar is a high elf from a family with ties to the Summer Court. She serves Zybilna as a spy in the courts of other archfey.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. Raezil rolls saves against being charmed with advantage, and magic cannot put her to sleep.
Sneak Attack (once per turn). A weapon hit deals 7 (2d6) extra damage if she had advantage on the attack roll. It also deals this extra damage if the target is within 5 ft. of one of her allies who is not incapacitated, provided she did not roll with disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Hand Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Cunning Action. On her turn, Raezil can Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a bonus action.
sections.Palace encounter: In the throne room (P31), Raezil begins petrified by Kelek’s cockatrices. Once magic ends the condition, the Feywild’s rule of reciprocity binds her to help her rescuers with their outstanding quests. She knows Zybilna as her employer and does not know the name Iggwilv.
sections.Base stat block: The adventure uses the 2014 Spy with the elf’s languages, darkvision and Fey Ancestry.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, ch. 5, p. 193 (area P31).

name: Ringlerun
description: This wizard of Valor’s Call won a Staff of Power from a marid in a sunken tomb. Kelek wants the staff and needs a unicorn horn to release its owner from the palace’s temporal stasis.

sections.Armor: AC includes the Staff of Power’s bonus.
sections.Traits: Special Equipment. The Staff of Power holds up to 20 charges and recovers 2d8 + 4 spent charges at dawn. If Ringlerun spends the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the staff keeps its +2 bonus to weapon attack and damage rolls but loses its other properties. On a 20, it recovers 1d8 + 2 charges.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any mix of Staff of Power and Freezing Ray. One can be replaced with a use of Spellcasting.
Staff of Power. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) if used two-handed. Spend 1 charge on a hit for 3 (1d6) extra force damage.
Freezing Ray. Ranged spell attack, +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one creature. A hit deals 27 (6d8) cold damage.
Staff Spell. While holding the staff, cast one spell by spending its listed charges. Spell save DC 14, spell attack +8. 1 charge: Magic Missile or Ray of Enfeeblement. 2: Levitate. 5: Cone of Cold (8d8 cold), Fireball (10d6 fire), Hold Monster, Lightning Bolt (10d6 lightning), or Wall of Force. 6: Globe of Invulnerability.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 14).
At will: Light, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation.
3/day each: Charm Person, Detect Magic, Sleep.
1/day each: Banishment, Dispel Magic, Fly, Knock.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix B, p. 227. Palace context in ch. 5, area P31.

name: Selenelion Twin
description: Gleam and Glister are high elf acrobats from the Witchlight Carnival. Gleam wears a crescent moon mask and Glister wears a sun mask. Use this profile for either twin, with only her own ray attack.

sections.Traits:
Fey Ancestry. The twin makes saves against being charmed with advantage, and magic cannot put her to sleep.
Regeneration. At the start of her turn, the twin recovers 5 HP if both sisters are alive and within 60 ft. of each other. She dies only if she starts her turn with 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
Twin Bond. While both are alive and on the same plane, each can sense how the other feels.
sections.Actions:
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage.
Moon Ray (Gleam only, 3/day). Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. A hit deals 12 (2d8 + 3) radiant damage. The target makes a DC 13 Wisdom save or becomes a Bat as with Polymorph for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Sun Ray (Glister only, 3/day). Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. A hit deals 12 (2d8 + 3) radiant damage. The target makes a DC 13 Wisdom save or is blinded for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Twin Sight (recharges after a short or long rest). The twin sees through her sister’s eyes for up to 1 minute while both are alive and on the same plane. The effect requires concentration as on a spell.
sections.Motherhorn encounter: Endelyn Moongrave cut off Gleam’s shadow with magic scissors and keeps Glister as a prisoner. When reunited, the twins plan to leave via the Fey Beacons and return to the Witchlight Carnival.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix C, p. 241. Encounter context in ch. 4, Yon.

name: Sir Talavar
description: A violet faerie dragon who serves the Summer Queen. Bavlorna caught him in an enchanted silver cage before he could report the Hourglass Coven’s takeover of Prismeer.

sections.Traits:
Limited Telepathy. Talavar can speak telepathically with other faerie dragons within 60 ft.
Magic Resistance. He makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
sections.Actions:
+1 Tiny Sword. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d4 + 6) piercing damage.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 1 piercing damage.
Euphoria Breath (recharge 5–6). Choose one creature within 5 ft. It must pass a DC 11 Wisdom save or lose its reactions for 1 minute. At the start of each of its turns, roll a d6. On 1–4, it takes no action or bonus action and spends all movement going in a random direction. On 5–6, it stays put and can only attempt the DC 11 Wisdom save, which ends the effect on success.
sections.Bonus actions: Superior Invisibility. Talavar and anything he wears or carries become magically invisible. This lasts until his concentration ends, as if concentrating on a spell.
sections.Innate spellcasting: Talavar uses Charisma (spell save DC 13) and needs no material components. As a violet faerie dragon, he knows the spells of his current color and all earlier colors. Each is available 1/day: Dancing Lights, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Color Spray, Mirror Image, Suggestion, Major Image, Hallucinatory Terrain, and Polymorph.
sections.Silver birdcage: While locked inside, Talavar cannot cast spells. His Euphoria Breath still works. The cage cannot be destroyed, and its lock cannot be picked. Jingle Jangle has the key. Knock or similar magic can also open it. If released, Talavar offers his tiny sword and departs to report to his queen.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, ch. 2, p. 69 (Slanty Tower). Base violet faerie dragon rules from Monster Manual (2014), p. 133.

name: Skabatha Nightshade
description: Granny Nightshade rules Thither from Loomlurch. Her skin resembles rotten bark beneath her toymaker’s disguise, and the windup key in her back slows as her temper worsens.

sections.Traits:
Boon of Immortality. Effects cannot age Skabatha, and old age cannot kill her.
Forgetfulness. The first creature Skabatha sees after a long rest becomes invisible to her. She cannot recall seeing it, and even her truesight cannot reveal it to her. This lasts until the end of her next long rest.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 25 (6d6 + 4) poison damage in her normal form, or 2 (1d4) poison damage when she is Tiny.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell, using Wisdom (spell save DC 14) without material components.
At will: Detect Magic, Druidcraft, Speak with Animals.
2/day each: Polymorph, Remove Curse, Speak with Plants.
1/day each: Awaken (cast as an action), Plane Shift (self only).
sections.Bonus actions: Alter Size. Skabatha shrinks to Tiny (4–8 inches tall) or returns to normal. If the available space cannot hold her normal form, she grows only as large as will fit. Worn and carried equipment changes with her. While Tiny, she deals the reduced Claw damage above, rolls Dexterity (Stealth) checks with advantage, and rolls Strength checks and Strength saves with disadvantage. All other statistics stay the same.
sections.Hourglass Coven shared spells: When Skabatha, Bavlorna Blightstraw and Endelyn Moongrave are all within 30 ft. of one another, any one of them can use an action to cast Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Finger of Death, Glibness, Locate Creature, or Mass Suggestion. Shared spells require no material components and use save DC 14. Each is available once to the coven as a whole, with all uses restored at dawn.
sections.Loomlurch encounter: When her clockwork key stops, Skabatha lashes out at anything nearby until a victory or other good turn lifts her mood. Each time she flies into such a rage, 1d3 redcaps sprout in the garden at L15. The key is part of her body and cannot be removed while she lives. Loomlurch’s other defenders try to capture intruders alive. If the fight goes badly, Skabatha rides her Flying Rocking Horse to Motherhorn. Bavlorna Blightstraw goes there too if present. If Skabatha dies, a beetle tells her killer that Endelyn Moongrave can be killed permanently during a real or symbolic eclipse.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix B, pp. 215 and 218. Loomlurch procedures in ch. 3, p. 114.

name: Detached Shadow
description: A detached silhouette brought to life by the Scissors of Shadow Snipping. Endelyn uses these shadows as spies.

sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained.
sections.Traits:
Amorphous. It can move through openings as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Shadow Stealth. In dim light or darkness, its Stealth bonus is +6 and it can Hide as a bonus action.
Sunlight Weakness. In sunlight, its attacks, ability checks, and saving throws have disadvantage.
sections.Actions: Strength Drain. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) necrotic damage and reduces the target’s Strength score by 1d4. If the score reaches 0, the target falls unconscious. A short or long rest restores the lost Strength and ends unconsciousness caused by this drain.
sections.Shadow Snipping: Use this stat block when the wielder of the Scissors of Shadow Snipping releases the shadow to act independently. The shadowless creature is cursed. Ending that curse or reducing the detached shadow to 0 hit points makes the detached shadow vanish and restores the creature’s ordinary shadow.
sections.Motherhorn theater: Eleven detached shadows in M10 are invisible while hiding in the shadows of the scenery. Moving the scenery reveals them. They attack only when threatened.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, pp. 30, 140, 159, and 213 (Scissors of Shadow Snipping and adventure encounters), with the Shadow from Monster Manual (2014), p. 269.

name: Skylla
description: A warlock of Baba Yaga also known as Charmay. A warning from Endelyn drove her out of the League of Malevolence and into Motherhorn.

sections.Traits: Special Equipment. Her Eldritch Staff holds up to 10 charges and restores 1d6 + 4 spent charges at dawn. When she spends its final charge, roll a d20. A 1 destroys the staff.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Eldritch Staff attacks. Skylla can substitute Spellcasting for one attack.
Eldritch Staff. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage, or 4 (1d8) with two hands. On the hit, Skylla can spend up to 3 staff charges. Each adds 4 (1d8) lightning damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell with Charisma (save DC 13), with no material components.
1/day each. Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Faerie Fire, Fly, Hypnotic Pattern, Invisibility, Mage Armor.
sections.Reactions: Eldritch Escape. When Skylla takes damage, she can spend 3 staff charges. She becomes invisible and teleports with her equipment to a visible unoccupied space within 60 ft. The invisibility ends at the start of her next turn or earlier if she attacks, casts a spell, or deals damage.
sections.Motherhorn workshop: The command word nocturli animates the eight props in M12. Use Animated Armor for each, with AC 19 for the stovepipe and gate, AC 15 for the coffin and wooden owlbear, AC 13 for the plaster elf king and cake, and AC 11 for the boar mannequin and stuffed golem. While they fight, Skylla takes Golmo and retreats toward the darklings in M2. If forced to surrender, she can say alfarian to return the props to normal.
sections.Printing note: The printed block gives AC 13 with Mage Armor and ends Eldritch Escape when Skylla deals damage. The local index omits both details.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, pp. 160 and 220 (M12 and Appendix B).

name: Squirt the Oilcan
description: A rusty oilcan animated during a Feywild party. Refill it with slippery boggle oil and it can guide the party from Thither to Yon.

sections.Traits:
False Appearance. When combat starts, Squirt rolls initiative with advantage if it is motionless. Anyone who has yet to see it move or act needs a DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize that it is animate.
Unusual Nature. Squirt needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Boggle Oil (3 applications). Spend one application to spill a 10-ft. square of slippery, nonflammable oil on the ground within 5 ft. The oil is difficult terrain and lasts 1 hour. A creature that enters it or starts its turn there makes a DC 11 Dexterity save or falls prone. Boggles are unaffected.
sections.Refilling the oilcan: Squirt has too little oil to use the action when found at Little Oak. It stores up to three applications of slippery Boggle oil indefinitely. A character can spend 1 minute collecting 1d3 applications from a Boggle’s slippery puddle before it evaporates. A friendly Boggle supplies three applications for a small gift. An indifferent Boggle expects a more valuable gift. A hostile Boggle cooperates only if captured and compelled.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, pp. 110 and 119 (Squirt and the Boggle Oil sidebar).

name: Strongheart
description: The founder of Valor’s Call, a paladin who prefers to take villains alive. He carries the sentient longsword Steel.

sections.Traits: Special Equipment. Steel is a sentient, lawful good +2 longsword.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Steel attacks.
Steel. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 9 (1d10 + 4) with two hands. Once on each of his turns when he hits, Strongheart can make the blade flare and leave the target blinded until the start of his next turn.
Revivify (recharges at dawn). Strongheart casts Revivify by touching the target with Steel.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell with Charisma (save DC 13).
3/day each. Command, Detect Evil and Good, Protection from Evil and Good.
1/day each. Lesser Restoration, Remove Curse, Zone of Truth.
sections.Reactions: Protect Another. When an attacker Strongheart can see attacks another creature within 5 ft. of him, Strongheart can impose disadvantage on that roll if he is carrying his shield.
sections.Palace rescue: Strongheart is frozen in time with 20 hit points, 60 ft. above the storm vortex. As an action, free him by touching him with a unicorn horn and speaking his true name. Secure him with a rope first or catch him with a DC 15 Strength check to prevent the fall. He weighs 240 pounds with his gear. Steel cannot be removed, communicate, or cast Revivify while frozen.
sections.Storm vortex: A creature that falls into the vortex takes 18 (4d8) force damage, then takes it again at the start of its turns until it escapes. Its speed is 0 and cannot be increased, and others cannot see it. Ending a turn in the vortex with 0 hit points destroys the creature and scatters its remains and gear across the planes. An ally can lower a rope and pull it out.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, pp. 181, 201, 214, and 228 (P13, P47, Steel, and Appendix B).

name: Swarm of Campestris
classification: Medium swarm of Tiny plants, unaligned
description: A cluster of singing mushrooms with speckled red or purple caps. They mimic any song they hear and dance around musicians.

sections.Languages: Understands Common. It speaks only through Mimicry.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, stunned.
sections.Traits:
Mimicry. Each campestri can imitate a voice or song it has heard, in a nasal falsetto.
Swarm. The swarm and another creature can share space. The swarm fits through any gap an individual Campestri can pass through. It cannot heal or gain temporary hit points.
sections.Actions:
Head Butts. Melee weapon attack, +0 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (4d4) bludgeoning damage, or 5 (2d4) while the swarm is at half its maximum hit points or less.
Spores (1/day). Spores spread 20 ft. around the swarm, including around corners. Constructs, Elementals, Plants, and Undead are unaffected. Each other creature in the area makes a DC 10 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is incapacitated and its speed is halved for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending both effects on a success.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 232 (Appendix C).

name: Thinnings
description: Zybilna’s stick-thin butler. He was away when the palace was frozen and now spies on the League of Malevolence.

sections.Traits: Sneak Attack (once per turn). A weapon hit deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage if Thinnings had advantage on the attack. He can also deal the extra damage if one of his allies is within 5 ft. of the target, that ally is not incapacitated, and the attack does not have disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Hand Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Change Shape. Thinnings can flatten himself like parchment or return to normal. While flat he can slide beneath doors, roll himself up, or fold himself between the pages of a book.
sections.Bonus actions: Cunning Action. Thinnings can Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a bonus action on his turn.
sections.Servants’ quarters: Thinnings usually hides under or behind a dresser in P15. Passive Wisdom (Perception) 14 spots him during a quick look. A thorough search finds him. A character can coax him into the open by reciting Demitasse’s rhyme and telling him a secret he does not already know. He knows how to end temporal stasis and where the Jabberwock and League of Malevolence are.
sections.Printing note: The printed rules appear at area P15 on p. 182. The local index gives 15 as the page.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, p. 182 (P15), with the Spy from Monster Manual (2014), p. 349.

name: Tin Soldier
description: A three-foot suit of armor with an infantryman’s shape. It follows Skabatha’s orders and rushes to investigate disturbances.

sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Antimagic Susceptibility. An Antimagic Field leaves the soldier incapacitated while it stays inside. If targeted with Dispel Magic, it must make a Constitution save against the caster’s spell save DC or fall unconscious for 1 minute.
False Appearance. While motionless, the soldier looks like an ordinary suit of armor.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Loomlurch barracks: Six soldiers emerge from L7 when they hear nearby combat, or when Skabatha Nightshade or Pincushion calls. Four others patrol L8 and L12. The six march with an Animated Drum. A soldier that can hear it gains +2 to its damage rolls. If the drum is destroyed, soldiers within 60 ft. are stunned until the end of their next turn.
sections.Animated Drum: Small animated object, AC 16, 25 HP, speed 30 ft., blindsight 30 ft., no effective attacks. Str 6, Dex 14, Con 10, Int 3, Wis 3, Cha 1. Immune to poison and psychic damage and the blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions. Its beat carries 60 ft.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, pp. 115 and 122 (Skabatha’s minions and L7), with the Animated Armor from Monster Manual (2014), p. 19. The adventure changes the armor’s size to Small and gives it 27 (6d6 + 6) hit points.

name: Treant Sapling
description: A young, talking treant. Northwind, a Prismeer native, works at the Witchlight Carnival and uses his gift to clear room for the wagons.

sections.Traits: False Appearance. The motionless sapling rolls initiative with advantage. A creature that has never seen it act or move needs a successful DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to tell that the tree is animate.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d10 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d10 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Animate Trees (1/day). Choose one or two visible trees within 60 ft. Each becomes an ally using the Awakened Tree stat block and cannot speak. The animation lasts up to one day. It ends for a tree if it dies, the sapling dies, or they move more than 120 ft. apart. The sapling can also end a tree’s animation as a bonus action. The tree takes root again if possible.
sections.Witchlight Carnival: Northwind greets visitors at the dragonfly ride. Red, his awakened squirrel companion, uses the Weasel stat block with Intelligence 10 and speaks Common.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, ch. 1, p. 36. Use the Monster Manual (2014), p. 317, for the animated tree.

name: Warduke
description: A scarred mercenary who conceals his face behind his dread helm. He guards Kelek for pay and has little interest in the League of Malevolence’s schemes.

sections.Traits: Special Equipment. Warduke has a Dread Helm and a Flame Tongue Longsword.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Flame Tongue and Dagger.
Flame Tongue. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage one-handed or 8 (1d10 + 3) with both hands. Add 7 (2d6) fire damage while the sword burns.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Bonus actions:
Flaming Blade. Ignite or extinguish the longsword. While it burns, it sheds bright light for 40 ft. and dim light for 40 ft. beyond that.
Second Wind (recharges after a short or long rest). Recover 13 HP.
sections.Palace encounter: At the throne room in area P31, Warduke stands beside Kelek with his sword already aflame. Treasure worth at least 2,500 gp buys his service for the remainder of the adventure. While he is with the party, Kelek and Zargash leave them alone. He can be persuaded to destroy Iggwilv’s Cauldron with his sword.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix B, p. 221, with the throne-room encounter in ch. 5, area P31.

name: Will-o'-Wells
description: The lights above Hither’s wells are drowned spirits. They will help travelers who promise to oppose Bavlorna, whose flood killed them.

sections.Languages: The languages it knew in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Acid, cold, fire, necrotic, and thunder. Also bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, poisoned, prone, restrained, and unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Ephemeral. It cannot carry or wear anything.
Incorporeal Movement. It moves through creatures and objects as difficult terrain. Ending its turn in an object deals it 5 (1d10) force damage.
Variable Illumination. Choose a radius from 5 to 20 ft. It sheds bright light within that radius and dim light for the same distance beyond it. It can change the radius as a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Shock. Melee spell attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 9 (2d8) lightning damage.
Invisibility. The spirit and its light become invisible until it attacks, uses Consume Life, or stops concentrating as if on a spell.
Magic Boon (recharges after a long rest). Grant a boon to one visible creature within 5 ft. that is not undead. Once within the next 24 hours, the recipient can roll a d4 and add it to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw. A creature can hold only one such boon at a time.
sections.Bonus actions: Consume Life. Choose one visible, living creature within 5 ft. that has 0 HP. It dies on a failed DC 10 Constitution save against this magic. If it dies, the spirit recovers 10 (3d6) HP.
sections.Hither wells: Each well is home to 1d4 spirits. They cannot travel more than a few hundred yards from their well. They ask visitors their intentions and offer a boon to those who promise to oppose Bavlorna Blightstraw.
sections.Base stat block: The adventure uses the 2014 Will-o’-Wisp rules, changes its alignment to chaotic good, and adds Magic Boon and the well’s travel limit.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, ch. 2, pp. 61–62, using Monster Manual (2014), p. 301.

name: Witchlight Hand (Medium)
description: Medium carnival worker with its own specialized trade. Mister Witch and Mister Light train the hands in small spells and issue pixie dust for the work.

sections.Traits: Secret Expertise. Choose one additional skill bonus for the hand: Acrobatics +6, Animal Handling +5, Arcana +5, Athletics +4, Medicine +5, or Performance +5.
sections.Actions:
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Pixie Dust (1/day). Give the hand or another visible creature within 5 ft. a 30-ft. flying speed for 1 minute. If it is still in the air when the effect expires, it descends safely, takes no falling damage, and lands on its feet.
sections.Spellcasting: As an action, cast Dancing Lights, Message, or Prestidigitation at will using Charisma.
sections.Size option: The published block supports both sizes. Medium has 9 HP (2d8) and Small has 7 HP (2d6). See Witchlight Hand (Small) for the other size option.
sections.Carnival staff: On duty, the hands wear fake butterfly wings. They agree to never harm other staff and to spend no longer than one day at a time away from the carnival.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, ch. 1, p. 27.

name: Witchlight Hand (Small)
description: Small carnival worker with a specialized trade. Uses the same spells, skills, and Pixie Dust action as the Medium Witchlight Hand.

sections.Traits: Secret Expertise. Choose one additional skill bonus for the hand: Acrobatics +6, Animal Handling +5, Arcana +5, Athletics +4, Medicine +5, or Performance +5.
sections.Actions:
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Pixie Dust (1/day). Give the hand or another visible creature within 5 ft. a 30-ft. flying speed for 1 minute. If it is still in the air when the effect expires, it descends safely, takes no falling damage, and lands on its feet.
sections.Spellcasting: As an action, cast Dancing Lights, Message, or Prestidigitation at will using Charisma.
sections.Size option: The published block supports both sizes. Medium has 9 HP (2d8) and Small has 7 HP (2d6). See Witchlight Hand (Medium) for the other size option.
sections.Carnival staff: On duty, the hands wear fake butterfly wings. They agree to never harm other staff and to spend no longer than one day at a time away from the carnival.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, ch. 1, p. 27.

name: Zarak
description: A short, avaricious assassin working for the League of Malevolence. He prefers thrown daggers against a group and his garrote when he can isolate the target.

sections.Traits: Special Equipment. Zarak has a Potion of Invisibility. He drinks it and flees if defeat looks likely.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Dagger attacks.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage. Add 5 (2d4) piercing damage when the target is a creature and Zarak has at least 18 HP.
Garrote. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one humanoid. A hit deals 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage and leaves the target grappled (escape DC 11). Until the grapple ends, the target takes 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage at the start of each of its turns. During that time, Zarak cannot grapple another creature or use Assassin’s Whim.
sections.Bonus actions: Assassin’s Whim. Take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.
sections.Reactions: Uncanny Dodge. Halve the damage from an attack if Zarak can see the attacker.
sections.Wayward Pool encounter: Kelek sent Zarak after the horn of Lamorna, the unicorn. At the shore he uses a fake unicorn horn to follow the party in. He attacks at the end of their conversation. Creatures with passive Perception of at least 17 avoid surprise. Lamorna teleports away on her first turn after the ambush. Zarak may withdraw or accept gold to abandon the hunt.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix B, p. 222, with the Wayward Pool encounter in ch. 3.

name: Zargash
description: A human priest of Orcus who wants to take Kelek’s place. He waits while Warduke protects Kelek. In combat he uses Silence to hinder spellcasters and Gaseous Form to escape.

sections.Traits:
Cling to Life (recharges after a long rest). The first time damage would reduce Zargash to 0 HP, he drops to 1 HP instead.
Special Equipment. His bat-shaped amulet has the properties of a Ring of Feather Falling.
sections.Actions:
Warhammer. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage one-handed or 7 (1d10 + 2) with both hands.
Deathly Ray. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. A hit deals 25 (4d10 + 3) necrotic damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
As an action, cast one listed spell with Wisdom (spell save DC 13).
At will. Light, Thaumaturgy.
1/day each. Command, Gaseous Form, Hold Person, Silence, Speak with Dead.
sections.Bonus actions: Animate Corpse (1/day). Choose a visible dead humanoid within 30 ft. It rises as a Zombie under Zargash’s control and takes its turn immediately after his. He must maintain concentration as if on a spell. The zombie becomes a corpse again after 10 minutes, when it reaches 0 HP, or when his concentration ends.
sections.Palace encounter: At the sludge pool in area P30, Zargash pretends to be frozen in time. A DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the trick. The first attack against him has advantage while he keeps up the act. If unmasked or attacked, he uses his next action to cast Gaseous Form on himself and flies through area P39 to warn Kelek and Warduke in P31.
sections.Printed source: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, appendix B, p. 223, with the sludge pool encounter in ch. 5, area P30.

name: Acererak
description: The archlich built the Tomb of the Nine Gods under Omu. He traps adventurers to feed on their souls and built the Soulmonger to sustain the Atropal.

sections.Languages: Abyssal, Common, Draconic, Dwarvish, Elvish, Giant, Infernal, Primordial, and Undercommon.
sections.Damage immunities: Necrotic and poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, and stunned.
sections.Traits:
Special Equipment. Acererak carries the Staff of the Forgotten One, wears the Talisman of the Sphere, and controls a Sphere of Annihilation. The staff has 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 spent charges at dawn. Undead of CR 2 or lower leave its bearer alone unless the bearer harms them.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Rejuvenation. At 0 HP, Acererak crumbles and leaves his equipment behind. After 1d10 days he re-forms at full HP within 5 feet of his hidden phylactery.
Turn Resistance. He has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
sections.Actions:
Paralyzing Touch. Melee spell attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 10 (3d6) cold damage. The target must pass a DC 20 Constitution save or be paralyzed for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect for itself on a success.
Staff (+3 Quarterstaff). Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage one-handed or 8 (1d8 + 4) with two hands. Both grips deal another 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.
Invoke Curse. Spend 1 charge from the held Staff of the Forgotten One and choose a visible creature within 60 ft. On a failed DC 23 Constitution save, the creature is cursed. It cannot regain HP and has vulnerability to necrotic damage. Greater Restoration, Remove Curse, or similar magic ends the curse.
sections.Spellcasting:
Acererak prepares wizard spells as a 20th-level caster, using Intelligence (spell save DC 23, +15 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will. Mage Hand, Ray of Frost, Shocking Grasp.
1st level at will. Ray of Sickness, Shield.
2nd level at will. Arcane Lock, Knock.
3rd level at will. Animate Dead, Counterspell.
4th level, 3 slots. Blight, Ice Storm, Phantasmal Killer.
5th level, 3 slots. Cloudkill, Hold Monster, Wall of Force.
6th level, 3 slots. Chain Lightning, Circle of Death, Disintegrate.
7th level, 3 slots. Finger of Death, Plane Shift, Teleport.
8th level, 2 slots. Maze, Mind Blank.
9th level, 2 slots. Power Word Kill, Time Stop.
sections.Legendary actions:
Acererak has 3 legendary actions. He can choose one option at the end of another creature’s turn and regains expended uses at the start of his turn.
At-Will Spell (1 action). Cast one of the spells listed as at will.
Melee Attack (1 action). Use Paralyzing Touch or make a staff attack.
Frightening Gaze (2 actions). Choose one creature Acererak can see within 10 ft. A failed DC 20 Wisdom save against this magic makes it frightened for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect. Once the creature succeeds or the fear ends, this gaze cannot affect it for 24 hours.
Talisman of the Sphere (2 actions). Move Acererak’s Sphere of Annihilation up to 90 ft.
Disrupt Life (3 actions). Each creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 20 Constitution save against this magic, taking 42 (12d6) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Tomb encounter:
Area 77, the Death God’s Nursery (p. 186). Acererak arrives when the party kills the Atropal. He has no lair actions in this encounter. If reduced below 100 HP, he tries to escape with Teleport on his next turn.
Wrath of the Trickster Gods. While a character hosting a trickster god can see Acererak, they gain 50 temporary HP at the start of each of their turns and deal an extra 3d6 psychic damage whenever they hit him with an attack roll.
sections.Source note: The printed Paralyzing Touch attack bonus is +8. Acererak separately has +15 to hit with prepared wizard spells. The printed skill list includes Religion +15.

name: Albino Dwarf Spirit Warrior
description: A Chultan dwarf chosen by a nature spirit. The spirit’s gift helps the warrior defend the jungle from unnatural threats.

sections.Traits: Dwarven Resilience. The dwarf has advantage on saving throws against poison.
sections.Actions: Handaxe. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.
sections.Innate spellcasting: Wisdom is the casting ability and no material components are needed. The dwarf can cast Hunter’s Mark, Jump, Pass without Trace, Speak with Animals, and Speak with Plants once each per day.
sections.Source note: The printed spirit warrior uses the Albino Dwarf Warrior block with innate spellcasting and challenge 1.

name: Albino Dwarf Warrior
description: A dwarf from Chult whose ancestors left their underground homes after volcanic upheaval. These warriors make equipment from dinosaur hide and bone, stone, and wood.

sections.Traits: Dwarven Resilience. The dwarf has advantage on saving throws against poison.
sections.Actions: Handaxe. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.

name: Aldani (Lobsterfolk)
description: A reclusive lobsterfolk of the Aldani Basin. It walks upright and peers out of its shell on long eyestalks.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The aldani breathes in air or water.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage and leaves the target grappled (escape DC 11). Each claw can hold one target.
sections.Encounter: When disturbed, aldani try to scare off visitors without killing them. If threats fail, they may offer a treasure or information in exchange for privacy.

name: Ankylosaurus Zombie
description: A shambling armored dinosaur with a heavy tail. It barely reacts to its surroundings until it closes on prey.

sections.Traits: Undead Fortitude. When damage would drop it to 0 HP, roll a Constitution save with DC 5 + the damage taken. On a success it stays at 1 HP. Radiant damage and critical hits bypass this trait.
sections.Actions: Tail. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (4d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.

name: Artus Cimber
description: A former Harper who travels Chult with Dragonbait. He seeks the vanished city of Mezro and his wife Alisanda, keeping the Ring of Winter out of hostile hands.

sections.Damage immunities: Cold, while attuned to and wearing the Ring of Winter.
sections.Traits: Special Equipment. Divination cannot target Artus or the Ring of Winter, and magical scrying sensors cannot perceive either. While attuned to and wearing the ring, Artus does not age or suffer extreme cold. Bookmark is his +3 Dagger.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using Bookmark or Longbow.
Bookmark (+3 Dagger). Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d4 + 5) piercing damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
Ring of Winter. With the ring worn and attuned, spend charges to use its powers. It holds 12 charges and restores all at dawn.
Lower Temperature (1 charge). Center a 120-ft.-radius sphere on a visible point within 300 ft. The area cools by 20°F per minute to −30°F. Frost and ice form below 32°F. The change lasts until Artus uses an action with the ring to end it. The area then warms back to its normal temperature at 10°F per minute.
Ring spells (spell save DC 17). Bigby’s Hand (2), Cone of Cold (2), Flesh to Stone (3), Ice Storm (2), Otiluke’s Freezing Sphere (3), Sleet Storm (1), Spike Growth (1), or Wall of Ice (2). Bigby’s Hand is ice, immune to cold, and its Clenched Fist deals bludgeoning damage. Flesh to Stone instead turns the target into solid ice with the properties of stone. The spikes in Spike Growth are ice.
Create Ice (2 or 4 charges). For 2 charges, make a nonmoving ice object that fits within a 10-ft. cube and is as durable and dense as metal or stone, as Artus chooses. For 4, make an animated ice creature modeled on a Beast of CR 2 or lower. It uses that creature’s statistics but is a Construct, is vulnerable to fire, is immune to cold and poison damage, and cannot be charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, or suffer exhaustion. It follows only Artus’s commands.
The ice object or creature appears in an empty space within 60 ft. It becomes water after 24 hours or at 0 HP. In extreme heat it loses 5 (1d10) HP per minute. Use the Dungeon Master’s Guide object rules for the object’s HP.
sections.Bonus actions:
Bookmark. While attuned and holding the drawn dagger, activate one feature as a bonus action.
Light. Turn the pommel gem on or off. It sheds bright light to 20 ft. and dim light for another 20 ft.
Compass. Lay Bookmark on Artus’s palm to make it point north.
Dimension Door. Cast it from Bookmark. This property recharges at dawn.
Compulsion. Cast it from Bookmark (save DC 15, range 90 ft.). It targets only spiders of the Beast type. This property recharges at dawn.
sections.Encounter: Artus is looking for the Guardian Naga Saja N’baza at Orolunga. He does not know where Omu is, but will set aside the search for Mezro to help characters who explain why they seek the Soulmonger.

name: Asharra
description: The elderly aarakocra whom Kir Sabal calls Teacher. She shelters the surviving heirs to Omu and can grant travelers flight for the journey to the city.

sections.Traits: Dive Attack. While flying, dive at least 30 ft. straight toward a target. A melee weapon hit against that target then deals 3 (1d6) extra damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Asharra is a 5th-level druid spellcaster using Wisdom (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will. Druidcraft, Mending, Produce Flame.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Faerie Fire, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots). Gust of Wind, Hold Person, Lesser Restoration.
3rd level (2 slots). Call Lightning, Wind Wall.
sections.Actions:
Talon. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Summon Air Elemental. Five aarakocra must stay within 30 ft. of one another and each spend their action and movement on an aerial dance for three consecutive turns. Each must maintain Concentration as if on a spell. Once all five complete the dance, an Air Elemental appears in an empty space within 60 ft. of the group, is friendly toward them, and follows spoken orders. It stays for 1 hour, until it dies, all its summoners die, or any summoner dismisses it as a bonus action. Each participant must finish a short rest before performing the dance again. When the elemental returns to the Elemental Plane of Air, any aarakocra within 5 ft. of it may go along.
sections.Dance of the Seven Winds: This 10-minute ritual requires an aarakocra elder, seven other aarakocra to chant without interruption, and a black orchid. Asharra grinds and inhales the orchid, then dances around up to ten creatures that cannot fly. Her wings disappear when the rite ends and each recipient gains a magical fly speed of 30 ft., enough to travel 4 miles per hour. After three days the recipients lose the flight and Asharra regains her wings and flying speed.
sections.Encounter context: Asharra offers the rite to travelers heading to Omu to destroy the Soulmonger. She directs them to find the orchid in Nangalore, whose Eblis have kept her people away. Kir Sabal also shelters Mwaxanaré and Na.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 69. Asharra uses the 2014 Aarakocra stat block with the changes printed in the Kir Sabal encounter.

name: Assassin Vine
description: A creeping plant that constricts its prey and feeds the soil around its roots. Bitter grapes can hang from its smaller vines, and underground specimens hide among fungi in warm caverns.

sections.Traits: False Appearance. A motionless assassin vine looks like an ordinary plant.
sections.Actions:
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 20 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage and grapple the target (escape DC 14). Until the grapple ends, the target is restrained and takes 21 (6d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. The vine can constrict one target at a time.
Entangling Vines. Animate roots and vines in a 15-ft. square on the ground within 30 ft. The square becomes difficult terrain. Creatures in the square when the effect begins must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or become restrained. A creature restrained this way can take an action to make a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check to escape. The terrain and restraints last for 1 minute, until the vine dies, or until it uses the action again.

name: Atropal
description: An abandoned, unfinished godling that drifts above the ground. Its withered cord draws on the Negative Plane. The specimen in the Tomb of the Nine Gods feeds on souls captured by the Soulmonger.

sections.Languages: Understands Celestial. Its utterances are incoherent.
sections.Damage immunities: Cold, necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Negative Energy Aura. Creatures within 30 ft. cannot regain hit points. A creature starting its turn within that distance takes 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. On a hit with a Vorpal Sword or another vorpal weapon, the attacker may sever the atropal’s cord in place of dealing damage. The atropal then loses this aura.
Turn Resistance Aura. The atropal and other undead within 30 ft. have advantage on saves against turning effects.
Undead Nature. The atropal needs no air, food, drink, or sleep. It cannot be raised or resurrected.
sections.Actions:
Touch. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.
Ray of Cold. Ranged spell attack, +12 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (6d6) cold damage.
Life Drain. Choose one visible creature within 120 ft. It makes a DC 19 Constitution save, taking 36 (8d8) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. The atropal regains half the hit points it dealt in damage.
Summon Wraith (Recharge 6). A Wraith appears in an empty space the atropal can see within 30 ft. It obeys the atropal, and only the atropal can control it. It disappears at 0 HP or when the atropal dies.
sections.Legendary actions:
The atropal has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Touch (1 action). Make a Touch attack.
Ray of Cold (2 actions). Use Ray of Cold.
Wail (3 actions). Each creature within 120 ft. that can hear the wail must succeed on a DC 19 Constitution save or gain one level of exhaustion.
sections.Death God’s Nursery: The atropal attacks creatures that threaten it or the Soulmonger. Killing the atropal brings Acererak to the south balcony. Destroying the Soulmonger ends the death curse and releases its trapped souls. A creature entering the lava by falling into it or starting its turn there takes 55 (10d10) fire damage.
sections.Soulmonger: The crystal cylinder is a Huge object (AC 15, 200 HP) vulnerable to radiant damage and immune to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Any one of its three adamantine struts breaking brings the whole device down. Each strut is a Large object (AC 20, 100 HP) immune to fire, poison, psychic, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. A creature taking damage while standing on a strut must make a DC 10 Dexterity save or fall into the lava unless secured. When a strut breaks, unsecured creatures on it fall. One within reach of a balcony can leap to safety on a successful DC 10 Dexterity save.
sections.Soulmonger tentacles: Once per turn, the Soulmonger responds to a melee weapon hit on the cylinder or a strut with one tentacle attack against the attacker. Reach 30 ft., +7 to hit, 24 (4d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. It can grapple in place of damage (escape DC 16). If the grappled creature weighs up to 330 lb., the tentacle can also move it to an empty space within reach or drop it into the lava. Each tentacle is a Huge animated object (Strength 22, AC 15, 30 HP) immune to poison and psychic damage.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 214–215, with the Soulmonger encounter on pp. 184–186. Condition immunities follow the printed p. 214 block.

name: Bag of Nails
description: An elderly tabaxi hunter who picks off travelers from the roofs of Omu. He came to find the Navel of the Moon in hopes of locating his missing son.

sections.Traits:
Feline Agility. When Bag of Nails moves on his turn in combat, he can double his speed until that turn ends. He regains use after a turn when he moves 0 ft.
Assassinate. On his first turn he has advantage against creatures that have yet to act. His hits against surprised creatures are critical hits.
Evasion. When a Dexterity save would halve damage, he takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Sneak Attack (1/turn). Add 14 (4d6) damage to a successful weapon attack if he has advantage. He can also add it if a non-incapacitated ally is within 5 ft. of the target and he lacks disadvantage on the attack.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shortsword attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 2 (1d4) slashing damage.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 24 (7d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. Apply the same poison save and damage as the Shortsword attack.
sections.Fallen Tree ambush: Bag of Nails begins hidden on the east bank, 150 ft. from the fallen tree bridge (DC 22 Wisdom (Perception) to spot him). He shoots when someone crosses and tries to hide at a new firing position after each shot. Below 39 HP, he surrenders and invites his enemies into his lair for stew. A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Insight) check exposes his intent. The stew contains Midnight Tears. If it has not been neutralized by midnight, the eater makes a DC 17 Constitution save, taking 31 (9d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. Five more doses can be found in the lair.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 102. The Fallen Tree encounter prints changes to the 2014 Assassin, including the claw attack and longbow.

name: Chwinga
description: A shy nature spirit about six inches tall. It peers out from rocks, plants, and streams, sometimes following a traveler to see what they do with their tools.

sections.Traits:
Evasion. When a Dexterity save would halve damage, the chwinga takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Unusual Nature. Chwingas sleep and need no air, food, or drink. When one dies, choose what remains: flower petals, a puff of pollen, a tiny statuette, a smooth stone, or fresh water.
sections.Spellcasting: Innate Spellcasting. Wisdom is the chwinga’s spellcasting ability. It needs no verbal or material components. At will: Druidcraft, Guidance, Pass without Trace, Resistance.
sections.Actions:
Magical Gift (1/day). Choose a humanoid the chwinga can see within 5 ft. The DM chooses one supernatural charm for that humanoid.
Natural Shelter. Enter a rock, living plant, or natural source of fresh water in the chwinga’s space. Attacks, spells, and other effects cannot target it while it is sheltered, and its blindsight still works. It can emerge as an action. Destroying the shelter puts the unharmed chwinga in the shelter’s space.
sections.Charm of Restoration: The chwinga in Nangalore’s eastern spirit dome can favor the tallest party member with this gift. It has 6 charges. As an action, spend 4 charges to cast Greater Restoration or 2 to cast Lesser Restoration. The charm disappears when its charges are spent.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 216–217. See p. 77 for Nangalore’s charm and p. 104 for the wagon encounter. Supernatural charms are in the Dungeon Master’s Guide (2014), chapter 7.
sections.Encounter context: In Omu, a chwinga shelters in a mossy disk beneath an overturned wagon. It comes out if travelers leave an offering or follows them secretly if they pass by. It favors curly hair or beards. Vegepygmies flee once they notice it with the party. It stays outside shrines and dungeons.

name: Clay Gladiator
description: A painted clay guardian of Shagambi’s shrine. It bears a bronze spear and a wooden shield, and returns to its cell when destroyed.

sections.Traits:
Climbing. It can climb difficult surfaces and ceilings without a check.
Steadfast. It cannot be disarmed or make ranged attacks.
Brute. Its melee weapon hits include an extra weapon damage die, already counted below.
Construct Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep and cannot speak.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks.
Spear. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) when wielded with two hands.
Shield Bash. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Reactions: Parry. Add 3 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. It must see the attacker and hold a melee weapon.
sections.Shagambi’s shrine: Four cells hold one guardian apiece. At least 50 lb. on the pit’s pressure plate raises the cell gates and calls the guardians. A gladiator fights if attacked or called to the pit. It cannot leave the shrine. At 0 HP outside the pit, it and its gear disappear and it immediately reforms in its cell at full health with spear and shield. It can then return to the pit. A gladiator destroyed in the pit leaves its spear behind as it reforms. If a spear leaves the shrine, it returns to the gladiator’s hand. When no other creatures remain inside, the gladiators return to their cells and the gates close. Place one spear from each guardian in the four warrior statues to free Shagambi’s puzzle cube.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 100. The shrine gives changes to the 2014 Gladiator stat block and separate reformation rules.

name: Dragonbait
description: A saurial swordsman who helps Artus Cimber search Chult. He communicates his feelings through scents and willingly puts himself in danger to help a friend.

sections.Languages: Understands Common but cannot speak it. His native clicks and whistles are above the human hearing range.
sections.Traits:
Divine Health. Dragonbait is immune to disease.
Magic Resistance Aura. While Dragonbait holds his Holy Avenger Longsword, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him have advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee weapon attacks.
Holy Avenger (+3 Longsword). Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d8 + 5) slashing damage when wielded in one hand, or 10 (1d10 + 5) in two hands. Against a fiend or undead, the hit also deals 11 (2d10) radiant damage.
Sense Alignment. Choose a visible creature within 60 feet and learn its alignment. This fails if magic shields that creature from divination.
sections.Encounter context:
Dragonbait met Artus Cimber in Port Nyanzaru and helps him look for his wife, Alisanda. If Artus agrees to destroy the Soulmonger, Dragonbait joins him. He has never been to Omu and cannot guide the party there.
