Scent cues. Brimstone signals confusion, roses sadness, lemon joy, bread anger, violets fear or danger, honeysuckle concern, wood smoke devotion, tar triumph, and ham worry.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, pp. 217–218. The stat block is on p. 218.

name: Eblis
description: An intelligent eight-foot crane that can handle objects with its beak and feet. It hides treasure in a woven reed hut and entices travelers into danger.

sections.Traits: Innate Spellcasting. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability (save DC 11). The eblis needs no material components and can cast Blur, Hypnotic Pattern, and Minor Illusion once each per day.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Beak attacks.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Jungle encounter: While traveling, the party encounters 1d4 + 1 eblis in stilt huts over a marsh or pond. They attack wounded or weak-looking travelers. A strong, armed party can buy directions to nearby landmarks for 50 gp in gems. Following those directions grants advantage on navigation checks to reach the landmarks. If the party defeats the eblis and searches the huts, roll three times on Treasure Drops. At a campsite, the eblis try to sneak in and carry away one traveler.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 219. The jungle encounter is in Appendix B, p. 199.

name: Giant Four-Armed Gargoyle
description: An eight- to nine-foot stone guardian created by Acererak. It waits on a tomb pedestal and can strike with all four claws in one turn.

sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks unless the weapon is adamantine.
sections.Traits: False Appearance. A motionless gargoyle looks exactly like an ordinary statue.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and four Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d4 + 4) slashing damage.
sections.Gargoyle Guardians: Four guardians perch around the shaft in Tomb of the Nine Gods area 45. Each humanoid owes a separate payment to each pedestal before leaving: 1 cp north, 1 sp east, 1 gp south, and 1 pp west. Higher-value coins or multiple coins of sufficient total value also work. Unpaid guardians animate when the humanoid leaves and attack that humanoid. A guardian also attacks if it or its pedestal takes damage. These triggers belong to the room.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 221. Gargoyle Guardians is in Chapter 5, p. 157.

name: Girallon Zombie
description: A reanimated four-armed ape with white fur. It bounds after living prey and can land a bite and four claw strikes in one turn.

sections.Traits: Undead Fortitude. When damage would drop the zombie to 0 HP, it makes a Constitution save with a DC of 5 plus the damage dealt. It drops to 1 HP on a success. Radiant damage or a critical hit bypasses this save.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and four Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d4 + 4) slashing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Aggressive. The zombie can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature it sees.
sections.Jungle encounter: On a 6 or 7 on the Appendix B zombie encounter d10, the party encounters 1d4 girallon zombies. The smell of death and the sound of the zombies moving through the undergrowth give warning.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 240. The zombie encounter is in Appendix B, p. 203.

name: Hew Hackinstone
description: A shield dwarf guide who lost his left arm at Wyrmheart Mine. He wants to lead a party back there to kill the dragon Tinder.

sections.Traits:
Dwarven Resilience. Hew resists poison damage and has advantage on saves against being poisoned.
Reckless. At the start of his turn, Hew can choose to roll melee weapon attacks with advantage for that turn. If he does, attacks against him have advantage until his next turn starts.
sections.Actions: Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage. Hew can wield the axe only one-handed.
sections.Encounter context: Hew offers his services in Port Nyanzaru and claims he can guide the party anywhere. If hired, he takes them to Wyrmheart Mine, where Tinder (Tzindelor) drove off his expedition. Use the Young Red Dragon profile for Tinder.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Chapter 1, p. 34. The adventure modifies the 2014 Monster Manual Berserker, including the weapon and its one-handed restriction.

name: Kamadan
description: A leopardlike hunter with six snakes growing from its shoulders. It hunts alone or in pairs and uses a cloud of sleep gas before closing in.

sections.Traits:
Keen Smell. The kamadan has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on scent.
Pounce. If it moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and hits it with Claw on the same turn, the target must pass a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone. If this knocks the target prone, the kamadan can use a bonus action to make one Bite and one Snakes attack against it.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite or Claw attack, plus one Snakes attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Snakes. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage. The creature also makes a DC 12 Constitution save, taking 21 (6d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sleep Breath (recharges after a short or long rest). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone must pass a DC 12 Constitution save or fall unconscious for up to 10 minutes. Damage or an action spent waking the creature ends the effect early.
sections.Hunting tactics: A kamadan opens with Sleep Breath if it can, then attacks conscious enemies before turning on sleeping ones.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 225.

name: King of Feathers
description: This feathered tyrannosaur hunts the ruins of Omu. Huge tracks and long scarlet, orange, and green feathers mark its amphitheater lair.
hpRule: The adventure fixes the King of Feathers at 200 hit points and gives no replacement Hit Dice expression.

sections.Traits:
Detect Invisibility. The king sees invisible creatures and objects as though they were visible.
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). When the king fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
sections.Innate spellcasting: The king can cast Misty Step at will as a bonus action. It uses Wisdom and needs no components.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail attack against different targets.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 33 (4d12 + 7) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 17) and restrained until the grapple ends. The king cannot bite another target while it holds that creature.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
Summon Swarm (Recharge 5–6). If its jaws are free of grappled creatures, the king exhales a Swarm of Wasps into a space within 20 feet. The swarm is an ally, takes its turn immediately after the king, and disperses after 1 minute.
sections.Amphitheater: When the party arrives, the king is home on a 50% roll by day or 25% at night. If it is out hunting, the chance it returns increases by 20 percentage points per hour. Five Deinonychuses prowl the ruin and attack on sight while the king is away. The king can also appear elsewhere in Omu, including during a rest or an ongoing fight.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, chapter 3, p. 106 (area 13). Use the Tyrannosaurus Rex baseline in Monster Manual (2014), p. 80, with the printed changes above.

name: Liara Portyr
description: Liara commands the Flaming Fist garrison at Fort Beluarian. She helps adventurers who serve the fort's interests and takes a share of the Jahaka pirates' profits.

sections.Traits:
Brave. Liara has advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
Flaming Fury. Once per turn, when Liara hits with a melee weapon, she can add 10 (3d6) fire damage to the hit.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks.
Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) if wielded in two hands.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Fort Beluarian: An exploration charter costs 50 gp, credited toward the Flaming Fist's claim on half the expedition's proceeds and discoveries. Charter holders can hire up to six guards at 1 gp per guard per tenday. Liara uses a Sending Stone to pass ship manifests and sailing schedules to Zaroum Al-Saryak. In exchange, the Jahaka pirates leave Baldur's Gate ships alone.
sections.Roleplaying: She values obedience, has sworn to hold the fort for Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard, and has little pity for those unable to defend themselves.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 227, and chapter 2, pp. 54–56 (Fort Beluarian).

name: Mantrap
description: A giant carnivorous flytrap releases pollen that draws prey within reach of its leafy jaws.

sections.Traits: False Appearance. While still, the mantrap looks like an ordinary tropical plant.
sections.Reactions: Attractive Pollen (1/Day). When it detects a nearby creature, the mantrap can release pollen in a 30-ft. radius. Each beast or humanoid in the area must make a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure, the creature uses all its movement on each of its turns to get as close as it can to the mantrap. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
sections.Actions: Engulf. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. On a hit the target is caught in the jaws, blinded and restrained. It has total cover against attacks and other effects from outside the mantrap and takes 14 (4d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns. The mantrap can engulf one creature at a time. Its death ends the restraint.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 227.

name: Mwaxanaré
description: The eldest living heir to Omu's royal families is a seventeen-year-old warlock under aarakocra protection in Kir Sabal. She wants to reclaim Omu and restore its royal line.

sections.Spellcasting:
A 2nd-level warlock who uses Charisma (spell save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). She regains expended slots on a short or long rest.
At will. Eldritch Blast and Mage Hand.
1st level (2 slots). Charm Person, Protection from Evil and Good, and Unseen Servant.
sections.Actions: Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 2 (1d4) piercing damage.
sections.Kir Sabal: Mwaxanaré made a pact with the Wind Dukes of Aaqa against Asharra's wishes. She believes retrieving the Skull Chalice of Ch'gakare will rally support to rebuild Omu. If the party is headed there, she asks them to recover it and can offer 250 gp worth of pieces from her treasury if pressed for a reward.
sections.Roleplaying: She insists on the respect due her station and sees her pact as a way to protect Na and the aarakocra who sheltered them.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 228, and chapter 2, pp. 69–70 (Kir Sabal).

name: Na
description: Mwaxanaré's six-year-old brother lives among the aarakocra of Kir Sabal. He made himself a birdfolk costume and sends homemade gliders out his window above the jungle.
hpRule: The adventure provides a fixed 3 hit points and gives no Hit Dice.

sections.Languages: Auran and Common. Na prefers Auran.
sections.Actions: Na is a noncombatant and has no listed attacks or combat actions. Use AC 10 and 3 HP if he is caught in an encounter.
sections.Roleplaying: He wants to fly like the aarakocra, loves his sister, and is curious about the plants and insects in the monastery gardens.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 228, and chapter 2, pp. 69–70 (Kir Sabal).

name: Pterafolk
description: These winged reptilian hunters dive on travelers in Chult and carry prey and plunder to high roosts. Firefinger is one of their strongholds.

sections.Traits: Terror Dive. After flying at least 30 feet straight toward a target in a dive, a hit with a melee weapon attack leaves that target frightened until the end of its next turn.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks, or make two melee Javelin attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Firefinger: Four elders in the level 3 nest have 13 hit points each. Six pterafolk occupy the pinnacle, including Nrak with 40 hit points. The flock can shove foes near the edge or circle the tower to set up a Terror Dive.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 229, and chapter 2, pp. 53–54 (Firefinger).

name: Ras Nsi
description: An exiled Chultan paladin and former warlord who joined the yuan-ti in Omu. He hopes to free Dendar the Night Serpent, but the Soulmonger’s death curse is consuming him.

sections.Traits:
Special Equipment. Ras Nsi wears Bracers of Defense, wields a Flame Tongue Longsword, and carries the Sending Stone paired with Salida’s.
Shapechanger. As an action, he can become a Medium snake or return to yuan-ti form. His statistics stay the same, his equipment keeps its form, and he does not revert when he dies.
Magic Resistance. He has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks, using Constrict at most once.
Bite (snake form only). Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing and 7 (2d6) poison damage.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage and grapples the target (escape DC 14). The target is restrained while grappled this way. Ras Nsi can constrict only one target at a time.
Flame Tongue Longsword (yuan-ti form only). Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) with two hands, plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.
sections.Innate Spellcasting:
Charisma, spell save DC 16. These spells require no material components.
At will: Animal Friendship (snakes only).
3/day: Suggestion.
sections.Spellcasting:
11th-level wizard. Intelligence, spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks.
Cantrips (at will): Chill Touch, Fire Bolt, Mage Hand, Mending, Poison Spray.
1st level (4 slots): Expeditious Retreat, False Life, Magic Missile, Shield.
2nd level (3 slots): Blindness/Deafness, Hold Person, Misty Step.
3rd level (3 slots): Animate Dead, Counterspell, Fireball.
4th level (3 slots): Blight, Polymorph.
5th level (2 slots): Contact Other Plane, Geas.
6th level (1 slot): Create Undead.
sections.Death curse: The printed unweakened average is 127 HP. Begin the adventure with Ras Nsi’s maximum reduced to 107 HP. Subtract 1 more from that maximum for each day that passes.
sections.Fane of the Night Serpent: Ras Nsi can enter any of the five disks in areas 8–12 and continue moving from any other disk in the temple. In his quarters (area 12), he can use a bonus action to say “Ssilum” and animate five shields. They initially raise his AC by 10. When they turn a hit into a miss, one drops and the bonus falls by 2. Only Ras Nsi can activate them, and their effect stays in his quarters. Once all five drop, he needs a long rest before using them again. Sekelok is his bodyguard. Acererak promised to help him free Dendar in exchange for protecting the tomb. If the party can show that stopping the death curse would help him, Ras Nsi may let them proceed.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 230. Death curse context, pp. 229–230. Fane teleporters and flying shields, pp. 114 and 121.

name: Spiked Tomb Guardian
description: The Tomb of the Nine Gods’ dwarves stitch together dead adventurers and bolt the resulting flesh golems into iron armor. Two guardians with spiked gauntlets stand watch in area 41.

sections.Armor: Plate armor bolted to its body (AC 17 for this printing).
sections.Damage immunities: Lightning, poison. Also bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks unless made with adamantine weapons.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.
sections.Languages: Understands its maker’s languages. Cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Aversion of Fire. After taking fire damage, the guardian has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks through the end of its next turn.
Berserk. At the start of a turn with 40 HP or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6 the guardian goes berserk and attacks the nearest creature it can see. If it cannot reach and attack a creature, it attacks an object, favoring one smaller than itself. It stays berserk until destroyed, healed to full HP, or calmed by its creator. To calm it, the creator uses an action within 60 ft. and succeeds on a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check. The guardian must be able to hear its creator. Further damage at 40 HP or fewer can cause it to go berserk again.
Immutable Form. Spells and other effects cannot change its form.
Lightning Absorption. Lightning damage instead heals it for the same amount.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Spiked Gauntlet attacks.
Spiked Gauntlet. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning and 7 (2d6) piercing damage.
sections.Chained pair (area 41): The two guards attack anyone who strikes them or tries to pass. The chain stops them from moving more than 15 ft. apart and spreads damage to either guardian evenly across both. The chain can be attacked. It has AC 18, 5 HP, damage threshold 10, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. If it breaks, both guardians immediately go berserk.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 5, p. 154, area 41. The printed adventure gives 7 (2d6) piercing for the gauntlet. Some secondary indexes show 9.

name: Stone Juggernaut
speed: 50 ft., straight in a direction chosen at the start of its turn
description: A massive rolling statue that crushes anyone caught in its path. Acererak named the one in the Tomb of the Nine Gods after Queen Napaka.

sections.Damage immunities: Poison. Also bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks unless made with adamantine weapons.
sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone.
sections.Traits:
Devastating Roll. The juggernaut can pass through the space of a prone creature. The first time per turn it enters a creature’s space, that creature makes a DC 17 Dexterity save. A failed save deals 55 (10d10) bludgeoning damage. A success halves the damage.
Immutable Form. Spells and other effects cannot change its form.
Regeneration. The juggernaut returns to full HP at dawn if it still has at least 1 HP. Reaching 0 HP destroys it.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures.
sections.Actions: Slam. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 25 (3d12 + 6) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must make a DC 17 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Napaka’s tomb (area 62): The juggernaut waits in area 62D until it takes damage or the door opens. Failing to pick the secret crawlway’s DC 21 lock by 5 or more also releases it. It rolls forward or backward along the hall and needs at least 10 ft. of width. Napaka’s scepter from area 53 destroys it on contact. Touch it with the scepter while it is inert, or hit it with a melee weapon attack using the scepter once it awakens.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 231. Area 62 encounter, pp. 172–173. The six ability scores follow the printed block.

name: Su-monster
description: A vicious primate that stalks caves and remote wilderness. Its tail can hold its weight, leaving all four claws free. A hunting group signals with tails and may bury surplus prey.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage, or 12 (4d4 + 2) if the su-monster hangs by its tail with all four limbs free.
Psychic Crush (recharge 5–6). One creature the su-monster can see within 30 ft. makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. A failure deals 17 (5d6) psychic damage and stuns the target for 1 minute. A stunned target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the effect on a success.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 232.

name: Tabaxi Hunter
description: A catfolk guide and wilderness tracker. Tabaxi hunters carry stories and treasures between far-flung settlements, and know how to keep a party alive in the jungle.

sections.Traits: Feline Agility. When the hunter moves on its turn in combat, it can double its speed until the turn ends. It cannot use this again until it moves 0 ft. on one of its turns.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Claws, Shortsword, or Shortbow.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 2 (1d4) slashing damage.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 232. The printed Shortsword deals slashing damage.

name: Tabaxi Minstrel
description: A traveling catfolk singer and storyteller. Tabaxi minstrels often roam in small troupes and earn their keep by performing when they reach a settlement.

sections.Traits:
Feline Agility. When the minstrel moves on its turn in combat, it can double its speed until the turn ends. It cannot use this again until it moves 0 ft. on one of its turns.
Inspire (1/day). During a short rest, the minstrel spends 1 minute performing. Choose up to five other creatures that can see and hear it. At the end of the minstrel’s rest, each gains 8 temporary HP.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claws attacks or two Dart attacks.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 2 (1d4) slashing damage.
Dart. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 233.

name: Tomb Dwarf
description: Acererak turned kidnapped dwarf miners into wights to build and maintain his tomb. A worker at the grand staircase wears a mask shaped like the entrance’s devil face.

sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.
sections.Languages: Any languages it knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, roll attacks and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks with disadvantage.
Undead Nature. It does not require air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Battleaxe attacks or two Light Crossbow attacks. One Battleaxe attack can be replaced with Life Drain.
Life Drain. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) necrotic damage. On a failed DC 13 Constitution save, reduce the target’s hit point maximum by the damage taken until it finishes a long rest. The target dies if the reduction leaves it with a maximum of 0. A Humanoid killed by this attack rises as a Zombie under the attacker’s control 24 hours later unless restored to life or its body is destroyed. Up to twelve Zombies can be controlled at a time.
Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) slashing damage, or 7 (1d10 + 2) if wielded in two hands.
Light Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Grand staircase: The dwarf retreats through a secret door to area 25 unless the characters catch it immediately in area 7A.
sections.Base stat block: The adventure uses the 2014 Wight with a Battleaxe and Light Crossbow. Its Multiattack uses those weapons in the roles of the Wight’s original weapons.

name: Tri-flower Frond
description: This walking Chultan plant grows three large trumpet-shaped flowers in orange, yellow, and red. Each flower attacks in a different way.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Use Orange Blossom, then Yellow Blossom, then Red Blossom.
Orange Blossom. Choose one creature the frond can see within 5 ft. On a failed DC 11 Constitution save, the target is poisoned for 1 hour and unconscious while poisoned this way. It can repeat the save at the end of every minute, ending the effect on a success.
Yellow Blossom. Choose one creature the frond can see within 5 ft. On a failed DC 11 Dexterity save, corrosive sap coats the target and deals 5 acid damage at the start of each of its turns. Each pint or flask of water poured over it reduces that recurring damage by 1.
Red Blossom. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 2 (1d4) piercing damage. The target is grappled (escape DC 11). While this grapple lasts, the target takes 5 (2d4) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. The blossom can grapple one target at a time. Another creature within the frond’s reach can use its action to free the target.
sections.Encounters: On the trail, a patch of 1d4 fronds passes for harmless plants until it strikes. Around a camp, the fronds creep closer and use Orange Blossom to incapacitate targets before attacking with the others. Three fronds grow in the garden at area 5B of Nangalore.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 234. The ability scores follow the printed stat block. See also appendix B for encounter tactics.

name: Tyrannosaurus Zombie
description: This reanimated dinosaur carries independent Zombies in its gullet. They can spill out even after the dinosaur falls.

sections.Traits:
Undead Fortitude. When damage would reduce it to 0 HP, roll a Constitution save with DC 5 plus the damage taken. On a success, it drops to 1 HP instead. Radiant damage and critical hits bypass this trait.
Disgorge Zombie. As a bonus action, a regular Zombie emerges into a free space within 10 ft. and acts on its own initiative count. After each use, roll a d6. On a 1, the dinosaur runs out of Zombies and loses this trait. If it has this trait when it dies, 1d4 Zombies burst out at the start of what would have been its next turn. They also act on their own initiative.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail attack against different targets.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 33 (4d12 + 7) piercing damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it is grappled (escape DC 17) and restrained until the grapple ends. The dinosaur cannot bite another target or Disgorge Zombie while holding it.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 241.

name: Valindra Shadowmantle
description: An elven lich working for Szass Tam, Valindra searches Chult for the Soulmonger. At the Heart of Ubtao she passes for a living scholar and may enlist the party to further her search.

sections.Languages: Abyssal, Common, Draconic, Dwarvish, Elvish, Infernal.
sections.Damage immunities: Poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Preparation. When preparing spells, she can replace any prepared spell with a wizard spell of the same level.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). She can choose to succeed when she fails a saving throw.
Rejuvenation. If destroyed with her phylactery intact, she returns at full HP in 1d10 days within 5 ft. of it.
Turn Resistance. Roll saves against effects that turn undead with advantage.
Undead Nature. It does not require air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: Paralyzing Touch. Melee spell attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 10 (3d6) cold damage. The target makes a DC 18 Constitution save or becomes paralyzed for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns it can repeat the save, ending the condition on a success.
sections.Bonus actions: Mask. Magically appear as a living elf. She can end the illusion with a bonus action. It also ends when she uses Frightening Gaze, drops to 30 HP or fewer, or is targeted by Dispel Magic.
sections.Legendary actions:
Valindra has three legendary actions. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn. Her uses refresh at the start of her own turn.
Cantrip (1 action). Cast a cantrip.
Paralyzing Touch (2 actions). Use Paralyzing Touch.
Frightening Gaze (2 actions). A creature she can see within 10 ft. must pass a DC 18 Wisdom save against this magic or become frightened for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the fear on a success. A successful initial save or the end of the effect grants immunity to her gaze for 24 hours.
Disrupt Life (3 actions). Each creature other than Undead within 20 ft. takes 21 (6d6) necrotic damage on a failed DC 18 Constitution save against this magic, or half on a success.
sections.Spellcasting:
18th-level wizard. Intelligence, spell save DC 20, +12 to hit with spell attacks.
At will: Mage Hand, Prestidigitation, Ray of Frost.
1st level (4 slots): Detect Magic, Magic Missile, Shield, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots): Detect Thoughts, Invisibility, Melf’s Acid Arrow, Mirror Image.
3rd level (3 slots): Animate Dead, Counterspell, Dispel Magic, Fireball.
4th level (3 slots): Blight, Dimension Door.
5th level (3 slots): Cloudkill, Scrying.
6th level (1 slot): Disintegrate, Globe of Invulnerability.
7th level (1 slot): Finger of Death, Plane Shift.
8th level (1 slot): Dominate Monster, Power Word Stun.
9th level (1 slot): Power Word Kill.
sections.Heart of Ubtao: Valindra cannot use lair actions here. She invites useful visitors up with an Arcane Gate scroll if necessary. If a fight starts, her undead servants engage while she escapes to Thay through her Teleportation Circle. Her phylactery stays in Thay. The return route’s destination sigils are absent from the Heart.
sections.Base stat block: The adventure uses the 2014 Lich, with the alignment, languages, spell preparation, Mask, and lair restriction given here.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 2, pp. 58–59 (Heart of Ubtao).

name: Withers
description: Once an Omuan engineer called Gorra, Withers now maintains Acererak’s tomb. He questions trespassers about the outside world before trying to kill them.

sections.Damage resistances: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.
sections.Languages: Any languages he knew in life.
sections.Traits:
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, roll attacks and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks with disadvantage.
Special Equipment. He wears the Amulet of the Black Skull. It holds 6 charges and regains 1d6 at dawn. As an action, spend a charge to teleport himself and his gear to a familiar spot within 100 ft. on the same plane, even through the tomb’s normal restrictions. Withers is Undead, so he does not roll the item’s transformation save.
Undead Nature. It does not require air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Longsword attacks. One may be replaced with Life Drain.
Life Drain. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) necrotic damage. On a failed DC 13 Constitution save, reduce the target’s hit point maximum by the damage taken until it finishes a long rest. The target dies if the reduction leaves it with a maximum of 0. A Humanoid killed by this attack rises as a Zombie under the attacker’s control 24 hours later unless restored to life or its body is destroyed. Up to twelve Zombies can be controlled at a time.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) slashing damage, or 7 (1d10 + 2) if wielded in two hands.
sections.Spellcasting:
9th-level wizard. Intelligence, spell save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks.
At will: Acid Splash, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation.
1st level (4 slots): Detect Magic, Expeditious Retreat, Feather Fall, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots): Darkness, Hold Person, Rope Trick.
3rd level (3 slots): Dispel Magic, Lightning Bolt.
4th level (3 slots): Blight, Wall of Fire.
5th level (1 slot): Telekinesis.
sections.Office encounter: Seven Crawling Claws follow his commands in area 28. When pressed, he uses magic to retreat and Wall of Fire to cut off pursuit. His journals record the arrival of the Atropal and the building of the Soulmonger.
sections.Base stat block: The adventure uses the 2014 Wight. Withers gains the printed Intelligence, CR, amulet, and Spellcasting changes and does not carry a longbow.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 5, pp. 145–146 (area 28), and appendix C, p. 206 (amulet). The second-level slot count follows the printed adventure.

name: Xandala
description: A half-elf sorcerer with fine draconic scales, Xandala wants the Ring of Winter for its power and longevity. She claims to be Artus Cimber’s daughter to get help finding him.

sections.Traits: Quickened Spell (3/day). When she casts a spell with a casting time of one action, she can cast it as a bonus action instead.
sections.Actions: Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage, or 4 (1d8) if wielded in two hands.
sections.Spellcasting:
9th-level sorcerer. Charisma, spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks.
At will: Acid Splash, Fire Bolt, Light, Mage Hand, Ray of Frost.
1st level (4 slots): Chromatic Orb, Feather Fall, Shield.
2nd level (4 slots): Invisibility, Misty Step.
3rd level (3 slots): Fireball, Fly.
4th level (3 slots): Ice Storm, Polymorph.
5th level (1 slot): Dominate Person.
sections.Encounter context: She plans to use Dominate Person to make Artus surrender the Ring of Winter, then escape with Fly. Her companion Summerwise is a Pseudodragon who thinks the quest is reckless. Good-aligned characters can win Summerwise over. Xandala trusts her draconic ancestry to carry her to greatness and treats others as fools.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 236. Four second-level slots are printed for this character.

name: Azaka Stormfang
description: A Chultan guide in Port Nyanzaru conceals her ability to take tiger form. She wants the pterafolk at Firefinger to return her family’s wooden tiger mask.
speed: walk 30 ft. (40 ft. in tiger form)

sections.Languages: Common. She cannot speak in tiger form.
sections.Damage immunities: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered. Her immunity does not prevent falling damage.
sections.Traits:
Shapechanger. As an action, take tiger form, tiger-humanoid hybrid form, or true human form. Statistics otherwise stay the same apart from size and the listed tiger speed. Gear does not change with her. She returns to human form when she dies.
Keen Hearing and Smell. She has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks using hearing or smell.
Pounce (tiger or hybrid). Move at least 15 ft. directly toward a creature, then hit it with Claw during that turn. The target makes a DC 14 Strength save or falls prone. If prone, it can be the target of one bonus-action Bite.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack (human or hybrid). In human form, make two Scimitar or two Longbow attacks. The hybrid can do the same or make two Claw attacks.
Bite (tiger or hybrid). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage. A humanoid target must pass a DC 13 Constitution save or contract weretiger lycanthropy.
Claw (tiger or hybrid). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage.
Scimitar (human or hybrid). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Longbow (human or hybrid). Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Adventure encounter: Azaka guides the party for free if they agree to recover her Mask of the Beast from the pterafolk. She avoids spreading her curse and refuses situations where a fall of more than 60 ft. is likely. At Firefinger she urges an attack under cover of dark or rain. She leaves if the party refuses to attack the pterafolk. See the Firefinger encounter and handout 2.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 33. Uses the Weretiger from Monster Manual (2014), p. 210.

name: Blind Artist
description: One of three undead artists in Acererak’s throne room. Its eyes and mouth are stitched shut, yet it can paint scenes of death that took place in the tomb.

sections.Languages: Understands the languages it spoke in life and cannot speak.
sections.Senses: Blindsight 30 ft. The Blind Artist is blind beyond that radius.
sections.Traits:
Undead Fortitude. When damage would drop the artist to 0 HP, make a Constitution save with a DC of 5 + the damage taken. On a success it has 1 HP instead. This cannot prevent a drop to 0 HP from radiant damage or a critical hit.
Undead Nature. The artist needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions: The printed Zombie variant has no effective attacks and awards 0 XP. It continues painting until disturbed.
sections.Adventure encounter: Three Blind Artists paint in area 52 of the Tomb of the Nine Gods. Turning or destroying any of them brings a Tyrannosaurus Zombie up through the floor to attack. It leaves a 20-ft.-wide hole and can use the wide passage east, but cannot fit through 5-ft. corridors.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 164. Uses the Zombie from Monster Manual (2014), p. 316.

name: Bosco Daggerhand
description: The tavernkeeper at Jahaka Anchorage keeps his hand near his dagger when he greets visitors. His trained guard dinosaur is called Knuckles.

sections.Traits: Pack Tactics. Bosco has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if an ally within 5 ft. of it is not incapacitated.
sections.Equipment: Ring of Animal Influence. It holds 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn. While wearing it, Bosco can use an action and spend 1 charge to cast Animal Friendship (DC 13), Fear (DC 13, only against beasts with Intelligence 3 or lower), or Speak with Animals.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Mace. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +2 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d10) piercing damage.
sections.Adventure encounter: At area 6A, Bosco uses his ring to keep the Deinonychus Knuckles in check. At any time, 2d6 pirates use the Bandit profile while drinking in the tavern. Another 1d6 have passed out.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 68. Uses the Thug from Monster Manual (2014), p. 350.

name: Drufi
description: Captain of the Hvalspyd, Drufi leads frost giants searching Chult for Artus Cimber and the Ring of Winter.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Greataxe attacks.
Greataxe. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 25 (3d12 + 6) slashing damage.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Adventure encounter: Drufi patrols with two other Frost Giants and two Winter Wolves. A DC 10 Wisdom (Survival) check recognizes that the oversized tracks and broken vegetation are foreign to the jungle. Success by 5 or more identifies frost giants. A Chultan guide has advantage but does not infer that frost giants made the trail. Drufi first asks what the group knows about Artus Cimber. A DC 10 Wisdom (Insight) check picks up her interest in his magic item. She may attack if provoked or if she believes the party is withholding its whereabouts.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 64. Uses the Frost Giant from Monster Manual (2014), p. 155.

name: Ekene-Afa
description: A retired arena champion and one of Port Nyanzaru’s merchant princes. She supplies weapons, shields, canoes, and traveling gear.

sections.Traits:
Brave. Ekene-Afa has advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
Brute. Her melee weapon hits deal an additional weapon damage die, included below.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks or two ranged attacks.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage if used two-handed in melee.
Shield Bash. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target must pass a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Reactions: Parry. Add 3 to her AC against one melee attack that would hit her. She must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.
sections.Business: Wakanga O’tamu enchants selected items for her shop. Listed prices are 50 gp per piece of +1 ammunition, 450 gp for a wooden +1 shield, and 500 gp for a +1 dagger or +1 yklwa. These are shop stock.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 25. Uses the Gladiator from Monster Manual (2014), p. 346.

name: Eku
description: A couatl guides travelers while disguised as a Chultan woman in light blue robes. She knows where Omu lies and seeks good-aligned adventurers to help her oppose evil in the jungle.

sections.Damage immunities: Psychic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Magic Weapons. Eku’s weapon attacks are magical.
Shielded Mind. Scrying cannot affect her. She is immune to effects that would locate her, read her thoughts, or sense her emotions.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage. On a failed DC 13 Constitution save, the target is poisoned for 24 hours and unconscious while poisoned in this way. Another creature can use an action to wake it.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. The target is grappled (escape DC 15) and restrained until that grapple ends. Eku can constrict only one target at a time.
Change Shape. Magically take the form of a humanoid or beast of CR 4 or lower, or return to true form. Eku resumes true form on death. At her choice, gear is absorbed or carried by the new form. She keeps her game statistics and speech except for AC, movement modes, Strength, Dexterity, and other actions, which the new form supplies. She gains capabilities of the new form she lacks, apart from class features, legendary actions, and lair actions. She can use her own Bite if the new form has a bite attack.
sections.Spellcasting:
Innate Charisma spellcasting, DC 14, verbal components only.
At will: Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts.
3/day each: Bless, Create Food and Water, Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration, Protection from Poison, Sanctuary, Shield.
1/day each: Dream, Greater Restoration, Scrying.
sections.Adventure encounter: Eku begins in her human guise. The printed adventure does not name a separate stat block for that guise. When a group needs direction, she suggests consulting the guardian naga of Orolunga. Near Mbala, she asks the party to help her confront Nanny Pu’pu, who destroyed the community there.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 34. Uses the Couatl from Monster Manual (2014), p. 43.

name: Elok Jaharwon
description: Elok seized command of the Dragonfang in a mutiny. He now wants the pirate captains to stop paying Fort Beluarian and has support among their crews.

sections.Armor: AC 10 in human form. AC 11 from natural armor in boar and hybrid forms.
sections.Languages: Common. Cannot speak in boar form.
sections.Damage immunities: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.
sections.Traits:
Charge (boar or hybrid only). Move at least 15 ft. directly toward a target and hit it with Tusks in the same turn for an extra 7 (2d6) slashing damage. A creature hit this way must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
Relentless (short or long rest). If 14 or less damage would take Elok to 0 HP, he drops to 1 HP instead.
sections.Actions:
Shapechanger. Change magically between human, boar, and hybrid forms. His equipment and other statistics stay the same. Use the listed form-specific Armor Class, speed, and action limits. On death he returns to human form.
Multiattack (human or hybrid only). Make two attacks, including at most one Tusks attack.
Maul (human or hybrid only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Tusks (boar or hybrid only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage. A humanoid hit must pass a DC 12 Constitution save or contract wereboar lycanthropy.
sections.Encounter context: At Jahaka Anchorage, the Dragonfang crew includes first mate Mad Kalita (a Spy), 15 Bandits, 3 Thugs, and Eye of the Deep (a Druid). Elok wants to break the pirates’ deal with Liara Portyr.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 67 (Dragonfang). Uses Wereboar from Monster Manual (2014), p. 209.

name: Faroul
description: A Calishite fortune hunter who lost his money at the Port Nyanzaru dinosaur races. He and Gondolo seek an equal share from anyone they guide to Needle’s Bones.

sections.Traits: Keen Hearing and Sight. Faroul has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or sight.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shortsword attacks or two Longbow attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter context: Faroul boasts of his fighting skill but draws his sword only in emergencies. Gondolo bought an accurate map to Needle’s Bones, where the pair expect to find a dragon hoard. They use their slow racing triceratops, Zongo, as a pack animal.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 34 (Faroul and Gondolo). Uses Scout from Monster Manual (2014), p. 349.

name: Fenthaza
description: The high priest of Dendar in Omu. A vision of the Black Opal Crown convinced her to plot a coup against Ras Nsi.

sections.Senses: Darkvision 120 ft., including in magical darkness.
sections.Traits:
Death Fangs (2/day). The first time Fenthaza hits with a melee attack on her turn, she can add 16 (3d10) necrotic damage.
Magic Resistance. She has advantage on saves against spells and other magic.
sections.Actions:
Shapechanger. Change into a Medium snake or back into yuan-ti form. Her equipment and statistics stay the same. She keeps her current form on death.
Multiattack (yuan-ti form only). Make one Constrict and one Scimitar attack.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller target is grappled (escape DC 14) and restrained until the grapple ends. Fenthaza can constrict only one creature at a time.
Scimitar (yuan-ti form only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Invoke Nightmare (short or long rest). Choose a visible creature within 60 ft. It makes a DC 13 Intelligence save. On a failure, it takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage and is frightened of an immobile, indestructible illusion visible only to it. Fenthaza maintains Concentration for up to 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the illusion on a success or taking another 11 (2d10) psychic damage on a failure.
sections.Spellcasting:
Only in yuan-ti form. Innate magic uses Charisma (save DC 13) and requires no material components. Animal Friendship is at will and works only on snakes. Suggestion is 3/day.
6th-level warlock. Spellcasting uses Charisma (save DC 13, +5 to hit). Recover both 3rd-level slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips: Chill Touch, Eldritch Blast (300 ft., +3 damage per hit), Mage Hand, Message, Poison Spray, Prestidigitation.
3rd-level slots: Arms of Hadar, Darkness, Fear, Hex, Hold Person, Hunger of Hadar, Witch Bolt.
sections.Encounter context:
Two type 2 Yuan-ti Malisons guard area 5. Fighting in the hall brings the broodguards from area 6 in 1 round. Fenthaza’s stone urn contains an Air Elemental that obeys her. Anyone else removing the lid releases it to attack. After an alarm, the guards cover Fenthaza while she releases the elemental. She tries to capture intruders alive for area 8 and may send a particularly troublesome captive to the altar in area 6. She carries keys to area 8’s restraints. If the party leaves before the coup, she can send the elemental after them. It returns when the pursuit ends.
If prisoners serve a day of labor without incident, she offers freedom and any of Ras Nsi’s puzzle cubes in exchange for taking him down. The agreement can open the armory and start an uprising. She means to betray the party if she can.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 111–114 and 117 (Fenthaza, temple roster, and area 5). Uses the Yuan-ti Nightmare Speaker reprinted on p. 239, originally from Volo's Guide to Monsters, p. 205.

name: Flask of Wine
description: A long-limbed tabaxi guide in Port Nyanzaru. He likes company even though he usually speaks only to echo his sister, River Mist.

sections.Traits: Feline Agility. When Flask moves on his turn in combat, he can double his speed until the turn ends. He can use the trait again after spending one of his turns without moving.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Claws, Shortsword, or Shortbow.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 2 (1d4) slashing damage.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage in the printed Tabaxi Hunter block.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter context: Flask and River Mist quietly hire out in Malar’s Throat and Tiryki Anchorage. They can guide travelers to Firefinger or Dungrunglung. The Zhentarim pay attention to what the two learn about Artus Cimber, and the pair report back unless given a reason to keep quiet.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 35 (River Mist and Flask of Wine) and p. 232 (Tabaxi Hunter).

name: Grabstab
description: Queen of the Biting Ant Batiri in Yellyark. She wears the amulet that controls Vorn and has no idea what it does.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks, the second with disadvantage.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) piercing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Nimble Escape. Take the Disengage or Hide action.
sections.Reactions: Redirect Attack. When a creature Grabstab can see targets her with an attack, choose another Goblin within 5 ft. The two swap places and the attack targets that Goblin instead.
sections.Encounter context:
Two goblins watch the hut and four attendants stay inside. One attendant has the cage key. Grabstab’s bronze-and-adamantine amulet can control Vorn, a Shield Guardian.
Yellyark lookout ponchos grant advantage on Stealth while the sentries stay still and impose disadvantage when they move. A search finds the alarm tripwires with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check. Passive Perception 13 also spots them. If the sentries spot intruders or hear an alarm, the village goes on alert.
sections.Village launch: Cut the anchor vine to spring the village’s net. The vine has AC 15 and 15 HP, vulnerability to slashing, resistance to fire and piercing, and immunity to bludgeoning, poison, psychic, and thunder. In daylight, a DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals how the mechanism works. Proficiency in Survival grants advantage on the check. Anyone caught in the net when it lands makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 28 (8d6) bludgeoning damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 89–90 (Yellyark and the queen’s hut). Uses Goblin Boss from Monster Manual (2014), p. 166.

name: Grandfather Zitembe
description: The senior priest of Savras in Port Nyanzaru. His divinations give the party a lead on the Soulmonger.

sections.Languages: Any two languages. The adventure does not specify which.
sections.Actions: Mace. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Divine Eminence. Expend a spell slot to add 10 (3d6) radiant damage to each hit with a melee weapon until the turn ends. A slot above 1st level adds another 1d6 per level above 1st.
sections.Spellcasting:
5th-level cleric. Uses Wisdom (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips: Light, Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy.
1st level (4 slots): Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt, Sanctuary.
2nd level (3 slots): Lesser Restoration, Spiritual Weapon.
3rd level (2 slots): Dispel Magic, Spirit Guardians.
sections.Encounter context:
At the party’s first visit three Zhentarim Assassins offer a ruby worth 500 gp for help finding Artus Cimber. Zitembe turns them away. The interruption leaves him inclined to help the party.
A convincing argument or a donation of at least 25 gp secures a 24-hour divination. He sees a southern jungle city ringed by cliffs and full of snakes, along with a vine-covered black obelisk. He urges the party to look for those landmarks.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 20–21 (Temple of Savras). Zitembe appears on p. 21. Uses Priest from Monster Manual (2014), p. 348.

name: Ifan Talro'a
description: Port Nyanzaru's merchant prince for trained animals. Zhentarim contacts protect his interests, and his flying snakes carry reports about treasure hunters heading south.

sections.Languages: Any two languages, as in the Noble block.
sections.Actions: Rapier. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack would hit, Ifan can add 2 to AC against that attack. The attacker must be visible to Ifan, who must be holding a melee weapon.
sections.Encounter context: Ifan's merchants sell mounts and pets and report back to him. He sells Flying Snakes trained to carry messages only to the Zhentarim. Omu's yuan-ti secretly pay him to report expeditions. He suspects who receives his messages.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, pp. 25–26. Use the Noble from Monster Manual (2014), p. 348.

name: Jessamine
description: Port Nyanzaru's merchant prince for plants, poisons, and sanctioned killings. She keeps her worsening death curse hidden beneath bandages.
hpRule: The listed dice are for the Assassin base. Jessamine starts the adventure with a maximum of 58 HP, down from the base average of 78.

sections.Languages: Thieves' Cant and any two other languages.
sections.Traits:
Assassinate. On her first turn, Jessamine has advantage on attacks against creatures that have yet to act. A hit against a surprised creature is a critical hit.
Evasion. If a Dexterity save would let her take half damage, she takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Sneak Attack (once per turn). A weapon hit deals an extra 14 (4d6) damage if she attacks with advantage. She can also add this damage without advantage if she has no disadvantage and an ally who isn't incapacitated is within 5 ft. of the target.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shortsword attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage. The target also makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 24 (7d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
Light Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. The target also makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 24 (7d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
sections.Death curse: Jessamine was restored to life years ago, so the Soulmonger reduces her maximum HP by 1 each midnight after the adventure begins. The loss cannot be restored while it is active. She dies at a maximum of 0 HP, and the curse traps her soul if she dies while the Soulmonger remains active.
sections.Encounter context: Jessamine is inclined to help anyone trying to end the curse. At the council she speaks little and often breaks ties. She sells poisons at market price and controls the city's lawful writs for sanctioned killings.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, p. 26, and Death Curse, p. 6. Use the Assassin from Monster Manual (2014), p. 343, with maximum HP reduced to 58 at the adventure's start.

name: Jobal
description: A former wilderness guide who now controls Port Nyanzaru's guide and mercenary trade. His trusted spy and partner, Aazon Talieri, arranges introductions.

sections.Traits: Keen Hearing and Sight. Jobal has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on sight or hearing.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks or two ranged attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter context: Aazon can introduce the party to Port Nyanzaru's wilderness guides. Jobal charges the party nothing up front because the guides owe him a share of their earnings. If he learns about Syndra Silvane's map, he wants to buy it and may turn to theft or murder if refused.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, p. 26. Use the Scout from Monster Manual (2014), p. 349. Aazon uses the Spy block.

name: Kupalué
description: Qawasha's vegepygmy companion, nicknamed Weed. The two use a sign language of their own.

sections.Languages: Vegepygmy. Uses a private sign language with Qawasha.
sections.Traits:
Plant Camouflage. Kupalué has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in terrain with enough plant cover to hide.
Regeneration. At the start of its turn, Kupalué regains 3 HP. Cold, fire, or necrotic damage prevents regeneration at the start of its next turn. Kupalué dies only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
sections.Actions:
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Sling. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Encounter context: Kupalué travels with Qawasha, a guide from Fort Beluarian who deliberately seeks undead to clear them out. Kupalué stands about 3 ft. tall and weighs about 30 lb. dry or 50 lb. wet.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, p. 35. Appendix D reprints the Vegepygmy on p. 234, matching Volo's Guide to Monsters, p. 196.

name: Kwayothé
description: A Port Nyanzaru merchant prince and priest of Kossuth, the fire god. She controls trade in fruit, wine, ale, tej, oils, perfume, and insect repellent.

sections.Languages: Any two languages, as in the Priest block.
sections.Damage resistances: Fire while wearing her attuned Ring of Resistance (fire).
sections.Special equipment: Ring of Resistance (fire). The garnet ring gives Kwayothé resistance to fire damage while she wears it. The ring requires attunement.
sections.Bonus actions: Divine Eminence. Spend a spell slot. Until the end of her turn, Kwayothé's melee weapon hits deal extra radiant damage. A 1st-level slot adds 10 (3d6). Add 1d6 more for each slot level above 1st.
sections.Actions: Mace. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Kwayothé is a 5th-level cleric spellcaster using Wisdom (spell save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will. Light, Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy.
1st level, 4 slots. Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt, Sanctuary.
2nd level, 3 slots. Lesser Restoration, Spiritual Weapon.
3rd level, 2 slots. Dispel Magic, Spirit Guardians.
sections.Encounter context: Her consorts, the Succubus Ixis and the Incubus Indar, pass for Chultan humans. Both are fiends. She undermines Zhanthi's family and business.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, p. 26. Use the Priest from Monster Manual (2014), p. 348, and apply the printed Ring of Resistance (fire).

name: Laskilar
description: The captain of the Stirge, a pirate ship out of Jahaka Anchorage. He hunts adventurers whose discoveries can be sold to wealthy buyers.

sections.Languages: Any two languages, as in the Bandit Captain block.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee Scimitar attacks and one melee Dagger attack, or two ranged Dagger attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
Cape of the Mountebank. While wearing the cape, Laskilar can cast Dimension Door as an action. It recharges at dawn. Smoke lightly obscures both the space he leaves and the space he arrives in. It lasts until the end of his next turn or until a light or stronger wind disperses it.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack would hit, Laskilar can add 2 to AC against that attack. The attacker must be visible to Laskilar, who must be holding a melee weapon.
sections.Encounter context: Heel, a half-orc Gladiator, is his first mate. The Stirge carries twelve Bandits, six Thugs, and Caldos Hellingskorn, a Priest of Umberlee. The Anchorage captains have a pact with Liara Portyr.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 2, p. 67. Use the Bandit Captain from Monster Manual (2014), p. 344, with the printed Cape of the Mountebank from Dungeon Master's Guide (2014), p. 157.

name: Mister Threadneedle
description: The Sewn Sisters' silent servant lays out a feast in the Trial of the Pentagon. An illusion makes him look like a gaunt man in a worn black suit.

sections.Languages: Understands Common. Communicates with gestures and facial expressions.
sections.Damage resistances: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned, unconscious.
sections.Traits:
False Appearance. While motionless in his true form, he passes for an ordinary scarecrow.
Construct Nature. He does not need air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (2d4 + 1) slashing damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or remain frightened until the end of his next turn.
Terrifying Glare. Choose one creature he can see within 30 ft. If it can see him, it must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or become magically frightened until the end of his next turn. The target is paralyzed while frightened by the glare.
sections.Pentagon trial: Detect Magic reveals the illusion. Dispel Magic exposes his true form with a successful DC 16 check. He attacks only in response to an attack or at the hags’ command. He carries their Hag Eye, the key to the cage in area 71, and a black marble that activates the Ebon Pool in area 81.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 5, pp. 180 and 182–183 (areas 71 and 74) and p. 189 (area 81). Use the Scarecrow combat rules from Monster Manual (2014), p. 268.

name: Musharib
description: Musharib guides travelers out of Port Nyanzaru while looking for help reclaiming Hrakhamar. He wears dinosaur-bone armor and carries a wooden maul he calls Skullbash.

sections.Armor: Hide armor made from dinosaur bones.
sections.Traits: Dwarven Resilience. Roll saves against poison with advantage.
sections.Innate spellcasting: Wisdom. He can cast Hunter's Mark, Jump, Pass without Trace, Speak with Animals, and Speak with Plants once each per day without material components.
sections.Actions: Handaxe. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.
sections.Hrakhamar: His standard fee is 5 gp per day. He hopes to recruit the party to reclaim the forge or recover Moradin’s Gauntlet. Musharib has the smith’s tools proficiency needed to make copies of the two treasury keys with Hrakhamar’s equipment. The attempt requires a DC 10 Intelligence check. Three failed attempts ruin the impressions.
sections.Equipment note: The encounter gives Musharib Skullbash, a wooden Maul. The Albino Dwarf Spirit Warrior profile supplies the Handaxe action. If you use Skullbash instead, apply the normal 2014 Maul rule (2d6 bludgeoning plus Strength), adding proficiency to hit if you treat him as proficient with his personal weapon.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, p. 34, ch. 2, p. 62 (Hrakhamar), and appendix D, p. 210 (Albino Dwarf Spirit Warrior).

name: Nanny Pu'pu
description: A green hag who poses as Mbala's last survivor. She wants the nearby pterafolk driven out and prefers to lure victims away from their companions.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. She breathes air and water.
Mimicry. She can copy animal sounds or humanoid voices. A listener identifies the imitation with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.
sections.Innate spellcasting: Charisma, save DC 12. At will without material components, cast Dancing Lights, Minor Illusion, or Vicious Mockery.
sections.Actions:
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Illusory Appearance. Use magic to disguise herself and her gear as a creature of similar size and humanoid shape. The illusion ends at her death or when she dismisses it as a bonus action. Physical contact exposes the disguise. A creature can also spend an action to study it and make a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check.
Invisible Passage. She and her gear become magically invisible until she attacks, casts a spell, or loses concentration as though concentrating on a spell. She leaves no physical traces while invisible and can only be tracked by magic.
sections.Mbala allies: Her whistle calls 2d6 Flying Monkeys that fetch food and supplies but refuse to fight for her. If she commands the Flesh Golem buried beside her hut to attack, it rises as a bonus action.
sections.Rite of Stolen Life: The rite takes one hour and uses an intact or mostly intact humanoid corpse, a gemstone worth 100 gp or more, and the sacrifice of another humanoid. The sacrifice’s spirit reanimates the corpse and takes on its knowledge and personality. Restore the returned character to full HP and keep its statistics. Change its type to Undead and remove the need to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep. Reduce its maximum HP by 1d4 at each dawn, and no effect can stop or reverse this decay. At a maximum of 0 HP, the gemstone breaks and the body dies again. If later raised or resurrected, the character keeps levels and XP earned during the rite’s effect and forgets that period. The hag asks the party to deal with the Pterafolk and may demand a token from Niles Breakbone or Saja N’baza as well.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 2, pp. 72–73 (Mbala and the Rite of Stolen Life). The Green Hag rules come from Monster Manual (2014), p. 177.

name: Nepartak
description: Napaka's granddaughter speaks into visitors' minds from a skull sealed in a crystal box in Moa's tomb. Panic can drive her to break the box and attack.

sections.Traits:
Illumination. Choose dim light in a 15-ft. radius, or bright light in that radius with dim light 15 ft. farther out. Switching modes takes an action.
Magic Resistance. Roll saves against spells and other magic with advantage.
Rejuvenation. After destruction she returns at full HP in one hour unless her remains are sprinkled with Holy Water or targeted by Dispel Magic or Remove Curse.
Undead Nature. She does not need air, food, drink, or sleep.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Use Fire Ray twice.
Fire Ray. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (3d6) fire damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
5th-level Intelligence spellcaster, save DC 13 and +5 to hit. The inherited Flameskull spellcasting needs no somatic or material components.
Cantrip at will. Mage Hand.
1st level, 3 slots. Magic Missile, Shield.
2nd level, 2 slots. Blur, Flaming Sphere.
3rd level, 1 slot. Fireball.
sections.Moa’s tomb: She senses intruders and questions them by telepathy. A lie takes a DC 12 Charisma (Deception) check. Ignoring her, telling her she is only a skull, or failing three Deception checks makes her break out and attack. Six Swarms of Insects (Spiders) enter from the niches at the start of the following round. Use the ordinary spider swarm statistics and allow effects that target Undead to affect them. The passages admit Tiny creatures freely and Small creatures if they squeeze.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 5, p. 137 (area 14), with the Flameskull from Monster Manual (2014), p. 134. The adventure replaces spoken language with telepathy.

name: Niles Breakbone
description: A Chondathan templar of Tyr and commander of Camp Vengeance. His two captains keep the fort running when he retreats to his command tent.

sections.Languages: Any two languages, as for the printed Noble.
sections.Actions: Rapier. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Reactions: Parry. When a melee attack would hit him, add 2 to AC against that attack if he can see the attacker and holds a melee weapon.
sections.Camp Vengeance: Parties arriving by boat are ordered to ferry messages and seven sick soldiers downriver to Port Nyanzaru. The soldiers have Blue Mist Fever, Shivering Sickness, or Throat Leeches. Parties arriving over land are ordered to lead four Guards and four Tribal Warriors on a two-week undead patrol back the way they came. Refusal brings arrest and trial. A guilty verdict means confiscation of gear and abandonment in the jungle. Undril Silvertusk can intercede for a party that earned her respect. Otherwise, a sound argument and a successful DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check with each of Ord Firebeard and Perne Salhana can prevent judgment.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 2, pp. 47–48 (Camp Vengeance and Command Tent), using the Noble from Monster Manual (2014), p. 348. Uses the official Blue Mist Fever erratum.

name: Orvex Ocrammas
description: A Red Wizard expedition's scribe and translator, trapped beneath a wall after the attack on its compound in Omu. He can read Old Omuan and knows the legend of the nine trickster gods.

sections.Languages: Common, Grung. He can translate Old Omuan.
sections.Traits: Sneak Attack (once per turn). A weapon hit deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage if Orvex has advantage. It can also deal the extra damage if an ally who is not incapacitated is within 5 ft. of the target and Orvex does not have disadvantage.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Hand Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Cunning Action. On each of his turns, Orvex can Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a bonus action.
sections.First encounter: Orvex starts with 3 of 27 HP and three levels of exhaustion. Under the 2014 rules, reduce his speed to 15 ft. and give him disadvantage on ability checks, attacks, and saving throws. If rescued and befriended, he can negotiate a truce with surviving Red Wizards and recount Omu’s legend once healed and rested.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 3, p. 96 (Omu, area 2). Use the Spy from Monster Manual (2014), p. 349, with the adventure’s starting injuries, exhaustion, alignment, and languages.

name: Qawasha
description: An Emerald Enclave guide based at Fort Beluarian who travels with the vegepygmy Kupalué. He deliberately takes routes through undead territory to help drive the undead out of Chult.

sections.Armor: AC 11, or 16 while protected by Barkskin.
sections.Languages: Druidic and two other languages. Qawasha and Kupalué use a private sign language with each other.
sections.Spellcasting:
4th-level druid, Wisdom, save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks. Treat him as a druid for magic item use and attunement requirements.
Cantrips (at will). Druidcraft, Produce Flame, Shillelagh.
1st level (4 slots). Entangle, Longstrider, Speak with Animals, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots). Animal Messenger, Barkskin.
sections.Actions: Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage, or 4 (1d8) with both hands. While Shillelagh is active, the attack is +4 to hit and deals 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Guide: Qawasha knows the jungle's plants and animals and can find campsites near Chwingas. When he guides an expedition, he deliberately seeks out undead-infested areas to clear them. He recommends buying an exploration charter before leaving Fort Beluarian because the Flaming Fist mistreats unlicensed explorers.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 35, handout 7 on p. 246. Use the Druid from Monster Manual (2014), p. 346, with the published errata.

name: River Mist
description: A quiet tabaxi guide who wears an eyepatch over her right eye. She prefers the jungle to crowds and guides out of Port Nyanzaru alongside her brother Flask of Wine.

sections.Traits: Feline Agility. When River moves on her turn in combat, she can double her speed for the rest of that turn. She regains this option after spending one of her turns without moving.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Claws, Shortsword, or Shortbow.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 2 (1d4) slashing damage.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Guide: The siblings meet clients discreetly in Malar's Throat or Tiryki Anchorage and can lead a group to Firefinger and Dungrunglung. The Zhentarim ask them to gather information on Artus Cimber. Unless given a reason to keep quiet, they report what they learn on their next visit to Port Nyanzaru.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 35, using the Tabaxi Hunter on p. 232. Handout 8 appears on p. 247.

name: Salida
description: A yuan-ti operative who passes as a Chultan guide in Port Nyanzaru. She tries to join expeditions headed toward Omu, even if the only available work is as a porter or paddler.

sections.Traits: Magic Resistance. Salida has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma, save DC 12, no material components.
At will. Animal Friendship (snakes only).
3/day each. Poison Spray, Suggestion.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.
sections.Equipment and allegiance: Salida carries one of a pair of Sending Stones in a pouch. She uses it to report expedition activity to Ras Nsi.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 35, handout 9 on p. 247. Use the Yuan-ti Pureblood from Monster Manual (2014), p. 310, and add Survival +5.

name: Sekelok
description: Ras Nsi's bodyguard in the Fane of the Night Serpent. Ras Nsi uses him to punish challengers in duels to first blood or death.

sections.Traits:
Indomitable (2/day). Reroll a failed saving throw.
Magic Resistance. Sekelok has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Innate spellcasting:
Charisma, save DC 13, no material components.
At will. Animal Friendship (snakes only), Poison Spray.
3/day. Suggestion.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using Greatsword or Shortbow.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage. If Sekelok has more than half his maximum hit points left, it deals an extra 7 (2d6) slashing damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage. If Sekelok has more than half his maximum hit points left, it deals an extra 7 (2d6) piercing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Second Wind (recharges after a short or long rest). Regain 20 hit points.
sections.Throne room: By day Sekelok guards Ras Nsi in area 11 with three Yuan-ti Broodguards. After Ras Nsi retires to area 12 at night, Sekelok usually stays at his post but sometimes slips away to see Neema in area 10. If the gong in area 9 sounds, he and the other yuan-ti guards investigate while the ghouls stay behind the throne and Ras Nsi withdraws.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 4, p. 120 (area 11), using the Champion printed on p. 216 (originally Volo's Guide to Monsters, p. 212). The variant changes defenses, senses, languages, and spells. It retains the Champion's 30-ft. speed.

name: Shago
description: Zhanthi's son guides expeditions from Fort Beluarian. He wants to impress Liara Portyr and earn an official place in the Flaming Fist.

sections.Traits:
Brave. Shago has advantage on saves against being frightened.
Brute. A melee weapon hit adds one weapon damage die, already included in the attacks below.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks or two ranged attacks.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) if he uses both hands in melee.
