Shield Bash. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Reactions: Parry. Add 3 to AC against one melee attack that would hit, provided Shago sees the attacker and is wielding a melee weapon.
sections.Guide: While Shago guides the party, characters have advantage on Charisma checks to influence Flaming Fist members. He works closely with the faction while presenting himself as independent. He shares little useful information with his mother.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 35, handout 10 on p. 248. Use the Gladiator from Monster Manual (2014), p. 346, and add Survival +7.

name: Skeleton Key
description: A roaming human skeleton whose skull has been carved into a key for the gate in the Sewn Sisters' lair. It usually flees when approached.

sections.Languages: Understands the languages it knew in life. It cannot speak.
sections.Traits:
Spider Climb. The skeleton can traverse difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Tomb Traps. The skeleton does not trigger traps in tomb rooms or on tomb doors.
Intact Remains. At 0 hit points it falls apart, leaving its skull and other bones intact.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee Dagger attacks.
Dagger. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Finding the keys: Place one skeleton on each of the first five tomb levels in a location marked by a skull on the level map. A DC 12 Wisdom (Survival) check follows a key's trail to the nearest unexplored location bearing that mark. The skulls are triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon, and octagon in level order. The key flees if it can to avoid capture or destruction. Characters can capture the skeleton or remove its skull.
sections.Skeleton gate: In area 71, completing each trial in areas 72 through 76 exposes one corresponding keyhole. Insert the matching skull and turn it clockwise. Once all five tumblers are unlocked, pull the door open to reach the stairs to area 77. Damage and spells cannot open the gate or remove its seals. The Sewn Sisters enter from the Border Ethereal when the party opens all five keyholes with the keys in hand. A hag that takes a key retreats into the Border Ethereal with it.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 126–127 and 180 (area 71), adapting the Skeleton from Monster Manual (2014), p. 272.

name: Syndra Silvane
description: A retired Tethyrian adventurer and merchant who hides the ravages of the death curse beneath a silver mask.

sections.Armor: AC 15 while Mage Armor is active.
sections.Damage resistances: Damage from spells. While Stoneskin is active, she also resists nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. Syndra has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Death Curse. Her maximum drops by 1 at midnight each day. She dies if it reaches 0. Destroying the Soulmonger stops the loss and restores her usual maximum. If Syndra has died, she can be raised only after the curse ends and only if her soul was never devoured.
sections.Actions: Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Syndra is an 18th-level wizard spellcaster using Intelligence (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks). She can cast Disguise Self and Invisibility at will.
Cantrips at will. Fire Bolt, Light, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation, Shocking Grasp.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Identify, Mage Armor, Magic Missile.
2nd level (3 slots). Detect Thoughts, Mirror Image, Misty Step.
3rd level (3 slots). Counterspell, Fly, Lightning Bolt.
4th level (3 slots). Banishment, Fire Shield, Stoneskin.
5th level (3 slots). Cone of Cold, Scrying, Wall of Force.
6th level (1 slot). Globe of Invulnerability.
7th level (1 slot). Teleport.
8th level (1 slot). Mind Blank.
9th level (1 slot). Time Stop.
She casts Mage Armor, Stoneskin, and Mind Blank on herself before a fight when able.
sections.Starting the adventure: Syndra gives the party a map and takes them to the Harbor Ward of Port Nyanzaru with Teleport if they agree. The adventure puts the group on target near the docks without an accuracy roll. She stays with Wakanga O'tamu. For ending the curse, each character can choose an appropriate uncommon or rare magic item with the DM's approval. If asked for an advance, she gives each character 50 gp.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 8–9. Syndra uses the Archmage from Monster Manual (2014), p. 342, with the adventure's alignment, languages, and reduced hit point maximum.

hpRule: At the start of the adventure, 79 is her death curse-adjusted maximum. The Hit Dice come from the Archmage, whose printed average is 99 HP.

name: Terracotta Warrior
description: An animated clay guardian standing watch over Shagambi's tomb with a sheathed shortsword.

sections.Senses: Blindsight 60 ft. Beyond that radius it is blind.
sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Antimagic Susceptibility. Inside an Antimagic Field, the warrior is incapacitated. If targeted by Dispel Magic, it must pass a Constitution save against the caster's spell save DC or become unconscious for 1 minute.
False Appearance. A motionless warrior passes for a terracotta statue.
Fragile. A critical hit shatters and destroys it.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shortsword attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Shagambi's tomb: Forty-eight warriors stand guard. Loud noise makes them draw their swords partway as a warning. On any further noise, they attack every creature in the tomb. Moving quietly without magic takes a DC 12 Dexterity (Stealth) check, at disadvantage when crossing pottery shards. Opening Shagambi's coffin can set off a music box that rouses them even if the room was quiet. A DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) check while carefully lifting the lid spots the wire. Cut it with thieves' tools and a successful DC 12 Dexterity check. Failure sets off the music.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 161, area 48. The adventure adapts Animated Armor from Monster Manual (2014), p. 19, and gives the warrior two Shortsword strikes and a vulnerability to critical hits.

name: Volothamp “Volo” Geddarm
description: An author and traveler visiting Port Nyanzaru to promote his monster guide and deliver signed copies to the merchant princes.

sections.Actions: Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Volo is a 1st-level wizard spellcaster using Intelligence (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will. Friends, Mending, Prestidigitation.
1st level (2 slots). Comprehend Languages, Detect Magic, Disguise Self.
sections.Port Nyanzaru: Look for Volo in a tavern or a merchant prince's villa. He offers credible lore mixed with unreliable tales and refuses to leave the city. The hardcover of Volo's Guide to Monsters costs 50 gp. Give readers useful in-world lore when they consult it. He willingly shares 1d4 + 1 clues from the chapter 1 Jungle Rumors table and might let the party accompany him on visits to the princes.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 235 for the stat block, pp. 24 and 236 for Port Nyanzaru and the rumor procedure.

name: Wakanga O'tamu
description: Port Nyanzaru's merchant prince of magic and lore. He shelters the Harpers in his villa and takes in his old friend Syndra.

sections.Languages: Any four languages, as for the printed Mage.
sections.Armor: AC 15 while Mage Armor is active.
sections.Actions: Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Wakanga is a 9th-level wizard spellcaster using Intelligence (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will. Fire Bolt, Light, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Shield.
2nd level (3 slots). Misty Step, Suggestion.
3rd level (3 slots). Counterspell, Fireball, Fly.
4th level (3 slots). Greater Invisibility, Ice Storm.
5th level (1 slot). Cone of Cold.
sections.Port Nyanzaru: Wakanga deals in potions, scrolls, and lost lore. He welcomes adventurers traveling with Syndra Silvane. He may help anyone pursuing the cause of the death curse, including selling magic items for coin, gemstones, or jewelry. He is unlikely to offer credit. Common potions cost 80 gp, uncommon potions 300 gp, 1st-level spell scrolls 100 gp, and 2nd-level spell scrolls 550 gp.
sections.Waard's journal: If the party befriends him, Wakanga gives them the journal and marks the hex where Vorn, a Shield Guardian, was found. The journal depicts the control amulet. For recovering Vorn and returning that amulet, Wakanga offers a spellbook with 15 random spells. Roll a d6 for each spell's level.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, p. 27. The adventure assigns the Mage from Monster Manual (2014), p. 347.

name: Wine Weird
description: A liquid elemental that emerges from a wine cistern when the false tomb floods.

sections.Damage resistances: Fire and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, poisoned, prone, restrained, and unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Invisible in Wine. The weird becomes invisible while fully submerged in wine.
Water Bound. The inherited binding applies to the liquid the weird inhabits. It dies if it leaves that liquid or if the liquid is destroyed.
sections.Actions: Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit for 13 (3d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target is grappled (escape DC 13) and pulled 5 ft. toward the weird. The target is restrained until the grapple ends. While holding it, the weird tries to drown the target and cannot constrict another.
sections.False tomb encounter: The entrance seals 1 round after the coffin is opened if the illusory sunlight strikes its plaque. Dispel Magic on the light prevents the trigger. Once the entrance seals, the wine rises 1 ft. a round and everyone rolls initiative. On round 3, three wine weirds emerge from the northwest, northeast, and southeast cisterns and attack everyone in the room. On round 12, the room fills. Apply underwater combat with 5 ft. of visibility. Water breathing gives no protection against drowning in wine. The block rises and the wine drains after 10 minutes.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 141, area 20. The adventure uses the Water Weird from Monster Manual (2014), p. 299, with invisibility in wine.

name: Yellow Musk Creeper
description: An orchid-like vine that grows on statuary, gravestones, and other shaded surfaces. Its bright petals release an irresistible scent.

sections.Traits:
False Appearance. A motionless creeper is indistinguishable from an ordinary flowering vine.
Regeneration. At the start of its turn the creeper recovers 10 HP. Taking fire, necrotic, or radiant damage disables this recovery at the start of its next turn. It dies only if it starts a turn at 0 HP and cannot regenerate.
sections.Actions:
Touch. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit for 13 (3d8) psychic damage. A humanoid reduced to 0 HP by the damage dies and receives a bulb. Unless the bulb is destroyed, the corpse becomes a Yellow Musk Zombie 24 hours after death. Raising the humanoid, casting Remove Curse on the corpse, or using similar magic destroys the bulb if done before it animates.
Yellow Musk (3/day). All humanoids within 30 ft. make a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure they are charmed for 1 minute and spend their turns moving as close to the creeper as they can, doing nothing else. They can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect.
sections.Hosts: The vine controls the zombie it animates. In seven days the new creeper grows to full size and emerges from the host, which collapses. If the zombie is destroyed first, the young plant withers and dies. A Small host produces a Small zombie with 27 (6d6 + 6) HP, otherwise using the Yellow Musk Zombie's statistics.
sections.Wilderness encounter: Place the creeper deep in a ruin and give it 3d6 Yellow Musk Zombies, scattered or clustered to suit the terrain. At camp, the zombies emerge from a nearby ruin and try to knock the characters unconscious and drag them to the plant.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 237 for the stat block and host procedure, p. 203 for the random encounter.

name: Yellow Musk Zombie
description: A creeper animates this corpse from within. The host moves just enough to guard the young vine until it can leave.

sections.Traits: Undead Fortitude. When damage reduces the zombie to 0 HP, it makes a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to 5 + the damage taken. On a success it drops to 1 HP instead. Fire damage and critical hits bypass this save.
sections.Actions: Slam. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) bludgeoning damage.
sections.Small variant: A transformed Small humanoid becomes a Small undead with 27 HP (6d6 + 6). Keep the rest of the statistics.
sections.Host and creeper: An implanted bulb animates the corpse after 24 hours. The zombie protects the growing Yellow Musk Creeper and feeds it. After seven days the mature creeper breaks free and the host collapses. If the zombie is destroyed first, the immature creeper dies with it.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 237.

name: Yorb
description: Chief Yorb is a gold-skinned grung who rides a trained hadrosaurus at Nangnang’s shrine. He is wary of strangers and has yet to learn that his favored son is missing.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. Yorb breathes air and water.
Poisonous Skin. A creature that grapples Yorb or touches his skin makes a DC 12 Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 minute. Once contact has ended, it can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the poison on a success.
Standing Leap. Yorb can long jump up to 25 ft. and high jump up to 15 ft. without a running start.
sections.Actions:
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 12 Constitution save or takes an extra 5 (2d4) poison damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 12 Constitution save or takes an extra 5 (2d4) poison damage.
Mesmerizing Chirr (recharge 6). Each humanoid or beast within 15 ft. that can hear Yorb makes a DC 12 Wisdom save or is stunned until the end of Yorb’s next turn. Grungs are immune.
sections.Optional gold grung poison: If using the optional Volo’s Guide to Monsters poison variant, a creature poisoned by Yorb is also charmed and can speak Grung while poisoned. The poison loses potency 1 minute after removal from a grung or after the grung dies.
sections.Nangnang’s shrine: Four orange Grung Elite Warriors stay with Yorb and his Hadrosaurus in the flooded courtyard. A red Grung Wildling and seven green Grungs hold the roof. If intruders fight back, 1d4 more green grungs arrive at the end of each round, up to twenty. If losing, Yorb and his elite guards retreat into the shrine and bar the doors. Forcing those doors takes a successful DC 25 Strength check. He will talk if the characters rescue his son and can communicate with him.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 3, pp. 108–109 (area 18A), and appendix D, p. 223 (Grung Elite Warrior). The optional poison rule is from Volo’s Guide to Monsters, p. 156.

name: Yuan-ti Priest
description: Arakiti, Kultha, and Nyss are serpent-bodied priests who serve Fenthaza and consult Dendar at the oracle pool.

sections.Traits:
Shapechanger. As an action, the priest changes into a Medium snake or returns to its true form. Its statistics stay the same and its equipment stays as it was. Death does not change its form.
Magic Resistance. The priest has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Spellcasting: Innate Spellcasting (yuan-ti form only). Charisma, save DC 13 and +5 to hit with spell attacks. No material components. At will: Animal Friendship (snakes only), Eldritch Blast (two beams, 1d10 + 3 force damage for each hit), Minor Illusion, Poison Spray. Three times per day: Suggestion.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack (yuan-ti form only). Make two attacks with Scimitar or Constrict. Use Constrict at most once. The priest carries no longbow.
Bite (snake form only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13). The target is restrained while grappled this way, and the priest cannot constrict anyone else.
Scimitar (yuan-ti form only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
sections.Oracle pool: Entering the sludge or starting a turn in it deals 5 (1d10) psychic damage. Staring into it for more than a few seconds produces a vision of Dendar swallowing the viewer. At the end of the vision, the viewer makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. Failure deals 5 (1d10) psychic damage and causes a random form of long-term madness.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 4, p. 118 (area 7), modifying the Yuan-ti Malison (Type 3) in Monster Manual (2014), p. 309.

name: Zalkoré
description: Omu’s exiled queen dwells in Nangalore. Feathered veils hide her face, and her tinctures let her see her long-dead consort, Thiru-Taya.

sections.Traits:
Petrifying Gaze. When a creature that can see Zalkoré’s eyes starts its turn within 30 ft. of her, she can call for a DC 14 Constitution save if she can see it and is not incapacitated. On a failure by 5 or more, the creature is petrified immediately. Any smaller failure leaves it restrained. A creature restrained this way repeats the save at the end of its next turn. Success ends the effect. On a failure, the creature is petrified. Greater Restoration or similar magic ends the petrification.
A creature that is not surprised can avert its eyes at the start of its turn. It then cannot see Zalkoré until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. Looking at her sooner forces an immediate save. If she sees her reflection on a polished surface within 30 ft. in bright light, her own gaze affects her.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Snake Hair and two Shortsword attacks, or make two Longbow attacks.
Snake Hair. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) poison damage.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.
sections.Nangalore: Zalkoré can describe Omu’s location and the yuan-ti interest in the city. She wants a gem, piece of jewelry, or art worth at least 500 gp for her Black Orchid, which Asharra needs for a ritual. She also accepts a character with Charisma 16 or higher as a slave in trade. Disturbing Thiru-Taya’s ashes or statue, repeatedly disparaging him, pulling the veil away, taking the orchid, or bringing out a mirror can turn the encounter violent.
sections.Poisoned hospitality: Zalkoré can ring for an Eblis to bring tainted fruit and wine. Spotting the contamination requires proficiency in Medicine and a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine) check. A creature that eats or drinks makes a DC 15 Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 hour or until it drinks 2 quarts of water. Zalkoré has built up a tolerance to this dose.
sections.Thiru-Taya: At 63 HP or fewer, Zalkoré calls on Thiru-Taya’s apparition. It cannot be harmed, turned, controlled, or affected by spells. It remains until she dies or returns to full HP. Once per turn, when a creature within 15 ft. of her damages her, the apparition automatically deals 15 (2d8 + 6) force damage to that attacker with its spear.
sections.Dreaming tincture: The lair holds 2d6 single-dose vials worth 10 gp each in Port Nyanzaru. A drinker makes a DC 15 Constitution save, succeeding automatically if immune to the poisoned condition. Failure causes convincing sensory hallucinations for 1d4 + 4 hours. Lesser Restoration or similar magic ends them early.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 2, pp. 79–80 (Nangalore, area 8), using the Medusa from Monster Manual (2014), p. 214.

name: Zaroum Al-Saryak
description: The captain of the Emerald Eye wears a gem-studded coat and keeps a magical gem in the socket of his lost left eye.

sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two melee Scimitar attacks and one melee Dagger attack, or make two ranged Dagger attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Reactions: Parry. Add 2 to AC against one melee attack that would hit. Zaroum must see the attacker and hold a melee weapon.
sections.Emerald Eye: Only Zaroum can use his eye gem to see ghostly paths to treasure. He carries a Sending Stone paired with Liara Portyr’s. His jeweled coat is worth 750 gp and his jeweled Scimitar 1,250 gp. Voltan, a Berserker, is his first mate. The crew includes twelve Bandits, two Thugs, and five Tribal Warriors.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 2, p. 67 (Jahaka Anchorage), using the Bandit Captain from Monster Manual (2014), p. 344.

name: Zhanthi
description: Zhanthi is a Port Nyanzaru merchant prince with royal ancestry. She trades in gems, jewelry, Chultan cloth, and light armor.

sections.Actions: Rapier. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Reactions: Parry. Add 2 to AC against one melee attack that would hit. Zhanthi must see the attacker and hold a melee weapon.
sections.Port Nyanzaru: Zhanthi belongs to the Ytepka Society and cultivated Zhentarim contacts to keep watch on that group. Her son Shago guides travelers from Fort Beluarian and sends her reports about the fort. Her goods include nonmagical Leather Armor, Studded Leather Armor, and Hide Armor.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, p. 27 (Merchant Princes), using the Noble from Monster Manual (2014), p. 348.

name: Zindar
description: The half-gold dragon harbormaster of Port Nyanzaru spends most of his day on the docks, sorting out disputes and keeping trade moving.

sections.Actions:
Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage in one hand or 6 (1d8 + 2) in two hands.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Choose Fire Breath or Weakening Breath. The two options share a single recharge.
Fire Breath. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.
Weakening Breath. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Strength save. On a failure, it has disadvantage on Strength-based attack rolls, Strength checks, and Strength saves for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns it can repeat the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
sections.Bonus actions: Dragon Wings. On his turn, Zindar can sprout wings as a bonus action and gain a fly speed of 30 ft. He can dismiss them with another bonus action.
sections.Spellcasting:
Zindar casts as a 14th-level sorcerer using Charisma. Spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks.
Cantrips (at will). Fire Bolt, Friends, Light, Mage Hand, Mending, Message.
1st level (6 slots). Magic Missile, Shield, Sleep.
2nd level (4 slots). Detect Thoughts, Knock.
3rd level (3 slots). Clairvoyance, Tongues.
4th level (3 slots). Dominate Beast, Stoneskin.
5th level (3 slots). Hold Monster, Telekinesis.
6th level (1 slot). True Seeing.
7th level (1 slot). Fire Storm.
sections.Encounter context: Zindar is secretly part of the Ytepka Society. Messages left at his office receive a reply in 1d6 hours. He offers 2,000 gp for each pirate ship brought back to port and 500 gp more for each captured captain. The targets are the Dragonfang, the Emerald Eye, and the Stirge. Zhanthi funds the bounty and has privately uncovered evidence of Liara Portyr's arrangement with the pirates.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 239. Port Nyanzaru encounter details appear on pp. 17, 22, and 27.

name: Zorbo
description: A koala-sized predator that nests in trees and caves. It uses long claws to break through protective gear and hunt for meat.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The zorbo has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Natural Armor. Its AC depends on the material it stands on or climbs. Use AC 15 for wood or bone, 17 for earth or stone, and 19 for metal. Use AC 10 when it touches none of those materials.
sections.Actions: Destructive Claws. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (2d6 + 1) slashing damage. If the target is a creature with armor, a shield, or an item that magically improves its AC, it also makes a DC 11 Dexterity save. On a failure, it chooses one eligible item it wears or carries. The AC that item provides drops by 1. This penalty is permanent and cumulative. The zorbo gains +1 AC until the start of its next turn. The item breaks if armor drops to AC 10 or if a shield or protective magic item drops to a +0 AC bonus.
sections.Encounter context: In the wilderness, travelers spot 2d6 zorbos in wukka trees. The zorbos warn off approaching creatures and attack if threatened. Around a campsite, hungry zorbos descend from the trees and attack outright. Four lurk near Obo'laka's shrine in Omu. They investigate the noisy entrance doors and target lone creatures or stragglers.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 241. The Omu shrine and wilderness encounters are on pp. 109 and 204.

name: Bodak
description: An undead devotee of Orcus. Orcus can recall anything the bodak witnesses and speak through it.

sections.Languages: Abyssal and the languages it spoke in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, and necrotic damage. It also resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Aura of Annihilation. The bodak can turn the aura on or off as a bonus action. While it is on, creatures within 30 ft. of the bodak take 5 necrotic damage when they end their turns there. Fiends and undead are immune to the aura.
Death Gaze. When a creature that can see the bodak’s eyes starts its turn within 30 ft. of the bodak, the bodak can force a DC 13 Constitution save. It must be able to see the creature and must not be incapacitated. A failure by 5 or more drops the target to 0 HP unless it is immune to frightened. A target that fails without dropping to 0 HP takes 16 (3d10) psychic damage. A creature that isn’t surprised can avert its eyes at the start of its turn and skip this save. It then attacks the bodak with disadvantage until its next turn starts. If it looks at the bodak before then, it makes the save immediately.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. The bodak takes 5 radiant damage if it starts its turn in sunlight. It has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks while in sunlight.
Undead Nature. The bodak needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Ravaged Soul. Restoring a bodak to its former life requires Wish or comparable magic.
sections.Actions:
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage.
Withering Gaze. One visible creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 13 Constitution save. It takes 22 (4d10) necrotic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Encounter context: Maze of Death, p. 162. Two bodaks emerge unharmed from the Sphere of Annihilation in area 49B and hunt in the maze. They drag anyone they kill back into the sphere. They return to the sphere when they think the maze is empty.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 215.

name: Firenewt Warlock of Imix
description: A priest of Imix who commands firenewt raids and claims the best spoils for the cult.

sections.Armor: AC 13 while it has Mage Armor.
sections.Senses: Darkvision 120 ft., including in magical darkness.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The warlock breathes both air and water.
Imix’s Blessing. The warlock gains 5 temporary HP when it reduces an enemy to 0 HP.
sections.Innate spellcasting: The warlock uses Charisma to cast Mage Armor on itself at will, without material components.
sections.Spellcasting:
Third-level warlock. Charisma is its spellcasting ability (save DC 12, +4 for spell attacks). Both spell slots cast at 2nd level and recharge on a short or long rest.
At-will cantrips. Fire Bolt, Guidance, Light, Mage Hand, and Prestidigitation.
1st- and 2nd-level spells known (two 2nd-level slots). Burning Hands, Flaming Sphere, Hellish Rebuke, and Scorching Ray.
sections.Actions: Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter context: Hrakhamar, pp. 62–63. A warlock supervises the forge, two in the stores debate whether to accuse that warlock of heresy, and two fight to the death with Firenewt Warriors at the shrine. A heavy patrol can include a warlock riding a Giant Strider (p. 199).
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 219.

name: Firenewt Warrior
description: An amphibious soldier of Imix trained to raid and patrol volcanic Chult.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The warrior breathes both air and water.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.
Spit Fire (recharges after a short or long rest). One creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 11 Dexterity save. It takes 9 (2d8) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Encounter context: Valley of Lost Honor and Hrakhamar, pp. 42, 61–63. Four mounted warriors typically patrol Ataaz Yklwazi. The eight warriors at the smelter are surprised unless the party draws attention. Two warriors and two Firenewt Warlocks of Imix defend the shrine to the death. For the wilderness patrol on p. 199, roll 1d4 warriors for a light patrol or 2d4 warriors and one warlock for a heavy patrol, with one Giant Strider per rider. These patrols aim to knock opponents unconscious and take them captive.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 219.

name: Flail Snail
description: A slow earth elemental with a brightly colored shell and five mace-tipped tentacles.

sections.Traits:
Antimagic Shell. The snail saves against spells with advantage. Spell attacks against it have disadvantage. Roll a d6 when the snail succeeds on a saving throw against a spell or a spell attack misses it.
1–2. An area or multitarget spell fails entirely. A spell aimed solely at the snail leaves it unharmed and rebounds at the caster with the original slot level, save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability.
3–4. Nothing else happens.
5–6. Each creature within 30 ft. of the snail makes a DC 15 Constitution save. It takes 1d6 force damage per level of the spell on a failure or half as much on a success.
Flail Tentacles. The snail starts with five. Every turn on which it takes at least 10 damage costs it one tentacle. As long as one remains, all dead tentacles grow back in 1d4 days. Losing the last tentacle sends the snail into its shell with total cover. It wails audibly out to 600 ft. until it dies 5d6 minutes later. Regenerate or other limb-restoring magic can stop it from dying.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Flail Tentacle attack per surviving tentacle, all against the same target.
Flail Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Scintillating Shell (recharges after a short or long rest). Until the end of the snail’s next turn its shell casts bright light for 30 ft. and dim light for another 30 ft. Creatures that can see the snail attack it with disadvantage during that time. Any creature in the bright light that can see the snail when it activates this effect must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or become stunned until the light goes out.
Shell Defense. The snail retracts into its shell, raising AC by 4 until it comes out. Emerging takes a bonus action on its turn.
sections.Encounter context: Unkh takes the form of a flail snail in Omuan stories (pp. 92, 102–103). A DC 10 Wisdom (Survival) check determines which way a snail was traveling from its slime trail (p. 199). An intact shell weighs about 250 lb. and is worth 2,500 gp.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 220.

name: Froghemoth
description: An amphibious swamp predator with four long tentacles. It leaves only its three-eyed stalk above water while waiting for prey.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The froghemoth breathes both air and water.
Shock Susceptibility. After taking lightning damage, it suffers these effects until the end of its next turn. Its speed is halved, its AC and Dexterity saves take a −2 penalty, and it loses reactions and Multiattack. On its turn it must choose between an action and a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks. The froghemoth may also use either Tongue or Bite.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. It also grapples a Huge or smaller creature (escape DC 16). Each of the four tentacles can hold one creature and can’t be used on another target while holding it.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage and swallows a Medium or smaller creature. The gullet holds up to two creatures. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects originating outside the froghemoth, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the froghemoth’s turns. If a creature inside deals at least 20 damage in one turn, the froghemoth must pass a DC 20 Constitution save at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which land prone within 10 ft. If the froghemoth dies, the restraint ends and a swallowed creature can spend 10 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting prone.
Tongue. One visible Medium or smaller creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 18 Strength save. On a failure, pull it to an empty space within 5 ft. of the froghemoth, which can then use Bite against that creature as a bonus action.
sections.Encounter context: Kubazan, the trickster god, takes the form of a froghemoth. At his shrine in Omu, a DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) check spots a froghemoth’s eyestalk in the murky, 6-ft.-deep pool. It attacks if someone disturbs the water or approaches the shrine, leaving the pool to pursue them (p. 97).
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 221.

name: Giant Strider
description: A fast, birdlike reptilian monstrosity that willingly carries elite firenewt riders.

sections.Traits: Fire Absorption. When fire would damage the giant strider, it takes none and instead heals half the amount it would have taken.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Fire Burst (recharge 5–6). Choose a visible point within 60 ft. Each creature in a 10-ft.-radius sphere centered there makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. It takes 14 (4d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The fire goes around corners and ignites flammable objects in the area that nobody wears or carries.
sections.Encounter context: Hrakhamar, p. 64. The firenewts keep twelve striders tethered in the mine cart bay. When a non-firenewt enters, the mounts become restless. Starting the following round, 1d3 break loose each round and attack. The striders spare firenewts, who can ride them with the standard Mounted Combat rules. A Firenewt Warrior patrol in the Valley of Lost Honor travels on these mounts (pp. 42, 83, 199).
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 222.
